Unveiling the Role of the Soil Matrix in Trichloroethylene Degradation by Ball-Milled Sulfidated Microscale Zero-Valent Iron
papers.abstract: Abstract Ball-milled sulfidated microscale zerovalent iron (S-mZVIbm) is highly effective in degrading trichloroethylene (TCE) in anoxic water. This study investigated its performance and soil-mediated regulation in a soil-water mixed system (SWMS) using two natural soils. The results show that soil addition markedly enhanced the reactivity of S-mZVIbm. Compared with the aqueous system, the degradation rate constant of TCE (kTCE) exhibited a 6.0–8.4-fold increase at a soil-to-water ratio (S/W) of 0.5 to 2.0, while H2 production concurrently increased 210%–450%. This activation was accompanied by a decrease in apparent electron efficiency from 74.3% in water to 15.9%–27.6% in SWMS. S-mZVIbm retained higher reactivity in SWMS than in water across pH 6–10, with a maximum kTCE of 0.26 h–1 at pH 8.0. SEM, XPS, and component-specific experiments indicated that soil-mediated surface restructuring and Fe(II) redistribution-induced depassivation increased the accessibility of Fe0-rich domains, whereas organic matter and Ca/Mg-bearing phases imposed inhibitory effects. Sulfidation suppressed H2 evolution and reduced soil-specific variability under multicontaminant conditions involving TCE, carbon tetrachloride, nitrobenzene, and perchloroethylene. These results identify soil as an active regulator of Fe0 accessibility and electron allocation rather than a passive reaction medium, providing a mechanistic basis for site-specific S-mZVIbm remediation.

papers.title: Aerosol Deposition in the Human Respiratory System from Distinct Urban Sources Using Multiple Exposure Metrics
papers.abstract: Abstract Targeting specific aerosol sources offers more effective air-quality control than focusing solely on ambient concentrations. Using source apportionment, major contributors to particle number concentrations in the diameter range of 6–1000 nm in urban background of Budapest, Hungary were identified, and their size distributions applied in lung deposition modelling under reference breathing conditions. In this study, we find that most particles penetrate to the deep lung with a maximum deposition at airway generations 17 to 21 depending on physical activity. Deposition fractions vary substantially by source, ranging from 76% (new particle formation) to 27% (solid fuel combustion). Exercise enhances overall deposition, and redistributes the deposited particles within the respiratory tract by decreasing extra-thoracic deposition and increasing the alveolar fraction. Our results also show that deposition rates are more sensitive to physical activity than deposition fractions. These deposition curves exhibit a levelling-off tendency in the extra-thoracic region, while continuing to increase in the lung. Particle number and particle surface area deposition curves are similar in shape, although the relative importance of aerosol sources and the most affected respiratory regions differ. We point that surface-density deposition rates are three orders of magnitude higher in the nose and mouth than in the lung.

papers.title: Synthetic DNA Tracers Enable Ultra-High-Reproducibility Characterization of Aquifer Hydraulic Conductivity and Contaminant Transport
papers.abstract: Abstract Reliable characterization of aquifer hydraulic conductivity (K) via tracer-based methods remains a major challenge due to environmental background noise. We report that synthetic DNA tracers, free of background-noise interference, enable highly reproducible tomographic inversion of K fields across six replicate experiments conducted in a heterogeneous laboratory sandbox measuring 180 cm (length) × 10 cm (width) × 90 cm (height) at a steady flow rate of approximately 177.4 cm3 min–1. The results demonstrate superior reproducibility of the DNA tracers relative to dye tracers across three evaluation levels: travel-time consistency, where the contrast is most pronounced (mean R2 = 0.84 for DNA tracers versus R2 = 0.10 for dye tracers), inverted lnK field coherence, and prediction-level robustness. Contaminant-transport forecasts under four scenarios, spanning pulse versus continuous releases and conservative versus decaying solutes, further indicate that DNA-derived K fields yield substantially more stable predictions than dye-derived K fields in nearly all cases. These advantages arise from the standardized molecular design of oligonucleotides and their sequence-specific quantitation via qPCR, which collectively mitigate background interference and tracer-specific transport artifacts. These findings show that synthetic DNA tracers constitute a promising tool for aquifer characterization, addressing a critical gap in tracer-based tomography for groundwater investigations.

papers.title: Phage Lysis Associated with Biodegradable Microplastics Mediates Microbial Physiological Adaptation to Transform Organic Matter in Soil
papers.abstract: Abstract Biodegradable microplastics (MPs) profoundly impact the storage and stability of soil organic matter (SOM), yet the mechanisms by which phages mediate the transformation of plant- and microbially derived SOM under biodegradable MP perturbation remain poorly understood. This study integrated multiomics, stable isotope techniques, and phage inoculation experiments to investigate how phages mediate SOM transformation following biodegradable MP addition in agricultural soil. The results revealed that lytic phage-bacteria interactions were central to MP-dependent SOM transformation. Polylactic acid (PLA) reduced plant-derived organic molecules by 15% without affecting microbially derived carbon. PLA increased phage lysis and enriched auxiliary metabolic genes (AMGs) such as queC (2.2-fold increase), which supports phage replication and reduces microbial biomass. Pure culture experiments supported that PLA increased phage lytic infectivity. Phage inoculation further revealed that lytic phages accelerated bacteria to shift toward catabolism (e.g., lignocellulose degradation, citrate cycle) in PLA-amended soil, reducing carbon use efficiency (CUE) and accelerating decomposition of plant- and microbially derived carbon through viral shunt. In comparison, polyhydroxyalkanoates (PHA) increased microbially derived molecules by 37%, particularly amino nitrogen compounds. The higher degradability of PHA stimulated lytic phage bloom with their hosts and enriched biosynthesis-related AMGs (e.g., cysH, glmS). Phage inoculation experiments showed that surviving bacteria assimilated phage lysate products into anabolism (e.g., amino acid and amino sugar biosynthesis), enriching metabolites such as l-isoleucine and MurNAc after PHA addition. This increased CUE and accumulation of microbial organics through viral shuttle. These findings uncover phage-mediated mechanisms linking microplastic perturbation to soil carbon cycling.

papers.title: Neglecting Changes in Salinity and Tidal Range Overstates Projected Increases in Greenhouse Gas Emissions from Mangrove Sediments
papers.abstract: Abstract Mangroves are important coastal blue carbon ecosystems, but future sediment GHG emissions remain uncertain because global projections have largely emphasized atmospheric climate drivers, with less attention to coastal hydrology, particularly sea-surface salinity and tidal range. Here, we compiled 810 sediment GHG flux measurements from 294 mangrove sites worldwide and used machine learning to project emissions to 2050, distinguishing climate-driven changes from the additional effects of projected shifts in sea-surface salinity and tidal range. We estimate a mangrove sediment GHG budget of ∼194 Tg CO2e yr–1 across reliably predicted mangrove areas worldwide around 2020. By 2050 under SSP5–8.5, projected changes in salinity and tidal range counteracted 41% of the climate-driven increase in emissions globally, with comparable offset effects among CO2, CH4, and N2O. Hydrological offset effects were strongest at 10–20° latitude in both hemispheres and weakened toward the equator and higher latitudes. Regionally, hydrological offset effects were greatest in East Africa, whereas the Indo-Pacific showed the largest absolute hydrology-driven reductions in emission budgets, largely owing to its extensive mangrove area. These findings highlight the importance of incorporating sea-surface salinity and tidal range into future projections of mangrove sediment GHG emissions under global change.

papers.title: Current Strengths and Limitations of Toxicokinetic-Toxicodynamic (TKTD) Models for Freshwater Microalgae
papers.abstract: Abstract Toxicokinetic-toxicodynamic (TKTD) models are increasingly used to enhance environmental risk assessment by linking laboratory toxicity data with dynamic exposure scenarios. For freshwater microalgae, which are crucial primary producers, TKTD approaches offer a framework to predict population growth inhibition and recovery under fluctuating chemical stress. A review of 12 studies (2012–2023) applying TKTD models to freshwater planktonic microalgae was conducted to compare their structural assumptions, end points, and validation methods. These models mainly focus on green algae and herbicides that inhibit photosystem II, with limited exploration of other taxonomic groups or modes of action. The complexity of models varies significantly, from simple structures assuming rapid equilibrium between external and internal chemical concentrations to mechanistic models that explicitly incorporate TK components and damage progression. While simple models support regulatory use, omitting TK processes can reduce their effectiveness for chemicals with delayed effects or complex uptake behaviors. Expanding taxonomic coverage and enhancing external validation under realistic exposure conditions is crucial to increasing the ecological relevance of algal TKTD modeling.

papers.title: Expansion of Freshwater Harmful Cyanobacteria in Brackish Waters: Salt Stress Responses, Toxigenic Dynamics, and Ecological Risks along the Freshwater-to-Marine Continuum
papers.abstract: Abstract In recent years, freshwater harmful cyanobacterial blooms (CyanoHABs) and their associated cyanotoxins have been increasingly detected in estuaries and coastal lagoons, indicating that some freshwater taxa can survive in low-to-moderate salinity and may maintain their toxigenic potential in brackish environments. These observations highlight the need to understand the distribution, persistence, and ecological risks of freshwater harmful cyanobacteria across connected aquatic systems. This review synthesizes global field and mechanistic evidence on the expansion of freshwater harmful cyanobacteria along the freshwater–to–marine continuum. Hydrodynamic processes facilitate downstream transport, while salinity gradients regulate cyanobacterial survival and physiological responses. Salt stress induces cellular damage but also triggers adaptive physiological responses supporting survival. The persistence of freshwater harmful cyanobacteria in these systems is shaped by both species- and strain-level differences in salt tolerance, as well as physiological conditioning and environmental conditions experienced during transport. In addition, salinity influences cyanotoxin production, release, partitioning between particulate and dissolved fractions, and environmental persistence, thereby influencing ecological risks in brackish waters. Overall, this review synthesizes cyanobacterial adaptation and cyanotoxin dynamics along the freshwater–to–marine continuum and emphasizes integrated monitoring and modeling to support risk assessment and management of CyanoHABs.

papers.title: Dark Evolution of Oxalate-Derived Radicals Unlocks Sustainable Decontamination via Soil Component Interactions
papers.abstract: Abstract We report a previously unrecognized dark aerobic pathway for radical formation from low-molecular-weight organic acids (LMWOAs)─distinct from well-documented photogenerated routes─that drives efficient soil decontamination. In ten ofloxacin-spiked soils with varying properties, oxalic acid (OA) boosted 24 h ofloxacin degradation from 20% (without LMWOAs) to 79% (7.5 mM OA), outperforming equimolar malic and citric acids. The degradation kinetics are governed by LMWOA molecular configurations─specifically, fewer carboxyl groups and lower pKa1 values that enhance reactivity─and correlate with soil organic matter (SOM) and iron contents. By combining a newly developed in situ fluorescence detector with quenching experiments, we demonstrated that in four representative soils with contrasting SOM-Fe combinations, higher Fe promotes the yields of •OH, O2•–, 1O2, and COO•–, but the coexisting SOM acts as the primary quencher. Validation experiments using artificial sand-based model soils and theoretical calculations revealed that crystalline Fe minerals (e.g., hematite), rather than dissolved Fe ions, drive radical evolution: oxalate coordinates to surface hydroxyls as a bifunctional ligand bearing electron-withdrawing carboxylates and transferable α-H, forming unstable ≡Fe(III)-oxalate complexes that undergo heterolysis and subsequent radical chain reactions, efficiently generating reactive species. Our study expands the understanding of LMWOA-derived radical geochemistry and provides a basis for nature-based, low-cost soil remediation using naturally occurring organic acids.

papers.title: Maillard-like Reactions Generate Secondary Organic Products with Oxidative Potential: Mechanisms and Photoaging Enhancement
papers.abstract: Abstract The formation mechanisms and atmospheric evolution of secondary organic aerosols contributing to the oxidative potential (OP) remain poorly understood, limiting the assessment of their potential health impacts. Here, we demonstrate for the first time that atmospheric aqueous Maillard-like reactions constitute an important pathway for generating secondary organic products with OP. Six representative dicarbonyl-nitrogen reaction systems were designed to systematically investigate the formation kinetics, molecular characteristics, and photoaging evolution of the products generated from the Maillard-like reactions. All reactions systems generated measurable intrinsic OP, with the methylglyoxal-ethylamine system exhibiting the highest intrinsic OP (9.8 ± 0.7 pmol/min/μg). The HULIS fraction was identified as the dominant contributor to OP, while molecular characterization further suggested that nitrogen-containing heterocyclic compounds within this fraction as important contributors to the observed OP. Photoaging further enhanced the intrinsic OP (3.8–42.3 pmol/min/μg) accompanied by an increased abundance of unsaturated chromophores with extended π-conjugation, which may facilitate electron transfer and redox cycling. These findings elucidate a mechanistic framework for understanding how Maillard-like reactions contribute to aerosol oxidative potential, thereby advancing our understanding of their potential health implications.

papers.title: Mechanistic Prediction and High-Throughput Risk Screening of Aquatic Contaminants Using Daphnia magna AOP Network
papers.abstract: Abstract Traditional toxicological testing cannot meet regulatory demands for numerous chemicals in aquatic environments. New Approach Methodologies (NAMs) such as High-Throughput Screening (HTS) and Adverse Outcome Pathway (AOP) framework offer sustainable alternatives. Here, we built a comprehensive Quantitative Structure–Activity Relationship (QSAR) prediction and risk assessment framework that integrates a multidomain deep learning model, applicability domain assessment, and toxicity risk prioritization. Specifically, by applying in vitro HTS bioactivity to multiple Molecular Initiating Events (MIEs) and Key Events (KEs) in Daphnia magna AOP network, we compiled a data set (6971 chemicals × 10,024 multidimensional structure descriptors) exhibiting high chemical structural diversity and strong representativeness of environmentally relevant chemicals. QSAR prediction models covering application domains of multiple MIEs/KEs were further developed. The 6971 chemicals were risk-prioritized based on the AOP network topology, with the ranking results consistent with existing toxicological evidence. In addition, chemicals with potential combined toxic risks were identified. An out-of-the-box aquatic toxicity prediction and risk assessment tool is provided, enabling automated multitarget bioactivity prediction, reliability and decidability evaluation, and toxic risk profiling for new chemicals. This study represents a concrete application of “AI for Science” in ecotoxicology, aiming to reduce the dependence on traditional animal experiments. It simplifies the identification of potential toxic effects and bypasses in vivo validation processes to advance the sustainable management of environmental chemicals.

Driving Mechanisms of Land Degradation Neutrality at the County Level and Zonal Strategies in the Yellow River's Key Ecological Region (Part II : Post‐Assessment Driver Analysis)
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Achieving land degradation neutrality (LDN) is critical for sustainable socio‐ecological development; however, its practical implementation is often hindered by scale mismatches between assessments and administrative units, coupled with an over‐reliance on static drivers. Focusing on the Key Ecological Region of the Yellow River (KER), this study addresses these challenges by establishing a county‐scale net land improvement rate ( NLIR ) and developing a dynamic–static integrated indicator system aligned with county governance. By combining spatial analysis with Random Forest models, we quantified dominant drivers, spatial heterogeneity, and nonlinear threshold responses of NLIR . Results indicate: (1) From 2000 to 2020, land degradation pressure in the KER remained relatively low, with 79.16% of counties exhibiting NLIR above 20%, although a decline in restoration capacity occurred in human‐intensive regions after 2010. (2) Spatially, counties with low NLIR values exhibited significant clustering in developed regions subjected to intense anthropogenic pressure, whereas high NLIR values were predominantly distributed across climatically favorable regions and areas where ecological conservation is prioritized. (3) The intensity of construction land change emerged as the dominant driver of NLIR , followed by the intensity of cultivated land change and per capita cultivated land area. (4) All driving factors exhibited pronounced nonlinear threshold effects, within which their marginal positive or negative impacts on NLIR were strengthened relative to other value ranges, indicating critical governance tipping points for land management. Based on these quantified driving mechanisms, four differentiated zoning categories are proposed to support territorial space optimization and high‐quality development in the KER.

papers.title: Effects of Composite Reclamation Models of Sea Buckthorn, A Pioneer Species in Semi‐Arid Regions, on Soil Quality and Microbial Communities
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Open‐pit coal mining severely degrades soil and ecosystem functions, constraining regional sustainability. Vegetation‐based reclamation has therefore been widely adopted as an effective approach to promote soil recovery and ecosystem restoration. In this study, eight reclamation models were established at the Antaibao Open‐Pit Coal Mine, all dominated by sea buckthorn ( Hippophae rhamnoides L.) and combined with Chinese pine ( Pinus tabulaeformis Carr.), black locust ( Robinia pseudoacacia L.) and littleleaf peashrub ( Caragana microphylla Lam.). Soil physicochemical properties and microbial community characteristics were systematically investigated in 2019 and 2022 to evaluate reclamation effectiveness. The results showed that the H. rhamnoides + C. microphylla model (SJ_NT) significantly increased soil available phosphorus (AP) (mean difference = 9.467 mg/kg, p < 0.001) and total nitrogen (TN) contents (mean difference = 211.333 mg/kg, p = 0.002), and was the only configuration that achieved sustained improvement in AP over time. Soil microbial communities exhibited clear temporal dynamics during reclamation. In 2022, the SJ_NT model displayed the highest fungal operational taxonomic unit (OTU) richness (439). At the bacterial phylum level, community dominance shifted from Actinobacteriota to Proteobacteria , with Cyanobacteria emerging as an additional dominant group. Functional prediction further indicated enhanced microbial metabolic potential, particularly for carbon metabolism–related and amino acid metabolism functional genes. Core microbial taxa were significantly correlated with soil nutrient availability, suggesting their role in stabilizing community structure through complementary metabolic functions. The SJ_NT reclamation model promotes ecological recovery through a positive feedback pathway involving improved soil nutrient status, optimized microbial community structure, and enhanced functional activity. This study provides practical guidance for vegetation configuration and ecological reclamation of open‐pit coal mines in semi‐arid regions.

papers.title: Evaluating sustainable mobility potential through geographical accessibility and individual access, skills and appropriation
papers.abstract: The 15-min city concept promotes accessibility to opportunities notably by encouraging the use of sustainable modes of transport for daily mobility. However, it may not be enough just to provide activities that are accessible via public transport (PT) within 15 minutes if individuals’ capacity to reach them by PT (i.e. their motility) is overlooked. By developing a score that combines geographical accessibility and individual motility, this study aims to better understand the sustainable mobility potential of the Lake Geneva region in terms of reaching goods and services by PT within 15 minutes or 30 minutes, for a time comparison. To calculate the accessibility score, we used the frequency of goods/services visits as a weighting factor, and the human needs that they can satisfy as an attractiveness factor by which to classify the destinations reachable within 15 or 30 minutes from the centroid of 1580 × 1 km 2 cells. Next, based on a self-reported survey of 10,202 individuals in the Lake Geneva region, we created a motility score that captures individuals’ access to PT, their skills in using PT, and their readiness to include activities near their residence in their mobility projects (appropriation). Then, we combine accessibility and motility scores, enabling us to identify four types of areas: with high accessibility and high motility (+A/+M), with high accessibility and low motility (+A/-M), with low accessibility and high motility (-A/+M), and with low accessibility and low motility (-A/-M). By categorising areas in this way, policy priorities can be set out either to improve PT and goods/services provision where accessibility is low, or to support individuals’ motility, enabling them to take advantage of this accessibility effortlessly with sustainable modes of transport.

papers.title: Will AI scoop your science? Some researchers see a gloomy future
Finite foresight in Chomp
Organizational Growth Reconsidered: A Systems‐Based Review and Research Agenda
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Recent years have witnessed a significant increase in post‐ and degrowth research, which explores the social and ecological consequences of, and alternatives to, economic growth. To date, however, the debate has primarily occurred at the macroeconomic level, leaving a gap in our understanding of the role of organizational growth in a post‐growth context. Therefore, in this paper, we review the general management and corporate sustainability literatures, which have long investigated organizational growth, to gain insights into the inputs, processes, and outputs of organizational growth across multiple levels of analysis. Drawing on these findings and adopting a systems perspective, we devise a research agenda for future growth‐critical research at the organizational level. We suggest that studying emergence, adaptation, interdependence, and feedback in relation to organizational growth has significant potential to advance the fields of both corporate sustainability and post‐ and degrowth. Additionally, our integrative review offers practical advice for managers and policymakers seeking to guide organizations toward post‐growth pathways.

papers.title: Digitalization and Environmental, Social, and Governance Reporting: Evidence from the US Banking Industry
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT We examine the relation between digitalization and environmental, social, and governance (ESG) reporting using a sample of listed US banks from 2010 to 2022. Our study is based on a two‐step theoretical framework, building on voluntary disclosure and signaling theory: First, we expect and find technological progress to enhance internal information quality. Second, we examine whether banks pass on this improved information to stakeholders via ESG reports. Our results suggest that banks are more likely to disclose an ESG report as they become more digitalized. Further, we find that digitalization is related to a higher extent and quality of ESG reporting. A difference‐in‐differences test and a mediation analysis corroborate our findings. Cross‐sectional tests indicate an attenuated association between digitalization and ESG reporting for banks with low data privacy and security disclosure. Our findings have practical implications because they highlight the potential of digitalization to improve ESG reporting but also possible drawbacks as digitalization comes along with certain risks.

The Inclusion Hangover: A Daily Diary Study of the Reflective Mechanisms for Employee Well‐Being
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT How included employees feel at work fluctuates meaningfully from day to day. Emerging research demonstrates that these fluctuations have important implications for employee well‐being. Yet little is known about the cognitive processes through which these effects extend beyond the workday. Drawing on Ilies and colleagues' (2024) model of work‐derived well‐being, we propose that evening work reflection constitutes a key mechanism linking daily perceptions of workgroup inclusion to next‐morning well‐being. We further argue that daily fluctuations in perceived workgroup inclusion carry greater psychological significance for employees who perceive themselves as underrepresented or non‐prototypical within their immediate work environment (i.e., contextual minorities), thereby exerting a stronger influence on subsequent work reflection and well‐being. Using a daily diary design with morning, afternoon, and evening surveys ( n = 3480 days; N = 389 employees), multilevel path analyses supported the proposed model, demonstrating that positive and negative evening work reflection explain how daily workgroup inclusion carries over to next‐morning well‐being. By identifying positive and negative work reflection as distinct pathways linking daily workgroup inclusion to employee well‐being, and establishing contextual minority status as a boundary condition of these processes, we advance understanding of how , and for whom , the effects of daily workgroup inclusion extend beyond the workday. Together, these findings underscore the importance of fostering day to day workgroup inclusion to support employee well‐being in increasingly diverse workplaces.

Meeting lifestyle recommendations among cancer survivors – a cross-sectional descriptive analysis from the Swedish CArdioPulmonary BioImage study (SCAPIS)
papers.abstract: Abstract Purpose This study aimed to describe lifestyle patterns in relation to recommendations —including physical activity, diet, smoking, alcohol consumption, and sleep quality—among Swedish cancer survivors, stratified by sex and age. Method A descriptive cross-sectional study was performed using data from the Swedish CArdioPulmonary BioImage study (SCAPIS). Questionnaires and accelerometers were used to collect data. SCAPIS data were linked to the Swedish in- and out-patient registry. Descriptive statistics were used to describe proportion meeting lifestyle recommendations in different cancer diagnoses. Results In total, 2576 individuals were identified as cancer survivors in the SCAPIS-cohort. The median age was 59 years, 57% were females, the median time since diagnosis was 13 years, and malignant melanoma was the most common cancer type (50%). Most cancer survivors in the sample met at least one lifestyle recommendation. Meeting multiple recommendations were significantly ( p < 0.001) more common among breast cancer and malignant melanoma survivors than among other cancer types. Females were significantly ( p < 0.001) more likely to meet multiple recommendations and were twice as likely (53%) to meet the dietary recommendation compared to men (26%). Conclusions In this study of cancer survivors, differences across cancer types were observed in meeting multiple lifestyle recommendations. Most survivors met at least one recommendation, while the lowest proportion meeting the recommendations was observed for diet and alcohol consumption. Implications for Cancer Survivors These findings suggest that cancer survivors might benefit from secondary prevention strategies targeting lifestyle factors in general and diet and alcohol consumption in particular.

Lattice-Oxygen-Mediated Electronic Reconstruction of High-Entropy Oxides for Durable Fenton-like Water Treatment
papers.abstract: Abstract High-entropy catalysts offer broad compositional tunability for peroxymonosulfate (PMS)-based water treatment, yet achieving rapid, selective, and durable oxidation remains challenging because metallic bonding in high-entropy alloys (HEAs) limits electronic communication among metal sites. Here, we construct a quinary high-entropy oxide (HEO, (FeCoNiMnCu)3O4) featuring an oxygen-bridged M-O-M framework that enables local electronic coupling among neighboring metal centers. X-ray absorption spectroscopy and theoretical calculations support oxygen-mediated charge redistribution, with Hirshfeld analysis indicating 0.46e of charge transfer toward adsorbed PMS. Temperature-dependent electrochemical impedance spectroscopy reveals a substantially lower apparent activation energy for interfacial charge transfer in the HEO (0.43 eV) than in the HEA (1.15 eV). Mechanistic experiments support a predominantly nonradical PMS activation pathway involving high-valent cobalt-oxo species and singlet oxygen. The HEO achieved near-complete phenol degradation and 87.9% total organic carbon removal within 10 min, with an apparent rate constant of 0.359 min–1 versus 0.113 min–1 for the HEA. The system maintained >90% phenol removal across pH 3–11, sustained activity over 30 reuse cycles, and retained effective contaminant removal during continuous-flow operation and 50 L bench-scale treatment. These results support lattice-oxygen-mediated electronic reconstruction as a strategy for coupling efficient PMS activation with structural durability in high-entropy oxide catalysts.

papers.title: Combined Residues of Frequently Detected Herbicides are Stronger Predictors of Soil Resistome and Virulence Potential than Single Residues
papers.abstract: Abstract Overuse of herbicides has resulted in a global epidemic of evolved resistance in soil ecosystems. While single herbicide risk has been documented, the impact of multiple herbicide residues on the soil resistomes remains poorly understood. Our study quantified the residues of 24 herbicides, profiled antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) and virulence factor genes (VFGs), and reconstructed 1086 metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) from 93 agricultural soils across China. The analytical results demonstrate that the frequently detected herbicide residues (e.g., 60–90% detection frequency) are stronger predictors of soil antibiotic resistomes than total herbicide load, unsupervised mixture based on principal component analysis (PCA), or single-herbicide models. For VFG abundance, the same mixture outperformed the best single herbicide and total herbicide concentration, although PCA–PC1 showed a moderately stronger correlation. Specifically, these commonly detected herbicides showed positive associations with ARG abundance through both direct linkages and bacterial community-dependent indirect pathways. Similar patterns were observed for virulence potential, where frequently detected residues maintained strong predictive performance and were predominantly associated with indirect pathways. Functional annotation patterns further suggest a concurrent enrichment of traits related to antioxidant defense, mobility, adherence, and immune modulation under elevated herbicide exposure. Notably, multiple herbicide residues were linked to the abundance of a Trinickia taxon, which was identified as a candidate ARG-VFG co-occurrence MAG carrying a high ARG load. Our findings highlight the need to integrate compound exposure of frequently detected herbicides into future risk assessment methodology for preventing the dissemination of ARGs in agricultural soils.

papers.title: Aging of Urban Traffic Fine Particles Modulates Toxicity Mechanisms and Oxidative Stress Responses
papers.abstract: Abstract Vehicular emissions are an important source of urban air pollution that can age through atmospheric processes, but how their health effects change during atmospheric aging remains poorly understood. To simulate realistic urban emissions, we sampled air in a parking garage where cold-start and urban emissions coexist. Following aging in an oxidation flow reactor (OFR), we studied the cellular and acellular effects of the fresh and aged aerosols. Photochemical aging in the OFR increased secondary organic aerosol (SOA) mass by up to 6.9-fold, the oxygen-to-carbon (O:C) ratio from 0.26 to 0.79, and both the intrinsic oxidative potential (OPm) and the volume-normalized oxidative potential (OPv). In contrast, the peroxide-sensitive DCF activity decreased following aging. Cellular exposure to aged aerosol extracts increased cellular reactive oxygen species (ROS) formation in lung (A549) and liver (HepG2) cells, whereas fresh extracts strongly reduced cellular respiration, particularly in HepG2 cells. Cell painting analysis showed distinct morphological profiles. Exposure to aged extracts showed greater oxidative stress and DNA damage responses than those of exposure to fresh extracts. These findings suggest that atmospheric aging shifts the toxicity of fresh emissions from suppression of mitochondrial respiration toward oxygenated organics that can drive intracellular oxidative stress and DNA damage phenotypes. In conclusion, atmospheric aging of cold-start and urban vehicular emissions contributes to enhanced SOA formation and leads to distinct biological outcomes that depend on the degree of oxidative aging.

Generative AI and Firm Values
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT How do recent advances in Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) affect firm value? We construct the first measure of firms' workforce exposures to Generative AI and show that an “Artificial‐Minus‐Human” portfolio earned 5% in the two weeks following the release of ChatGPT. The labor‐exposure effect is more pronounced for firms with greater data assets and is distinct from the effect of firms' product exposures to AI. We assess whether exposed workforces are substituted or complemented by Generative AI based on whether their exposed tasks are core or supplemental. Examining firms' labor demand and profitability following the release of ChatGPT supports a labor‐technology substitution channel.

papers.title: Why do people migrate irregularly? Evidence from a lab-in-the-field experiment in West Africa
papers.abstract: Irregular migration to Europe by sea, though risky, remains one of the most popular migration options for many Sub-Saharan Africans. This study examines the drivers of irregular migration decisions using an incentivized lab-in-the-field experiment in rural Gambia, the African country with the highest per-capita rate of irregular migration to Europe. Potential migrants substantially overestimate the probability of dying en route , reporting an average belief of 51 percent compared with a best available estimate of about 20 percent. In the experiment, reducing the probability of dying en route from 50 to 20 percent raises willingness to migrate irregularly by 3.0 percentage points, while reducing the probability of obtaining legal residence from 50 to 30 percent lowers it by 2.1 points. Our results highlight the importance of potential migrants’ prior beliefs in shaping responses to information and suggest that information policies that fail to account for these beliefs may backfire.

papers.title: Morality and climate policy attitudes
papers.abstract: This paper studies the moral roots of climate policy attitudes. We fielded a survey with a representative sample in the US to study the predictive power of moral universalism in explaining heterogeneity in specific climate policy attitudes. Our results reveal that universalism is significantly related to support for various policy measures that prevail in current policy debates in most countries, including domestic policies such as a carbon tax and a green infrastructure program, as well as international policies such as international burden-sharing. Supporting evidence comes from simple bystander allocation decisions in which respondents are asked to decide “who should pay” to fight climate change or to mitigate the adverse consequences of global warming. Open-text elicitations further corroborate these results and identify moral universalism as a key aspect of how people reason about climate policies.

papers.title: When Trade Policy Shocks Hit the Pit: Pricing, Volatility and Speculation in the 2025 Soybean Futures Market
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT This paper explores responses to major trade policy shocks in the soybean futures market in 2025. Using an event‐study framework, we analyse short‐run movements in soybean futures prices, historical volatility, implied volatility and speculative positioning around three major policy shocks: the U.S. tariff announcement targeting China on February 1, the reciprocal tariff announcement on April 2, and Argentina's temporary suspension of soybean export taxes on September 22. Broader in scope, the April reciprocal tariff package was associated with the clearest and strongest response. Futures prices fell by about 6% within two trading days, while implied volatility rose sharply. Following the February announcement, implied volatility increased immediately and then receded, while downward repricing became evident only after China's retaliatory tariffs took effect, suggesting that uncertainty rose before the implications for U.S. export demand became clearer. Argentina's export‐tax suspension, by contrast, was followed by limited repricing, a later decline in implied volatility, and greater speculative positioning relative to commercial hedging needs. The cross‐event comparison suggests that the timing and composition of market adjustment vary with the scope, directness and subsequent evolution of each policy episode.

papers.title: Revealing tax evasion: Experimental evidence from a representative survey of Indonesian firms
papers.abstract: Measuring tax evasion by firms is notoriously difficult: direct questions yield biased responses while administrative data captures only detected violations. This paper examines the prevalence of reported tax non-compliance in Indonesia through a randomized, double-list experiment embedded in a nationally representative survey of 2,955 registered firms that preserves anonymity. The results indicate that around one-quarter of firms indirectly report not paying all taxes they are required to pay. An indicative back-of-the-envelope calculation suggests that the associated revenue losses could be economically meaningful, in the order of two percent of GDP. Heterogeneity analyses suggest higher reported non-compliance among firms that do not export, face informal-sector competition, and view tax administration as a major obstacle. These findings help inform tax authorities, which face substantial challenges in estimating levels of tax evasion and identifying non-compliant taxpayers, by providing the first representative estimates of firm tax evasion in a major middle-income country.

papers.title: Political elites and access to economic opportunities in China’s rural market transition
The Olympic effect revisited: 1950–2019
papers.abstract: Rose and Spiegel (2011) identified a positive trade-promoting effect of hosting the Olympic Games, yet they did not account for multilateral resistance terms in their analysis, which are emphasized in the structural gravity model by Anderson and van Wincoop (2003). This paper revisits the trade effects of the Olympics using a nonparametric matching method developed by Chang and Lee (2011), analyzing a comprehensive gravity dataset encompassing 187 economies from 1950 to 2019. Our findings suggest that hosting the Olympics is positively associated with bilateral trade. For pairs in which both countries have hosted, the matching estimate corresponds to a long-run trade difference with an implied increase of approximately 15 times relative to matched nonhost pairs. Under an assumed trade elasticity of 4, this estimate corresponds to an illustrative trade-cost equivalent of approximately 50%.

papers.title: Drought, women’s time poverty, and the development costs of water collection in Sub-Saharan Africa
papers.abstract: Drought can impose development costs that are not fully captured by income, production, or formal water access indicators. This paper examines one such hidden cost in Sub-Saharan Africa by focusing on women’s time poverty arising from household water collection. Combining harmonized Demographic and Health Surveys with geocoded drought exposure measured at the survey cluster level, we estimate how local drought conditions are associated with women’s annual water collection burden and broader household adjustments. We find that drought exposure is associated with higher water-collection time for women, with larger estimated increases among women living in poor households, women with no formal education, and women living in households without piped-water access. Intermediate-outcome evidence shows that drought is associated with lower local water availability and a higher likelihood of very long collection trips, particularly journeys exceeding 60 minutes. These water-time burdens are also associated with greater engagement in flexible, household-based, family-based, and self-employed forms of work among women rather than with a simple expansion of protected paid employment. In addition, higher community water burdens are associated with poorer schooling outcomes among girls, including a greater likelihood of being out of school and larger grade-for-age gaps. Household-linked evidence further shows that poorer girls’ schooling outcomes are associated with larger household shares of adult women in unpaid or in-kind work, self-employment, and family work. The findings suggest that drought-related water insecurity can redistribute adaptation costs within households, making women’s unpaid time a key margin through which climate stress produces hidden development costs.

papers.title: Understanding conflict in protected areas: integrating justice considerations with economic perspectives

The Depositary of Last Resort
papers.abstract: Abstract What are the consequences of making central bank deposits accessible to actors beyond the banking sector? We collect novel micro data on deposit accounts historically held with the Bank of England by individuals and firms other than banks to study their role in the financial panic of 1866. We document that the use of deposit accounts at the central bank soared during the crisis, while commercial banks permanently lost funding. The expansion in the number of active accounts was fueled by individuals, but the intensive margin increase in balances came almost entirely from firms. Recourse to central bank deposits was heterogeneous and persisted well beyond the panic, reflecting easy access, low opportunity costs, and positive network externalities. At the same time, retail borrowers seeking liquidity support from the Bank during the crisis preferred receiving loan proceeds in the form of cash rather than deposits. JEL Classification: E58, G01, G11, G20, N13, N23

papers.title: How Strategic Leaders Drive Firms in Ecosystems: Envisioning Value, Orchestrating Knowledge, and Shifting Roles
papers.abstract: Abstract Research on business ecosystems has illuminated how ecosystems emerge, evolve, and transform, revealing ecosystem‐level dynamics and the central actors that orchestrate them. Yet, it is individual firms that continuously attempt to establish and shift the roles they play within ecosystems through the vision and choices of their strategic leaders. How do strategic leaders drive these shifts? Through a longitudinal case study of Dallara Automobili (1972–2025), we trace how the CEO's prior professional experience shaped an evolving theory of value – a set of conjectures about how value should be created that guided the development of organizational routines enabling progressively more expansive knowledge orchestration. This process shifted Dallara from a peripheral component supplier to a boundary‐spanning knowledge orchestrator. Our recursive process model theorizes how the leader's conjectures drive firm role shifts within an ecosystem: experience shapes the leader's theory of value, which drives organizational routines and knowledge orchestration; knowledge orchestration, in turn, redefines the firm's ecosystem role. Ecosystem responses then feed back, augmenting prior experience and, in turn, refining the theory of value so that each round operates at a broader scope. We contribute to ecosystem research by identifying knowledge orchestration as the mechanism through which a leader's theory of value translates into shifts in the firm's role and by showing how this process unfolds recursively as ecosystem responses reshape the leader's conjectures.

papers.title: Neither Here Nor There: Confronting Internalized Colonialism
Social Media Toxicity and Capital Markets
Building Better Information: Reporting Technology, Internal Information Frictions, and Investment Efficiency
Collective Activism
papers.abstract: Can investor stewardship codes that call for coordinated activism be satisfied by an Investor Collective Action Organization (ICAO)? In an ICAO, investors work collectively, like a large shareholder, to monitor management and increase value. We analyze the endogenous formation of an ICAO and its equilibrium size, considering free-rider problems and coordination costs. While the ICAO overcomes free-rider problems among its members, it exacerbates them between the ICAO and solo activists. The benefit of joining an ICAO is hump-shaped in size. With moderate coordination costs, ICAO formation features multiple equilibria. Small changes in coordination costs significantly influence ICAO formation and activism. This paper was accepted by Will Cong, finance. Funding: L. Yang thanks the support from the Social Sciences and Humanities Research Council of Canada [Grants 435-2021-0040, 435-2026-0060] and the Bank of Canada [Fellowship]. Supplemental Material: The online appendix is available at https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2025.02975 .

papers.title: Reconceptualizing Network Change: Robustness and Resilience of Interorganizational Networks
papers.abstract: Existing research on interorganizational network dynamics has largely treated network change as gradual, local, and primarily oriented toward private organizational advantage. Yet contemporary cooperative interorganizational systems are highly interconnected across industrial sectors and geographies and are routinely exposed to shocks that simultaneously disable multiple organizations or relationships among them. These shocks stem from pandemics, natural disasters, wars, sanctions, and cascading partner failures, and can rapidly reconfigure whole‑network architectures and undermine collective outcomes. In light of this new reality, we reconceptualize interorganizational networks as loci of frequent, punctuated change at the whole network level, with primary implications for collective outcomes. We develop this reconceptualization through a robustness–resilience lens, defining network robustness as an interorganizational network’s capacity to maintain its collective outcomes in the immediate aftermath of a shock, and network resilience as its capacity to recover and potentially surpass pre‑shock collective outcomes over the longer term. We then outline the theoretical and methodological opportunities that this robustness–resilience perspective opens for the study of network change.

papers.title: Legal Chameleons: Political Ideology, Institutional Histories, and Firms’ Management of Identity Cues
papers.abstract: This study examines how foreign firms strategically manage the salience of foreignness when facing unfavorable domestic evaluators. Foreign firms do so by altering the ethnic composition of the agents representing them before the evaluators. We examine this question in the context of Asian firms’ selection of legal counsel in U.S. federal courts. Prior research suggests that foreign firms may anticipate less favorable evaluations in courts that have historically favored domestic over foreign firms and in those with conservative judges. We argue that, in such evaluative settings, Asian firms adjust the ethnic composition of their external legal teams to manage the salience of foreignness, and that such adjustments are especially likely in courts that combine judge conservatism with pro-domestic ruling histories. We test these arguments using data on U.S. patent litigation from 2000 to 2016 and validated measures of courts’ political ideology and pro-domestic ruling histories. We find that Asian firms reduce the proportion of Asian-origin lawyers and increase the proportion of White lawyers when litigating in conservative courts, particularly when these courts also have pro-domestic ruling histories. By contrast, the ethnic composition of lawyers representing domestic firms remains stable across courts. Evidence of implicit bias against Asians among legal professionals provides additional support consistent with the theorized mechanism. Post-hoc analyses reveal that adjusting the ethnic composition of external legal teams attenuates the likelihood of unfavorable outcomes in conservative courts. These findings contribute to research on liability of foreignness by identifying agent selection as a specific mitigation mechanism in evaluative arenas.

papers.title: Colleagues that work together move together: How co-moving among newcomers affects individual and team performance.
papers.abstract: As teams and team membership become more dynamic, colleagues from the same prior team increasingly transition together to a new team as a cohort: a phenomenon known as co-moving. Drawing on theories of shared team experience and team receptivity, we develop a multilevel, multi-theory, and multi-period model to examine how co-moving affects individual and team performance. We theorize that co-movers carry forward proximal shared team experience which they can leverage immediately to support their own performance relative to solo movers, who must build new working relationships. However, we also theorize that co-movers’ proximal shared team experience hinders team performance, though these detrimental effects attenuate over time. We test our theory using archival data from the National Basketball Association, supplemented by qualitative interviews with individuals involved in professional basketball. Our findings reveal that co-movers exhibit better individual performance than solo movers on their new teams and in our robustness checks we find that greater shared tenure on the prior team further enhances this advantage. At the team level, teams with co-movers perform worse than teams with solo movers, and we find partial support that this disadvantage attenuates over time. Additional analyses show that co-movers’ individual performance advantage persists over time in the new team. The findings from our interviews illuminate how these processes unfold both on and off the court. Our research contributes to the literature on shared team experience and newcomer integration by highlighting a multilevel tradeoff: while co-moving benefits individuals, it can initially undermine collective performance.

papers.title: Worker Repositioning and Technological Change: Evidence from an Online Labor Market
papers.abstract: Technological change reshapes labor markets not only by changing labor demand but also by altering labor supply, as workers reallocate effort across tasks and opportunities in response to technological advances. Yet research has focused more on demand-side effects than on how workers themselves adapt. In this research, we examine worker repositioning on a large online labor market following the launch of ChatGPT in November 2022. We argue that the launch of ChatGPT reduced expected returns to labor in exposed skill domains and develop and test a series of hypotheses regarding how this shock is associated with participation, horizontal positioning, and vertical positioning among workers on the platform. Using proprietary data on incumbent freelancers and a difference-in-differences design that leverages cross-sectional variation in pre-period AI exposure and skill-level, we show that freelancers more exposed to AI shift away from prior domains and reorient bidding toward higher-value contracts. In contrast, high skill-level freelancers, who face greater adjustment costs, are less likely to reduce participation on the platform, reposition across domains, and move upmarket. These findings highlight how technological shocks reshape labor markets through supply-side adaptation and how domain-specific human capital constrains worker responses.

papers.title: The Sustainability Claim Paradox: When Green Marketing Encourages Greater Consumption
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Sustainability claims are assumed to promote responsible consumption, yet consumption itself drives environmental harm. Drawing on moral licensing theory, this study asks whether such claims instead licence greater consumption across the purchase, use/replacement and disposal stages of one cycle. A between‐subjects experiment ( N = 303) manipulated claim strength (control, light, strong) in a product advertisement, and the hypothesised effects were estimated jointly using partial least squares structural equation modelling. Stronger claims raised perceived environmental impact, which raised intended purchase quantity, and this belief carried the total purchase effect entirely, consistent with static moral licensing. The evidence is mixed thereafter: Claim strength had no net effect on intended use or replacement, and although it showed a small total effect on justifying earlier disposal, perceived impact did not carry that effect, and the direct path was inconclusive under the inferential rule adopted here. Environmental concern attenuated rather than amplified the effect.

papers.title: When Premium Product Strategy Meets Sustainability: Environmental–Economic Trade‐Offs in Japanese Manufacturing
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Corporate sustainability has become a central concern for business stakeholders, yet little is known about how premium product strategies shape firms' sustainability orientations and performance. Drawing on stakeholder theory, this study examines whether pursuing premium products is associated with firms' adoption of environmental and economic sustainability orientations and how these orientations, in turn, relate to corporate performance. Using survey data from 128 directors and managers responsible for overseas operations in manufacturing firms listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange, analyzed with structural equation modelling, we find that a premium product strategy is positively associated with both environmental and economic sustainability orientations. However, their performance implications differ: economic sustainability is positively related to firm performance, whereas environmental sustainability shows a significant negative association. These results suggest that, among Japanese manufacturing exporters, premium product strategies simultaneously foster sustainability ambitions and expose firms to short‐term trade‐offs between environmental and economic outcomes.

papers.title: Digitalisation, Organisational Innovation and Firms' Environmental Protection Expenditures: Evidence From Spanish Manufacturing
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT This paper investigates how digitalisation and organisational innovation shape firms' routine environmental protection efforts in Spanish manufacturing. Using an unbalanced panel of 2348 firms and 7603 firm‐year observations from 2009–2023 drawn from the Survey on Business Strategies (ESEE), the study examines the determinants of current environmental protection expenditures as a recurrent form of operational green capability rather than radical eco‐innovation. The empirical analysis relies on panel‐data logit models that relate firm characteristics at time (2009–2022) to current environmental protection expenditures at time (2010–2023), with firm‐level controls and sector and period effects, and reports average marginal effects. The results show that digitalisation is strongly and consistently associated with routine environmental protection efforts. Firms that use robotics in production, invest in external ICT training and implement software‐based process innovations exhibit around 8–11 percentage points higher predicted probabilities of undertaking current environmental protection expenditures than otherwise similar firms. Organisational innovation, measured through the introduction of new work‐organisation practices, also displays a positive and significant association, with an average marginal effect of about 8–9 percentage points. Participation in EU research programmes is likewise positively associated with environmental protection expenditures, although this result applies to a relatively small share of firms and should be interpreted with caution, as it likely reflects the behaviour of a self‐selected subset of highly capable, outward‐oriented firms. The findings indicate that digital and organisational capabilities, together with cooperative engagements, act as key enablers of operational green practices, even though interaction terms provide only weak evidence of strong complementarities in this specific outcome. The paper contributes novel firm‐level evidence on how the twin green–digital transition materialises in ongoing environmental management within a manufacturing sector dominated by SMEs in Spain, shifting attention from one‐off eco‐innovations towards the stabilisation of everyday environmental routines and highlighting the role of capability bundles in supporting sustained environmental protection efforts.

papers.title: Contracting as Sensemaking Infrastructure: Enacting Sustainability Strategy in Business‐to‐Business Relationships
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Firms articulate sustainability objectives but depend on suppliers and business partners to enact them. As commitments cross organizational and professional boundaries, their meaning may fragment even when parties agree in principle. This theory‐synthesis article examines B2B contracting as sensemaking infrastructure for enacting sustainability strategy across interorganizational relationships. Integrating sensemaking, proactive contracting, and contract design, it develops the sensemaking‐based contracting framework. The framework identifies four interdependent functions: framing clarifies what the relationship seeks to govern; translation connects that understanding to responsibilities, data, and routines; adaptation organizes legitimate revision; and signaling connects relationship‐level performance to external credibility. The article repositions contracting from downstream compliance to strategy enactment. It shows that preserving contractual wording is insufficient when purpose becomes disconnected from performance and directs managerial attention to connections among purpose, responsibility, capability, review, and evidence. Whether this infrastructure supports shared meaning depends on power, network position, and actors' ability to question established interpretations.

papers.title: Warehouse logistics and task switching theory revisited: asymmetric height switching costs in order picking systems
papers.abstract: Purpose This study investigates the impact of pick location height switching on task performance time in manual order picking systems. Drawing on task switching theory, we examine whether switching between ground- and chest-level pick locations increases task performance time, whether switching costs are asymmetric, and whether item weight strengthens possible differences between ground-to-chest and chest-to-ground switches. Design/methodology/approach We adopt a two-stage approach that combines internal validity and operational generalizability. First, a controlled eye-tracking experiment simulates a simplified order picking scenario to explore the cognitive mechanisms underlying visual search when repeating versus switching pick location heights. Second, we analyze 3,537,973 pick location visits from a German grocery retail warehouse to test the effects of pick location height switching in a real-world operational environment with professional order pickers. Findings The eye-tracking experiment provides mechanism-oriented evidence that switching between pick location heights increases visual search time and reorientation demands under controlled conditions. The archival field study complements these behavioral insights by showing that height switching is associated with longer task performance time. It further shows that switching costs depend on direction, with ground-to-chest switches being more time-consuming than chest-to ground switches. This directional difference becomes more pronounced as item weight increases. Practical implications The findings suggest that warehouse managers should consider not only the frequency but also the direction of height switches when designing picking sequences. Batching and routing algorithms could incorporate switching costs as a weighted parameter, with particular attention to ground-to-chest switches involving heavier items. However, reducing height switches should be balanced against ergonomic risks, as long sequences of ground-level picks may increase repetitive bending and musculoskeletal strain. Originality/value This study provides the first empirical evidence on pick location height switching in warehouse operations and extends task switching theory to a new operational context. By combining mechanism-oriented eye-tracking evidence with large-scale field data, we show that height switching is associated with asymmetric switching costs and provide insights into the cognitive and motor reorientation processes that may underlie these effects.

papers.title: Understanding the mixed consequences of diversity practices: A typology of migrant employees
Understanding and Confronting Organizational Corruption and Wrongdoing in the Era of Grand Societal Challenges: Past, Present, and Future Perspectives
papers.abstract: Organizational corruption and wrongdoing remain persistent problems in contemporary life and are closely linked to the grand societal challenges humanity faces. This Special Issue, therefore, asks: How are organizational corruption and wrongdoing linked to grand societal challenges? We posit that corruption and wrongdoing are dynamic forces that interact reciprocally with grand societal challenges. In an inside-out dynamic, organizational corruption and wrongdoing hinder, distort, or reverse progress on grand societal challenges. In an outside-in dynamic, grand societal challenges and broader societal transformations reconfigure the incentives, opportunities, pressures, justifications, and visibility conditions through which corruption and wrongdoing emerge. This editorial traces the evolution of corruption research from classic economic and public-sector accounts toward a business-and-society perspective and develops a dynamic framework of the corruption–grand societal challenges nexus. We analyze how the Special Issue articles advance this conversation and conclude with a research and practice agenda for scholars and practitioners.

papers.title: Corporate strategic distinctiveness in the aftermath of natural disasters
papers.abstract: Purpose This study examines how natural disasters affect corporate strategic distinctiveness and investigates the moderating roles of CEO early-life disaster experience and CEO tenure. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on organisational adaptation theory, we construct a multidimensional measure of strategic distinctiveness using quarterly data on Chinese listed firms from 2009 to 2019. We estimate difference-in-differences models, with disaster data web-scraped from the National Disaster Reduction Centre of China. To address endogeneity and robustness concerns, we conduct placebo tests, propensity-score matching, subsample analyses and textual analysis of earnings conference call transcripts. Findings We find that natural disasters reduce corporate strategic distinctiveness, indicating that firms adopt more conforming strategies to secure legitimacy and resources. This effect is stronger for climate-related disasters and is amplified when CEOs have early-life disaster experience or longer tenure. Further analysis shows firms conform more strongly when disasters recur. Originality/value This study highlights how firms adapt to risks posed by natural disasters. By showing the tendency of firms to converge towards industry norms and the role of CEO characteristics in shaping this response, this study enriches the broader discourse on management accounting and corporate governance in the context of major external shocks.

The AI CEO: A conceptualisation and outline for future research
