Striking the right balance: How sanctions and consequences of customer misbehavior shape hotel guests’ fairness perceptions and rebooking intentions
Professional identity as the missing link: Understanding motivational pathways among hotel employees
Serendipity and innovation in new ventures: The moderating role of primary investor type
Response to ‘Optimal tourism taxation with externalities: A rejoinder to Rosselló-Nadal and Sard (2026)’
Institutional Ownership and Corporate Exposure to Equal Employment Opportunity Lawsuits
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Research Question/Issue This study investigates whether and how institutional ownership is associated with firms' exposure to equal employment opportunity (EEO) lawsuits under Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964. These lawsuits capture an underexplored form of downside ESG risk arising from firms' treatment of employees, who constitute a key corporate stakeholder group. Research Findings/Insights Using a dataset of 22,501 EEO lawsuits filed in US federal courts from 2001 to 2020, this study finds that firms with higher institutional blockholdings experience significantly fewer EEO lawsuits. This relationship persists across active, passive, long‐term, and transient investors and remains robust to an instrumental variable analysis exploiting Russell 3000 Index inclusion, change analyses, industry adjustments, and numerous robustness tests. Post‐lawsuit responses reveal three mechanisms: The largest investors withdraw capital (exit); transient investors increase voting engagement (voice); and forced CEO turnover increases, particularly in high‐blockholding firms (discipline). Institutional investors' role is amplified in low‐skilled labor environments and complemented by independent board monitoring. Theoretical/Academic Implications This study documents the role of institutional investors in mitigating the risk of workplace discrimination litigation, advancing the literature on institutional monitoring, ESG, employee welfare, and corporate governance. EEO lawsuits provide an objective, non‐self‐reported measure of a specific downside ESG risk. This study further shows how heterogeneous investors deploy different mechanisms to improve EEO outcomes. Practitioner/Policy Implications Workplace discrimination poses a threat to employee well‐being and firm reputation. Uncovering institutional investors' role in safeguarding employees' civil right to EEO provides useful insights for policymakers, boards, and investors.

papers.title: One size does not fit all: management strategies to reduce turnover intention among public sector employees
Childhood abuse profiles and psychological distress in emerging adulthood: Gender differences across housing cost burden contexts
How childhood sexual abuse disclosure response practices shape survivors' psychological wellbeing
Why Do Spanish University Students Flirt in Nightlife Venues?
Using Artificial Intelligence to Access Reproductive Healthcare Information by U.S. States Following Sexual Assault
“There’s No Magic Pill to Help Me, Right?”: Sex After Early Midlife Bilateral Salpingo-Oophorectomy
papers.abstract: Abstract Women with risk-reducing bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy (RRBSO) report poorer sexual health than women of a similar age with intact ovaries. Since women with RRBSO lose the ability to make endogenous 17-β-estradiol (E2), open questions include whether: (1) poorer sexual function is associated with E2 loss and (2) exogenous estradiol therapy (ET BSO ) is related to amelioration of objective decrements and subjective experiences. We combined online questionnaires with qualitative interviews to explore the sexual function of women with pathogenic variants in the BRCA1/2 genes and RRBSO not taking ET BSO (RRBSO) and those taking ET BSO (RRBSO + ET BSO ). We compared their quantitative responses to those of age-matched women with intact ovaries (AMC) and women in spontaneous menopause (SM). RRBSO had lower total sexual function scores than AMC and more sexually related distress than AMC than SM. In terms of lived experience with RRBSO + /–ET BSO , qualitative interviews mirrored the quantitative data with reports of pain, loss of sexual desire, and dryness, in addition to concerns about identity, relational challenges, and lacking crucial information regarding sexual response after RRBSO. The combination of the objective and subjective reports details worse sexual function and experience of younger women with RRBSO regardless of ET BSO . Since ET BSO does not appear to ameliorate all aspects of sexual function and distress for many women with RRBSO, it is critical to consider other interventions including fully informed consent prior to RRBSO.

Medium-Entropy LDH-Driven Electronic Coupling of MnO x for Preferential Oxidation of Formaldehyde
papers.abstract: Abstract Preferential oxidation of formaldehyde (HCHO) in natural gas engine exhaust is pivotal to prevent NH3–SCR catalyst deactivation and inhibit highly toxic hydrogen cyanide (HCN) formation. Although manganese-based catalysts exhibit prominent activity for HCHO oxidation, complete mineralization is still hindered by poor electron-transfer efficiency and insufficient reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation. Herein, we fabricate hierarchical medium-entropy LDH nanoflower-anchored MnOx catalysts (MnO2@NiMgAl-MELH) via a facile in situ growth strategy, enabling 100% mineralization of HCHO at room temperature. Structural characterizations and DFT calculations verify that Ni–Mn electronic coupling optimizes the electronic structure, facilitates charge transfer, reduces oxygen vacancy formation energy, and boosts O2 and H2O activation to generate abundant ROS (O2–, O22–, and surface −OH). Furthermore, in situ DRIFTS confirms that ROS synergistically accelerate HCHO and formate intermediate oxidation, achieving complete mineralization of HCHO. This work develops a low-cost and high-performance catalyst for HCHO preferential oxidation and offers a broadly applicable strategy for air pollutant purification.

papers.title: PFAS in Follicular Fluid, Anti-Mullerian Hormone, and Oocyte Developmental Competence: A Prospective Study in GIVES
papers.abstract: Abstract In this prospective study based on the Guangxi In Vitro Fertilization and the Environment Study (GIVES) cohort, we measured poly- and perfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) in the ovarian follicular fluid of 729 participants to investigate their association with oocyte developmental competence. The PFAS mixture was negatively associated with Metaphase II (MII) oocyte rate, with chlorinated polyfluoroalkyl ether sulfonic acids (Cl-PFESAs) identified as the primary contributor in Bayesian kernel machine regression (BKMR) models. Cl-PFESAs were negatively associated with oocyte maturation [relative risk (RR) = 0.67, 95% CI: 0.56–0.79], fertilization (RR = 0.78, 95% CI: 0.67–0.90), blastocyst formation (RR = 0.81, 95% CI: 0.70–0.94), and high-quality blastocyst formation (RR = 0.49, 95% CI: 0.41–0.58). Serum anti-Müllerian hormone (AMH) may act as a key modifier, with a stronger association observed in women with low AMH for MII oocyte rate [relative excess risk due to interaction (RERI) = 0.33, 95% CI: 0.12–0.54] and fertilization rate (RERI = 0.24, 95% CI: 0.003–0.49). Our findings indicate that PFAS, particularly Cl-PFESAs, in follicular fluid are linked to impaired oocyte developmental competence, with AMH serving as a potential modifier. Further studies are warranted to validate our findings and assess the implications of PFAS for reproductive outcomes.

papers.title: Learning dependency structures of urban vitality at the census-block level using Bayesian networks and multi-source data
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Urban vitality captures the dynamic interplay between human activity and the built environment, serving as a critical metric for guiding urban planning and design toward more livable, inclusive, and resilient cities. However, existing studies have largely overlooked the underlying dependency relationships shaping urban vitality, particularly when analyzing large-scale and multi-source urban data. To address this gap, this study proposes a data-driven framework to model and interpret urban vitality intensity at the census-block level in Manhattan, New York. Within this framework, a composite Urban Vitality Index (UVI) is first constructed by integrating dynamic and static proxies of urban activity, derived from street-level imagery–based object detection and POI density, respectively. Second, sixteen influencing factors spanning neighborhood attributes, urban form, building form, and environmental perception are incorporated to represent multi-dimensional characteristics of the urban system. Third, a Bayesian Network is employed to capture the dependency structure, revealing probabilistic relationships and underlying pathways associated with urban vitality and its influencing factors. The results indicate that socio-spatial factors, particularly ethnic diversity and road network density, are strongly associated with urban vitality through interconnected pathways, whereas localized morphological characteristics exhibit comparatively weaker effects. By leveraging deep learning and interpretable probabilistic modeling, this study facilitates knowledge discovery in urban systems, providing a scalable approach for evidence-based urban planning and design.

papers.title: Coupling coordination characteristics of the “water-urban-land-population-production-greening” system: Spatiotemporal variation and risk probability
Composition-controlled NaOH/Na2CO3 fusion activation of coal gasification slag: Structural reconstruction, cementitious reactivity, and environmental performance
From passive carriers to selective filters: how microplastic aging shapes antibiotic resistance gene abundance
Should you ask directly? What rice farmers reveal in list experiments regarding improper disposal of agricultural waste
Advancing nutrient circularity in agriculture: Critical perspectives on recycling-derived bio-based fertilisers, production, and adoption challenges
papers.abstract: Recycling-derived bio-based fertilisers (RD-BBFs) are an emerging sustainable solution for nutrient management in agriculture, addressing the pressing need to reduce reliance on mineral fertilisers sourced from finite resources. This paper reviews journal articles and EU legislative documents, primarily focusing on RD-BBFs, which involve sources such as animal manure, agri-food industry waste, urban green waste, and food waste. They are produced through various processes, including composting, anaerobic digestion, stripping, scrubbing and precipitation, among others. The Fertilising Products Regulations 2019/1009 create a market for RD-BBFs in the EU, encouraging their use among farmers; however, the legislation has not covered all the RD-BBFs. Additionally, this study provides an overview of RD-BBF pathways through material flow analysis (MFA) and life cycle assessment (LCA), as analytical tools that help assess the environmental and economic benefits of RD-BBFs. Most analytical studies are limited to a few nutrients and RD-BBFs; further comprehensive studies are needed to consider other nutrients and RD-BBFs. Considering their mineral fertiliser equivalent value (MFEV), this study demonstrates how RD-BBFs could help to close the nutrient loop and enhance agricultural sustainability. Further studies are needed to investigate the long-term effects of RD-BBFs in various geographical regions across Europe. Furthermore, this review identifies hurdles to RD-BBF adoption, including variability in nutrient content, plant available MFEV, economic considerations, and societal acceptance. Strategies for overcoming these constraints are presented. Overall, RD-BBF is a viable option for reducing dependency on fossil-based fertilisers. This study highlights the potential for RD-BBFs to promote sustainable agriculture while enhancing resource efficiency and promoting environmental preservation.

papers.title: Mealworm frass affects the chemical properties and nutrient dynamics in two lupin varieties under contrasting soils
Enzymatic PET depolymerization: a review of engineering biocatalysts and systems for efficient plastic deconstruction
papers.abstract: The ever-increasing accumulation of polyethylene terephthalate (PET) waste poses a severe threat to global ecosystems and human health. Biological upcycling (integrating enzymatic depolymerization with microbial conversion of the resulting monomers) has emerged as a promising approach to overcome the limitations of traditional mechanical and chemical recycling. This review provides a systematic and critical synthesis of recent advances in PET bio-upcycling, covering the period from 2016 to 2026. We first discuss the discovery, classification, structural features, and catalytic mechanisms of PET-hydrolyzing enzymes, highlighting the rate-limiting constraints imposed by glass transition temperature, substrate crystallinity, interfacial interactions, and product inhibition. We then evaluate protein engineering strategies that have dramatically enhanced thermostability, substrate binding, and multi-enzyme synergy, yielding benchmark variants capable of near-complete depolymerization of post-consumer PET within hours to days. Concurrent innovations in whole-cell biocatalysis, enzyme immobilization, surface display, and microbial consortia are examined, with emphasis on how metabolic division of labor and substrate channeling can alleviate product inhibition and process mixed plastic waste. We also summarize metabolic engineering efforts that have enabled conversion of PET-derived terephthalic acid (TPA) and ethylene glycol (EG) into more than 25 value-added products, including biopolymers, platform chemicals, pharmaceuticals, and specialty compounds. Finally, we discuss remaining technological barriers, economic feasibility, and future frontiers (including computational enzyme design, synthetic consortia, tandem chemo-biological processes, and industrial-scale demonstration) and propose a phased roadmap for industrial translation. This review aims to provide a comprehensive resource for advancing PET bio-upcycling from laboratory innovation toward practical implementation in a circular plastics economy.

papers.title: Electrospun Co3O4/CeO2 hollow nanotubes for photocatalytic degradation of PET plastics with peroxymonosulfate activation: Performance and DFT insight
papers.abstract: Polyethylene terephthalate (PET) plastics cause significant environmental harm. Traditional treatment methods, such as landfilling and incineration, can cause secondary pollution. Here, an efficient synergistic photocatalytic system is presented, based on Co 3 O 4 /CeO 2 hollow nanotubes prepared by electrospinning, to activate peroxymonosulfate (PMS) and promote the degradation of PET plastics. The results show that the as-prepared Co 3 O 4 /CeO 2 composite catalyst exhibits the best performance under illumination; the weight loss rate of PET can reach ∼82.7 ± 4.5% in the presence of a 3 mM PMS solution (pH 7). The effects of parameters (e.g., PMS dose and coexisting anions) on PET degradation were systematically investigated. Electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) and free radical quenching experiments confirm that the •OH, 1 O 2, and SO 4 •− active species contribute the most to the degradation of PET plastics. Density Functional Theory analysis shows that Co-d-pDOS and Ce-f-pDOS modulations in Co 3 O 4 /CeO 2 synergistically enhance the PET photocatalytic decomposition efficiency. Finally, we discuss the mechanism by which the catalyst/light/PMS system degrades PET in water.

papers.title: Flow regulation capacity determines reservoir phytoplankton community assembly: threshold, mechanisms, and implications
papers.abstract: Dam construction changes lotic rivers to lentic reservoirs with divergent hydraulic residence time (HRT), altering phytoplankton communities. However, how community assembly shifts along HRT gradients and the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Here, we investigated phytoplankton communities from 21 reservoirs spanning a broad HRT range (0.21–94.65 d) in China, quantifying assembly patterns and disentangling the roles of the regional species pool and local habitat in shaping community assembly. The modified stochasticity ratio (MST) declined non-linearly with increasing HRT and a breakpoint at 10 d was identified. Reservoirs with HRT < 10 d had MST > 0.5, whereas those with HRT > 10 d showed an MST < 0.5, indicating a shift from stochastic- to deterministic-dominated assembly across this threshold. For reservoirs with HRT < 10 d, observed β–γ relationships matched null expectations, consistent with a stronger influence of the regional species pool; stochastic processes were dominated by drift and dispersal. Among reservoirs > 10 d HRT, observed β–γ relationships deviated from null expectations, indicating stronger local habitat filtering. Nutrients (nitrogen and phosphorus) explained ∼33% of habitat effects, while water temperature explained ∼13%. Deterministic assembly was characterized by strong species sorting and niche partitioning. By linking HRT to phytoplankton assembly timescales, our findings identified an operationally relevant 10-day HRT threshold, highlighting that strategic manipulation of HRT can steer phytoplankton assembly and support ecosystem resilience in dammed rivers.

papers.title: Integrating MaxEnt and explainable AI to assess habitat suitability and conservation gaps of Przewalski's gazelle (Procapra przewalskii) in the Qinghai Lake region
papers.abstract: Habitat suitability assessment and conservation gap identification are critical for endangered species conservation. Using Przewalski's gazelle ( Procapra przewalskii ), an endangered ungulate endemic to China, we assessed habitat suitability, key environmental predictors, and conservation gaps in the Qinghai Lake region. Based on 1597 field occurrence records collected from 2020 to 2025, we integrated the Maximum Entropy (MaxEnt) model with explainable artificial intelligence (XAI), including SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) and Partial Dependence Plots (PDPs), and GAP analysis. The selected MaxEnt model showed high discriminatory ability within the surveyed region (mean test AUC = 0.972 ± 0.003). The Human Influence Index (HII), mean temperature and precipitation of the driest quarter, elevation, and vegetation type were key predictors associated with habitat suitability, while mean diurnal range and HII had the highest mean SHAP importance. Suitable habitats were concentrated around Qinghai Lake and in the northern Gonghe Basin. The Qinghai Lake Basin represented the current core distribution area, whereas the Gonghe Basin contained extensive currently predicted suitable habitat and may represent an important conservation opportunity. GAP analysis showed that 71.83% of suitable habitat and 52.34% of the current distribution range lay outside the protected-area boundaries assessed in this study. Fence occurrence in the Hubei population area was significantly associated with relatively high predicted habitat suitability and showed marked spatial clustering. These findings provide spatially explicit evidence for protected-area optimization and habitat management of Przewalski's gazelle.

papers.title: Biochar granulation and particle size influence hydrological performance of green roof substrates
papers.abstract: Green roofs are increasingly implemented in cities to improve stormwater management and provide additional ecosystem services. Biochar, a carbon-rich material derived from pyrolyzed biomass, has emerged as a promising substrate additive to improve hydrological performance of green roofs. Biochar granulation and particle size modification have been suggested as effective approaches to mitigate erosion losses but research on the effects of biochar post-processing on hydrological performance remains scarce, and data on fundamental hydraulic properties of biochar-amended green roof substrates is entirely lacking. We investigated how biochar granulation and particle size influence surface and pore characteristics and hydraulic properties of green roof substrates in laboratory experiments. Granulated biochars exhibited collapsed surface morphology and pore structure, resulting in consistent hydrological responses across particle size ranges, likely due to the homogeneous structure formed during granulation. In contrast, unprocessed biochars showed a significant increase in Brunauer-Emmett-Teller (BET) specific surface area and pore volume with decreasing particle size. The amendment of granulated biochars improved substrate field capacity, suggesting potential enhancement of stormwater retention. The addition of fine (0.5–1 mm) and intermediate-sized (2–2.8 mm) unprocessed biochars also increased plant available water. Although reduced saturated hydraulic conductivity associated with fine unprocessed biochars may improve green roof detention capacity, fine biochar particle size may increase erosion losses and periodic waterlogging. We conclude that the application of either granulated biochar or intermediate-sized unprocessed biochar may provide a balanced enhancement of stormwater retention and detention capacities, as well as improved plant available water in green roof systems.

papers.title: Potentials and drivers of soil quality improvement – an index based on-farm evaluation
Remobilization risk of Cd in aged pig manure biochar under rice rhizosphere influence: Evidence from six-season cultivation
papers.abstract: Biochar is widely used to immobilize cadmium (Cd) in contaminated paddy soils; however, the long-term stability of biochar-adsorbed Cd under rice rhizosphere influence remains poorly understood, raising concerns about its potential secondary release. Herein, we investigated the remobilization behavior and speciation evolution of Cd from Cd-loaded pig manure biochar (Cd-PMB) using a six-season rice pot experiment, combined with a sequential simulated aging procedure designed to decouple the contributions of soil solution chemistry, root exudates, and oxidative processes. Two rice cultivars with contrasting Cd accumulation capacities were employed. Total Cd in Cd-PMB decreased by 84.3%–89.2% after six seasons, with >50% of the loss occurring during the first season, driven predominantly by cation exchange and rhizosphere acidification. Speciation analysis revealed that the ion-exchangeable Cd fraction was almost completely released (>95%) irrespective of planting treatment, while physically adsorbed and hydrogen-bonded Cd were preferentially remobilized under rhizosphere influence. Notably, complexed Cd exhibited a dual-phase dynamic, which initially increased by 8.1%–19.3% through secondary complexation onto newly formed carboxyl sites and subsequently declined during prolonged aging as these sites underwent protonation and oxidative degradation, as confirmed by Fourier‐transform infrared and X‐ray photoelectron spectroscopy analyses and further supported by significant Pearson correlations between COOH/ C O 3 2 − and Q com -Cd (r = 0.801, p < 0.05). The simulated aging experiments confirmed that soil solution, root exudates, and oxidative aging synergistically promote Cd release from distinct binding pools. Our findings demonstrate that biochar-adsorbed Cd undergoes substantial, binding form–dependent remobilization during aging, posing a secondary risk that necessitates explicit consideration in long-term safety assessments of biochar-amended soils.

papers.title: A bioindicator-based approach for evaluating environmental dioxin-like POPs burden: Implications for contamination surveillance and exposure risk assessment
papers.abstract: Recent global emission inventories, attributing significant releases of dioxin-like persistent organic pollutants (dl-POPs) to open burning activities, necessitate surveillance and emission control measures that invariably extend to non-point sources alongside conventionally weighed stationary point sources. The study presents an integrated field-based approach that employs foraging animal-origin food as bioindicators to systematically investigate and compare the environmental fingerprints and exposure risks of dl-POPs under such emission scenarios. The chosen study sites, viz. a legacy municipal solid waste (MSW) dumpsite and a biomedical waste incinerator (BMWI), along with a rare case of accidental fire incidents, represented classic real-world instances of transient/non-point and continuous/point sources. The observed substantially higher median dl-POPs levels in cow's milk and chicken eggs from the BMWI site (8.04 and 10.8 pgTEQ/g fat), relative to the MSW dumpsite (2.78 and 2.89 pgTEQ/g fat), highlighted continuous point sources as critical contributors to environmental burdens. Notably, dynamic trends of PCDD/Fs levels in milk and eggs over successive sampling phases suggested the contributive effect of fire breakouts to locally produced food contamination. Based on dietary exposure assessment, median dl-POPs weekly intake from the BMWI site and MSW dumpsite ranged up to 11.2 and 3.88 pgTEQ kg −1 bw week −1 , respectively, which are up to 5.6 and 1.9 times the EFSA-assigned tolerable weekly intake, indicating elevated health risk for consumers. The study upholds great relevance for data-deficient emerging economies to validate emission inventories, strengthen monitoring and source-specific emission control, and support regulatory frameworks in food commodities.

papers.title: RSM and ANN-driven optimization of Reactive Blue 221 biosorption by inactive Aspergillus niger: Mass transfer mechanisms, pareto analysis, and a circular economy approach
papers.abstract: Synthetic reactive dyes are persistent pollutants often found in textile wastewater due to their complex aromatic and sulfonated structures. This study evaluated inactive Aspergillus niger biomass as a biosorbent for removing Reactive Blue 221 (RB 221) from aqueous solutions. Batch experiments indicated that the Langmuir isotherm best described the equilibrium data, with a maximum monolayer capacity of 32.89 mg/g at 30 °C. Kinetic data fit well with the pseudo-second-order and Elovich models, pointing to physicochemical interactions on a heterogeneous surface. Kinetic evaluation via Weber-Morris and Boyd models indicated that the mass transfer rate was co-limited by both external film and intraparticle diffusion. Meanwhile, SEM, EDS, and FTIR analyses confirmed the localized physicochemical binding mechanisms, revealing post-biosorption morphological changes, dye-specific elemental signals, and the participation of protonated amines in binding sulfonate-rich RB 221. Thermodynamic parameters (ΔG° < 0 and ΔH° > 0) confirmed a spontaneous, endothermic process. Response Surface Methodology (RSM) with a Central Composite Design optimized the process, where conditions of pH 5.25, 7.95 g/L dosage, 30 °C, and 87.50 mg/L dye concentration yielded a maximum predicted removal efficiency of 89.17%, which was experimentally validated at 89.25%. Contribution analysis highlighted biosorbent dosage as the key operational parameter, accounting for ∼90% of the total process variance. An Artificial Neural Network (ANN) with a 4-20-10-1 topology yielded superior predictive accuracy compared to the quadratic RSM model (R 2 = 0.9941 vs. 0.968). Combined with a preliminary cost assessment and a proposed waste-to-energy disposal route, these findings demonstrate that inactive A. niger is a practical, low-cost, and sustainable biosorbent for textile wastewater treatment.

papers.title: Managing urban park landscape patterns to balance plant diversity and biotic homogenization across life forms: A case study of Chaoyang District, Beijing
papers.abstract: Biodiversity loss and the homogenization of plant communities are commonly observed in urbanized environments, highlighting the importance of maintaining plant diversity and compositional distinctness in urban green spaces. Urban parks are key refugia for plants, yet it remains unclear how their landscape patterns can be configured to simultaneously enhance species richness and reduce compositional homogenization across different plant life forms. Based on transect surveys of 820 plant species in 31 urban parks in Chaoyang District, Beijing, we combined multi-life-form analyses with a data-driven landscape framework to (i) identify the landscape metrics that best explain variation in plant richness and community composition, and (ii) quantify the trade-offs involved in reconciling their divergent requirements. We found consistently high levels of biotic homogenization across all plant types (all species, trees, shrubs, herbs and vines). Seventeen key landscape metrics were selected as important predictors of richness and composition, among which the interspersion and juxtaposition index provided particularly clear ecological interpretation. Higher morphological complexity of water bodies was associated with lower species richness, which may partly reflect shoreline hardening or reduced riparian habitat quality, whereas higher patch numbers of both green space and water generally promoted species richness and compositional distinctness. However, patch-number adjustments should not simply aim for maximization, but may instead follow a conceptual “peak-shaving and gap-filling” heuristic to balance additional patch creation with reduced redundancy in landscape configurations. For parks lacking water bodies, introducing water features may be considered where hydrologically and ecologically feasible, particularly when designed with naturalized shorelines to support plant richness and compositional distinctness. Our results provide a conceptual and data-driven framework for targeting landscape pattern adjustments in urban parks to promote plant diversity while alleviating biotic homogenization.

papers.title: Particle size-dependent carbon source capture and carbon allocation pathways by activated sludge
Differences in Dust Emission and Near‐Surface Transport Patterns Among Three Surface Substrate Types
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Soil wind erosion is a major driver of atmospheric dust emissions and land degradation. Many studies have examined dust release from different substrates, but differences in methods and units still limit quantitative understanding of how surface conditions and wind jointly control dust emission and near‐surface transport. A closed‐circuit wind tunnel was used to compare dust emission and vertical transport from dune sand (sand, D 50 = 176 μm), farmland soil (sandy loam, D 50 = 86 μm), and dry lakebed sediments (sand, D 50 = 153 μm). At 14 m s −1 , farmlands transported 6.2–7.2 times more PM 2.5 and 7.1–8.3 times more PM 10 than the other two substrates ( p < 0.001), while dunes and lakebeds transported more total mass. In the emitted material, dunes contributed the lowest fine particle proportion (PM 63 < 6.6%), farmlands maintained high fine fractions (PM 63 up to 55.5%), and lakebeds produced fine‐rich emissions at low wind speed but shifted towards low fine fractions as speed increased. Vertically, fine‐particle proportions increased with height over farmland soil across all wind speeds. Under the strongest wind, dune sand and dry lakebed sediment showed declining transported‐mass profiles and no significant height trends in particle‐size proportions. These results show that the surfaces that dominate total mass are not the same as those that dominate health‐relevant PM. This unified comparative analysis, grounded in controlled wind‐tunnel observations, supports targeted mitigation through modest‐height windbreaks for fine‐dust control on farmland, surface‐roughness enhancement on dunes, and crust stabilization on dry lakebeds.

JACKKNIFE EMPIRICAL LIKELIHOOD FOR INFINITE-ORDER U -STATISTICS
papers.abstract: Infinite-order U -statistics play a vital role in modern statistics. However, given their degree k n $k_n$ k Subscript n depends on the sample size n , quantifying their variability is quite challenging, as fixed-degree theories cannot be directly adopted. In this article, we propose a jackknife empirical likelihood (EL) framework that can be used to construct confidence intervals for an infinite-order U -statistic. We establish sufficient conditions for the limiting chi-squared distribution of the JEL ratio statistic and introduce an efficient partition-sampling realization for practical implementation. To evaluate the performance of the proposed methodology, we conduct simulation studies in the context of subsampling-based ensemble methods and the maximum test, respectively, comparing its performance with four competing methods. The simulation studies yield satisfactory results across the board. Finally, we demonstrate the practical application of our method using a United States Forest Service timber auctions dataset to predict the highest bid at an auction.

papers.title: Vertical Integration and Coordination in Modernising Staple Food Value Chains: Evidence From Myanmar's Rice Sector
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Increased vertical integration and coordination are defining features of transforming and modernising agricultural value chains in low‐ and middle‐income countries, with important implications for market efficiency and farm‐level transformation. However, research documenting these processes in transforming domestic value chains is limited, with existing studies largely focusing on large firms, foreign direct investment and high‐value food products, leaving less understood how domestic processors in staple food value chains expand into complementary businesses and services. We study these processes in the rice value chain—the most important staple in Southeast Asia—in Myanmar, using unique large‐scale data from domestic rice mills and farmers. We show that both modern and traditional mills serve as key nodes in local rice value chains, fulfilling diverse roles beyond processing at both the farm and post‐harvest levels. Yet, statistical tests that control for mill and farmer characteristics, respectively, show that modern mills are more engaged in vertical integration and coordination, particularly in post‐harvest value chain segments, highlighting the co‐development of modern processing and business expansion. Consistent with this pattern in the miller data, farmers using a modern mill are more likely to receive complementary services—especially post‐harvest—and to adopt modern production practices more broadly. However, this expansion is uneven, with services reaching large farms more frequently than small and medium farms.

papers.title: Mitigating School Closures: Parental Responses and Tutoring Vouchers
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT We investigate how school closures affect educational outcomes through parental responses. Using quasi‐experimental variation in school‐level closure days and linked administrative‐survey data, we find that 10 additional closure days raise private tutoring expenditure by 4.1% and within‐school test‐score dispersion by 25%; over the average 53‐day closure, low‐income students lose 0.09 SD. To quantify substitution between schooling and parental investment and evaluate compensatory policy, we estimate a tournament model in which schooling and tutoring jointly produce test scores. Tutoring substitutes for in‐person days, burdening low‐income households disproportionately. Counterfactuals show a means‐tested voucher fully offsets the resulting rise in inequality.

papers.title: Environmental Incidents and Sustainability Pricing Provisions
papers.journal_name: Journal of Money, Credit and Banking

papers.title: Measuring Measurement Error
papers.abstract: Abstract We collect 2,848 instrumental variable (IV) regressions from 391 papers published in top economics and finance journals and show that estimated IV coefficients are often much larger than their OLS counterparts, even when theory suggests they should be smaller. We derive meta-regression estimators that distinguish measurement error bias from omitted variable bias and simultaneity bias; applying our estimators to a set of 1,040 comparable regressions from 139 papers, we find that measurement error shrinks reported coefficients by about two to four times. Measurement error remains quantitatively important even after accounting for weak instruments, publication bias, instrument invalidity, and heterogeneous treatment effects. Our results suggest that measurement error is a severe, pervasive, and understated source of bias in economics and finance.

papers.title: Generalizing the Pareto principle with endogenous populations
Simulating competitive collocation strategies with deep reinforcement learning
papers.abstract: Abstract This paper introduces a simulation model based on deep reinforcement learning to study competitive collocation strategies of two internationalizing firms. Drawing on the strategic interaction and competitive collocation literature in IB, we explore the factors determining the performance-optimizing degree of collocation in market-seeking internationalization for a duopoly in product markets. Our simulation suggests that a high degree of collocation between the two firms is optimal in many circumstances. Whereas mid-to-high levels of collocation are driven by low competitive intensity, low entry barriers, low home-market size, and high market-size variation, complete collocation emerges under high competitive intensity, low first-mover advantage, and smaller home-market size. High entry barriers, combined with low variation in market size and strong liabilities of foreignness, drive the opposite case of complete mutual avoidance. A key takeaway from the simulation is a focus on the competing firm in global expansion: in many cases, it becomes key to limit the rival’s growth options and to enter key markets before access becomes more restricted. We discuss the possibilities of using computer-simulation-based approaches to theorizing on internationalization.

papers.title: CEO Ideologically (In)Congruent Activism and Investor Reactions: An Attribution of CEO Intentions Perspective
papers.abstract: Abstract The phenomenon of chief executive officers (CEOs) taking activism stances on contested sociopolitical issues is increasing, yet it remains unclear how observing investors discern CEO intentions behind activism engagements, thereby shaping their judgments and subsequent reactions. By relaxing the assumption that CEO activism is an unabashed expression of personal beliefs, we propose the concept of CEO ideologically (in)congruent activism and develop a framework wherein investors may attribute CEO intentions underlying incongruent (versus congruent) activism engagements as more organization‐driven (versus self‐driven) interest pursuits, thereby leading to more positive investor evaluations and reactions. Furthermore, we argue that the positive effect of CEO ideologically incongruent activism on investor reactions will be amplified when the CEO owns a higher level of stock ownership but weakened when the firm receives a greater corporate social responsibility (CSR) rating. We corroborate our propositions using a sample of CEO activism events for S&P 500 firms from 2012 to 2021. Our findings demonstrate the heterogeneity and critical influence of CEO intentions behind activism engagements and shed light on how investors integrate multi‐informational cues when evaluating and reacting to managerial incongruent behaviours.

papers.title: EXPRESS: The Role of Digital Ad Clutter in Ad Viewership and Memory
papers.abstract: Advertisers face an increasingly cluttered digital ecosystem where customer attention matters. Despite this, the extent to which digital advertising clutter influences ad viewership remains unclear. This paper presents three separate eye-tracking experiments (subjects: N = 99, N = 250, and N = 575) using over a dozen custom-built web pages to better understand how digital ad clutter affects consumers’ viewing of digital ads. Across experiments, we show that increased clutter led consumers to allocate more attention to the overall advertising space and adjust how they distribute viewership across ad positions. A complementary survey revealed that clutter also reduced ad memory and recall for individual ads. We discuss the implications for advertisers and publishers regarding ad pricing and placement in crowded digital environments.

papers.title: EXPRESS: Correcting omitted-variable bias without instruments: An ICA-based alternative to Gaussian copula methods
papers.abstract: This paper proposes an instrument-free correction for omitted-variable bias and overcomes a key limitation of Gaussian copula control function (GCCF) approaches. Omitted-variable bias is the most common source of endogeneity in marketing, and many articles apply GCCF to address it. Yet GCCF require a nonlinear regressor-error relation, whereas textbooks assume linear, additive relationships between regressors and omitted variables. The authors prove that GCCF is biased in classical omitted-variable settings. Extant articles that address omitted-variables with GCCF also show language cues implicitly assuming linear relationships, which invalidate the use of GCCF. The proposed endogeneity correction is tailored to this prominent case, utilizing independent component analysis (ICA). It assumes a latent normally distributed component that additively influences both the endogenous regressor and the error. This can be interpreted as the sum of omitted variables, which, according to the Central Limit Theorem, add up to a normal distribution. Through ICA, this component is identified and extracted from the endogenous regressor, rendering the regression model free of endogeneity and enabling causal inference. The paper proves that the model is point-identified despite endogeneity due to omitted variables, that the proposed estimator is consistent and asymptotically normal, and that Jackknife resampling yields valid standard errors.

papers.title: EXPRESS: Why are products so similar despite diverse consumer needs? The interplay between advertising and horizontal product differentiation
papers.abstract: Firms are often less differentiated than standard price-competition models predict. We explain this gap by showing how firms can use informative or reminder advertising to soften competition. When firms choose locations, advertising, and prices endogenously, they may choose to soften price competition through limited advertising rather than greater product differentiation, allowing them to locate closer together while limiting price competition. This outcome of low advertising and central collocation is especially likely when advertising costs are high. We also observe that partially-differentiated equilibria, with one firm locating centrally and the other at an edge, and full differentiation, can each emerge under certain conditions. Thus, firms endogenously choose a mix of advertising and product differentiation to moderate price competition. Further, the shape of travel costs influences the equilibrium outcome. If the disutility from distance is highly convex, such as occurs when consumer preferences exhibit satisficing, central collocation becomes the unique equilibrium when more consumers are concentrated at the edge locations. However, when the disutility from distance is linear, having more customers located towards the edge locations makes collocation less likely. Overall, the interaction of advertising costs, consumer preferences, and location choices help explain why firms often forgo product differentiation.

papers.title: Competition and Diversity in Generative AI
papers.abstract: Recent evidence, both in the laboratory and in the wild, suggests that the use of generative artificial intelligence reduces the diversity of content produced. As generative AI penetrates more markets and reaches widespread adoption, should we still expect to see content homogenization? Our work begins with a simple observation: content producers do not act in isolation. Instead, they compete with one another (e.g., for customers or attention). We explore the impact competition has on both content diversity and overall social welfare when producers use generative AI. Through a formal game-theoretic model, we show that competitive markets select for diverse AI models, mitigating monoculture. We further show that a generative AI model that performs well in isolation (i.e., according to a benchmark) may fail to provide value in a competitive market. Our results highlight the importance of evaluating generative AI models across the breadth of their output distributions, particularly when they will be deployed in competitive environments. We validate our theoretical results with a series of experiments involving generative text and image models. Overall, our results suggest that homogenization due to generative AI is unlikely to persist under strong competition. This paper was accepted by Itai Ashlagi, market design, platform, and demand analytics. Supplemental Material: The online appendix and data files are available at https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2025.02761 .

papers.title: The Buy-in Effect: When Increasing Initial Effort Encourages Follow-Through
papers.abstract: Behavioral interventions often focus on reducing friction to encourage behavior change. In contrast, we provide evidence that adding initial friction to a sign-up process can increase follow-through behavior. In a field experiment with a state department of transportation ([Formula: see text]), we test whether adding modest friction during sign-up for a carpool platform increases usage. Although a more effortful sign-up process leads to 25% fewer sign-ups, overall usage increases. Importantly, these results were only partly explained by selection: Using an intent-to-treat analysis, participants with a more effortful sign-up process took 1.6 times more carpool trips per week over four months, leading to more overall trips despite fewer users. In a second experiment with online task work, participants with more effortful sign-up were 37% more likely to return the next day and completed more work overall. These results suggest that adding friction may be an overlooked strategy when follow-through, rather than initial uptake, is the primary goal. This paper was accepted by George Wu, behavioral economics and decision analysis. Funding: The authors acknowledge funding from the University of Konstanz for Study 2, Harvard University Pershing Square Foundation for Human Research, and Harvard Business School. The funders had no role in data collection and analysis, the decision to publish, or preparation of this manuscript. Supplemental Material: The online appendices and data files are available at https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2023.03600 .

papers.title: Measuring Organizational Constructs in Large-Scale Text: An interpretive framework combining topic modeling and BERT
papers.abstract: Measuring organizational constructs in large-scale unstructured text requires methods that preserve interpretive depth while enabling systematic, per-document classification. Structural Topic Modeling (STM) supports interpretive depth by surfacing patterns that inform construct operationalization, but its topic proportions are not designed as standalone per-document construct measures; transformer-based models such as BERT can scale measurement but require construct operationalization grounded in interpretive work. We address this challenge through a two-stage framework in which STM and BERT play structurally distinct roles. Coding schemes are developed through qualitative interpretation and STM analysis; BERT is then fine-tuned to apply these schemes across documents. We formalize two research approaches—construct-guided and pattern-discovery—that provide principled paths from different theoretical starting points toward a shared methodological endpoint: validated, auditable per-document construct measures. We illustrate the framework using more than 20,000 employee reviews. The framework supports iterative construct validation, using computational diagnostics to guide interpretive refinement and producing document-level measures suitable for theory-informed organizational analysis.

papers.title: Media Review: Homebound: Caste, Muslim Identity, and the Organizational Politics of Stigmatized Lives
Media Review: The Ocean between Utopias and Dystopias
Media Review: The Objects That Count Us
Media Review: Moving From Robust Identities to Ontological Differences in Organization Theory?
Who Qualifies to Assure? The Professional and Managerial Capture of Sustainability Assurance
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines how the qualification of assurors in sustainability and environmental reporting assurance (SERA) is constructed and why it remains fiercely contested. Drawing on actor–network theory (ANT) and qualitative evidence from regulators, NGOs, assurors and reporting companies in India, we conceptualise ‘qualification’ as a ‘boundary object’ flexible enough for competing actors to invoke, yet too ambiguous to secure substantive credibility. Assurance standards do not license practitioners, a function ordinarily undertaken by regulators and professional bodies. Nevertheless, ISAE 3000 (Revised) requires the engagement partner to possess ‘sufficient competence in the underlying subject matter’ and requires practitioners who are not professional accountants to identify the equivalent professional requirements under which they operate. Our analysis examines what becomes of these competence requirements when no external mechanism consistently verifies the claims made. The findings reveal that assurance standards require competence but rely substantially on practitioners to identify and disclose the professional requirements governing their work, without themselves providing an external licensing or verification mechanism. This ambiguity enables professional and managerial actors to privilege reputational legitimacy over the transparent demonstration of expertise, potentially reducing assurance to a symbolic exercise rather than a mechanism of substantive accountability. The study contributes to the SERA literature by reframing qualification as a fragile, networked achievement rather than a fixed credential. It highlights the need for transparent, dialogic and enforceable mechanisms through which competence claims can be demonstrated, scrutinised and sustained, thereby safeguarding independence, rigorous materiality assessments and stakeholder trust. These findings offer theoretical and practical insights for standard setters and policy makers seeking to mitigate greenwashing and strengthen the integrity of sustainability assurance.

papers.title: Biodiversity Action Planning Within a Global Agricultural Supply Chain
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Agriculture is a primary driver of biodiversity loss through habitat conversion and degradation. Companies are increasingly being asked to investigate, disclose, and act on their biodiversity impacts by both regulatory policies and voluntary commitments. Yet companies lack practical guidance for identifying actions that mitigate negative externalities and improve natural systems on commodified lands and throughout their supply chains. We collaborated with an international food and beverage company sourcing from 120 regions around the world to develop a generalizable opportunity mapping framework based on cost‐effectiveness. We used publicly available datasets, a decision‐theoretic prioritization framework, and included both quantitative and qualitative insights. Our intent is to demonstrate how opportunity mapping and prioritization can integrate biodiversity into a company's decisions or nature strategies. Our approach helps companies see where and how their activities may contribute to pressures on biodiversity. We then help companies operationalize those insights into sourcing policies, regional investment, and engagement strategies across supply chains.

papers.title: Beyond Disclosure: Sustainable Finance Regulation and the Pricing of ESG Performance in Mature Capital Markets
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines whether and under what conditions Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) performance becomes financially meaningful in mature capital markets. Using a longitudinal transatlantic panel of large firms listed in the EURO STOXX 50 and S&P 100 over the period 2015–2024, we analyse the within‐firm association between lagged ESG performance, market valuation, and accounting profitability. We further examine whether this relationship changes around the 2018 EU Action Plan on Financing Sustainable Growth and the 2021 implementation of the Sustainable Finance Disclosure Regulation, and whether ESG controversies moderate the financial relevance of ESG performance. Firm and year fixed‐effect models show that improvements in ESG performance are positively but only weakly associated with Tobin's Q , whereas no systematic relationship emerges with accounting profitability. Policy interaction models and a dynamic event study provide no evidence of a discrete strengthening of the ESG–valuation relationship for EU‐domiciled firms relative to US‐domiciled firms following the selected regulatory milestones. ESG controversies are directionally associated with weaker ESG value relevance, although the evidence is more pronounced for profitability than for market valuation. Moreover, the Environmental, Social, and Governance pillars are not statistically distinguishable from one another. Among large and highly visible firms, sustainable finance regulation may operate as institutional codification and credibility infrastructure rather than as an abrupt valuation shock, although the evidence is equally consistent with limited statistical power and with measurement error in a domicile‐based indicator of regulatory exposure. The results highlight the conditional and statistically fragile nature of ESG value relevance and should be generalized cautiously beyond institutionally mature capital markets.

papers.title: Research on the mechanism of linking time pressure to career growth among hotel employees
papers.abstract: Research overlooks how and why identical cognitive appraisals of time pressure translate into divergent coping behaviors. Drawing upon the cognitive appraisal theory of stress, this study investigates the mechanisms linking time pressure to the career growth of frontline hotel employees. Utilizing a three-wave time-lagged design, we collected survey data from 323 frontline hotel employees in China and analyzed it using PLS-SEM via SmartPLS 4.0. The results reveal that challenge appraisal and hindrance appraisal play differentiated mediating roles between time pressure and career growth, with job crafting serving as a crucial behavioral bridge in the transformation from stress appraisal to career growth. Furthermore, achievement motivation significantly moderates this transformation from stress appraisal to job crafting behavior. This study provides empirical evidence for the hospitality industry to implement differentiated stress management and employee development interventions.

papers.title: How much greenery matters: effects on visual attention, guest perceptions and brand outcomes
papers.abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate how varying levels of indoor greenery capture visual attention and affect guest perceptions and brand outcomes. It also examines the mediating roles of fascination and perceived aesthetic quality in linking greenery to brand outcomes. Design/methodology/approach A mixed-design experiment exposed participants to two virtual hotel lobbies: a control with no greenery and one of three greenery conditions (low: 2% coverage, medium: 16% or high: 30%). Eye tracking captured gaze behavior during exposure, while post-exposure surveys measured fascination, aesthetic quality, brand love and willingness to pay more. Findings Indoor greenery attracted greater visual attention than the no-greenery condition, as indicated by generally higher fixation counts and longer dwell times. Even low greenery enhanced fascination, aesthetic quality, brand love and willingness to pay more, with medium and high conditions producing progressively stronger effects. Fascination and aesthetic quality increased brand love, which subsequently strengthened willingness to pay more. Practical implications The findings highlight the strategic value of indoor greenery as a visually salient hospitality servicescape feature that enhances guest perceptions and supports brand outcomes. Furthermore, this study suggests that indoor greenery can serve as a strategic brand-signaling cue that helps align guest perceptions with desired market positioning. Originality/value By combining eye tracking and self-reported measures across four experimental conditions, this study provides objective evidence of greenery’s visual salience and identifies the perceptual pathways linking it to brand outcomes.
papers.journal_name: International Journal of Contemporary Hospitality Management

papers.title: International scaling of social innovations through digitalization: A 3D framework
papers.abstract: Social enterprises that embed social innovations (SIs) play a critical role in advancing the UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), representing an estimated US$12 trillion market opportunity. Yet, how SIs internationalize in the presence of institutional voids remains underexplored in international business research. Using a history-to-theory and history-in-theory approach, this study examines how dynamic capabilities and digitalization enable the international scaling of SIs. We find that international diffusion depends on capabilities such as boundary spanning, international sensing, legitimacy building, business diplomacy, and market shaping. Digitalization accelerates scaling, contingent on factors including timing, resources, intellectual property ownership, purpose, and technology scope. Our findings also suggest that traditional internationalization metrics—such as exports, FDI, subsidiaries, and foreign sales—do not adequately capture SI internationalization. Instead, internationalization is reflected in the cross-border diffusion of innovations and social impact, alongside the ability to attract international funding, partnerships, talent, and legitimacy while balancing social impact with financial sustainability.

papers.title: The SME network dilemma: Capability building versus capability erosion
papers.abstract: Cluster membership is widely expected to make small firms innovative. Often it does not. We locate the explanation inside the firm rather than in its network position. Integrating the dynamic capabilities and attention-based views, we argue that an SME’s external ties matter less for the resources they carry than for what they do to the routines that process those resources—building them in one case, eroding them in the other. Evidence from a four-informant survey of 186 SMEs in government-led Chinese industrial clusters is consistent with this account. Business ties are associated with higher innovativeness indirectly, through stronger absorptive capacity and firm agility. Political ties, once their substantial overlap with business ties is held constant, run in the opposite direction: they are associated with weaker agility, and their negative association with absorptive capacity falls short of conventional significance. Neither tie type retains a detectable direct association with innovativeness: network position appears to matter through the internal routines that convert it. We name this second pathway capability erosion, a decay that we attribute not to overuse or historical lock-in but to the systematic diversion of scarce managerial attention, and we offer it as one explanation for why so many SMEs remain innovation laggards in resource-rich clusters.

papers.title: The yin and yang in the angel market: Angel group gender diversity and investment performance
Bouncing, believing and building: Resilient coping, entrepreneurial self-efficacy, perceived venture performance, and state fragility
papers.abstract: Using data from 19,593 entrepreneurs across 37 countries, we examine whether the associations among resilient coping, entrepreneurial self-efficacy, and perceived venture performance vary across levels of state fragility. The results show that the conditional indirect effect of resilience on perceived venture performance through entrepreneurial self-efficacy is stronger in non-fragile contexts than in the most fragile contexts represented by the Iraqi and Nigerian samples. In the most fragile context, resilience is more directly associated with perceived venture performance, while the association between resilience and entrepreneurial self-efficacy becomes stronger under moderate fragility before weakening under extreme fragility. This exploratory pattern is consistent with the possibility that resilience may serve multiple functions across contextual conditions, while primarily supporting capability building in more stable environments and serving a more direct, maintenance-oriented role under extreme fragility. The findings point to the importance of context-sensitive approaches to entrepreneurial support and capability development.

papers.title: How strong event systems influence organizational features in multinational enterprises: the case of global mobility during COVID
papers.journal_name: The International Journal of Human Resource Management

papers.title: Critical accountants in the face of ecological crises: towards a more-than-human critical resilience
papers.abstract: This study investigates the identity work of critical accountants in the face of ecological crises, drawing on 28 semi-structured interviews and an autoethnographic account. Identity work encompasses the mental and physical practices critical accountants employ to sustain their identity in adequacy with their community of scholars. The findings show that critical accountants exhibit a variety of resilience mechanisms but rely heavily on collective practices, challenging previous accounts that focus on individual strategies. The study nevertheless shows that these collectives do not include their non-human relatives. The article argues that this disconnect might explain a relative disengagement from critical environmental accounting research, while attenuating the negative effects of ecological crises on critical accountants' well-being. Based on these findings, the article proposes adopting “more-than-human critical resilience,” which refers to the land-based and ethical collective practices developed by humans and non-humans to resist the neoliberal capture of society.

papers.title: Do textual attributes of management commentary matter for analyst coverage and information quality: evidence from the United Kingdom
papers.abstract: Purpose This study examines whether the readability of management commentary is associated with analysts' coverage and the precision of analysts' information sets. It further investigates whether analysts' experience, access to resources and forecast boldness moderate these relationships. Design/methodology/approach Using 5,117 firm-year observations from 974 UK-listed firms, we employ ordinary least squares (OLS) regression models to examine the association between management commentary readability and analyst outcomes. To address potential endogeneity concerns and assess the robustness of our findings, we conduct additional analyses using entropy balancing, the Heckman (1979) two-stage procedure, omitted variable bias analysis, instrumental variable estimation and alternative measures of readability. Findings We find that firms with less readable management commentary have greater analyst coverage and higher precision of analysts' information sets. Decomposing total information precision into public and private components, we find that lower readability is positively associated with both public and private information precision. These findings are consistent with lower readability increasing the value of analysts' information-processing and information-production activities and suggest that analysts respond to less readable commentary by both processing publicly available information and acquiring additional private information. We further show that analyst experience and forecast boldness strengthen the positive association between lower readability and both analyst coverage and information precision. In contrast, analysts' access to resources strengthens the association between lower readability and analyst coverage but does not significantly moderate the association with information precision. Additional analysis indicates that the component of textual complexity attributable to observable business complexity is positively associated with analyst coverage and with total and public information precision, but not with private information precision. Research limitations/implications The findings have implications for regulators, standard setters, firms and investors by highlighting the need to distinguish unnecessary complexity from textual complexity arising from economically relevant information. Originality/value This study contributes to the literature on narrative disclosures readability and analyst behaviour by highlighting analysts' information-provider role and demonstrating that the association between management commentary readability and analyst outcomes varies with analysts' attributes, particularly their experience and forecast boldness.

papers.title: The upside of Mess: conceptualising (dis)order as a dynamic family resource
papers.abstract: This study examines how domestic (dis)order emerges as shifting states shaped by everyday socio-material interactions. Drawing on assemblage theory and photo-elicitation interviews with 22 households, we show how (dis)order develops through dynamic relations among family members, objects, spaces, and temporal rhythms. We identify three assemblage capacities—transient, functional, and conducive—that shape how disorder materialises and is understood, along with three corresponding management strategies: restoring, tolerating, and concealing. Beyond the home, these capacities extend assemblage theory by providing a transferable framework for theorising how assemblages generate distinct emergent states across consumer and marketplace contexts. Reconceptualising (dis)order as an emergent assemblage property rather than an individual shortcoming, the study reveals conditions under which mess serves as a productive resource supporting household flow, functional efficiency, and relational harmony. The study also offers practical implications for flexible storage design, functional mess zone identification, and organisation solutions that support family wellbeing.

papers.title: The Effect of Smile Cues on Food Calorie Perception: The Moderating Role of Dietary Restraint
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Consumers are becoming increasingly attentive to healthy eating and the caloric content of their food. However, when judging a food's calories, they often lack sufficient knowledge or objective information and therefore rely on marketplace cues to make subjective evaluations. Although smile cues are widely used in food marketing, little is known about how consumers' dietary restraint shapes the calorie‐related inferences they draw from such cues. Across five studies, we show that, for foods that are inherently indulgent or can meaningfully be construed in indulgence‐related terms, smile cues increase perceived indulgence, which in turn leads to higher calorie perceptions more strongly when dietary restraint is higher or situationally activated. Extending the focal calorie perception process to downstream behaviors, we further show that consumers were less likely to choose foods with a smile cue when dietary restraint is activated than not. These findings contribute to the literature on food calorie judgment, smile, and dietary restraint.

papers.title: Smiling in influencer marketing: how smiles shape authenticity and consumer engagement
papers.abstract: Purpose Many influencer marketing campaigns feature smiling influencers. However, whether smiling is always beneficial, and under which circumstances it might not be, remains underexplored. This paper aims to examine how an influencer’s smile (vs no smile) affects consumer engagement with influencer posts. Design/methodology/approach The authors conducted a field study and several online experiments. In the field study, they analyzed 802 influencer campaigns with a total of over 125 million consumer interactions (i.e. liking and commenting). In the experiments, participants viewed influencer posts featuring commonly promoted products such as headphones (nStudy2 = 192, nStudy4 = 231), sunglasses (nStudy3 = 304) and protein bars (nStudy5 = 236, nSupplemental = 247). Findings The authors show that a smile (vs no smile) in influencer posts can backfire. Smiling can lead to lower engagement by reducing perceived authenticity. However, this negative effect is contingent upon influencer type (micro vs macro) and sponsorship presence (sponsored vs. non-sponsored). Research limitations/implications While Instagram was the authors’ focus, smile effects may be different on other platforms. Although they focused on engagement, other marketing outcomes may exhibit different patterns. Finally, other contextual factors may influence whether smiling backfires or not. Practical implications Marketers and influencers should carefully consider the use of smiles when endorsing products on social media. While smiling may enhance engagement for micro influencers, it can have the opposite effect for macro influencers. However, for macro influencers, smiling may still boost engagement when the product recommendation is not sponsored. Originality/value In revealing a negative effect of smiling in influencer posts, along with an underlying mechanism and boundary conditions, the authors’ study advances the influencer marketing literature. The authors show that a smile can increase engagement and purchase likelihood for some influencer types and campaigns, while it can decrease it for others. Thus, they provide a nuanced picture of the importance of smiling in influencer marketing on social media.

papers.title: Can leisure travel help combat loneliness in later life?
Leading by example: how major customers shape suppliers' implementation of process-based rights
papers.abstract: Purpose Drawing from research on dependence and embeddedness in supplier-major customer relationships, this study examines the implementation level of process-based rights (PBR) – including freedom of association, workforce diversity, and fair and non-discriminatory treatment of workers – within supplier-major customer dyads. The study also empirically investigates how customers' transactional governance and relationship history with suppliers interplay in suppliers' PBR implementation. Design/methodology/approach Using 482 unique supplier-major customer dyads over 14 years (2010–2024), we performed hierarchical analysis to estimate the direct and interaction effects of customers' PBR implementation, transactional governance, and relationship history on their suppliers' PBR implementation. Findings Our results show that major customers exert a significant influence on suppliers' PBR implementation. Furthermore, transactional governance and a long relationship history work in synergistic ways only when the customer itself demonstrates average to high levels of PBR, but not when customer PBR implementation levels are low. Originality/value As one of the first studies to explore PBR within supplier-major customer dyads, our findings underscore the important role of customers in leading the implementation of labor standards, rather than as an enforcer of labor standards, in motivating supplier compliance.
papers.journal_name: International Journal of Operations & Production Management

papers.title: Big Data Development and Corporate Environmental Strategy: Evidence from Green Innovation Engagement
Who Gains from creative destruction? Evidence from high-quality entrepreneurship in the United States
papers.abstract: The question of who gains from high-quality entrepreneurship is crucial to understanding whether investments in innovative startup firms produce socially beneficial outcomes. Although entrepreneurship is widely viewed as a central driver of economic growth, recent research has raised concerns that it may also exacerbate inequality and other undesirable social outcomes. We bring new evidence to this debate by analyzing the impact of entrepreneurship on a variety of local economic outcomes, including income inequality, average incomes, and income mobility, using IRS and U.S. Census Bureau microdata. We find that entrepreneurship indeed increases income inequality, although this effect fades in the years after firm founding. While entrepreneurship produces statistically significant income gains across the distribution, the economic magnitude of these effects varies dramatically, with benefits concentrated among top earners. We also find that entrepreneurship can serve as a mobility tool for less well-off individuals, increasing their probability of rising to the top of the income distribution. These income and mobility gains, however, are uneven across demographic groups.

papers.title: Routinized Deference: Predictive Screening and Bureaucratic Capacity in Child Protective Services
papers.abstract: Abstract Predictive algorithms are increasingly used to support frontline decision-making in public administration, but evidence remains limited on how they affect bureaucratic capacity. This study examines county-level adoption of predictive screening tools in U.S. Child Protective Services using NCANDS data (2010–2023) and a stacked difference-in-differences design. Leveraging staggered adoption, I find no change in the total number of investigations opened and a sizable decline (about 15%) in the share of investigations that are substantiated. These results are inconsistent with operational capacity gains and more consistent with misclassification that erodes analytical capacity. These findings are consistent with a mechanism of routinized deference: under workload and accountability pressures, algorithmic recommendations can become procedurally defensible defaults. Overall, this study argues that predictive screening is not capacity-enhancing by default, as routinized deference can undermine the professional judgment central to bureaucratic work.
papers.journal_name: Journal of Public Administration Research and Theory

papers.title: Unpacking the causal complexity of collaborative effectiveness in urban marginalized community regeneration: a fuzzy-set configurational analysis
papers.abstract: This study examines the causal conditions shaping collaborative effectiveness in the regeneration of marginalized urban communities. Using fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis of 22 Chinese cases, it identifies facilitative leadership as a necessary condition for achieving high collaborative effectiveness and weak institutionalization as a necessary condition for low effectiveness. The sufficiency analysis reveals three distinct pathways to effective collaboration and three to ineffective collaboration. The findings show that collaborative effectiveness depends on context-specific configurations of resource support, institutionalization, governance structure, and facilitative leadership. No single condition is sufficient in isolation; rather, effectiveness emerges through complementarity, functional equivalence, and asymmetric substitutability among conditions. The study contributes to a more context-sensitive and configurational understanding of collaborative governance.

papers.title: Mapping empathy in policy work: how public servants understand and use it
Representative Bureaucracy in Private Philanthropy: Testing Discretion and Racial Representation in Community Foundation Grantmaking
papers.abstract: As public service delivery increasingly involves non-governmental actors, public administration theory needs to examine how its core frameworks operate beyond traditional bureaucracies. This study extends representative bureaucracy theory to private philanthropy, an increasingly crucial actor in local public service delivery, by testing whether racial representation in leadership corresponds with equitable grantmaking outcomes. Analyzing longitudinal data from 912 U.S. community foundations between 2012 and 2016, this study finds that racial representation in foundation leadership corresponds with increased grantmaking to organizations serving communities of color when leadership retains sufficient discretion, but that this relationship weakens as donor control rises, particularly through donor advised funds. These patterns are consistent with representative bureaucracy theory's emphasis on discretion as a key mechanism linking passive and active representation. These findings advance theoretical understanding by illuminating the interplay between representation and discretion within private philanthropy, while carrying implications for equitable resource distribution as public services increasingly involve non-governmental actors.
papers.journal_name: The American Review of Public Administration

papers.title: Severity at the Gates: Or Why Prevention is the Aim of Reproductive Genetic Carrier Screening
papers.abstract: Reproductive autonomy is usually described as the aim of publicly funded reproductive genetic carrier screening. I argue that this misdescribes the practice. These programs do not include conditions because any information might support choice. They include them because severity sets the scope. The aim of these programs, therefore, is prevention: not preventing the birth of particular persons, but offering a preventive response to the serious suffering associated with some severe inherited conditions. Reproductive autonomy, however, is the legitimate means by which a liberal program may pursue that aim, through information, counseling and voluntary decision making. That pursuit must satisfy what I call a liberal proviso, so that prevention does not become pressure, stigma or eugenic state steering. Naming prevention also enriches the disability critique. It makes both inclusion and exclusion morally visible and warranting justification, since both express judgments about which forms of suffering warrant collective response.

papers.title: Missed opportunities: lessons from Haitian AIDS patients and their relevance today
Authors’ Response: Quasi-experiments rely on design choices: a reflection on Renson and Westreich’s “What makes a study design quasi-experimental?”
Navigating GenAI in the workplace: skills transformation & tension
papers.abstract: By automating the content creation process, Generative AI is reshaping creative work, but its impact on knowledge workers remains underexplored, which this study seeks to examine. Drawing on in-depth interviews with 20 knowledge workers, this study examines what is being transformed in the workplace and how these shifts are being perceived by the knowledge workers who use GenAI.
