Using Social Shaping of Technology (SST) as a conceptual lens to understand the interaction between technology and knowledge workers, the study finds that participants perceived GenAI as an efficient tool that provides cognitive relief and enhances productivity during times of resource constraint. Tensions also arose around authenticity, creativity, a sense of fulfillment, and the perception of effort. The adoption of GenAI has created downstream labor and demand for new skills as it shifts knowledge workers’ roles away from creator to editor/fact-checker while creating tension as participants balance their desire for efficiency with fears of diminished creativity and domain knowledge, skills atrophy, and threats to content ownership.

papers.title: A Bayesian Approach to Estimating Changes in Small Area Life Expectancy Disparities in Philadelphia
papers.abstract: There is substantial geographic variation in life expectancy (LE). The COVID-19 pandemic caused a mortality crisis, but it is unclear how small-area variations in LE changed during the pandemic. We estimated gender-specific LE by census tract in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania (2017–2019 and 2020–2022), and compared disparities in LE at birth before and during the pandemic. To account for small counts, we employed a Bayesian Poisson model borrowing strength from neighboring census tracts by using conditional autoregressive priors, and from known age-specific mortality patterns by using an adaptation of the TOPALS (tool for projecting age patterns using linear splines) method. We then summarized LE and computed total and income-based disparities in LE by period. The median [10th–90th percentile] change in LE during the pandemic was −2.10 [−5.39 to 0.40] and −1.37 [−3.23 to 0.39] years for men and women, respectively. Declines were concentrated in the same areas that had lower LE at baseline. We found widening disparities due to a steeper decline in LE in lower-income areas during the pandemic. Our study leveraged Bayesian models to produce reliable local-level estimates in small areas, highlighting the disparate impacts that the pandemic had on population health.

papers.title: Developing the Universal Child Abuse Screening Tool (U-CAST) for Epic: A Qualitative Analysis of Expert Working Groups
papers.abstract: Child abuse and maltreatment remain major public health concerns in the United States. Early identification is challenging, particularly for clinicians without specialized pediatric training, and disparities in detection raise concerns about bias. Universal screening integrated into electronic health records (EHRs) may improve detection and equity. To develop an evidence-based, user-friendly, and broadly applicable universal child abuse screening tool (U-CAST) for integration into the EPIC Foundation System. A qualitative study engaged nine expert working groups comprising 17 specialists in child abuse pediatrics, pediatric trauma surgery, general pediatrics, and pediatric emergency medicine. Between February and April 2022, groups met virtually to discuss screening content, clinical decision support, workflow integration, and implementation considerations. Meeting transcripts were analyzed using inductive coding and thematic analysis. Five themes emerged: (1) the importance of universal screening; (2) essential tool components; (3) appropriate clinical settings; (4) actionable follow-up protocols for positive screens; and (5) local program evaluation. Preliminary implementation data demonstrated successful integration, high screening completion rates, and encouraging performance in identifying children with suspected physical abuse. U-CAST was developed through a multi-disciplinary expert process and designed for integration into Epic workflows. Preliminary findings support its feasibility and clinical utility.

papers.title: Reliability and quality of YouTube exercise videos for people living with lung cancer: a cross-sectional content analysis
Rethinking Multilevel Governance. By ArthurBenz. Cheltenham, UK: Edward Elgar Publishing, 2024. 208 pp. ISBN: 978‐1‐03‐530628‐2
Social-media engagement in municipalities: a citizen perspective
papers.abstract: This article focuses on citizen engagement through social media. While prior research has addressed engagement from an administration-centred viewpoint, this study prefers a citizen perspective, interpreted with the Uses and Gratifications Theory. We administered a survey through Facebook pages of the largest cities in Quebec and boroughs of Montreal. Results show that informative content is more likely to increase engagement. The publication of good news and timely responses by municipalities also seem to foster engagement, while elements such as media richness seem less relevant. Our findings highlight several implications for public administrations seeking to promote a citizen-centred approach.

papers.title: Dynamic start-up and operating window analysis of an ammonia-fueled SOFC system with flexible cracking ratio operation
A GPU-accelerated multi-physics coupling framework based on the lattice boltzmann method for performance analysis of utility-scale photovoltaic power plants
An interpretable aging prediction model for Ni-rich all-solid-state batteries informed by mechanistic modeling
papers.abstract: Ni-rich all-solid-state batteries (ASSBs) are promising candidates for next-generation energy storage technology, while they suffer from much more severe capacity fading than lithium-ion batteries with liquid electrolyte, severely compromising their practical application and commercialization. Accurate degradation prediction is required to improve the operational stability of Ni-rich ASSBs. A novel degradation prediction framework for NCA (LiNi 0.8 Co 0.16 Al 0.03 , Nickel content: 80%) cathode ASSBs is proposed based on a mechanism model combined with deep neural network in this study. This study first constructs a three-dimensional physical model of ASSBs with NCA cathodes. On the basis of experimental observations, three cathode capacity degradation processes, namely interfacial side reactions, interfacial delamination and particle cracking, are parameterized. Subsequently, the CNN-LSTM hybrid framework is constructed for model training, and a multi-level prediction module is further embedded into the architecture to leverage the advantage of physical model in capturing battery internal characteristics, e.g., the Li concentration as an additional feature. Validated by simulation data, the proposed model possesses the high prediction accuracy in estimating NCA-based ASSBs degradation. Comparative analyses are carried out against the prediction model without concentration correction to further verify the rationality of the proposed prediction framework, indicating that concentration correction substantially enhances the prediction accuracy under small-sample scenarios. The three-dimensional mechanism model-neural network fusion framework proposed in this work verifies that neural networks embedded with physical prior information such as lithium-ion concentration exhibit stronger learning capacity. Even under limited data conditions, the framework can accurately predict capacity degradation of ASSBs with NCA cathodes. This study provides theoretical references for performance prediction and battery management of NCA-based ASSBs.

papers.title: Assessing behavior-conditioned building flexibility potential across building types for photovoltaic accommodation
papers.abstract: Building flexibility is increasingly recognized as an important demand-side resource for renewable energy integration, yet its characterization in real buildings remains challenging because flexibility is strongly conditioned by operational behavior and is difficult to quantify without detailed system information. This study proposes a behavior-informed framework to assess behavior-conditioned flexibility potential across building types using historical operation data, and further examines its potential implications for photovoltaic (PV) accommodation under building-cluster scenarios. Using 15-min measured electricity data from multiple types of public buildings in Hangzhou, China, the framework first establishes baseline load behavior through quantile-based modeling, then identifies feasible operating ranges from historically comparable operating conditions, and finally estimates behavior-conditioned flexibility potential in terms of both instantaneous adjustable power and duration-based adjustable energy. XGBoost-SHAP analysis is further employed to interpret the statistical associations between input features and the estimated flexibility indicators, and an aggregated analysis is conducted to evaluate the value of flexibility potential for PV accommodation under different curtailment constraints. For the studied public-building dataset, the estimated flexibility potential shows clear heterogeneity across building types. Load level, hour of day, outdoor temperature, and daily load characteristics show the largest contributions to the model predictions, suggesting that the estimated flexibility potential is closely associated with energy-consuming behavior. At the cluster level, the results further reveal that high flexibility does not necessarily translate into high PV accommodation potential. Under a 15% curtailment threshold, the average PV capacity factor of the realistic mixed-building aggregation scenario increased from 0.288 to 0.369 in the flexibility-enhanced scenario, corresponding to an absolute increase of 0.08 and a relative improvement of 27.9%. Across different aggregation capacity levels, the relative improvement in PV accommodation ranged from 23% to 30%. These results indicate that the cluster-level value of flexibility depends strongly on the temporal match between flexible load patterns and PV generation. This study provides a scalable data-driven approach for characterizing building flexibility from historical operational data and offers new insights into the potential contribution of behavior-conditioned flexibility to renewable energy integration and building-cluster planning under specified scenarios.

papers.title: Estimation of aggregate flexibility regions for distributed flexible resources using limited information
papers.abstract: Distributed flexible resources (DFRs) can support power-system operation only if aggregators can report their flexibility regions as operating conditions change. Existing aggregation methods generally require detailed device-level states, which may be unavailable, as well as repeated online optimization. This paper proposes a limited-information physics-informed neural network (PINN) for estimating aggregate flexibility regions of DFRs. Its inputs are low-dimensional operating-condition descriptors, and its output is a feasibility-oriented representative polyhedral region conditioned on those descriptors. Physical feasibility and boundary tightness are embedded through support- and projection-based errors and differentiable active-hyperplane residuals, enabling training without precomputed ground-truth flexibility-region labels. The proposed pretraining, full-network training, and loss-weight scheduling scheme prioritizes physical feasibility while retaining boundary tightness. Case studies show that the estimated regions vary predictably with operating conditions and achieve a favorable balance between physical implementability and economic performance relative to alternative aggregation models. Across the operational tests, 96.25% of PINN dispatch trajectories had zero relative disaggregation error, and the maximum error was 4.72%. Dispatch costs remained comparable to those of the full-information inner approximation. Once trained, the estimator requires neither complete device-level information nor an online optimization solver. The proposed framework therefore lowers the deployment barrier for condition-dependent flexibility estimation in practical distributed-resource aggregation.

papers.title: Hydrogen integration for sustainable aviation propulsion: Evaluating recirculation efficiency in PEMFC systems
Shaping street rhythms: Spatial context and the temporal patterns of pedestrian activity
Solar PV as a buffer against energy security risks during geopolitical shocks: The case of Pakistan during the 2026 US–Iran war
papers.abstract: The 2026 US–Iran war disrupted global energy markets, particularly in economies dependent on imported fossil fuels. Pakistan, given its geographic proximity to the Strait of Hormuz and high reliance on imported oil and liquefied natural gas (LNG), was expected to face severe stress in its electricity sector. However, a comparison of key energy-sector indicators before and during the conflict, benchmarked against the 2022 Russia–Ukraine energy-price shock, suggests that the impact on Pakistan’s electricity sector was comparatively moderate relative to the 2022 energy-price shock, despite the severity of the external shock. The evidence indicates that the rapid expansion of distributed solar played an important role by reducing reliance on imported fuels and weakening the transmission of international fuel-price volatility into domestic electricity markets. These findings reveal that distributed renewable energy can serve not only as a pathway to decarbonization but also as a strategic instrument for strengthening energy security and resilience to geopolitical shocks in an increasingly volatile global energy landscape.

papers.title: From data-driven prediction to closed-loop intelligent bioconversion: A framework for artificial intelligence in organic solid waste treatment
papers.abstract: Organic solid waste (OSW) bioconversion has become a key strategy for converting biodegradable wastes into renewable energy, stabilized products, and recoverable nutrients. However, aerobic composting and anaerobic digestion are inherently dynamic and heterogeneous biological processes, where substrate variability, microbial succession, mass transfer, process instability, and greenhouse gas emissions complicate reliable operation. Current AI applications span methane-yield and compost-maturity prediction, soft sensing, process optimization, digital twins, and simulation-based control modeling. Nevertheless, most existing applications remain confined to prediction, optimization, or advisory functions and lack direct integration with on-site physical feedback. In this critical review, we systematically evaluate the current capability distribution and deployment maturity of AI-enabled OSW bioconversion, while distinguishing demonstrated implementations from a proposed pathway toward closed-loop operational intelligence. Among 85 direct AI/model implementation studies, 38 primarily addressed prediction, diagnosis, or soft sensing, 36 addressed optimization or advisory decision support, and 11 addressed simulation-based control modeling; none demonstrated supervisory/semi-autonomous or fully closed-loop operation on physical OSW-bioconversion equipment. Particular attention is paid to process-state representation, mechanism-informed interpretation, sensing infrastructure, predictive and optimization models, deployment maturity, and the persistent gap between model outputs and implementable control actions. We further propose a normative cyber–physical framework that integrates multi-source sensing, state reconstruction, world modeling, decision optimization, actuation, and feedback updating. This review reframes AI in OSW bioconversion as an engineering tool for carbon mitigation, nutrient recovery, and circular waste infrastructure rather than only a means of improving prediction accuracy.

papers.title: Synergistic decomplexation and electrosorption for sustainable copper recovery from photovoltaic wastewater: An integrated O3/SPC-MCDI process
Molecular Size Mediates Sunlight Effects on the Biodegradation of Aquatic Dissolved Organic Matter: Insights from the Reservoir Wetland and Incubation Experiment
papers.abstract: Abstract Dissolved organic matter (DOM) in aquatic ecosystems is crucial to climate, water quality, and water sanitation. However, little is known about how photochemical and biological processes interact to regulate the cycling of DOM in water environments. Here, we investigate the photobiochemical processing of different molecular weight (MW) fractions of aquatic DOM by incubating them with microbes in the dark and light/dark cycling environments via microcosm experiments. Light exposure has distinct effects on the medium (MMW; 1–20 kDa) and low (LMW; <1 kDa) MW fractions and can enrich photoautotrophic bacteria and taxa that could benefit the utilization of aromatic compounds. The decay of the MMW fraction displays the highest light sensitivity, with light increasing the net depletion of tannin- and condensed aromatic-like molecules and production of labile substrates (e.g., protein-like) from photoautotrophic bacteria. In contrast, the net decomposition of the LMW fraction is the least promoted by light exposure, as light induces the net production of complex aromatic molecules that are more persistent. Our findings provide new insights into the photobiochemical and molecular mechanisms underlying the ecological impacts of aquatic DOM and their relevance for wider processes.

papers.title: Selective Oxidation of Sulfoxide to Sulfone in Chloride/Peroxymonosulfate Systems: Reassessing a Diagnostic Probe for High-Valent Metal-Oxo Identification
papers.abstract: Abstract The selective oxidation of sulfoxides to sulfones, particularly using methyl phenyl sulfoxide (PMSO), has been widely adopted for over a decade as a diagnostic method for high-valent metal-oxo (HVMO) species in advanced oxidation processes (AOPs). Here, we demonstrate that this transformation proceeds efficiently via non-HVMO pathways in metal-free systems, challenging the probe’s specificity. Using the chloride/peroxymonosulfate (Cl−/PMS) system as a model, PMSO is converted to methyl phenyl sulfone (PMSO2) with high selectivity (83.5%−98.7%) across pH 3.5−11. Kinetic, isotopic, and computational analyses reveal a pH-dependent mechanistic switch for the high-yield transformation of PMSO to PMSO2. Under acidic conditions, Cl2/HOCl generated from the two-electron oxidation of Cl− by HSO5− through nucleophilic addition mediate oxygen-atom transfer from water via a chlorosulfonium cation intermediate, with Cl2 dominating PMSO selective oxidation (kapp = 1.58 × 106 M−1 s−1; 47.91 M−1 s−1 for HOCl). Under alkaline conditions, nucleophilic attack by SO52− formed via PMS hydrolysis becomes predominant (16.38 M−1 s−1). The reaction kinetics are linearly dependent on Cl− concentration, and similar selective oxidation is observed in other metal-free AOPs (e.g., base/PMS, HCO3−/PMS, and Cl−/peracetic acid). Our findings necessitate reassessing the sulfoxide probe’s specificity for HVMO identification in PMS-based systems containing chloride or alkalinity, and underscore the imperative for rigorous mechanistic validation in water treatment.

papers.title: Perspectives and Mitigation Methods for Underappreciated Amine Escape from CO2 Desorption
papers.abstract: Abstract Amine-based CO2 capture is increasingly limited by amine escape and aerosol emissions that drive solvent loss and secondary pollution. Research has focused on the absorber, leaving the desorption section─where intensive CO2 release, water-vapor entrainment, and rapid cooling coincide─overlooked as an escape source. Here, we combine molecular dynamics simulations with bench-scale experiments to resolve the mechanism and control of amine escape during CO2 desorption. Counter to absorber-side expectations, a CO2-rich atmosphere suppresses rather than promotes aerosol nucleation: elevated CO2 competitively disrupts the H2O–H2O hydrogen-bond network stabilizing water-centered nuclei, with stable clusters essentially absent at 75 vol % CO2. New aerosol formation is thus favored near the low-CO2 reboiler outlet, while cooling in the upper column grows preexisting aerosols. Measurements revealed an 82% decrease in the total amine concentration along the column, consistent with the descending rich solvent acting as an important amine sink, while preexisting aerosols continued to grow in the upper section. Guided by this mechanism, a combined mitigation strategy is proposed: a low-volatility solvent formulation lowered aerosol by 66% relative to MEA, increasing the rich-solvent CO2 loading offered a favorable trade-off, and upstream scrubbing–condensation captured residual species. Together, these measures reduced amine escape by over 99% (to <1.4 ppm) while increasing CO2 product purity. By reframing the desorber as a key emission unit, these results support strategies for reducing desorber-side amine and aerosol emissions.

papers.title: Halogenated Nucleosides: Highly Toxic Biogenic Disinfection Byproducts Prevalent in Drinking Water
papers.abstract: Abstract Five decades of research on disinfection byproducts (DBPs) reveals only the tip of the iceberg, with humus as their primary precursor. Here, we identified 15 halogenated nucleosides (HNSs) as new DBPs originating from biological materials in drinking water. A nationwide survey across China revealed that their individual detection frequencies ranged from 87% to 100%, with the maximum concentration reaching 141 ng/L. Two quantitative structure–activity relationship (QSAR) models were developed based on the cytotoxicity and genotoxicity data, with dipole moment (μ) and sum of the degree of valence (SVDe) as key cytotoxicity descriptors, and molar refractivity (R) together with number of H-bond donors (NHD) for genotoxicity. Integrated concentration and toxicity data revealed that halogenated (deoxy)cytidines and halogenated (deoxy)adenosines warrant priority regulatory consideration. The concentrations of HNSs were positively correlated with both pH (r = 0.6, P = 0.0005) and residual chlorine (r = 0.5, P = 0.0095) of drinking water samples, which may be related to local precipitation, temperature, and economic development. This study expands the scope of DBP research beyond humus-derived DBPs to biomolecule-derived ones.

papers.title: Unveiling Whole Water Neurotoxicity through Sensitive Electrophysiological Functional Profiling: Beyond Conventional Morphological Metrics
papers.abstract: Abstract Neuroactive contaminants typically coexist as complex mixtures in aquatic ecosystems, exerting deleterious effects through combined exposures. However, current assessment approaches based on morphological endpoints (e.g., neurite outgrowth) lack sufficient sensitivity to capture functional neurotoxicity of these mixtures. To address this gap, this study establishes in vitro functional neurotoxicity testing (iFNT), an ultrasensitive bioassay leveraging high-density microelectrode arrays to profile cortical network electrophysiology. Validated using reference toxicants, their mixture, and whole water samples, iFNT achieves 5- to 500-fold higher sensitivity than the neurite outgrowth assay. This heightened sensitivity enables clearer discrimination of functional phenotypes for both individual compounds at environmentally relevant concentrations (10–8 M) and whole water samples without preconcentration, providing a powerful tool for evaluating real-world neurotoxic risks. Alarmingly, conventional monitoring indicators exhibited a pronounced mismatch with iFNT profiles across wastewater treatment stages, demonstrating that seemingly acceptable routine readings masked the persistence of latent neurotoxicity. This study challenges morphology-based paradigms, revealing that accurate whole water risk assessment necessitates integrating functional biological endpoints into future monitoring frameworks.

papers.title: Bromine Monoxide Radical Likely Dominates Dimethylsulfide Oxidation before the Springtime Onset of Arctic Ice Melt
papers.abstract: Abstract To understand the atmospheric fate of dimethylsulfide (DMS) during the Arctic spring-to-summer transition, we measured volatile methylated sulfur (VMS) species, including DMS and DMS-derived oxidation products, dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO), and dimethylsulfone (DMSO2), in the Fram Strait during May and June of 2023. Elevated DMSO contributions to VMS accompany depleted O3, high surface albedo, and air temperatures < 0 °C in air masses influenced by snow-covered sea-ice regions, suggesting that BrO•-initiated oxidation dominated DMS loss prior to the onset of sea-ice melt. In GEOS-Chem simulations, BrO• is the dominant oxidant for DMS, but modeled BrO• concentrations from sea-salt debromination alone are too low to replicate observed O3, DMSO, and DMSO2, suggesting a missing source of reactive bromine from sunlit saline snow. BrO•-initiated oxidation reduces the DMS lifetime and oxidizes DMS through methanesulfinic acid (MSIA) more quickly in the gas phase and in higher yields compared to •OH-initiated oxidation alone. Once melt onset begins and snowpack-driven halogen activation shuts off, •OH oxidation likely dominates Arctic DMS oxidation. Our observations highlight the seasonal variability of halogen oxidation impacting sulfur species in the Arctic marine region, which are likely to change as the sea-ice extent decreases and the melt season in the Arctic lengthens.

papers.title: Atmospheric Removal of Nitrous Oxide: Approaches and Feasibility
papers.abstract: Abstract Nitrous oxide (N2O) is the third-largest contributor to anthropogenic greenhouse gas forcing and the dominant anthropogenic ozone-depleting emission. While mitigation can flatten emissions, there is no clear pathway to eliminate residual emissions from agriculture and other diffuse sources, a key challenge for climate stabilization. The potential role of atmospheric removal has not been holistically assessed, yet N2O’s high potency and long atmospheric lifetime indicate the potential for a durable climate benefit. This review synthesizes emerging approaches for atmospheric N2O removal, organized by reaction mechanism (thermal destruction and thermocatalysis, photolysis, gas-phase radical reactions, photocatalysis, and biological reduction) and deployment format (closed versus open system). Each is evaluated for technical efficacy, climate viability, environmental and social viability, and economic plausibility using lower-bound cost models. No approach yet satisfies all four: gas-phase radical reactors are precluded by their kinetics, thermocatalytic and photocatalytic reactors require ten- to hundred-fold performance gains, and open-system approaches have the lowest cost floors but face the greatest measurement and governance challenges. These results identify the performance thresholds and broader constraints that govern feasibility across pathways, providing a foundation for a research agenda and for assessing the role of N2O removal alongside emissions mitigation.

papers.title: Toward Rational Design of Low-Salt-Rejection Reverse Osmosis for Minimal and Zero Liquid Discharge
papers.abstract: Abstract Low-salt-rejection reverse osmosis (LSRRO) has emerged as a promising technology for concentrating high-salinity brines in minimal- and zero-liquid-discharge (MLD/ZLD) applications. However, rational LSRRO design remains hindered by uncertainties about how existing modeling frameworks should be interpreted and applied. In this Perspective, we critically examine the limitations of process modeling and module-scale analysis in LSRRO design. Conventional process models can yield misleading predictions for spiral-wound LSRRO modules because the stagewise concentration cutoff embedded in these models is based on the cumulative permeate composition rather than the local permeate conditions that govern water transport. Experimental results and local transport calculations show that the brine concentration in spiral-wound LSRRO stages is not constrained by a fixed thermodynamic concentration cutoff. Nevertheless, standalone process models remain inherently limited in assessing practical feasibility because they do not resolve kinetic constraints, such as declining water flux along the module. Module-scale analysis is therefore essential for linking local transport behavior to practical design metrics, including membrane area requirements, productivity, and achievable brine concentration. However, its predictive accuracy is constrained because transport parameters derived from conventional local transport models vary with salinity, which challenges their use as constants across the module. This Perspective therefore highlights the need for condition-dependent and experimentally validated local transport descriptions to enable rational LSRRO design for future MLD/ZLD applications.

papers.title: Dynamic Nature of Soil Iron Minerals: Recent Advances Using Iron Isotope Tracers and Mössbauer Spectroscopy
papers.abstract: Abstract Iron plays a central role in defining the redox and surface chemical environment of soils and sediments, by mediating the behavior of nutrients, pollutants, and carbon compounds. However, the mechanisms that drive dynamic changes in Fe speciation and mineral composition can be difficult to trace. Over three decades, technical advances in spectroscopy and theoretical modeling techniques have revealed detailed mechanisms of Fe mineral recrystallization and transformation. Here, we provide a perspective on the application of iron isotopic tracers to the development of atomic-scale mechanistic understanding of Fe mineral dynamics. We review key milestones in the advancement of 57Fe tracers coupled with 57Fe Mössbauer spectroscopy and draw links between the understanding of Fe dynamics with 57Fe tracers and biogeochemical cycling of other elements in soils and sediments. Iron isotopes are increasingly used in Fe biogeochemistry research, and our analysis will point out unique opportunities offered by 57Fe tracers to unravel important questions in soil biogeochemistry today.

papers.title: Sex-Specific Associations of Gestational OPE Exposure with Offspring Digit Ratio: A Birth Cohort Study
papers.abstract: Abstract The effect of prenatal organophosphate esters (OPEs) exposure on offspring reproductive development and the potential role of the placenta remain unclear. We investigated the associations of prenatal OPE exposure with the second-to-fourth digit ratio (2D:4D) and the mediating role of placental DNA methylation (DNAm) levels of PPAR pathway genes. Maternal urine OPE metabolites at 12–16 gestational weeks were measured. Placental DNAm levels at birth and children’s 2D:4D at ages 4 and 6 years were assessed. Multiple linear regression, BKMR, and causal mediation analyses were applied. We observed associations between prenatal exposure to BBOEP, BEHP, DBP, and DPP and increased 2D:4D in boys, whereas DBP and DCP were associated with decreased 2D:4D in girls. BKMR identified alkyl-OPEs, particularly BBOEP, as the primary contributors in boys. Moreover, hypermethylation of RXRA, ACAA1, and ACADM was associated with decreased 2D:4D in all populations. In girls, the associations among higher OPE exposure, increased ACAA1 methylation, and lower 2D:4D suggested a potential mediation pathway, while the mediation effects were not statistically significant. These findings suggest sex-specific associations between prenatal OPE exposure and 2D:4D. The potential role of placental PPAR-related DNAm in these associations warrants further investigation.

papers.title: Fluid–structure interaction analysis of an asymmetric thin downstream bluff body for a tandem bladeless wind turbine
papers.abstract: The present study investigates a fixed thin downstream bluff body (TDB) as a passive flow-control strategy for enhancing the post-onset oscillatory response and energy-harvesting performance of a bladeless wind turbine operating through flow-induced vibration (FIV). The proposed asymmetric TDB reorganizes the wake interaction between the oscillating primary cylinder and the fixed downstream body, thereby strengthening aerodynamic excitation and fluid–structure energy transfer over the investigated operating range. The experiments examined fifteen TDB geometries grouped according to cross-sectional shape, together with four aspect-ratio values and multiple spacing ratios. The effects of these parameters were evaluated through vibration response, power generation, flow visualization, particle image velocimetry (PIV), proper orthogonal decomposition (POD), pressure recovery, Reynolds shear stress, velocity deficit, turbulent kinetic energy, and enstrophy analyses. The results demonstrate that the introduction of a properly designed TDB fundamentally reorganizes the wake dynamics. An optimum spacing range of 0.3 ≤ Z / D ≤ 0.4 was identified, while AR = 0.17 was the best-performing aspect ratio within the investigated range, resulting in voltage and power enhancements of approximately 56% and 81%, respectively, compared with the baseline configuration without a TDB. Among all investigated geometries, the asymmetric TDB exhibited the best overall performance within the tested configurations, producing approximately 7.5% higher voltage and 15.5% higher power than the primary rectangular TDB, together with a stronger sustained post-onset oscillatory response. Flow-field analyses revealed enhanced wake confinement, increased circulation and vorticity, stronger coherent vortex interaction, delayed pressure recovery, and greater concentration of energy within low-order POD modes. Enstrophy analysis further showed reduced mean enstrophy and transport accompanied by increased fluctuating enstrophy, indicating a transition toward a more coherent and energetically efficient wake. These findings demonstrate that asymmetric downstream bluff-body design provides an effective approach for enhancing fluid–structure energy transfer and improving the viability of bladeless wind energy harvesting technologies.

papers.title: Decarbonizing industrial process heat: energy, economic, and environmental analysis of a high-temperature solar-assisted heat pump using low GWP refrigerants
papers.abstract: Decarbonizing high-temperature industrial processes is essential to achieve global climate neutrality by 2050. This study evaluates the technical, energy, economic, and environmental performance of solar-assisted heat pumps (SAHPs) for industrial laundry applications, including hot water production at 80 °C and pressurized water (steam economizer) at 140 °C. A validated simulation framework was developed to analyze up to 130 combinations of system configurations and refrigerants. Eight configurations were assessed, comparing single-stage (SS) and two-stage cascade (TSC) cycles using ambient air or solar collectors as heat sources. Low-global warming potential (GWP) refrigerants, including hydrofluoroolefins (HFOs) such as R1233zd(E) and R1336mzz(Z), and hydrocarbons such as R600 and R601a, were considered. For hot water production, solar-assisted systems provide more stable performance than air-source configurations, with photovoltaic-thermal heat pumps (PV/T HP, SS) achieving the highest COP values (3–5), depending on refrigerant and climate. For steam generation, only PV/T HP TSC configurations are technically feasible, with COP values of 1.6–2.0. Economic analysis, compared with conventional gas boilers, systems using R1233zd(E) and R600 achieve the highest profitability, with payback periods of 3.5–7 years over a 20-year lifetime. The best configurations reduce CO 2 emissions by up to 50 %. Overall, optimal system design requires balancing energy efficiency and investment costs, with specific refrigerant–cycle combinations outperforming fossil-fuel technologies across different climates.

papers.title: Liquid-Recirculation-Assisted Anion exchange membrane ammonia Electrolysis: Simultaneous Closed-Loop NH3 recovery and improved H2 purity
papers.abstract: Ammonia (NH 3 ) as a hydrogen carrier is limited by the energy-intensive reconversion to high-purity hydrogen at the point of use. Anion exchange membrane (AEM) ammonia electrolysis offers a low-voltage, low-temperature alternative, but unreacted ammonia is emitted at the anode and crosses over to the cathode, degrading both efficiency and hydrogen purity. Here, two alternative recovery units—a pressurized tank and a wet scrubber—were independently integrated with an AEM electrolysis cell. With the pressurized tank, increasing the anode-side pressure from 1 to 10 bar reduced the outlet NH 3 concentration from 3.64 to 0.65 vol% (82.1 %) but increased the cell-electrical specific energy consumption (SEC) from 55.78 to 69.62 k ⁢ W ⁢ h ⁡ / k ⁢ g H 2 (24.8 %). At the matched 240 mA/cm 2 condition, the atmospheric-pressure wet scrubber reduced outlet NH 3 to approximately 0.475 vol% (87.0 %) with an SEC of 55.4 k ⁢ W ⁢ h ⁡ / k ⁢ g H 2 and maintained the outlet concentration at or below 0.50 vol% across the tested current range. The NH 3 -loaded solution was reused once as the anolyte with a 3.7 % increase in SEC at the matched current density, supporting proof-of-concept closed-loop reuse. A pH-dependent emission model indicated that NH 3 re-volatilization is strongly suppressed when the scrubbing-medium pH is around 6. Furthermore, a pressure-sensitivity analysis indicated that operation without a trans -membrane pressure differential avoids an additional pressure-driven NH 3 crossover, while the measured dry-gas composition corresponded to a bulk H 2 purity of 98.1–98.5 %. These results establish the wet scrubber as the simpler and more energy-efficient route for integrating NH 3 emission control, recirculation, and cathodic H 2 -purity improvement in modular or on-site ammonia-to-hydrogen systems.

papers.title: Performance and transient behavior of a hydrogel flat-plate/finned dual-source heat pump under multi-mode heating: An experimental study
papers.abstract: Conventional solar-air dual-source heat pumps employ separate evaporators, complicating system coordination. This paper presents a direct-expansion heat pump with an integrally formed flat-plate/finned dual-source (FFDS) heat exchanger and a thermochromic hydrogel coating—transparent in winter for solar absorption and opaque in summer for solar rejection. Focusing on winter heating, multi-mode experiments (DHW-only, combined intermittent/continuous space heating) were conducted under various weather conditions. Through high-resolution transient measurements, the study innovatively reveals the generation and evolution mechanisms of sawtooth oscillations in temperatures and pressures under real-time EEV dynamic regulation, including phase shift relationships and the attenuation of superheat oscillation amplitude with increasing condensing pressure—a mechanistic explanation rarely addressed in the literature. Comparative experiments quantify the asymmetric sensitivity of evaporator- and condenser-side parameters to environmental disturbances: compared with sunny conditions, overcast conditions reduce evaporating temperature and pressure by 10.42 °C and 0.136 MPa, raise the pressure ratio from 3.71 to 5.13, and lower the average COP from 4.77 to 3.67, while the condenser side varies modestly. Performance evaluation demonstrates the system’s adaptability to different weather scenarios and user demands: even under nighttime continuous heating with no solar energy input, the system maintains stable operation with an average COP of 3.23. These findings deepen the understanding of transient dynamics and multi-mode performance responses of integrated dual-source heat pumps under EEV dynamic regulation, and provide empirical data and insights for the development of stable and reliable control strategies and integrated system designs.

papers.title: Reducing energy consumption in underwater vehicle hovering operations using a variable structure controller
papers.abstract: Autonomous underwater vehicles and sensor platforms play a crucial role in the long-term monitoring of marine environments; however, their operational endurance is limited by energy constraints. Effective energy management is therefore essential, particularly with regard to actuation mechanisms, which are among the primary consumers of onboard energy. Consequently, control laws that reduce energy consumption while maintaining performance are of significant importance, as they contribute to more efficient energy utilization. The main contribution of this paper is the proposal of a novel depth control law that exploits the passive dynamics of buoyancy-controlled vehicles to save energy during hovering tasks. The proposed control strategy expends energy only in two situations: 1) to counteract conditions in which the system’s natural dynamics is detrimental to control objectives, and 2) to drive the system to rest when it is near the target depth. Both simulation and experimental results show that this approach reduces energy consumption compared to PID-based controllers and to recently reported energy-efficient strategies. Against the latter, the proposed method achieves energy savings of up to 13% while simultaneously reducing the average depth control error by 50%.

papers.title: The social in the scientific discussion on wildfire risk management in Chile
A dynamic and viewing-direction-aware 3D visuospatial analysis framework for indoor environments based on embodied 3D isovist
papers.abstract: Quantitative analysis of dynamic visuospatial experience is increasingly important as behavioural experiments provide fine-grained positional and viewing records. Isovist analysis is a well-established method for visuospatial analysis of architectural spaces, and Embodied 3D Isovist represents one extension of this approach to three-dimensional analysis. However, methods for applying Embodied 3D Isovist to path analysis remain underdeveloped, particularly in representing continuous movement and direction-dependent visual experience. The present study proposes a framework that directly operates on time-series position and viewing direction data. A case study compared grid-like and continuous conditions, limited- and unlimited-FOV conditions, and opposing movement directions along the same path. The results showed that grid-like analysis generally approximated continuous analysis, whereas FOV limitation produced clear direction-dependent differences, particularly in open spaces. The case study also identified a limitation in the original definition of the properties and indicated a potential relationship between dynamic visibility transitions and spatial cognition. The proposed framework extends Embodied 3D Isovist towards analysing dynamic visuospatial experience during movement.

papers.title: Is Australia part of the Pacific? Re-imagining Australia’s Pacific identities and relationships for an ‘Island’ future
papers.abstract: Since the beginning of colonisation, Australian authorities have had a persistent desire to control the Pacific. While Australia is a long-standing key partner for Pacific Island states, there is an underlying discontent with the often domineering and exploitive nature of Australia in the region. Seeking to understand why this approach to diplomacy in the Pacific has been so hard to change for Australia, I suggest it is because ideas of Australia as a powerful regional administrator have become so central to its collective identity that they have been fused into the diplomatic, strategic, and political culture in Canberra. Using lenses of ontological security, narratives, and articulation theory, I examine how this identity has evolved through three vignettes: the initial portrayal of Australia as a Western, continental, colonial controller; the discursive construction of Australian primacy in relation to the Pacific and its peoples; and an examination of recent diplomatic interactions between Australia and Pacific partners. Drawing on Teaiwa’s vision of articulation theory, I suggest these ideas have become akin to a bodily part of Australia’s core identity concerns—and it will generally act to preserve its sense of this self. However, while difficult, change is possible. In a forward-looking coda, I propose that future change is funnelled towards ‘islanding’ Australia. A fundamental reorientation of identity, culture, and practice that embraces Australia’s vulnerability and possibility could open the space for a more productive future with Pacific partners and a more comfortable relationship with Australia’s own core identity.

papers.title: IceCube just won a Nobel prize. Protect astroparticle physics projects with the same potential
Briefing Chat: An invisible tattoo that appears under UV light – and then disappears
History’s long-secret codes are being cracked by amateurs using AI
A platform for change? Core component innovations, complementor adaptation, and multihoming in platform‐based ecosystems
papers.abstract: Abstract Research Summary Digital platforms coordinate complementor innovations through interfaces into their core components. However, when interfaces themselves evolve alongside core component innovations, complementors may exhibit behaviors that are not entirely predictable. Using granular data from Apple's five major iOS releases, we abductively examine App developers’ responses following Apple's core component innovations. We document that, in post‐release periods, complementors simultaneously increase co‐innovation on iOS while being more likely to multihome by diversifying to the competing platform. These choices are further explained by whether architectural changes reflect cross‐platform standardization or platform‐specific differentiation. Standardization spurs both complementor co‐innovation and multihoming, while differentiation reduces diversification tendencies. The patterns that we document reveal an important tension: governing through interfaces enables platforms’ scalability but constrains their ability to control complementors as platforms evolve. Managerial Summary Digital platforms like Apple coordinate large scale innovation through standardized interfaces, but those interfaces must evolve as platforms compete, and the direction of that evolution has consequences managers should attend to. Analyzing Apple's five major iOS releases, we find that architectural changes are associated with increased co‐innovation but also a higher likelihood that developers diversify to a competing platform. This pattern is particularly pronounced when updates bring iOS closer to Android, suggesting that architectural convergence may lower the barriers to cross‐platform expansion for developers. Importantly, this behavior is strongest among highest‐value developers. Platform managers should therefore treat architectural evolution not merely as a technical decision, but as a strategic one with direct implications for ecosystem loyalty, competitive differentiation, and the retention of valuable ecosystem partners.

papers.title: Do Investors Follow Their Heart? The Role of Value Congruence in Guiding Investors' Decisions
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Retail investors evaluating impact‐oriented opportunities must weigh economic, social, and environmental performance simultaneously, yet it remains unclear why they prioritize these dimensions so differently. We propose that personal values act as a weighting mechanism in multiattribute investment decisions. In a discrete choice experiment with 547 US retail investors, financial performance and risk dominate on average, but altruistic, biospheric, and egoistic values are each associated with greater weight on the corresponding performance dimension; attribute salience also varies across investment domains. Personal values thus help explain preference heterogeneity that demographic characteristics and cognitive biases alone leave unaccounted for.

papers.title: Bank Risk-Taking and Deposits Around Going Concern Opinions
papers.abstract: We investigate bank risk-taking and deposit flows around first-time going concern opinions (GCOs). Although GCOs may strengthen market monitoring, they are also often accused of destabilizing banks by triggering depositor runs. Our evidence is difficult to reconcile with that concern. Uninsured deposits begin to decrease several quarters before the GCO, but insured deposits increase over the same period, leaving total deposits broadly stable around the opinion. This pattern suggests that more sophisticated depositors respond to timelier information than the annual audit report and shift from uninsured to insured funding before the GCO becomes public, whereas insured retail depositors do not exhibit large-scale withdrawals around the GCO. We also document that bank risk measures increase in the quarters leading up to the GCO and then stabilize and subsequently decrease after the opinion. In addition, severe enforcement actions become more likely in the post-GCO period. Taken together, these patterns are consistent with an indirect supervisory channel that may help interpret the post-GCO change in bank risk-taking. Overall, our findings suggest that concerns about GCOs precipitating depositor runs may be overstated and that systematic auditor forbearance is not clearly justified on financial-stability grounds.

papers.title: Institutional Amnesia and the Loss of “The Why Rationale” in Central Government Agencies
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Data from 115 interviews conducted with officials in the Westminster systems of Australia, New Zealand, and the United Kingdom is used to substantiate a corrosive relationship between institutional amnesia and the ability of public servants to make sense of their organizational context. A process in which public servants question why the policies, procedures, and organizational frameworks that surround them is proposed as one medium through which this relationship operates. Four problematic effects produced by this relationship and process are subsequently analyzed: (1) public servants following but not understanding procedures, (2) inexplicable organizational aspects getting abandoned, (3) the layering of new organizational features on top of old ones, creating complexity, and (4) public service inefficiencies and associated public servant frustration. The article concludes with the implications of this important relationship for public administration scholars and practitioners.

papers.title: Crime and EITC Refunds
How CBO Uses Research to Inform Congressional Budget Analysis
IRS Staff Cuts and Individual Taxpayer Implications of Geographic Proximity to State Tax Agencies
Voltage-Dependent Metabolic Shifts Regulate the Fouling Behavior of the Anaerobic-Anodic Membrane
papers.abstract: Abstract Fouling remains the key barrier to durable membrane operation, against which electrochemical processes offer a promising fouling control strategy. However, the performance of an anodic membrane under anaerobic conditions exhibits significant instability, the mechanism of which remains unclear and represents a critical knowledge gap. This study systematically investigated the response of membrane fouling evolution to gradient electric fields within anodic membranes. A distinct threshold behavior of electric field strength on membrane fouling was observed, with a system-dependent threshold occurring between 0.7 and 1.0 V. Following an initial fouling layer, subthreshold fields (≤0.7 V) exacerbated fouling accumulation, whereas supra-threshold fields (≥1.0 V) slowed down membrane fouling development. Comprehensive analysis revealed that surpassing critical field strength enhanced anodic electron-accepting capacity, likely facilitating microbial extracellular electron release and alleviating reductive pressure. This triggered a nonlinear, threshold-dependent metabolic switch from biosynthesis-dominated to catabolism-enhanced pathways, coupled with quorum quenching that inhibited biofilm maturation. These synergistic transitions underpinned the fouling reversal. This work advances the understanding of anaerobic-anodic membrane fouling from an empirical observation into a threshold-governed electrochemical–microbial switching process, thereby providing the scientific foundation for harnessing this interplay to achieve durable and efficient operation in anaerobic wastewater treatment and resource recovery systems.

papers.title: Evaluating Community-Level Effects of 6PPD-Quinone in a Natural Boreal Lake Ecosystem
papers.abstract: Abstract 6PPD-quinone (6PPD-Q), a transformation product of the tire rubber antioxidant 6PPD, is an emerging contaminant known for its acute toxicity to certain salmonids. However, its potential impacts on aquatic communities remain poorly understood. To address this knowledge gap, 6PPD-Q-spiked limnocorrals were deployed in a natural boreal lake, and water chemistry, phytoplankton, zooplankton, and benthic invertebrate communities were assessed over 28 days following a single pulse exposure (0–100 μg/L) simulating stormwater runoff. Waterborne 6PPD-Q concentrations declined by 80–99% by the end of the study, with no detectable effects on water chemistry or aquatic communities. Temporal changes in chlorophyll-a concentrations and zooplankton abundance were attributed to seasonal dynamics rather than 6PPD-Q exposure, and benthic invertebrate community composition remained unchanged. Concurrently, wild-spawned fathead minnow (Pimephales promelas) embryos were exposed to 6PPD-Q-spiked water collected from the limnocorrals. Larval survival declined significantly at 100 μg/L, with altered hatch timing and sublethal effects including reduced growth, changes in eye, yolk sac, and pericardial areas, and altered energy allocation. These effects occurred at 10.6–22.4 μg/L and above, concentrations that exceed those so far reported in surface waters and stormwater by approximately an order of magnitude. Collectively, this study provides the first field-scale assessment of 6PPD-Q effects on aquatic communities and early life-stage fish. Environmental Significance. This study provides the first field-scale assessment of 6PPD-Q impacts on freshwater communities. While broad aquatic communities appeared resilient to short-term exposure scenarios, early life stages of fish responded at concentrations above those currently reported in the environment, identifying developmental end points that warrant attention when assessing the risks of tire-derived contaminants in freshwater ecosystems.

papers.title: Economic Trade and Atmospheric Transport in Shaping China’s Nitrogen Deposition Patterns
papers.abstract: Abstract Atmospheric nitrogen deposition in China is driven not only by local emissions but also by global economic demand and transboundary atmospheric transport. Unraveling these dual influences is critical for effective environmental governance. Here, we integrate an economic-emission analysis with a high-resolution atmospheric chemical transport model to quantify, for the first time, the distinct roles of domestic consumption, international trade, and atmospheric transport in shaping China’s nitrogen deposition patterns. We find that domestic consumption is the dominant contributor, responsible for 67.6% of the total deposition, involving a substantial interprovincial transfer of emissions from affluent coastal provinces to less developed inland regions. International trade attributes 7.8% of China’s deposition to foreign consumption, primarily driven by demand from the USA and Western Europe. In contrast, trans-national atmospheric transport directly accounts for 12.8%, with a disproportionately high impact on ecologically sensitive western China. Natural sources contribute the remaining 11.8%. Our results reveal a complex web of drivers extending beyond China’s borders. Mitigating nitrogen deposition, therefore, requires moving beyond local emission controls to embrace consumption-based accountability and enhanced international cooperation on both trade and atmospheric pollution to protect vulnerable ecosystems.

papers.title: Deep reinforcement learning-based UAV navigation in 3D urban boundary layers

Exploring hydrogen production from plastic waste for urban transportation in Hong Kong and its environmental impact mitigation: integrating dynamic material flow analysis and life cycle assessment
papers.abstract: Plastic waste to hydrogen technology offers a sustainable clean energy pathway while reducing landfill and incineration burdens. However, its feasibility as a feedstock for urban mobility decarbonization at the city scale remains largely unexplored. Hong Kong, as a densely populated metropolitan region facing substantial plastic waste challenges, presents an ideal case study to assess the viability of plastic-derived hydrogen for transportation applications. This study developed an innovative waste-to-wheel framework to assess the mitigation of environmental impacts on Hong Kong's urban mobility through plastic waste-to-hydrogen technology. Dynamic material flow analysis was used to quantify historical and future plastic waste generation, while life cycle assessment (LCA) was adopted to assess the environmental impacts associated with urban transportation in Hong Kong. The results indicated that accumulated plastic waste in Hong Kong is projected to reach 27.6 million tonnes (Mt) between 2026 and 2050, with polypropylene and polyethylene comprising 58.7% of the total, providing substantial feedstock for hydrogen production. Hydrogen demand in the transportation sector is estimated at 880.1 thousand tonnes of coal equivalent (tce) by 2050 under the hydrogen scenario. LCA results revealed that waste-based hydrogen production achieves the lowest global warming potential at −1.36 kg carbon dioxide equivalent (CO 2 -eq) per kg hydrogen, reducing transportation sector emissions to 193 thousand tonnes CO 2 -eq by 2050, which is 78.2% lower than the business-as-usual scenario. Plastic-derived hydrogen could supply 101.7% (97.5%-105.4%) of cumulative transportation hydrogen demand during 2026-2050. These findings validate plastic waste as a sustainable transportation fuel, guiding Hong Kong's hydrogen and circular economy planning.

papers.title: Soil CH4 and CO2 emissions mediated by water and afforestation in Horqin Sandy Land
papers.abstract: Ecological restoration in arid and semi-arid regions plays a vital role in maintaining regional carbon balance under global change. Although water management and vegetation composition regulate soil carbon cycling, their combined effects on greenhouse gas source/sink dynamics in sandy ecosystems and the underlying microbial mechanisms remain unclear. This study examined sand dunes (Sd) and 35-year-old typical afforestation types including Caragana microphylla Lam. (Cm), Populus simonii Carr. (Ps), Pinus sylvestris var . mongolica Litv. (Pm), and mixed forests of Ps + Pm and Pm + Cm in the Horqin Sandy Land. Through a controlled incubation experiment at 30% and 60% water holding capacity (WHC), we systematically analyzed the effects of afforestation and water management on soil methane (CH 4 ) and carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) emissions. Linear regression analyses of functional gene abundances and environmental factors further revealed microbial mechanisms. All afforested soils acted as CH 4 sinks, Ps, Pm, Ps + Pm, and Pm + Cm showed the strongest CH 4 uptake, correlated with higher pmoA gene abundance and lower mcrA / pmoA . 30% WHC enhanced CH 4 oxidation by improving soil aeration, whereas CO 2 emissions increased significantly under elevated water content. Cm showed the highest CO 2 emissions, whereas mixed forests (Ps + Pm and Pm + Cm) maintained high CH 4 uptake even under high CO 2 emissions. These findings indicate that water management and afforestation legacy interactively shape carbon cycling pathways in sandy ecosystems. Mixed forests optimize microbial community function, balancing carbon cycling efficiency with greenhouse gas mitigation across water regimes, providing a scientific basis for carbon management in ecological restoration of the Horqin Sandy Land and comparable semi-arid regions.

papers.title: River network position and cascade dam effects on macroinvertebrate communities: implications for hierarchical river conservation
papers.abstract: The interplay between the natural gradient of river networks and the fragmentation effects of cascade dams in shaping macroinvertebrate diversity and community assembly remains unclear. This study focused on the middle Jialing River in the upper Yangtze basin, a highly developed area. We quantified taxonomic and functional α- and β-diversity across the river network. Generalized additive models revealed a clear spatial gradient. Dam impacts amplified in distal secondary tributaries and attenuated in proximal mainstem reaches. The strongest dam-related effects occurred in secondary tributaries, where high local damming intensity co-occurred with low background connectivity. Random forests and structural equation modeling showed that dam distance consistently affected diversity. This effect was strong on taxonomic β-diversity in secondary tributaries, with a direct path coefficient of 0.53. Functional β-diversity was highly responsive to dam distance and exhibited a pronounced nestedness pattern in secondary tributaries. Variation partitioning revealed that community assembly mechanisms shifted along the river network. Dispersal limitation dominated at the basin scale. Environmental filtering drove the mainstream and primary tributaries. Secondary tributaries were jointly driven by dam distance, environmental filtering, and spatial constraints. These findings extend the network position hypothesis to regulated rivers by re-parameterizing its dispersal-directionality assumption. We recommend designating secondary tributaries as priority conservation areas, primary tributaries as connectivity management zones, implementing multi-site protection along the mainstream, and incorporating functional β-diversity into routine monitoring as a sensitive indicator for ecological assessment. This study provides new insights into the coupled effects of cascade dams and natural river network structure, offering a scientific basis for hierarchical river management in the upper Yangtze River.

papers.title: Porous geopolymer from cyanobacterial sludge and coal fly ash as shape-stabilizing matrix for thermal energy storage using phase change paraffin
papers.abstract: The consumption of fossil fuels drives both the energy crisis and greenhouse gas emissions, while the accumulation of solid wastes such as coal fly ash (CFA) and cyanobacterial sludge (CS) exerts considerable ecological pressure. This study explores the utilization of CS and CFA as raw materials, employing egg white powder as a surfactant and hydrogen peroxide as a blowing agent to fabricate a highly porous geopolymer (CCG). The organic fibers in CS act as pore templates and reinforcing agents, while their partial degradation in the alkaline environment participates in the gelation process. The optimal formulation comprises a 9 mol/L sodium hydroxide solution, 3 wt% egg white powder, 7 wt% hydrogen peroxide, a CS:CFA mass ratio of 2:8, and a sodium silicate to sodium hydroxide solution ratio of 2.5:1. Following synthesis, CCG underwent vacuum impregnation with phase change paraffin (PCP). The capillary forces within the porous matrix effectively encapsulate the molten PCP, yielding a shape-stabilized phase change composite (CCGP). Relative to CCG the CCGP exhibits a thermal conductivity enhancement of 0.081–0.168 W/(m·K). The solidification and melting enthalpies of the CCGP were 67.58 J/g and 69.23 J/g, respectively, with remarkable thermal stability at temperatures up to 600 °C. This study not only achieves high-value utilization of CS and CFA, but also provides new insights into protein-assisted foaming and fiber pore formation in geopolymer systems, offering guidance for the design of shape-stabilized phase change composites with optimized encapsulation efficiency and long-term thermal stability.

papers.title: The role of immigrant caregivers in improving the welfare of elders and reducing public health costs
papers.abstract: Abstract This paper examines the impact of paid migrant home care on elderly health outcomes in Italy. The results show that an increase in migrants’ presence reduces both the frequency and duration of hospitalisations. Specifically, a 1 percentage-point increase in the migrant-to-elderly ratio leads to a decline in long-term and rehabilitation inpatient (LRI) admissions of 118 cases per 100,000 elders, with no measurable effect on acute inpatient stays. There is also a reduction in the average length of stay of 0.141 days, rising to 0.956 days for LRI cases. These effects are driven by diagnoses related to traumatic injuries, musculoskeletal, and genitourinary conditions — areas closely linked to home mobility and care management. Back-of-the-envelope calculations suggest that the average annual increase of 1.3 percentage points in the migrant-to-elderly ratio observed during the study period corresponds to an 8% reduction in elderly LRI hospitalisation costs, equivalent to 252.3 million euros.

papers.title: Carbon taxes crowd out low-carbon choices: Evidence from a consumer experiment
papers.abstract: We examine the impact of a carbon tax on consumer choices via a large-scale online randomized controlled trial. Higher taxes generally reduce the demand for high-carbon goods. Compared to an import tax, a carbon tax reduces demand when the tax is zero (i.e., announced but not levied) but leads to relatively higher demand for high-carbon goods when a positive tax is introduced. This difference in demand responses, despite identical prices, is concentrated among climate-concerned consumers. Our findings suggest that carbon taxes can crowd out the effect of climate concerns on consumer choices, with important implications for policy.
