papers.title: Combining management control practices for organizational learning: A situational strength perspective
papers.abstract: Organizational learning (OL) is a critical organizational capability. Yet designing management control (MC) that effectively supports OL is challenging, as learning outcomes are often intangible and unfold over extended time horizons. Employing situational strength theory, we examine combinations of MC practices that affect OL contingent on environmental uncertainty. Drawing on a survey of 210 senior business unit controllers, we use fuzzy-set Qualitative Comparative Analysis (fsQCA) to identify multiple combinations of MC practices that achieve high OL in different uncertainty contexts. In a subsequent step, we examine whether the situational strength of certain combinations of MC practices is associated with OL. Results show that in a low-uncertainty environment, the combined use of diverse performance measures and social controls, as well as performance pay and a mechanistic administrative structure, have a synergetic effect on OL. In a high-uncertainty context, the combined use of measure diversity and deliberate formal strategic planning is beneficial for achieving OL. Our results suggest that the effectiveness of MC practices for OL depends on aligning MC practices with the internal as well as the external context.

papers.title: Business Group Affiliation and Environmental Innovation: The Moderating Role of Board Diversity
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines the relationship between business group (BG) affiliation and corporate environmental innovation, with a particular focus on the moderating role of board diversity. Drawing on resource dependence theory (RDT) and agency theory, we argue that although BGs provide affiliated firms with strategic resources, their governance structures may constrain the deployment of these resources for environmental innovation. Using 38,395 firm‐year observations from Chinese A‐share listed firms between 2009 and 2023, we find that BG affiliation is negatively associated with environmental innovation, suggesting that governance constraints may outweigh the resource advantages associated with BGs. We further find that board diversity significantly weakens this negative relationship, consistent with its proposed role in strengthening governance and facilitating strategic resource deployment. These findings advance understanding of the role of organisational structures and internal governance in corporate environmental innovation, offering practical insights for managers and policymakers seeking to promote environmental innovation in emerging economies.

papers.title: Does Green Supply Chain Partnership Governance Pay Off? An Investigation of the Impact on Corporate Financial Performance
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines whether governance of green supply chain partnerships (GSCPs) using environmental criteria for supplier selection and termination is positively associated with corporate financial performance of focal firms. Drawing on the social capital theory, this study highlights the dichotomous nature of social capital in GSCPs, showing whether firms can gain corporate reputation and then financial benefits while proactively managing GSCPs. This study analysed the panel data of 994 firm‐year observations from UK FTSE All‐Share firms obtained from the Thomson Reuters Eikon's ESG (Environmental, Social, and Governance) database. Analysis result shows that although there is evidence that GSCP governance is positively related to corporate reputation, no evidence shows that corporate reputation will be a mediator between GSCP governance and corporate finance performance. Instead, GSCP governance variables have shown positive direct relationship with financial performance. Findings provide practical guidance for managers seeking to strengthen financial performance through GSCP governance approaches.

papers.title: Adaptive vs. Commitment Governance in Circular Value Chains: Contracting and Pricing Under Uncertainty in Wind Turbine Blade End‐of‐Life Management
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Circular business models rely on interfirm recovery relationships in which effort is difficult to monitor and operating conditions evolve over time. Using wind turbine blade end‐of‐life management, we develop a finite‐horizon dynamic principal–agent model of a circular manufacturer, a recycler and downstream competition with a virgin‐material manufacturer. We compare ex‐ante commitment to a time‐varying incentive sequence with adaptive governance, under which the performance‐based incentive can respond to observed recovery conditions and circular‐material availability before effort is chosen. Because the adaptive policy set contains the committed policy set, adaptive governance yields weakly greater gross circular‐manufacturer value. Numerically, its advantage comes from better incentive targeting, not higher average incentive intensity. Manufacturer value and certified recovery increase despite slightly lower average incentives and effort. In the numerical analysis, the value of adaptation rises with observable operating‐state heterogeneity, but adaptation is attractive in net terms only when these gains exceed monitoring, verification, information‐processing and contractual‐adjustment costs.

papers.title: ESG Reliability Post‐Paris Agreement: Evidence From S&P 500 Firms
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT This research investigates whether the 2015 Paris Agreement has changed environmental, social, and governance (ESG) performance scores. We compiled a balanced panel of 392 S&P 500 companies from 2010 to 2025 using Refinitiv data. The final dataset contained 6272 observations on the 10 ESG scores at the most detailed level possible. Based on stakeholder theory, interrupted time series analysis (ITSA) was applied to determine whether the intercorrelations among the ESG variables decreased post‐Paris. Moreover, in accordance with legitimacy theory, the reported ESG measures were examined using Benford's law. It was found that the uniformity of the last digits improved over time. Three robustness checks were carried out: (a) an out‐of‐sample ITSA with 293 STOXX‐listed companies, (b) a quadratic ITSA, and (c) placebo tests with different breakpoints. The evidence indicates (1) the downward trend became stronger in the period after the Paris Agreement and (2) the differentiation among ESG scores accelerated in a nonlinear manner. We conclude the reliability of ESG performance scores has increased over time, providing a more trustworthy foundation for stakeholders' decision‐making.

papers.title: Digitalisation and Carbon Efficiency: Does the Digital Economy Enable Sustainable Production Systems?
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT This paper examines the effect of digitalisation on carbon intensity in 44 countries from 2000 to 2024 using a principal component index that combines internet use, mobile connections and landline telephone ownership. The standard model uses a static Common Correlated Effects Mean Group (CCEMG) regression. Other specifications, such as CS‐ARDL(1,0), interaction, quadratic, interactive fixed‐effects CCEMG threshold and dynamic subgroup estimators, allow for cross‐sectional dependence, adjustment dynamics and heterogeneity. The results show no statistically significant average, short‐run or long‐run effect of digitalisation on carbon intensity. The interaction terms of financial development and institutional quality, and the squared digitalisation index, are also not statistically significant. Although the threshold model estimates a digitalisation level of 1.438, the likelihood‐ratio confidence interval covers the search range, suggesting weak identification. Furthermore, digitalisation does not significantly affect carbon intensity in most country subgroups; the only exception is a long‐run positive and marginally significant effect in countries with high‐energy intensity. Energy intensity stands out as the most significant positive contributor to carbon intensity. Hence, the results refute the theoretical expectations of Ecological Modernisation and Socio‐Technical Transition about the inherent environmental benefits of digital growth. Digital connectivity is an enabling infrastructure, with environmental impacts conditional on electricity supply and use. Given policy and firm practices, investments in digital connectivity should go hand in hand with investments in clean electricity, energy efficiency improvements and industry decarbonisation to advance SDGs 9, 12 and 13.

papers.title: When do hedonic appeals backfire? Credibility, scepticism and the disconnect between emotional engagement and pro-environmental intention
papers.abstract: This study examines why emotional engagement with hedonic sustainability communication does not always translate into pro-environmental behavioural intention. Drawing on the Persuasion Knowledge Model and Truth-Default Theory, it investigates consumer responses to pleasure- and comfort-based hotel food-waste messages. A sequential mixed-method design combined a laboratory experiment, projective interviews, and a follow-up online experiment testing green scepticism. Findings show no robust statistically significant physiological differentiation across message types, but substantial differences in perceived credibility, sincerity and emotional meaning. Pleasure-based appeals were interpreted as enjoyable but superficial and less trustworthy; comfort-based appeals were warmer and more relational, yet both hedonic appeals produced lower behavioural intention than the control message. Green scepticism strengthened this negative effect, particularly for comfort-based appeals. The findings suggest that hedonic sustainability communication operates less through heightened physiological arousal than through interpretive credibility evaluation, particularly among sceptical consumers.

papers.title: The persuasive power of video in hospitality: How guest-generated video reviews influence customer engagement
papers.abstract: Guest-generated video reviews are increasingly prevalent on online travel platforms, yet their effects and mechanisms remain underexplored. Drawing on media richness theory, this study is among the first to examine whether and how such reviews enhance customer engagement, measured by subsequent review volume. We adopt a multimethod approach that combines econometric analysis with a controlled experiment to establish causal inference and uncover underlying mechanisms. Using a 24-month panel of 4471 hotels on Ctrip.com, difference-in-differences results show that guest-generated video reviews significantly increase customer engagement, with stronger effects for higher-tier or large hotels. Experimental evidence further demonstrates that these effects operate through increased information diagnosticity and social presence. Additional video content analysis reveals that human presence, higher informational richness, better visual quality, and longer duration further amplify the positive effects. These findings extend media richness theory to consumer-generated video reviews and offer insights into how richer review media stimulate engagement in hospitality settings.

papers.title: How to deal with AI technology anxiety and its negative consequences? The role of strengths-based leadership
The shapes of knowledge spillovers: the AC-KS model
papers.abstract: Abstract Why do some regions achieve higher levels of economic development while others do not? This paper introduces the Agglomeration-Clustering-Knowledge Spillovers (AC-KS) model, a conceptual framework for better understanding the nature of such differences. We argue that the missing piece of this puzzle is the process by which localized anchors ignite dynamic triangular forces between agglomeration, clustering, and knowledge spillovers, setting in motion a life cycle of first- and second-generation knowledge spillover effects. In this framework, we conceptualize that the spread and positive effects related to knowledge spillovers are governed by the strength-length-completeness triad of the triangularity relationship among agglomeration, clustering, and knowledge spillovers. These interactions then result in conical shapes whose base area and height, respectively, capture decaying effects of geographic reach and local intensity of knowledge-spillover entrepreneurship. The model’s originality lies in its geometric characterization of knowledge spillovers and in integrating fragmented literatures on the relationship among agglomeration, clusters, and knowledge spillovers. Its value is both theoretical and practical: the framework predicts when benefits concentrate or diffuse, offering diagnostic guidance for balancing reach (base) and intensity (height) across the knowledge spillover lifecycle stages of spark, expansion, and decline.

papers.title: Sorting Scams: Understanding Patterned Wrongdoing in Grand Challenges
papers.abstract: Organizational wrongdoing is foundational in Grand Challenges (GC), and a GC itself. Understanding patterns of wrongdoing, rather than idiosyncratic cases, would facilitate management of GCs. Fraud patterns – scams – show five aggrandizing mechanisms, the structured processes by which fraudsters make themselves better off: demanding, taking, diverting, steering, and assuring. Eight patterns of manipulation are generated: Demand manipulations (speculation events – manias, bubbles, panics; cons – Ponzi schemes); and supply manipulations (exploits – exploitation of the formal reward system; cost off-loading/risk-shifting; extraction/extortion/rent-seeking behavior; expropriation; enticement; and normative rents – e.g., abuses of trust). The approach makes possible analysis of the logics of corruption and its construction, and of its prevention and repair via “braking and breaking the scam.” Finally, the article discusses some GCs that feature wrongdoing, identifies their aggrandizing mechanisms, offers sample strategies to brake or break the potential for wrongdoing, and discusses why organizational wrongdoing is indeed foundational in GCs.

papers.title: The transparency dividend: Effects of corporate environmental management information disclosure on green-tech FDIs in emerging-market cities
papers.abstract: Cities in emerging markets increasingly shape sustainable development, yet the city-level characteristics attracting green-tech foreign direct investment (FDI) remain underexplored. Drawing on information cost economics, we conceptualize a city's corporate environmental management information disclosure (EMID) as an information-based regulatory feature that reduces foreign investors' information acquisition costs by transforming previously private firm-level environmental management knowledge into publicly accessible information. We further argue that the effectiveness of EMID depends not only on the availability of disclosed information but also on its quality, particularly its credibility and completeness. Using panel data for 2008–2023 from 285 Chinese cities, we find that higher EMID levels are associated with greater green-tech FDI inflows. Moreover, this positive relationship is strengthened by stringent environmental regulation, which enhances disclosure credibility, and is weakened by prevalent ESG underreporting, which undermines disclosure completeness. Our findings contribute to subnational FDI location research and the environmental regulation literature by demonstrating how local information environments shape green-tech investment allocation.

papers.title: Semantic similarity score: A new method for mapping intellectual structures in business research
Donation overperformance duration and visual salience in CSR reports
papers.abstract: Although performance-feedback research increasingly considers duration, how persistent overperformance on contested organisational targets relates to visual salience remains unclear. Using 8,287 firm-year observations from Chinese listed firms (2007–2022), we examine how the duration of above-aspiration donations relates to visual salience in CSR reports. We control for reporting status and estimate separate models for mandatory and voluntary reporters. Visual salience follows a U-shaped pattern, declining then rising as overperformance persists. This pattern is consistent with firms behaving as if short surpluses raise efficiency concerns, whereas sustained surpluses signal capability. The pattern survives controls for visual-design inertia and industry-year reporting prevalence and remains robust across alternative estimators. Industry culpability flattens the curve, whereas competition mainly steepens its later upward arm. We introduce retained-image area and area-weighted colourfulness and document a non-monotonic duration pattern that disclosure-volume measures miss. The findings suggest that duration is a candidate contingency for performance-feedback research on contested targets.

papers.title: “The Right to Repair”: A systematic literature review and research agenda for an emerging interdisciplinary field
papers.abstract: The Right to Repair (R2R) is an important arena in which restrictive repair practices, including limits on access to spare parts, manuals, software, and specialised tools, as well as product designs that inhibit repair, are being contested. Although scholarly interest in R2R is growing rapidly, research remains fragmented across disciplinary and empirical domains, limiting the development of a coherent understanding of its implications for technology-society relations. In response, this paper presents a systematic literature review that maps and synthesises existing research on R2R. Specifically, it (1) consolidates empirical evidence on the implications of R2R; (2) examines how the concept has been theorised across disciplines; and (3) identifies key conceptual and methodological gaps that constrain theoretical and empirical advancement in the field. By organising this literature into coherent thematic domains and tracing the relationships between them, the review argues that the effective realisation of R2R depends on a socio-technical capacity: the practically exercisable ability to repair produced through the interaction between legal entitlements, technological architectures, economic arrangements, and social capabilities. It also reveals disciplinary and geographical imbalances and identifies four tensions structuring future research: formal ownership versus effective control, legal entitlement versus practical repair capacity, universal frameworks versus situated repair practices, and systemic transformation versus continuity.

papers.title: Causality: Effects-of-Causes, Causes-of-Effects, and Question-Design Fit
papers.abstract: Causal claims sit at the center of many fields of inquiry, including tourism research, yet causal questions do not all ask the same thing. One class of questions asks what happens when a researcher, manager, or policymaker changes a condition ( effects-of-causes ). Another asks why an observed outcome arose in the first place ( causes-of-effects ). Drawing on causal inference scholarship, this letter distinguishes effects-of-causes from causes-of-effects and argues that conflating them narrows methodological choice and encourages claims that outrun design. Recognizing this distinction widens the methodological landscape of tourism research and allows scholars to employ diverse empirical strategies to investigate causal relationships. The letter sets boundaries around those alternatives by clarifying that no method becomes causal merely through its label and that defensible causal claims still require theory, explicit assumptions, and careful wording. Overall, greater precision about causal questions can strengthen theoretical contribution, sharpen empirical claims, and substantiate practical relevance.

papers.title: Processed meat, unprocessed red meat, poultry, seafood, and egg intake and stomach cancer risk: a pooled analysis of 20 cohorts
Religious information repertoires in Switzerland’s hybrid information environment: asymmetric associations with trust and reputation
papers.abstract: In hybrid media environments, public understanding emerges from patterned combinations of legacy news media, digital platforms, and interpersonal communication. Rather than relying on single channels, individuals assemble repertoires of mediated sources, interpersonal encounters, and direct personal experiences that structure how they make sense of public issues and evaluate social groups. Religion provides an instructive case: as a morally charged and contested domain, it circulates across hybrid media environments while also being shaped by biographical and interpersonal experience. Drawing on a Swiss online survey conducted in 2024 (N = 1,000), we use latent class analysis (LCA) to identify six religious information repertoires based on patterns of digital media use, legacy news consumption, and interpersonal experience. These repertoires are associated with distinct patterns of trust and reputation across Christianity, Islam, Judaism, Hinduism, and Buddhism. Overall, this study advances research on hybrid media environments by showing that combinations of various sources function as infrastructures of public evaluation. The findings indicate that legacy news media and interpersonal experience remain central, while digital-born sources play a more selective role. The study refines repertoire theory and illustrates how everyday information behavior is associated with social recognition and mistrust, with implications for the social-relational foundations of cohesion in pluralistic societies.

papers.title: Crash risk estimation in freeway exit influence areas considering exit configurations: An interpretability-informed Bayesian hierarchical extreme value model
papers.abstract: Freeway exit influence areas concentrate mandatory diverging maneuvers and exhibit substantially higher crash risk than basic freeway segments. Although direct-type and parallel-type exits differ in their diverging characteristics, most existing studies treat them as homogeneous objects, leaving their crash risk and influencing mechanisms insufficiently understood. This study proposes an interpretability-informed Bayesian hierarchical extreme value framework for crash risk estimation across different exit configurations. A Quasi-Kinetic Energy Risk Indicator (QKERI) is first developed to jointly characterize potential collision damage and the spatiotemporal proximity of interacting vehicles. Quantile regression is then used to determine the threshold for extreme conflicts, while the Conditional Shapley Value Index (CSVI) provides an interpretable basis for covariate selection. Finally, a peaks-over-threshold generalized Pareto model is estimated within a Bayesian hierarchical framework. The proposed approach is evaluated using 3027 conflict events extracted from more than 1200 min of trajectory data collected at 15 consecutive exit influence areas along a 200 km freeway. The estimated annual daytime crash frequencies are evaluated against three years of observed daytime crash records using Poisson confidence intervals, MAE, RMSE, and MAPE. The results indicate that the threshold for extreme conflicts is primarily determined by short-term traffic stream characteristics, whereas crash risk is mainly associated with adjacent lane density difference, heavy vehicle proportion, and conflict location. Among these factors, heavy vehicle proportion remains statistically significant throughout the modeling process. And the three scale covariates retain consistent coefficient signs across all 15 leave-one-site-out refits. Further discussion finds consistency between the CSVI results and the extreme value estimation, and the effective diversion length of a site is more decisive than the exit configuration in explaining differences in crash risk. These findings provide insights for the geometric design and proactive safety management of freeway exit areas.

papers.title: Weather extremes and ENSO teleconnections drive yield variability of soybean, a major food crop in India
Regulatory Agencies Under Mutating Populism in Office: Insights From Italy (1990–2025)
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Our paper builds a bridge between the emerging strand of research on public administration under populist rule and the established literature on delegation to independent regulatory authorities (IRAs). We focus on Italy, a critical case in Western Europe, which between 2001 and 2025 experienced six coalition governments dominated or strongly influenced by populist parties of different ideological orientations. Findings highlight that delegation to IRAs is remarkably resilient once institutionalized, even under sustained political contestation. Despite repeated populist participation in government since the early 2000s, Italian IRAs have not been subject to systematic de‐delegation or statutory retrenchment. However, the preservation of formal independence has not implied the absence of means for political control. Our analysis shows that populist governments have systematically relied on political appointments. Interestingly, political appointments have not been driven by partisan loyalty or overt politicization. Instead, the intervention of populist parties has operated along a different dimension of political control that has received less attention in delegation theory: the specialization of appointees. Populist governments have displayed a preference for appointing IRAs' board members with lower levels of domain‐specific specialization, privileging generalist profiles over specialists.

papers.title: Coordinated operation of Mobile substations and multiple Mobile flexible resources in coupled power distribution and transportation networks
A two-layer safe deep reinforcement learning framework for coordinated control of radiative cooling envelopes and HVAC systems
papers.abstract: Integrating passive daytime radiative cooling (PDRC) envelopes into buildings is an effective strategy for reducing cooling energy demand. However, due to their limited cooling capacity, HVAC systems remain necessary to maintain indoor thermal comfort. The performance of PDRC envelopes is strongly influenced by meteorological conditions, limiting the effectiveness of conventional rule-based control strategies. To address this, a two-layer safe deep reinforcement learning (DRL) framework is proposed to coordinate PDRC envelopes and HVAC systems for enhanced energy savings while maintaining thermal comfort. In the training layer, a Lagrange multiplier is incorporated into the reward function to dynamically penalize comfort violations, enabling the agent to learn a weather-adaptive trade-off between comfort and energy use. In the deployment layer, a physics-based predictor and optimizer is used to reduce the risk of thermal comfort violations. A comparative study of building energy performance under different control strategies is conducted. Results show that PDRC envelopes significantly reduce the interior surface temperatures of roofs and walls, improving thermal comfort even at the same indoor air temperature. Compared with rule-based control, the proposed framework further reduces cooling-season electricity consumption and cost by 12.1% and 13.5%, respectively, while also outperforming standard DRL control in thermal comfort. This study provides new insight into intelligent control of buildings with PDRC envelopes.

papers.title: Global green hydrogen site suitability and cost competitiveness: an open-source geospatial and uncertainty assessment across 182 countries
papers.abstract: Green hydrogen facility siting is commonly guided either by techno-economic cost minimization or by multi-criteria suitability assessment, yet the extent to which these approaches identify the same development priorities remains unclear. A site that can produce low-cost green hydrogen may not necessarily be suitable. Here, we develop an open-source, spatially explicit framework covering 182 countries that applies both approaches independently to a common technically eligible land base. The framework's methodological novelty lies in independently applying cost minimization and multi-criteria suitability assessment to a common eligible land base, enabling a consistent spatial comparison of cost-optimal and highly suitable locations while integrating spatial exclusions, hourly solar and wind generation modelling, plant-gate levelized cost of hydrogen estimation, spatial water-supply pathways, and Monte Carlo uncertainty analysis. Spatial exclusions reduce globally eligible land to 40%. Solar is the least-cost option across 81% of eligible areas, whereas wind-dominated locations achieve a lower median hydrogen cost of $2.8/kg compared with $3.1/kg for solar. However, it was demonstrated that the lowest-cost locations do not consistently coincide with the highest-suitability areas. These findings show that cost competitiveness and development suitability are related but non-equivalent, and that their combined assessment provides a more robust basis for prioritizing large-scale green hydrogen production.

papers.title: Continuous health monitoring of solid oxide electrolyzers using pulse-width modulation current interrupt analysis
papers.abstract: As solid oxide electrolyzer (SOE) technology moves from button cells to commercial stacks, there is a growing need for fast and inexpensive methods to track the stack’s state-of-health during operation. Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) is the standard diagnostic at the lab scale, but the cost, current limitations, and test duration of frequency-response analyzers make routine EIS measurements impractical for large stacks/systems. To address this problem, pulse-width modulation is combined with current-interrupt analysis (PWM-CI) to achieve continuous, in-situ monitoring of SOE health. The proposed PWM-CI method utilizes the “off” portion of the PWM cycle (when the applied voltage to the cell is removed) to perform rapid current interrupt measurements and analyzes the resulting voltage transients using a developed state-space model that explicitly accounts for cable inductance, switch capacitance, and oscilloscope properties. A fitting framework is developed that extracts ohmic, polarization, and total resistances from individual interrupts using only 50 ms of voltage decay, while avoiding the multi-minute interruption of hydrogen production required for EIS. PWM-CI tracking of button cells over 500 h generates ohmic resistances and time constants in agreement with EIS and distribution-of-relaxation-times analysis respectively, and accurately captures the degradation trends. The PWM-CI method is further demonstrated on a 45-cell commercial technology demonstrator stack, where inductive and capacitive effects cause oscillatory transients that are accounted for using the state-space model. After calibration of the electronic parasitics, PWM-CI yields stable resistance and time-constant estimates over 957 h of stack operation. The developed PWM-CI approach provides a practical pathway toward continuous health monitoring of SOE stacks under realistic dynamic operating conditions.

papers.title: MERIF: a market-informed electricity-price risk and interval forecasting framework for renewable-rich power markets
Revealing inter-cell water-gas-coupled transfer characteristics and degradation-driven evolution within large-scale fuel cell stacks
papers.abstract: Hydrophobicity decay is a critical driving force behind the degradation of proton exchange membrane fuel cells. However, the cross-scale linkage between microscopic material-level hydrophobic degradation and macroscopic stack-level water-gas transfer behaviors remains largely obscure, as well as the further inducing consequences. Bridging the gap, this study reveals the inter-cell water-gas-coupled transfer characteristics and degradation-driven evolution within large-scale fuel cell stacks. Applying the micro-current excitation method on a 60-cell stack, the evolution of membrane electrode assembly (MEA) material states is recognized after the 1000-h durability test. Except for typical catalyst degradation, an anomalous degradation feature is captured, wherein hydrophobicity degradation facilitates internal water accumulation and reduces ohmic resistance, consequently leading to the performance rise in ohmic polarization region. The degradation inconsistency within stack is found to be correlated with flow maldistribution. At the inter-cell level, cells with lower flow rates suffer from more severe degradation due to water accumulation and potential air starvation, which is especially pronounced in end cells. At the intra-cell in-plane level, the hydrophobicity degradation of MEA at the air downstream region is also more serious. For stacks assembled with MEAs with different hydrophobic states driven by degradation, the internal water accumulation difference and inter-cell coupling effect combine to cause gas redistribution. The evolution of gas distribution with humidity clearly indicates that the tendency of water accumulation within degraded cells increases the flow resistance and decreases the flow rate under high humidity conditions. Consequently, degraded MEAs suffer a greater risk of water flooding and significant deterioration in dynamic response performance, which forms a vicious cycle of accelerated degradation. This study enriches the cross-scale degradation mechanism theory of fuel cell stacks and holds significant values for consistency guarantee and lifetime extension.

papers.title: Sustainable aviation fuel production from electrified biogas reforming and SOEC-assisted Fischer-Tropsch process: Multi-product configurations and long-term projections
Rethinking carbon lock-in: Financial and contractual drivers in Southeast Asian power systems
Methane mitigation for climate goals: A life-cycle review of source control, recovery, destruction and removal from the atmosphere
papers.abstract: Methane mitigation is often evaluated by sector or by reactor performance, although deployment changes energy, food, waste, and wastewater systems beyond the point of treatment. This critical review evaluates prevention, recovery, destruction, and atmospheric removal within a common life-cycle framework. Evidence is screened by methane concentration, source controllability, recovery value, auxiliary demand, burden shifting, evidence maturity, governance fit, and net cost and incentives. Across sectors, prevention is considered first when methane generation or release can be avoided before dilution. Recovery is credible for concentrated streams only when collection losses are low and recovered products displace existing supply. Destruction is justified for controlled residual streams, but conversion efficiency alone does not establish net benefit. Atmospheric methane removal remains an early stage option. At a concentration of approximately 1.9 ppm, methane removal requires large volumes of air and may impose substantial energy, land, and material demands. Reported technology rankings are conditional on the counterfactual, system boundary, operating context, and evidence scale. The resulting stage-gated framework links production and consumption choices to intervention timing, life-cycle performance, and verification. Atmospheric removal is treated as a research contingency, not a substitute for source mitigation. The final gates specify the evidence required before an emerging approach can progress beyond controlled research.

papers.title: A decision making framework for traffic noise prediction using artificial intelligence techniques
papers.abstract: Road traffic is one of the primary contributors to environmental noise pollution. The study presents a literature review on traffic noise exposure, prediction models, comparative performance and explainability of prediction models, traffic noise action plans, and a conceptual decision making framework in urban environments. In total, 136 studies from 1999 to 2026 were reviewed and synthesized. A Boolean search approach was used to understand the different aspects of traffic noise prediction. The results from field studies showed that conventional models achieved R 2 values ranging from 0.54 to 0.96, whereas machine learning (ML) models achieved R 2 values ranging from 0.81 to 0.99, although these are indicative values from heterogeneous studies and not a strict ranking. Moreover, deep learning (DL) in some studies has demonstrated stronger performance on large datasets. The present study also analyzed the interpretability constraints of ML and DL models, which are further addressed by the utilization of explainable artificial intelligence (AI) algorithms. The key research gap is that very few studies employed cross-study validation of the developed noise models, and there remains a shift needed from prediction oriented modelling to decision oriented noise management. To address these gaps, the study proposes a conceptual decision making framework coupled with a traffic noise action plan to offer a structured pathway for sustainable environmental management.

papers.title: Material-engineered localized ion enrichment for critical mineral recovery via solar-driven interfacial evaporation
SCREEN-LCA: Ex-ante prioritization of bio-based pathways for chemicals and plastics under a climate-mitigation objective
papers.abstract: Life cycle assessment (LCA) is a key tool for guiding circular bioeconomy strategies, including the substitution of fossil carbon with bioresources. However, its data- and time-intensive nature can hinder its use when there are numerous candidate pathways, particularly in the chemical sector. Here, we developed SCREEN-LCA, a stepwise ex-ante framework designed to prioritize case studies before conducting full LCA. The framework combines: (i) sector-level impact estimation; (ii) identification of hotspot products within targeted sectors; (iii) mapping of corresponding alternative bio-based pathways; and (iv) pathway prioritization based on multiple criteria. We applied SCREEN-LCA in a France-oriented demonstration to prioritize residual-biomass-based pathways for subsequent LCA. The greenhouse gas footprint of incumbent petrochemicals and plastics, feedstock compatibility, and technological maturity were used as screening criteria. An extensive graph database covering 50 hotspot products and their alternative bio-based routes was assembled. Ethylene, propylene, methanol, and PET emerged as priorities with promising bio-based alternatives.

papers.title: Life cycle assessment of compostable plastics: critical review and gap analysis
papers.abstract: Bio-based and biodegradable plastics are increasingly considered sustainable alternatives to fossil-based plastics due to their potential for environmental benefits and circularity. However, evaluating their overall sustainability requires assessment of environmental impacts across the entire life cycle to avoid burden shifting and unintended consequences. This study presents a critical review and gap analysis of 63 published life cycle assessments (LCA) studies on bio-based compostable plastics, focusing particularly on compostable plastic and how end-of-life is modelled. The review identifies key data gaps and methodological limitations that affect the accuracy of environmental evaluations. Key findings reveal the inconsistent modelling approaches for composting processes, with significant data gaps concerning the temporal dynamics of CO₂ emissions during biodegradation, the environmental consequences of compost application to soil, and polymer-specific degradation rates that determine the persistence of materials and their potential contribution to plastic leakage. The analysis highlights the need for material-specific life cycle inventory (LCI) data capturing emissions to air and impacts on soil, as well as improved reporting of plastic leakage and microplastic flows, for which inventory methods and characterization factors are increasingly available but remain unevenly applied. Addressing these gaps is essential for improving the reliability and completeness of environmental assessments of compostable plastics.

papers.title: Gas–Liquid Interface Enhanced Selective Adsorption of Long-Chain PFAS by Novel Floating Macroporous Resins
papers.abstract: Abstract Long-chain per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) in industrial wastewater are a significant source of PFAS contamination. Anion exchange resin (AER) adsorption is an advantageous technology for PFAS removal, but existing AERs suffer from limited selectivity. In this study, our synthesized novel macroporous AERs with asymmetric long-chain amine groups, MP-(12–1–1) and MP-(16–1–1), exhibited a unique floating behavior on the water surface after drying and achieved significantly enhanced PFAS removal from chromium-plating wastewater, with the gas–liquid interface playing a critical role. Molecular dynamics simulations revealed that the rough surfaces and hydrophobic functional groups of the dry MP-(12–1–1) and MP-(16–1–1) enable them to maintain the Cassie wetting state in water without transitioning to the Wenzel state, thereby forming a stable gas–liquid interface. The gas–liquid interface exhibited adsorption free energies reaching −7.6 to −9.5 kcal/mol for long-chain PFAS, increasing the selectivity of the floating macroporous AERs for various long-chain PFAS by 6–81 times. This provides a new approach for the efficient removal of long-chain PFAS and offers new insights for the design of selective adsorbents based on the gas–liquid interface.

papers.title: Ocean Acidification Impairs Olfaction in the Large Yellow Croaker, Larimichthys crocea , by Disrupting Sensory Integrity and Neural Processing
papers.abstract: Abstract Ocean acidification (OA) poses a significant threat to marine organisms, yet its effects on fish sensory systems remain poorly understood. This study investigated the effects of elevated pCO2 on olfactory function in the large yellow croaker, Larimichthys crocea. Elevated pCO2 reduced peripheral olfactory sensitivity, as evidenced by suppressed electro-olfactogram responses. This impairment was accompanied by epithelial disorganization, cellular damage, increased apoptosis in the olfactory epithelium, and reduced expression of olfactory neuron markers. In vitro analyses using a selected recombinant L. crocea odorant receptor LORA1–1 showed that acidified pH altered its physicochemical properties and odorant-specific receptor–ligand interaction dynamics. OA also downregulated genes associated with odorant receptor expression, G protein-mediated signaling, calcium-related transduction, and neuronal maturation. Telencephalic responses included altered ion-transport ATPase activities, histopathological abnormalities, oxidative stress, enhanced apoptotic activity, and reduced neuropeptide Y expression. Transcriptomic and proteomic analyses further identified telencephalic molecular changes associated with altered neuroactive ligand–receptor interaction, calcium signaling, glutathione metabolism, apoptosis, mitophagy, MAPK signaling, and olfactory transduction. Our findings suggest that epithelial injury, altered odorant recognition, and disrupted peripheral signaling contribute to OA-induced olfactory impairment in L. crocea, with potential consequences for migration and reproduction that depend on olfactory cues.

papers.title: Submicroscale and Molecular Insights into Labile Organic Matter Transformation and Sequestration at Newly Formed Iron Minerals–Water Interfaces during O2-Mediated Fe(II) Oxidation
papers.abstract: Abstract Abiotic Fe(II) oxidation and subsequent precipitation are key pathways for controlling labile organic matter (OM) dynamics in O2-perturbed subsurface environments, yet the underlying coupling mechanisms remain poorly understood. Herein, OM transformation and sequestration during O2-mediated heterogeneous Fe(II) oxidation were evaluated at neutral pH across various C/Fe ratios. Increasing C/Fe ratios impeded Fe(II) oxidation but enhanced the level of reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation. Despite efficient sequestration, the OM immobilization efficiency varied with C/Fe ratios, with a minor fraction of OM being oxidized by ROS. Higher C/Fe ratios promoted ferrihydrite formation but inhibited its transformation into lepidocrocite, forming mineral-organic composites constituted by Fe–O cores and edge-/corner-sharing Fe–Fe shells. A direct visualization at submicroscale revealed heterogeneous spatial distributions of different organo functional groups on newly formed Fe mineral surfaces, reflecting OM selective immobilization. Newly formed Fe minerals preferentially immobilized high-molecular-weight compounds and those with more oxygenated or highly unsaturated structures, with stronger molecular fractionation at higher C/Fe ratios. Molecular-level analysis revealed that a lower C/Fe ratio promoted the conversion of phenols to quinones, aromatic ring opening, and carboxylation of aromatic substituents but inhibited polymerization of phenolic substances. Collectively, these findings deepen our knowledge of heterogeneous Fe mineral formation coupled with OM sequestration and transformation, advancing our understanding of Fe and C geochemical cycling in oxic soils and sediments.

papers.title: Nanoplastic Size Governs the Decoupling of Microbial Survival from Antibiotic Degradation
papers.abstract: Abstract Nanoplastics (NPs) and antibiotics co-occur in wastewater systems, but how NP size influences antibiotic biodegradation by specialized degraders remains unclear. Here, we investigated the effects of europium-doped polystyrene nanoplastics (PS-NPs; PS20 and PS100) on sulfadiazine biodegradation by Arthrobacter sp. strain D2. Modified Gompertz modeling revealed two contrasting inhibition regimes. For PS100, inhibition was dominated by lag-phase prolongation, with no detectable sulfadiazine removal over 48 h at a PS100 concentration of 100 mg L–1. In contrast, PS20 reduced the maximum sulfadiazine degradation rate by ∼40% while causing only minor changes in lag time, indicating rate-dominated inhibition. Quartz crystal microbalance with dissipation monitoring at a model sulfadiazine-enriched interface showed that PS100 markedly reduced the deposition of NP-pre-exposed cells, whereas PS20 only partially impaired adhesion. Transmission electron microscopy coupled with energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy further revealed intracellular accumulation of PS20, whereas PS100 remained predominantly extracellular. Phase-specific physiological measurements and transcriptomics suggested that PS20 induced oxidative-stress responses associated with reduced sulfadiazine biodegradation rates, whereas PS100 elicited dose-dependent transcriptional changes during lag-phase extension. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that nanoplastics impair antibiotic attenuation through distinct size-dependent mechanisms involving interface-associated constraints and intracellular interference, highlighting particle size as a key determinant of antibiotic fate in plastic-contaminated wastewater environments.

papers.title: Micromolar Experiments, Nanomolar Environments
Uncovering the Fate and Global-Scale Risk-Based Threshold Contents of Organophosphate Esters in Indoor Environments: A Tiered Modeling Approach
Life-Cycle Burden Shifting in Solvent-Based Regeneration of PFOS-Laden Granular Activated Carbon
papers.abstract: Abstract Granular activated carbon (GAC) is widely used to remove perfluorooctane sulfonate (PFOS) from contaminated water, yet its sustainable regeneration remains challenging. Solvent-based regeneration preserves the carbon matrix but may shift environmental burdens toward solvent production, chemical use, energy demand, and downstream waste management. Here we present a life cycle assessment (LCA) of PFOS-laden GAC regeneration using deionized water (GAC-WR) and ethanol (GAC-ER). We identify electricity-driven elution and downstream incineration as the dominant environmental hotspots across 18 midpoint impact categories. Selected chemical-assisted configurations (NaOH-modified water and HCl-modified ethanol) improved regeneration efficiency and reduced environmental impacts under the evaluated conditions by reducing virgin GAC supplementation. An industrial-scale model incorporating equipment upscaling and thermal integration further mitigated laboratory-specific energy overestimation. Compared with the corresponding baseline scenarios using the global electricity mix, hydropower-based electricity reduces global warming potential to 3.30 and 8.26 kg CO2e kg–1 for GAC-WR and GAC-ER, respectively, while increasing life-cycle water consumption to 230% and 266% of the respective baselines. This cross-category burden shift demonstrates that reducing climate impacts does not necessarily reduce the broader life-cycle environmental footprint. Overall, sustainable solvent-based GAC regeneration requires balancing regeneration efficiency, energy supply, chemical inputs, solvent recovery, and management of PFAS-containing wastes.

papers.title: Early Life Ambient Air Pollution, Sex Steroids and Neurodevelopment: Target Trial Emulation in a Prospective Cohort
papers.abstract: Abstract Ambient air pollution may impair childhood neurodevelopment, but sensitive windows, mediating pathways, and the neurodevelopmental benefits of air-quality interventions remain unclear. In this prospective birth cohort of 3575 mother–child pairs in Wuhan, China (2014–2019), neurodevelopment at age two was assessed using the Bayley Scales, and cord serum sex steroids were measured in 897 pairs. Associations of air pollution exposure from preconception through the second postnatal year with neurodevelopment at age two and potential sex-steroid mediation were evaluated. Target trial emulation (TTE) was used to estimate neurodevelopmental differences associated with China’s 2013–2017 air-quality intervention. Most air pollutants were inversely associated with neurodevelopment across multiple exposure windows, with associations generally strongest during the first postnatal year. Mediation analyses suggested that androstenedione mediated 5–12% of associations between specific preconception/prenatal air pollutant exposures and Psychomotor Development Index, although inverse-probability-weighted indirect effects were no longer statistically significant. TTE suggested significant neurodevelopmental benefits following the air-quality intervention, with Mental Development Index and Psychomotor Development Index improving by 7.27 and 6.41 points in the later policy-period group, respectively. These findings support more stringent long-term air pollution standards and sustained air-quality interventions to protect child neurodevelopment.

papers.title: Hydrogen production by catalytic supercritical water gasification of representative biomass-derived model mixtures
papers.abstract: Supercritical water gasification enables hydrogen production from wet biomass-derived feedstocks without the need for a drying step. The catalytic supercritical water gasification of three representative multicomponent model mixtures was investigated in a continuous tubular reactor using a commercially available Ni-based catalyst. The mixtures combined model compounds representing organic families found in fruit residues, sewage sludge and dairy effluents. Experiments were conducted at 240 bar and 500–800 °C, using feed concentrations of 5 and 7.5 wt%, a liquid flow rate of 1 L h⁻ 1 and catalyst loads of 10 and 20 g. The results were compared with chemical equilibrium predictions and corresponding non-catalytic experiments performed with the same mixtures and reactor configuration under identical operating conditions. Higher temperatures and lower weight hourly space velocity resulted in higher hydrogen production, a lower liquid organic fraction and gas yields closer to chemical equilibrium. The maximum hydrogen yield reached 10.29 mol H 2 mol⁻ 1 organic feed, while the carbon-to-gas efficiency reached 94.4 % at 800 °C and 5 wt% feed concentration. Compared with the corresponding non-catalytic experiments, the H 2 yield increased from 3.52 to 8.73 mol H 2 mol⁻ 1 organic feed at 800 °C and 7.5 wt% feed concentration using 10 g of catalyst. Thus, the Ni-based catalyst substantially increased hydrogen production and reduced the fraction of organic carbon remaining in the liquid phase. The experimental results also indicate that the hydrothermal reactions occurring upstream of the catalytic bed influence the subsequent conversion of oxygenated, aromatic and nitrogen-containing intermediates and, consequently, the overall gasification performance. The apparent turnover frequencies and Arrhenius parameters were used as reactor-scale indicators to compare the catalytic response rather than as intrinsic kinetic parameters. Overall, the results indicate that the kinetic constraints associated with multicomponent hydrothermal conversion can be mitigated by catalytic supercritical water gasification but not completely overcome.

papers.title: Combined cycle power plant with chemically recuperated high-temperature gas turbine: Thermal efficiency, energy and material balance via comparative analysis
papers.abstract: The global transition to low-carbon energy systems drives the need for continuous efficiency improvements in fossil-fuel-based power generation. Combined cycle power plants (CCPPs) represent the state-of-the-art in commercial thermal power generation, yet further efficiency gains through conventional methods face diminishing returns. This paper presents a comprehensive thermodynamic analysis of a combined cycle power plant integrated with a chemically recuperated gas turbine (CCPP-CRGT) based on a modern high-temperature gas turbine with turbine inlet temperature of 1600 °C. Unlike conventional recuperation that transfers sensible heat, thermochemical recuperation utilizes exhaust heat to drive endothermic steam methane reforming, converting exhaust heat into chemical energy stored in hydrogen-rich syngas. The performance of the CCPP-CRGT is benchmarked against a conventional CCPP across a range of steam-to-methane molar ratios (S/C = 1.0–3.0). The results demonstrate that thermochemical recuperation shifts the power generation from the steam turbine cycle towards the more efficient gas turbine cycle, increasing the gas turbine net work from 465 MW in the conventional case to 598 MW at S/C = 3.0, while reducing condenser heat rejection from 327 MW to only 117 MW. The overall combined cycle efficiency improves from 62.49% to 65.42%, representing a gain of 2.93 percentage points. The temperature-heat transfer profiles reveal that the reformer consumes up to 28% of the available exhaust heat, displacing the superheater section of the heat recovery steam generator. The material balance shows a progressive reduction in air mass flow rate from 2680 t/h to 2463 t/h as S/C increases, while the syngas flow grows correspondingly to 323.3 t/h. These findings confirm that the CCPP-CRGT configuration offers a viable pathway to surpass the efficiency ceiling of conventional CCPPs by leveraging the high-temperature end of the exhaust heat cascade for thermochemical recuperation rather than for steam generation, thereby reducing the heat rejected in the bottoming cycle by redirecting a portion of the exhaust heat.

papers.title: Reducing experimental effort in the certification process through model-based performance prediction of variable-speed heat pumps
papers.abstract: Heat pumps are essential for decarbonizing the heating sector, particularly air–water heat pumps, which are favored for their low costs and ease of installation. In case of unrefurbished existing buildings, hybrid heat pumps – combining heat pump and gas boilers – offer the possibility to decouple the replacement of the heating system from further renovation measures to the building envelope. For tailoring the heat pump capacity to the building demand, manufacturers offer different variants with different nominal capacities that are based on similar hardware, but certification costs quickly add up if each different combination of heat pump and boiler needs to be measured. To reduce certification cost, we evaluate the possibility of using standard test data for monoenergetic electric heat pumps to derive operating points required by the EN14825 standard for different hybrid heat pump capacities. To achieve this, we present and evaluate a semi-analytical heat pump model with focus on reducing the number of required parameters. The model predicts efficiency (COP) and heat flow rates across various operating points. As a result, the model requires a small experimental dataset of 9 laboratory measurements and only 5 input parameters to fit 5 unknown parameters. Using 115 performance measurements of five commercial heat pumps tested in a certified laboratory, the prediction quality is evaluated and additionally benchmarked against an innovative AI method based on the tabular foundation model TabPFN. The semi-analytical model can predict COP with an average error margin of 6.6% for norm measurements, and SCOP with a maximum error of 9.2%. The efficiency class of the machines according to the Ecodesign regulation (EU 813/2013) is correctly predicted in 8 out of 10 cases using the semi-analytical model, and up to 10 out of 10 cases using the tabular foundation model.

papers.title: Carbon-Negative Dual-Source polygeneration integrating biogas combustion and geothermal energy for Water–Energy–Carbon Nexus; 5E + LCA assessment and Ridge Regression–ALA optimization
papers.abstract: The pressing necessity to reduce carbon emissions and shift to sustainable energy systems stimulates the creation of innovative polygeneration technologies, maximizing resource productivity and reducing environmental impact. This paper suggests and critically analyzes an innovative dual-source multi-generation system as a synergistic integration of biogas-combustion flue gas, geothermal energy, and LNG regasification with cold-energy recovery to co-produce electricity, heating, cooling, liquid CO 2 , hydrogen, oxygen, and desalinated water. This system has net carbon-negative performance, and the global warming potential of the life cycle is −0.09 kgCO 2 -eq/kWh, which highlights its environmental excellence and compliance with the objectives of cleaner production. Based on a comprehensive 5E (Energy, Exergy, Economic, Environmental, and Exergo-environmental) analysis and the stepwise Life Cycle Assessment (LCA), the system has proven a baseline polygeneration energy efficiency of 50.30% and a levelized cost of energy (LCOE) of 0.23 $/kWh. Moreover, an advanced machine learning and multi-objective optimization (ML-MOO) framework, based on the Ridge Regression surrogate modeling and Artificial Lemming Algorithm (ALA), leads to a significant improvement in the system performance, namely, an increase in polygeneration exergy efficiency to 28.69% while reducing LCOE to 0.210 $/kWh. The work offers a validated, scalable template of sustainable energy integration within the water-energy-carbon nexus, and a technically viable, economically competitive, and environmentally transformative route to decarbonized multi-generation.

papers.title: Longitudinal dynamics of nitrogen and phosphorus forms along agricultural drainage ditches: Evidence for nitrate source mixing and possible transformation
papers.abstract: Diffuse nitrogen (N) and phosphorus (P) pollution from agriculture is a leading cause of freshwater eutrophication. Agricultural drainage ditches can modify the concentrations and forms of nutrients transported from fields to receiving waters. We characterized springtime concentration patterns of N and P forms and dissolved organic carbon (DOC) in four agricultural drainage ditches differing in site characteristics, vegetation, and nutrient management. Dual nitrate isotopes (δ 15 N–NO 3 − and δ 18 O–NO 3 − ) were measured along one ditch to evaluate longitudinal nitrate isotopic patterns in relation to potential source mixing and possible transformation. DOC was strongly and positively correlated with dissolved organic nitrogen (DON) and orthophosphate–P (PO 4 –P), moderately and negatively correlated with NO 3 –N, and weakly correlated with ammonium–N (NH 4 –N). In the two ditches draining fields that received poultry litter during the study, DOC, DON, and PO 4 –P increased following litter application and subsequent rainfall, consistent with field-derived inputs. On May 17, DOC, DON, and PO 4 –P decreased from the field-edge to the outlet, with the largest DON and PO 4 –P concentration declines in two ditches occurring between the field-edge and the first in-ditch sampling location. NO 3 –N behaved differently, including a 6.8-fold increase from 0.46 mg L −1 at the field-edge to 3.12 mg L −1 at the outlet of the isotope-monitored ditch. In that ditch, upper-reach isotopic patterns were consistent with changing nitrate-source contributions and mixing, whereas the lower reach showed a positive relationship between δ 18 O–NO 3 − and δ 15 N–NO 3 − (slope = 0.907, R 2 = 0.857), consistent with possible isotope-fractionating nitrate transformation. These results indicate that agricultural ditches are not uniform nutrient conduits: organic N, P, and nitrate follow distinct longitudinal patterns, and increases in nitrate concentration coincide with isotopic patterns consistent with possible fractionating transformations within the same ditch. Consequently, longitudinal nutrient patterns may reflect the combined influence of field inputs, hydrologic source mixing, and in-ditch processing.

papers.title: Operationalizing systems thinking in water governance: A framework for advancing regional water security
papers.abstract: Despite major advances in hydrological science and water management technologies, regional /national water crises persist. This study argues that these challenges arise less from scientific limitations than from fragmented governance systems that hinder coordination across sectors, scales, and institutions. We develop a systems governance framework that operationalizes systems thinking by embedding it within institutional practice through four interdependent mechanisms: leadership, organizational coordination, education/institutional learning, and stakeholder platforms (LOEP). Drawing on comparative analysis of China’s River Chief System and the United Kingdom’s Yorkshire Integrated Catchment Solutions Programme, we illustrate how the LOEP governance framework enables coordinated decision-making, policy integration, and sustained implementation. The findings show that systems thinking becomes effective only when supported by institutional arrangements that align knowledge production with governance processes. By reframing systems thinking as an operational governance capacity, this study provides a structured and operational framework that extends beyond existing analytical approaches for policymakers and practitioners seeking to advance water security and sustainability transitions under complex socio-ecological systems.

Investigations on the delamination mechanism of double-glass photovoltaic modules based on laser treating
papers.abstract: The growing number of decommissioned photovoltaic (PV) modules calls for efficient recycling methods with minimal material damage. This study developed a preheating-assisted pulsed laser strategy for interfacial delamination of double-glass crystalline silicon PV modules and investigated the underlying mechanisms. Preheating softened the EVA encapsulant and broadened the laser-processing window, although preheating alone was insufficient to induce EVA/Si delamination. Among the investigated conditions, a heater setpoint of 200 °C provided the widest stable-delamination window. The laser beam passed through the top glass and upper EVA encapsulant with limited optical loss and was predominantly absorbed by silicon. Four characteristic states emerged with increasing laser energy density: non-separable, difficult-to-delaminate, stable delamination, and carbonized delamination. Interfacial weakening involved coupled responses of EVA, the SiN x antireflection layer, and the silicon surface. EVA deacetylation reduced the abundance of polar ester groups and weakened chemical adhesion, while damage to the SiN x layer and localized silicon melting–resolidification altered the interfacial bonding environment and reduced mechanical interlocking. Transient pressure from localized vaporization and volatile-product release may have further assisted crack propagation across regions where the pyramidal texture remained intact. These coupled effects enabled relatively continuous EVA/Si delamination with limited material damage. Excessive energy input caused EVA carbonization, severe surface ablation, and silicon fracture. These findings provide a mechanistic basis for process optimization and low-damage recovery of materials from double-glass PV modules.

papers.title: Transport of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) in DOM-influenced complex groundwater systems: Insights into aromatic ring number and π-electron characteristics
Community gardening underpins collective and relational values for urban nature
papers.abstract: Understanding how people perceive nature is essential for aligning greenspace provision with everyday needs, well-being and environmental preferences. Such perceptions are heterogeneous, shaped by gender, socioeconomic context and how people engage with informal greenspaces. Community gardens and other resident-led spaces remain comparatively underexplored as sites of relational value in lower-income urban contexts yet offer hands-on interactions that differ markedly from formal parks and private gardens. These dynamics are especially relevant in rapidly urbanising lower-income cities, where community gardens, often operating on vacant land, are among the few accessible, resident-managed greenspaces. In Accra, Ghana, such gardens provide everyday engagement with biodiversity across neighbourhoods of varying income. We used Q-methodology, which identifies shared viewpoints through structured sorting of statements and images, to capture diverse perceptions of urban nature. Sixty participants sorted items representing Nature's Contributions to People and biodiversity-health pathways, comparing community garden members and non-members across contrasting neighbourhoods. Four viewpoints emerged: nature as a practical and spiritual resource ; nature as a source of comfort and protection ; selective engagement shaped by safety and predictability ; and nature as a social and cultural space . Participants expressed least preference for certain animal biodiversity and allergenic risks, while consistently preferring accessible medicinal plants and private gardens. Perceptions centred on comfort, familiarity and social connection rather than ecologically beneficial species, shaped by everyday environments, safety concerns and conditions of encounter. Community garden membership was associated with more relational, multifunctional understandings of nature, while neighbourhood conditions and gender also shaped preferences. These insights are vital for urban planning, where residents’ preferences can align with or challenge ecological priorities.

papers.title: Unrevealing biofouling in a solar-powered membrane distillation process operated with intermittent mode

Understanding public preferences for urban wildflower meadows
papers.abstract: Accelerating urbanisation challenges biodiversity and human wellbeing, demanding effective urban nature-based solutions. Urban wildflower meadows are increasingly popular interventions that may offer biodiversity and wellbeing benefits. However, realising their potential depends on public support, which requires robust evidence on which meadow design attributes the public prefers and values most. We conducted a choice experiment with urban greenspace users across three UK cities to quantify willingness-to-pay (WTP) for some of the key characteristics of wildflower meadows in public parks, namely flower colour diversity, native species composition, plant species richness, and pollinator habitat quality. Respondents generally preferred wildflower meadow options over the status quo of mown amenity grass and were willing to pay for improvements to meadow attributes through increased local taxation. Respondents had positive WTP for more colourful, pollinator-friendly meadows with more native species, but not for additional plant species. Preferences were largely consistent across respondents interviewed at different meadow types (annual, perennial, or control sites), suggesting that enhanced attribute salience from direct exposure to existing meadows had minimal influence on stated preferences. Methodologically, this suggests that in situ surveys of preferences for urban greenspace are broadly robust to salience effects and can inform management beyond the surveyed sites. Attributes that offer positive outcomes for biodiversity, such as supporting pollinators and including native species, were aligned with, rather than conflicting with, public preferences. Urban greenspace managers can enhance public support while achieving ecological objectives by designing meadows with moderate colour diversity, high native species content, and demonstrable pollinator benefits.

papers.title: Micro-processes in science-industry transfer
Collective ambiguity attitude as response to individuals’ ones and belief disagreements
papers.abstract: Abstract This paper axiomatically characterizes the rule of aggregating individuals’ ambiguous beliefs into the society’s ambiguous belief. We consider a family of social rankings over acts which are indexed by pairs of utility profiles and ambiguous belief profiles, and impose variable-profile axioms which express how society should respond to changes in belief profiles and changes in how beliefs disagree. Our characterization allows two kinds of collective ambiguity aversion, one arising due to individuals’ ambiguity aversion and the other arising due to disagreements in beliefs.

papers.title: Perceived-Control Salience in Service Recovery: Area-Level Economic Disadvantage and Consumer Disputes
papers.abstract: This study develops a perceived-control salience framework for understanding the experiences of consumers in economically disadvantaged areas during service recovery. Drawing on 141,251 complaint narratives submitted to the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, we examine how seven salience dimensions relate to dispute escalation. The results suggest that cognitive-control and behavioral-control salience have the strongest positive associations with disputing. Emotional-control salience, decision-control salience, and predictive-control salience have weaker positive associations, whereas information-control salience is negatively associated with dispute escalation. The study contributes to service recovery and consumer vulnerability research by showing how economic disadvantage changes which control-related cues become behaviorally predictive in institutional complaint systems. The findings suggest that effective recovery should reduce comprehension burdens, lower action costs, and avoid treating disclosure alone as sufficient consumer support.

Modeled Groundwater Decline is Associated with Lower Arsenic Concentrations in Hanoi
papers.abstract: Abstract Elevated arsenic concentrations in groundwater pose health risks. Geogenic arsenic contamination is driven by biogeochemical mobilization and groundwater dynamics. Intensive pumping can initially exacerbate contamination by drawing arsenic or mobilizing organic matter into aquifers, but over longer time scales may also promote dilution and flushing in some settings. To better understand the mechanisms controlling arsenic concentrations, we examined changes over two decades in Hanoi (Vietnam), a hotspot of geogenic arsenic contamination and groundwater pumping. Arsenic concentrations from 470 wells sampled in the year 2000 were compared with 434 wells sampled in the same area in 2013 and 2023. Median concentrations declined from 14 to 8 μg/L between 2000 and 2023, while mean concentrations and the proportion of high-arsenic wells (>100 μg/L) remained similar. Using hydrochemical and groundwater-level data, CatBoost models combined with SHAP analysis assessed changes in predictor importance. In 2000, arsenic was more strongly associated with redox predictors, whereas groundwater-level predictors became more important in 2023. Within wells used to evaluate groundwater-level change (n = 251), larger decadal declines were associated with lower arsenic concentrations (median = 31 μg/L) than wells without declines (median = 120 μg/L). We hypothesize a decadal mechanism shift, from redox to hydrological controls, particularly driving arsenic declines.

papers.title: Institutional closure in development governance: The repositioning of local voice
papers.abstract: Large-scale industrial projects linked to the green transition can proceed through accelerated and procedurally insulated authorization while formal opportunities for participation or contestation remain available. This article develops the concept of institutional closure to denote configurations in which competence allocation, authorization design, and procedural sequencing leave locally accessible intervention weakly aligned with the arenas and stages at which consequential development choices remain open. Using a structured qualitative comparison of six battery-related projects across five Hungarian municipalities, the analysis reconstructs authorization arrangements and traces local voice across political, participatory, administrative, and legal arenas. The comparison identifies patterned but non-deterministic variation among three predominant trajectories: juridified voice, in which legal and administrative arenas gain relative importance; procedural exhaustion, in which repeated engagement loses timely leverage over core authorization; and managed engagement, in which involvement remains concentrated on implementation or mitigation. Across the cases, local voice persisted without following a uniform trajectory or retaining uniform effectiveness. The findings illuminate a recurrent tension between speed and coordination on the one hand and deliberation and contestability on the other in green transition-linked industrial development. The framework provides a basis for examining other fast-track or procedurally insulated development settings.
