papers.title: Does testosterone predict pathogen disgust sensitivity? Cross-sectional and longitudinal evidence from three diverse developmental and endocrine contexts
papers.abstract: Testosterone has been hypothesized to help explain sex differences in pathogen disgust sensitivity (PDS), which is a measure of how intensely one experiences disgust toward pathogen threats. Guided by the sexual selection framework, researchers have theorized testosterone may downregulate PDS to facilitate mating effort. Yet, this relationship remains largely untested outside women samples. The present study (total N = 355) assessed salivary testosterone and PDS in three distinct populations: A sample of adults from Boston including 1) cisgender men ( N = 116), 2) transmasculine adults on hormone therapy ( N = 30), and 3) a longitudinal sample of juveniles and adolescents from Utila, Honduras ( N = 209; 119 girls). Across all cohorts, testosterone showed no significant associations with PDS. Collectively, we found no evidence that testosterone levels meaningfully shape PDS, regardless of developmental stage, route, or level of hormone exposure.

papers.title: Visceral Volunteer Work: The Emotional Labour of Crisis Helpline Volunteers
papers.abstract: Crisis helplines provide frontline support in suicide prevention, yet the emotional labour of volunteers who sustain these services has received little attention. Drawing on 40 interviews with volunteers across five branches of a U.K. crisis helpline, this article introduces visceral volunteer work to conceptualise a form of volunteering characterised by the emotional demands arising from sustained exposure to others’ distress. This study identifies four interrelated emotional practices: readiness, immersion, containment and recovery. Through these practices, it shows how emotional labour extends beyond individual encounters and operates as a continuous and cyclical process. It further uses the unpaid context of volunteering to show how this labour is regulated and sustained outside conventional wage-based and managerial forms of control. Together, these contributions make visible the demanding emotional work obscured by conventional accounts of volunteering while extending theorisation of emotional labour beyond paid employment.

papers.title: Nonprofit Fiscal Sponsorship: How Capacity Shapes Coordination and Cooperation
papers.abstract: Fiscal sponsorship is a growing mode of nonprofit program delivery, yet theory treats it as a uniform interorganizational relationship. Drawing on Castañer and Oliveira’s distinction between coordination and cooperation, we argue that sponsorship models occupy different positions on a coordination–cooperation continuum, and these positions demand different capacities. We assemble a novel dataset linking the Fiscal Sponsor Directory to 2022 Internal Revenue Service (IRS) Form 990 filings and estimate count and logistic regression models. Results show that organizational maturity predicts consolidation into fewer models without a contraction of services, while revenue scale predicts deeper service provision without a wider model portfolio. Arts sponsors are less likely to operate the Direct Project model, indicating that field membership rather than capacity distinguishes cooperators. Conventional capacity slack- and diversification-based measures do not predict continuum position. Overall, fiscal sponsorship supports multiple stable organizational forms, and funders and policymakers should consider sponsor capacity relative to the model(s) they operate.

papers.title: Reshaping Work: Job Reallocation and Job Attributes During the Great Resignation in Italy
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The Covid‐19 pandemic reshaped labor markets worldwide, including the emergence of the “Great Resignation” (GR). This study examines whether Italy's GR reflects labor force exits or job switching and identifies and explores which job attributes are associated with these reallocation patterns. Using Italian Labor Force Survey data, we construct a job‐switching indicator that aligns with administrative resignation trends and enables the exploration of potential determinants through a task‐based approach. Results are consistent with the interpretation that Italy's Great Resignation mainly reflects job reallocation across occupations characterized by differences in flexibility, meaning, and working conditions.
papers.journal_name: Industrial Relations A Journal of Economy and Society

papers.title: Tax Credits and Shared Parenthood: Improving Child Tax Benefits for Children when Parents Live Apart
papers.abstract: When parents live apart, typically one parent may claim the child for tax credit purposes. We estimate the impact of alternative policy options, allowing either parent’s earnings or joint earnings to be used to claim the earned income tax credit (EITC) and the child tax credit (CTC). When either parent’s earnings may be used, the estimated share of families qualifying for the EITC grows from 53.9 to 73.8 percent; among parents with earnings below the poverty level, 28.9 percent newly qualify. CTC participation rises 14.7 percentage points; among poor families, participation rises 32.9 percentage points, substantially increasing the anti-poverty impact for single-parent families.

papers.title: The Same but Different: How the Income Tax Affects Black, Hispanic, and White Households
papers.abstract: The federal income tax does not explicitly discriminate by race or ethnicity but can still generate disparate outcomes when a group’s activity correlates with determinants of tax liability. Using Survey of Consumer Finances data and NBER’s TAXSIM model, we find that untaxed forms of income accrue disproportionately to white households across most income levels. Black and Hispanic households face lower tax rates than whites in low-income groups due to differences in filing status and dependents, but Black units face higher rates than whites in high-income groups due to differences in income composition. We also examine cross-group implications of historical and prospective policy changes.

papers.title: Quantifying the power system benefits of building upgrades for passive survivability in a changing climate
Spatio-temporal large language model for zero-shot EV charging demand prediction: Beneficial to station energy management under data scarcity
Coopetition and coordination mechanisms between energy and peak-shaving benefits in giant cascade hydropower systems: From mechanism identification to operational application
Energy management of pumped thermal electricity storage: a framework integrating a rule-based expert system with robust data-driven control
Feasibility assessment of solar-driven underground hydrogen storage through integrated surface and subsurface modelling
A hierarchical framework and Bayesian game model for multi-load aggregator strategic interaction under incomplete information
papers.abstract: High renewable penetration intensifies power fluctuations in distribution networks, making load aggregators (LAs) essential providers of flexibility. However, in practice, multiple LAs operate within the same area, with their decisions coupled through dynamic interactions in power flows and profits. Commercial privacy further creates information barriers, forcing LAs to decide under incomplete information and uncertain outcomes. To address these challenges, this paper investigates the modeling of multi-LA strategic interactions. A hierarchical information-decision-execution framework is formulated, in which a Bayesian game model is used to describe the physical and economic interdependencies among LAs, with equilibrium solutions defining the optimal strategies. Furthermore, a Productive Mixed-Attention Transformer (PMA-Transformer) is developed to enable the DSO to accurately estimate each LA's regulation capacity and resource composition, providing reliable type estimates for dynamic prior construction in the game. Finally, a constraint-aware vSoC balancing and priority-based allocation strategy (CSB-PAS) is proposed for node-level power allocation, improving computational efficiency while respecting user comfort and device constraints. Simulation results show that the proposed approach effectively meets the regulation target and enhances voltage quality. Compared with the complete information game approach, it also improves the total utility by 5.06%.

papers.title: Coordinated secondary frequency regulation of thermal power units and feeder loads under high renewable penetration: Joint economy-performance optimization and distribution network PCC power tracking
papers.abstract: Large-scale integration of high-penetration renewables aggravates net-load fluctuations and brings uncertainties to secondary frequency-regulation demands. Limited by adjustable capacity, ramping capability and operational costs, conventional thermal generating units cannot independently provide frequency-regulation support balancing economic and dynamic performance. Different from existing user-side frequency-regulation schemes relying on end-user authorization, massive communication terminals, aggregator coordination and dedicated compensation-settlement mechanisms, this work exploits voltage-power coupling of feeder loads and grid-controllable voltage-regulation devices to incorporate feeder clusters into the active-power frequency-regulation resource pool. Three core challenges are addressed: quantification of feeder safe adjustable capacity, coordinated command allocation among heterogeneous resources, and sustained Point of Common Coupling (PCC) power tracking over regulation cycles. First, the Conservation Voltage Reduction (CVR) coefficient of feeder loads is identified via grid-side voltage-driven exogenous excitation. Combined with a Z -bus-based linearized power-flow model, feeder safe adjustable capacity is evaluated subject to full-node voltage constraints. Second, considering discrepancies in cost, tracking accuracy and response speed between continuously-regulated thermal units and feeder clusters, a joint economy-performance command-decomposition model is built. The trade-off solution is obtained using the ε-constraint method, Pareto filtering, TOPSIS evaluation and knee-point identification. Finally, a real-time tracking strategy with disturbance observation and sensitivity-weighted allocation is proposed to mitigate PCC deviations induced by second-scale source-load fluctuations. Simulations verify that the proposed method reduces frequency-regulation costs, improves response accuracy and speed, and enhances PCC tracking and system frequency-support capability while guaranteeing feeder node-voltage security.

papers.title: Bridging the climate to energy data gap: simulated annealing for representative climate year selection
papers.abstract: Energy system models are increasingly dependent on representative climate input. Yet, a fundamental mismatch persists between the hundreds of simulated years often used in climate science and the handful of years that computationally demanding power system models can process. Current practice, including ENTSO-E’s European Resource Adequacy Assessment, relies on climate year selections that have not been validated against explicit representativeness criteria. This risks biased investment decisions and blind spots for plausible weather conditions. This study proposes simulated annealing as an optimisation method for selecting representative subsets of complete climate years from large climate ensembles. Representativeness is quantified using the seasonal sliced Wasserstein distance, a metric from optimal transport theory that captures representativeness of marginal distributions, inter-variable correlations, and seasonal structure simultaneously. We evaluate simulated annealing against the alternative methods of random search, filtered random search, and K-Medoids clustering across three test cases spanning the Netherlands and Europe, using 180 climate years from the Pan-European Climate Database as a reference. Simulated annealing consistently produces the most representative subsets and outperforms the compared methods. Simulated annealing achieves an effective sample size three to five times the actual subset size. The resulting subsets are roughly 2.5–4 times more representative than the current ENTSO-E practice. The method is application-agnostic and its output can serve as a validated climate data input to any subsequent (energy) impact study.

papers.title: Cold start of proton exchange membrane fuel cells in high-altitude cold regions: coupled heat-water-oxygen mechanisms, system constraints, and engineering validation
papers.abstract: Cold start remains a major barrier to the reliable deployment of proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs) in subfreezing environments. High-altitude cold regions impose a compound operating boundary in which low temperature, reduced ambient pressure and oxygen partial pressure, dry air, cold-soak history, compressor demand, coolant thermal inertia, and limited auxiliary energy act simultaneously. This critical review integrates previously separated evidence on generic cold start, high-altitude operation, residual-water control, air supply, heating, and liquid-cooled thermal management. The literature is classified according to whether a study directly tests the coupled high-altitude/subfreezing boundary, tests only one constituent boundary, provides validated simulations or architecture-specific evidence, or supports an engineering synthesis. The combined evidence indicates that reduced oxygen availability may constrain the admissible heat-generating current before water production becomes the sole limiting factor, while minimum cell voltage and coolant response emerge as key stack-scale variables. On this basis, the review proposes an altitude-aware sequence linking purge, loading, air supply, heating, and coolant operation and defines success through thermal, electrochemical, system-energy, and durability criteria. Because direct full-size liquid-cooled validation under simultaneous reduced pressure and subfreezing temperature remains scarce, the immediate priorities are compound-environment experiments, platform-specific weakest-cell safety boundaries, and experimentally verified air-current-coolant switching with unified net-energy accounting.

papers.title: A novel unsupervised anomaly detection and traceability method for battery voltage inconsistency based on the time-segmented DBSCAN algorithm
papers.abstract: Voltage inconsistencies in lithium-ion battery packs are a primary driver of performance degradation and thermal runaway. Accurate diagnosis from real-world operational data remains hindered by highly dynamic driving conditions, continuous measurement noise, and scarce labeled faults. To address these challenges, an unsupervised anomaly detection framework utilizing a time-segmented Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise algorithm is proposed. High-dimensional voltage features, capturing both transient fluctuations and long-term aging behaviors, are extracted via a multi-scale sliding window mechanism. Principal Component Analysis is subsequently applied to decouple absolute voltage levels from dynamic inconsistency patterns. Time-segmented clustering then facilitates highly efficient local anomaly detection, generating a continuous Consistency Health Index for the quantitative grading of individual cell health. The framework was rigorously validated using actual operational data from two distinct electric vehicles that experienced severe thermal runaway. The failed cells (Cell #126 in EV 1; Cells #52 and #53 in EV 2) were accurately flagged one full month prior to the catastrophic incidents, achieving significantly high Anomaly Signal-to-Noise Ratios of 8.98 and 10.18. Quantitative comparisons confirm the proposed methodology significantly outperforms benchmark algorithms in isolating true fault signals from background noise, fundamentally eliminating the ranking inversion issue across diverse battery systems.

papers.title: Physics-constrained multi-task energy consumption prediction for the safe operation of embodied mobile robots
papers.abstract: Reliable task-level energy assessment is essential for sustained mission execution and safe operation of battery-powered mobile robots under dynamic conditions. State of charge (SOC) and fixed-capacity estimates provide limited information about the effective energy reserve under changing electrical, thermal, and locomotion conditions. This study proposes a two-level indicator system comprising task-available energy (TAE) and a predictive relative risk margin. TAE characterizes the energy reserve available for a specific task under current operating conditions, extending conventional SOC-based assessment toward task-conditioned energy availability. An 85-day operational dataset covering five gait modes is segmented into task fragments. The proposed physics-constrained multi-task model combines categorical embeddings, stacked long short-term memory encoding, temporal attention, and current-state fusion to jointly predict TAE, future energy consumption, future minimum voltage, and future maximum battery temperature. On the independent test set, normalized root-mean-square error (NRMSE) values of 1.34%, 1.60%, 0.68%, and 0.59% are obtained for the four targets, respectively. Compared with the strongest energy-related baselines, the NRMSE values for TAE and future energy are reduced by 72.4% and 65.6%, respectively. The predictive relative risk margin integrates energy, voltage, and thermal constraints, achieving a coefficient of determination of 0.993, a risk-level agreement of 94.01%, and a dominant-risk-factor accuracy of 93.30%. This work reframes battery management as a task-aware predictive capability that integrates energy state assessment, operational risk evaluation, and autonomous decision-making, enabling safer and more reliable operation of mobile robots in dynamic environments.

papers.title: Electrode crosstalk in rechargeable aqueous zinc batteries: species transport, interfacial reactions and coupled full-cell failure
papers.abstract: Rechargeable aqueous zinc batteries fail through reactions that couple the two electrodes as well as through local degradation. Dissolved cathode products, soluble redox intermediates and electrolyte gradients can cross the separator, alter the receiving interface and redistribute active material, zinc and water. This Review defines electrode crosstalk by a source, a transmitted species or perturbation, and a consequential interaction at the opposite electrode. It distinguishes direct chemical transfer from electrolyte-mediated coupling while allowing both pathways to operate in the same cell. Manganese, vanadium, Prussian blue analogue, halogen, selenium and organic cathodes are compared through their carrier chemistry and zinc-side reactions. Liquid, gel and solid electrolytes are examined in terms of their conducting phase, species partitioning and interfacial contact. A six-level evidence hierarchy separates source generation, crossover, arrival, receiver reaction and causal intervention. Consistent definitions of permeability, molar dose and reaction-associated charge loss connect these measurements with cell capacity without conflating ionic charge and reaction stoichiometry. Quantitative examples show how imported species and interfacial regulation affect corrosion, hydrogen evolution and zinc deposition. Mitigation is assessed against resistance, recoverable inventory and cell-level energy, including the possibility of relocating failure. Comparisons of lean-electrolyte and pouch cells identify the operating conditions under which crosstalk becomes consequential. The outlook develops a route for combining spatially resolved measurements, reaction–transport models and data-driven screening to design mutually compatible electrode environments.

papers.title: Coordinated supply scheduling of offshore and onshore hydrogen considering power and transportation networks
papers.abstract: Converting offshore wind energy into hydrogen is a promising approach to improving renewable energy utilization. Coordinated offshore and onshore operation can further enhance hydrogen supply flexibility. Despite this potential, most existing studies model offshore hydrogen production and onshore demand delivery separately. This paper therefore proposes a coordinated supply scheduling model of offshore and onshore hydrogen considering both power and hydrogen transportation networks. The model coordinates power system operation with maritime and onshore hydrogen transportation scheduling under network constraints, capturing the spatiotemporal interactions among offshore production, port buffering, onshore production, truck routing, storage operation, and hydrogen refueling demand satisfaction. A time-window mapping method is developed to couple continuous time transportation events with discrete time power and hydrogen scheduling constraints. To handle renewable generation uncertainty, the proposed model is extended into a two-stage stochastic formulation. An accelerated progressive hedging algorithm (PHA) with adaptive penalty updating and stable binary variable fixing is developed to improve the efficiency of solving problems with multiple scenarios. Case studies on modified IEEE 24-bus and IEEE 118-bus systems validate the effectiveness of the proposed model and algorithm. The proposed accelerated PHA substantially reduces solution time while maintaining negligible deviations in the objective value.

papers.title: Source-attributed DLMP settlement with price-anticipating load response
Income responsiveness of household energy expenditure across life-cycle stages: Evidence from China
papers.abstract: Energy policies targeting households by income may overlook differences in energy expenditure across the household life cycle. Using 44,581 household-year observations from the China Family Panel Studies (2014–2022), this study distinguishes six stages and estimates income elasticities with two-way fixed effects. Elasticities are positive across all stages, but highest in formation and substantially lower in the remaining stages. Childrearing, burden-peak, and stabilization households nevertheless have higher expenditure than formation-stage households at comparable income and household size. Therefore, higher expenditure and stronger income responsiveness characterise different stages. Durable-goods accumulation offers a possible explanation for the stronger formation-stage response, while consumption structure is associated with income responsiveness across stages. Overall responsiveness is higher in the north than in the south. Among initial gaseous-fuel users, it is higher in rural than in urban areas. These findings support considering family stages alongside income when designing household energy policies. Equipment support during formation could account for both purchase and operating costs, while assistance for childrearing, burden-peak, and stabilization households could reflect actual energy bills. Such measures also need to consider local heating charges and the recurring costs of cleaner fuels.

papers.title: Perceived market potential of blue coal in Poland: the role of regulatory signals and consumer demand as seen by fuel distributors
‘Not in my backyard’ or ‘Not in our backyard’? The influence of spatial proximity and regional belonging on attitudes and opinion expression on site selection for a nuclear waste repository
Calcium-based materials for thermochemical energy storage: Advances in synthesis, granulation and lab-scale reactor validation
papers.abstract: The rapid growth of renewable energy technologies has driven demand for high-density and long-duration energy storage systems. Thermochemical energy storage (TCES) stands out owing to its high energy storage density, minimal self-discharge loss, and wide operating temperature ranges. Calcium looping (CaL) represents one of the most competitive TCES routes, benefiting from abundant low-cost feedstock, large reaction enthalpy and compatibility with high-temperature solar utilization. However, the practical application of CaL-TCES remains constrained by severe cyclic degradation, intrinsic trade-offs between solar absorptance and energy density, and poor engineering feasibility of raw powdered materials. This review consolidates recent progress on Ca-based TCES materials across three interrelated research directions: material synthesis, granulation modification, and lab-scale reactor development. Key advances include multiscale strategies for enhanced cyclic stability, feasible granulation methods for raw powders, trade-off optimization between solar light absorption and heat storage capacity, and the advancement of lab-scale reactor platforms toward realistic solar-driven CaL-TCES evaluation. Future research directions are outlined, including the development of durable, transportable Ca-based TCES materials for long-duration energy storage, alongside solar-driven Ca-based thermochemical conversion into fuels. This review elucidates the design principles of high-performance Ca-based TCES materials, providing theoretical insights and practical guidance toward stable, efficient, and scalable solar TCES systems.

papers.title: Piezoelectric and triboelectric nanogenerators for smart cities: Bridging gaps from laboratory validation to real-world deployment
Machine learning for gasification systems: from process modeling to sustainability-oriented decision making
papers.abstract: Gasification provides a flexible route for converting coal, biomass, plastics, and waste-derived feedstocks into syngas, hydrogen, fuels, chemicals, power, and carbon materials. Its modeling and operation remain difficult because feedstock composition, reaction regimes, multiphase transport, reactor configuration, sensor availability, and downstream integration vary simultaneously. Machine learning (ML) has consequently expanded from static performance prediction to CFD surrogate modeling, soft sensing, fault diagnosis, predictive control, digital twins, and sustainability assessment. However, the literature remains dominated by application-specific accuracy reports, and R 2 , RMSE, and MAE values are often compared without accounting for sample size, data provenance, validation strategy, domain shift, uncertainty, or deployment conditions. This review combines a broad Web of Science corpus of 951 records with a 417-record direct-topic sensitivity subset and a separately screened technical evidence layer. It reorganizes the evidence through a system-level framework linking gasification science, descriptor engineering, task–model matching, trustworthy validation, cyber–physical integration, and sustainability-oriented decision making. Representative studies demonstrate large reductions in surrogate-computation time and credible industrial optimization, but few establish closed-loop deployment. In an adjacent solar-thermochemical membrane-reactor study, a learning-assisted feedforward–feedback controller reduced the control integral error by 82.4%, increased hydrogen recovery and yield by 43% and 33%, respectively, and reduced the input preheat ratio by 30%; these results are informative for controller architecture but are not direct gasification evidence. The review proposes gasification-specific descriptor classes, a task–data–model selection matrix, evidence levels for validation and deployment, and a decision chain coupling uncertainty-aware prediction with scenario evaluation, robust Pareto optimization, risk filtering, governed execution, and feedback learning. The central conclusion is that progress depends less on marginal in-distribution accuracy than on transferable, physically consistent, uncertainty-aware, and governed ML systems that convert predictions into verifiable operating and sustainability decisions.

papers.title: Heterogeneous drivers and transition typologies of agricultural reactive nitrogen emissions: Evidence from 340 Chinese cities (2000–2020)
Expanding cerium magnet deployment for balanced and sustainable use of light rare earths
papers.abstract: Rare earth elements (REEs) are geologically co-existed and co-produced but are used in highly differentiated downstream markets. The rapid expansion of NdFeB magnet use has made neodymium (Nd) and praseodymium (Pr) the primary drivers of light REEs production, while resulting in the large and growing surplus of lanthanum (La) and cerium (Ce) that have very limited application. However, cerium magnet, an important alternative to NdFeB magnet, is rapidly developing and has substantial potential to expand cerium use. Here, we develop a material flow analysis framework to quantify China’s historical and future cerium surplus and evaluate the mitigation potential of cerium magnets under nine scenario combinations of NdFeB demand pathways and cerium magnet adoption levels. We find that cerium surplus increased from 2 kt to 51 kt during 1990–2025. Under a scenario in which cerium magnet deployment remains limited, the surplus is projected to expand to 244–295 kt by 2050. China’s cerium magnet demand could reach 163–453 kt by 2050 across all scenario combinations, mitigating 25% (conservative cerium magnet adoption and aggressive NdFeB demand scenario) to 97% (aggressive cerium magnet adoption and moderate NdFeB demand) of projected cerium surplus. Under the moderate scenario, cerium magnets could mitigate 25% of projected Ce surplus through direct Ce utilization in cerium magnet production and an additional 44% by partially substituting NdFeB magnets and avoiding co-produced Ce supply. This study reveals the structural elemental imbalance embedded in co-produced REE systems and demonstrates how demand-side technological substitution can rebalance material flows.

papers.title: An integrated life cycle assessment framework for bike share systems incorporating battery swapping and data-driven rebalancing modeling
papers.abstract: Bike share systems are widely promoted as sustainable transportation solutions, yet existing life cycle assessment (LCA) studies often underestimate operational emissions. This study develops an integrated LCA framework that explicitly incorporates station energy use, battery swapping trips, and data-driven rebalancing modeling. Battery swapping routes are optimized using a Vehicle Routing Problem with Time Windows (VRPTW) model, while rebalancing trips are estimated through empirical activity identification and routing. Using Chicago’s Divvy system as a case study, results show that battery swapping is a major operational impact source, accounting for 9–12 % of total system emissions. Integrating battery swapping with rebalancing reduces operational travel and lowers system-level greenhouse gas (GHG) emission intensity by approximately 4 %. Overall, the life cycle GHG emission intensity of the station-based Divvy system is 103–107 g CO₂-eq per bike-km. The proposed framework improves the completeness and accuracy of environmental assessments for bike share systems.

papers.title: Single-Cell Insights into Size-Dependent Heterogeneous Bioconcentration and Distribution of Metal Species Ranging from Ions to Nanoclusters and Nanoparticles in Chlorella vulgaris
papers.abstract: Abstract Particle size is a key factor influencing metal uptake by aquatic unicellular primary producers. To investigate size-dependent bioconcentration ranging from ions to nanoclusters (NCs) and nanoparticles (NPs), we used cytometry by time-of-flight (CyTOF) to quantitatively examine single-cell uptake, retention, and bioconcentration in Chlorella vulgaris exposed to Au3+ ions, three glutathione (GSH)-protected AuNC preparations (Au10–12SG10–12, Au15SG13, and Au25SG18), and four GSH-coated AuNPs (5, 15, 25, 50 nm). Au3+ and AuNCs showed rapid cell-associated accumulation but followed exponential-decay and two-phase clearance kinetics, indicating efficient cellular elimination and a tendency to be released back into the medium. In contrast, AuNPs followed saturation-type bioconcentration kinetics, with larger particles showing more persistent cell association. Single-cell analysis revealed strong size-dependent heterogeneity: under equal-mass exposure, the fraction of Au-positive cells decreased exponentially with increasing atom number, whereas the Au burden per Au-positive cell increased approximately linearly. Larger particles exhibited higher volume concentration factors (VCFs) with a small subset of “high-VCF” cells. These results highlight that both particle size and cellular heterogeneity jointly govern algal bioconcentration patterns and should be accounted for in environmental risk assessment of metal-based nanomaterials.

papers.title: Absolute Environmental Sustainability Assessment: From Academia to Decision Support in Industry and Government
Integrating Lattice and Molecular Oxygen Pathways to Enhance Toluene Oxidation via Mn Substitution in Fe x Co3– x O4 Spinel
papers.abstract: Abstract Activation of lattice oxygen and molecular oxygen critically governs the catalytic degradation of volatile organic compounds (VOCs), driving substantial research into harmonizing the bonding state of oxygen atoms in transition-metal oxides to facilitate VOCs abatement. However, the underlying mechanism of oxygen activation via cation substitution in spinel remains to be explored owing to its significant flexibility in both tetrahedral and octahedral sites. Herein, a Mn-substituted FexCo3–xO4 spinel catalyst was developed for promoting oxidation of toluene (one of the typical aromatic VOCs), with the temperature of 90% toluene conversion decreasing by approximately 51 °C relative to the pristine one. Multiple characterizations and theoretical calculations revealed that Mn3+ substitution at octahedral Co3+ sites of FexCo3–xO4 modulated the metal–oxygen bonds within the Mn–O–Co structure for activating surface lattice oxygen, accompanied by the creation of abundant oxygen vacancies for O2 excitation. The combined results of temperature-programmed analyses, isotopic labeling experiments, and in situ spectroscopy showed that the adsorbed toluene could be synchronously oxidized by activated lattice oxygen and chemisorbed oxygen generated via O2 activation, thereby accomplishing the deep oxidation of toluene. This study clarifies the synergistic role of lattice and molecular oxygen in toluene oxidation and affords a potential catalyst for environmental remediation.

papers.title: Bioinspired Phototropic Endogenous Heating for Low-Temperature Biological Wastewater Treatment
papers.abstract: Abstract Biological wastewater treatment in cold regions faces a low-efficiency and high-energy paradox due to low-temperature inhibition. Inspired by plant phototropism, this study reports bioinspired phototropic endogenous heating (Bio-PEH) based on the underwater opto-thermomechanical response. Upon illumination, cryopolymerized macroporous reduced graphene oxide@poly(N-isopropylacrylamide) fibers undergo asymmetric contraction, which reorients the illuminated surface to be normal to the light vector, so as to maximize photothermal flux under oblique incidence. Meanwhile, flash heating further enhances water-confined heat transfer and expands the effective heating domain. Bio-PEH arrays raise bulk wastewater from 7.8 to 30.2 °C, which improves NH4+ removal by 2.8-fold, accounting for 25.3–169.7% enhancement compared with Joule heating (JH), direct solar heating (DH), and static endogenous heating (SEH). Global simulations further indicate multifold thermal compensation at high latitudes with substantial carbon and energy cost reduction. This study provides a biophysically inspired strategy by utilizing opto-thermomechanical response to realize heating of low-temperature wastewater, making wastewater treatment in cold regions more efficient, economical, and sustainable.

papers.title: Early Life Stage Exposure to Environmentally Relevant Concentrations of TCPP Induces Multigenerational Reproductive Toxicity in Estuarine Fish: A Study Based on Whole-Genome Methylation and Steroidogenesis Pathway
papers.abstract: Abstract Tris (1-chloro-2-propyl) phosphate (TCPP) is ubiquitous in estuarine environments. Parental TCPP exposure impaired reproduction and offspring developmental in zebrafish; yet its multigenerational and transgenerational effects and epigenetic mechanisms in estuarine fish remain unknown. Here, Mugilogobius chulae embryos were exposed to TCPP until 25 days posthatching and reared in clean seawater until F2 hatching. Reproductive and gonadal end points were assessed across generations, while gonadal steroidogenesis and whole-body DNA methylation in larvae were analyzed in F0 and F1 to investigate potential endocrine and epigenetic mechanisms. TCPP induced multigenerational reproductive toxicity that was transmitted to F2 embryos, with F1 and F2 lowest observed effect concentrations 1 order of magnitude lower than that in F0. In F0, 100 μg/L TCPP reduced fecundity and male gonadosomatic index. In F1, 10, and 100 μg/L prolonged spawning latency and affected male gonadal development. In F2, 10 μg/L reduced embryonic hatching. Disruption of steroidogenesis gene expression and hormone levels occurred in F0 and F1 male gonads but only in F1 females. Whole-genome DNA methylation revealed persistent hypermethylation of nerve growth factor receptor (NGFR) and calcium voltage-gated channel auxiliary subunit γ 2 (CACNG2) in the mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) pathway across F0 and F1. Their hypermethylation and reduced expression were associated with decreased steroidogenic acute regulatory protein (STAR) and cytochrome P450 family 11 subfamily A member (CYP11A) in male gonads, suggesting NGFR and CACNG2 may represent candidate epigenetically regulated genes associated with TCPP-induced multigenerational reproductive toxicity. This study reveals transgenerational risks of environmental concentrations of TCPP to estuarine fish and provides epigenetic evidence for multigenerational endocrine disruptors.

papers.title: Building Resilience into Large-Scale Seawater Desalination
Evaluating Critical Raw Materials in the energy sector through an energy criticality index
Temporal feature augmentation for transient fuel consumption prediction of heavy-duty trucks: Toward sustainable road freight and cleaner operations
Hofstede cultural dimensions and sustainable development goals disclosure: Evidence from Europe
papers.abstract: This study examines whether national culture is associated with Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) disclosure among 1650 firms in 21 EU countries over 2019–2024 (9900 firm-year observations). SDG disclosure is measured as a provider-coded indicator of disclosure breadth: the share of the 17 SDGs that Refinitiv/LSEG codes as addressed in firms' reporting, while culture is captured using Hofstede's six dimensions. Pooled OLS with year and industry fixed effects is complemented by firm- and country-clustered inference, wild-cluster-bootstrap tests and multiple robustness analyses. Indulgence shows the most consistent positive association with SDG disclosure and is the only dimension that remains significant under country-clustered inference after a Holm adjustment for testing six dimensions, although not under the wild-cluster bootstrap. Masculinity is negatively associated and uncertainty avoidance positively associated under firm- and country-clustered inference, but neither survives the wild-cluster bootstrap. Power distance, individualism and long-term orientation show weaker, specification-sensitive associations. Disclosure is also highly persistent over time. The evidence is therefore suggestive rather than robust, and is consistent with persistent cultural heterogeneity in SDG disclosure under increasingly common European reporting pressures. The findings also show the importance of matching statistical inference to the country level at which cultural variables vary and caution against treating disclosure breadth as equivalent to sustainability performance.

papers.title: Continuous score-based optimization of pressure sensor placement for burst detection in water distribution networks
Utilization of carbonyl-modified carbon nanotubes for selective removal of perfluorinated sulfonates from surface water
Impact of slurry additives on nitrogen emissions, grass agronomy and soil microbial communities following slurry landspreading
papers.abstract: This study assessed the effects of specific slurry additives on nitrous oxide (N 2 O) emissions, grass herbage yield and N uptake and soil microbial communities. The experimental work was conducted on two soil types: i) a moderately to poorly drained fine loam and ii) an imperfectly drained clay loam over two growing seasons. Cattle slurry was applied in three split applications at both sites simulating trailing shoe application method and the treatments were control (no treatment), unamended slurry, slurry + sulphuric acid, slurry + biochar, slurry + gypsum and urea + urease inhibitor N-(n-butyl) thiophosphoric triamide (NBPT) (NBPT-urea). Nitrous oxide was measured during the growing period using the static chambers and dry matter yield was measured at every harvest. Ammonia (NH 3 ) was also quantified at one of the sites, therefore NH 3 responses are site-specific. Ammonia was measured within the first week of slurry application using dynamic chambers coupled with a photoacoustic gas analyser. Soil samples were collected after the end of the experiment for microbial analysis at both sites. The acidified slurry increased grass yield by more than one tonne ha −1 , increased plant N recovery by 21 to 24 kg N ha −1 , suggesting improved nitrogen conservation may have contributed to these agronomic benefits, and increased fungal abundance however, it also increased N 2 O on one occasion. The other slurry amendments did not have significant effect on N 2 O. The cumulative N 2 O emissions from the moderately drained soil were significantly lower than the imperfectly drained soil. None of the amendments significantly reduced NH 3 emissions in the moderately to poorly drained soil, while biochar increased NH 3 during a single application timing.

papers.title: Unlocking the carbon reduction potential of building integrated photovoltaics beyond rooftops in an urban core considering inter building shading
Sustainable production of ultrahigh-temperature thermal energy storage particles from molten steel slag
papers.abstract: Steel slag (SS), a high-volume byproduct (150 kg/ton steel) with severe disposal burdens, poses critical environmental challenges. To transform this waste into value, we propose the novel TERSEG protocol–a sustainable valorization route that, for the first time, simultaneously enables ultrahigh-temperature thermal energy storage (TES) particle production from molten SS via centrifugal granulation and recovers its >1400 °C waste heat. By modifying molten SS with blast furnace slag (BFS) to drastically reduce its viscosity by ∼90% (to 0.23 Pa s at 1500 °C), we overcome prior barriers to granulation. The engineered particles (1-3 mm) exhibit exceptional thermal stability (<1% mass loss over 10 cycles at 400-1000 °C), good sphericity (axis ratio of 1.5), and low porosity (<4%), making them ideal TES materials. This approach recovers >1400 °C waste heat and converts hazardous slag into functional materials. The TES particle production scalability is demonstrated via an empirical correlation validated across broad operational conditions. This approach pioneers a sustainable valorization route that simultaneously recovers >1400 °C waste heat and converts hazardous slag into functional TES materials. This work provides a circular economy strategy for the steel industry, diverting slag from landfills, reducing industrial CO2 footprint, and advancing net-zero goals.

papers.title: Ranking green finance instruments and finance-linked environmental transition mechanisms within the environmental, social, and governance (ESG) framework: Empirical evidence from Saudi Arabia's petrochemical industry
papers.abstract: The petrochemical industry faces increasing pressure to decarbonize due to its high energy intensity, carbon emissions, and environmental footprint. This study evaluates and ranks green finance instruments and finance-linked environmental transition mechanisms within the Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) framework to identify the highest-ranked mechanisms for supporting the sustainable transition of Saudi Arabia's petrochemical industry. A two-stage multi-criteria decision-making (MCDM) framework integrating the Analytic Network Process (ANP) and fuzzy Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution (TOPSIS) was employed to assess six alternatives comprising four green finance instruments and two finance-linked environmental transition mechanisms against three ESG dimensions and fifteen industry-specific sub-criteria. The results show that the Environmental dimension carries the highest priority, followed by Governance and Social, highlighting the importance of measurable environmental outcomes supported by robust governance structures. Among the evaluated alternatives, green tax policies ranked first, followed by green credit mechanisms and investor risk mitigation instruments. The findings suggest that progressive environmental taxation, preferential green lending, and blended-finance mechanisms are better positioned to support industrial decarbonization while limiting abrupt cost pressures during the transition. Furthermore, the effectiveness of green bonds and emission trading systems depends on transparent governance, regulatory compliance, and credible sustainability reporting frameworks. This study provides policy insights for aligning industrial finance with Saudi Vision 2030, the Saudi Green Initiative, and the Kingdom's 2060 net-zero target, while offering a practical decision-support framework for prioritizing sustainable finance in energy-intensive industries.

papers.title: Reconfiguring urban mining: Orchestrating multi-actor E-waste supply chains for circular value recovery through an integrated DEMATEL–BWM–Agent-Based Modeling framework
papers.abstract: The accelerating generation of e-waste in developing economies presents both an environmental challenge and an opportunity for circular value recovery through urban mining, yet fragmented coordination among heterogeneous formal and informal actors limits the realization of this potential. This study addresses the gap between causal diagnosis and dynamic simulation by proposing an integrated DEMATEL–BWM–Agent-Based Modeling (ABM) framework for reconfiguring multi-actor e-waste supply chains toward enhanced circular value recovery. The framework was operationalized through ten expert panelists who validated fifteen coordination factors. DEMATEL identified causal structures and systemic influence, BWM established strategic priorities, and ABM translated these findings into agent-level behavioral rules and environmental conditions across six orchestration scenarios. The DEMATEL analysis revealed regulatory and institutional factors as primary causal drivers, with regulatory enforcement exerting the strongest systemic influence. The BWM analysis confirmed regulatory enforcement as the most strategically important factor. The ABM simulation demonstrated that combined orchestration achieved a 134.81% improvement in recovered material and a 100% collection rate, while economic incentives provided the best overall multi-metric performance. The constant recovery rate across all scenarios confirmed that improvements were driven by increased formal participation and collection throughput rather than technological efficiency, underscoring systemic coordination failures as the primary barrier to circular value recovery. The priority-causal matrix identified regulatory factors and formal-informal integration as priority intervention points offering both high causal influence and strategic importance. These findings are conditional on expert-elicited parameters and should be interpreted as exploratory simulation evidence rather than externally validated prediction. This study provides a methodological foundation for bridging causal diagnosis, strategic prioritization, and dynamic simulation in circular supply chain research, offering practical guidance for policymakers and practitioners seeking to unlock the value of the urban mine in developing economy contexts.

papers.title: From past trends to future costs: The influence of economic parameter selection on building life cycle costs in Belgium
Solvothermal carbonization of waste activated sludge using deep eutectic solvents: A solvent-directed route to tunable biochar properties
papers.abstract: The disposal of waste activated sludge (WAS) poses a persistent environmental challenge. While hydrothermal carbonization (HTC) enables sludge valorization without pre-drying, the resulting hydrochar often exhibits low carbon content, high nitrogen levels and inferior fuel properties. This study aimed to determine whether the acidity/basicity and composition of preformed DES-based media could redirect the carbonization pathways of WAS compared with conventional aqueous HTC. Unlike previous DES-assisted HTC systems, in which low-dose DESs are added to water-dominated media, the preformed DES-based media replaced the conventional bulk aqueous medium. Acidic DES showed characteristics consistent with enhanced dehydration, decarboxylation, and condensation characteristics, producing a biochar with substantially higher carbon content (21.97% vs . 9.60% for HTC), low H/C (1.57) and O/C (0.41) atomic ratios, relatively enhanced aromatic character, reduced hydrophilicity, and higher thermal stability (dominant combustion peak at 445.1 °C). In contrast, alkaline DES was associated with enhanced hydrolysis and solubilization, yielding a carbon-depleted, highly hydrophilic residue. Neutral DES exhibits intermediate behavior, producing an oxygen-enriched surface. Overall, DES chemistry produced distinct transformation pathways and tunable biochar properties relative to conventional HTC, providing insights into solvent-mediated regulation of sludge-derived carbon materials.

papers.title: Multilayer active magnetic regenerator refrigeration for high-efficiency hydrogen liquefaction
A dual spectrally driven heat balance model for optimizing atmospheric water condenser in different thermal environments
Measuring the margins: A combination-based indicator for boundary ecosystem assessment
papers.journal_name: The Science of The Total Environment

papers.title: The gap between law and practice: CSR decoupling in Tanzania's mining sector post-regulatory mandate
papers.abstract: This study contributes to CSR decoupling theory by examining stakeholder perceptions of Tanzania's 2017 mandatory Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) regulation through a case study of two major gold mines in the Geita and Mara regions. Using a sequential explanatory mixed-methods design in which we first collected survey data and then explained them through qualitative interviews, we find that respondents report CSR initiatives have become more standardised following the regulation, with more projects in education, health, and water infrastructure. However, the research reveals substantial challenges, including patterns consistent with CSR decoupling, where compliance is often symbolic rather than substantive. Bureaucratic delays, limited community involvement, and sustainability issues further undermine the regulation's effectiveness. Analysed through Institutional and Stakeholder Theories, the findings indicate that while formal practices have changed following regulatory pressure, the regulation is not perceived to have fostered genuine community ownership. The study recommends policy reforms to enforce participatory planning, independent auditing, and post-implementation support to bridge the gap between regulatory intent and community benefit.

papers.title: Construction and energy-consumption analysis of a carbon capture heating system based on waste heat utilization in a coal-fired power plant
papers.abstract: Conventionally, the heat of the reboiler in monoethanolamine (MEA)-based post-combustion CO 2 capture (PCC) system is supplied by intermediate-pressure extraction steam which temperature is higher than the needed, causing energy losses and capture cost increases. This study develops a staged, synergistic heat-supply scheme for a 600 MW unit, featuring exhaust-steam dominance, flue-gas-heat compensation and minimal extraction steam as backup. Low-pressure exhaust-steam heat is upgraded by a compression heat pump and converted to reboiler via flashing, while the waste heat of tail-end flue-gas is recovered through a closed-cycle water loop and delivered to the reboiler via water-water heat exchange and flashing; the extraction steam is introduced only to minimally close the heat balance when waste heat is insufficient. A coupled unit-PCC model is established in Ebsilon and Aspen Plus, and steady-state simulations are performed at 100%/75%/60%/50%/40% THA, followed by improved grey wolf optimizer (IGWO) optimization with the levelized cost of CO 2 capture (LCOC) as the objective. At 0.01 MPa back pressure, the proposed waste-heat strategy reduces LCOC by 19.96%, 13.57%, 11.59%, 9.64% and 6.63% across the five THA conditions relative to the benchmark, while increasing the overall energy utilization rate by 11.4% on average. At 100% THA, the waste heat utilization rate remains 92%-94% and the specific capture energy decreases from 3.20 to 3.06 GJ·tCO 2 −1 . The results demonstrate that the proposed staged framework enables effective substitution of high-grade extraction steam by in-plant low-grade waste heat over a wide load range, providing a practical pathway for cost-effective decarbonization retrofits of coal-fired units.

papers.title: Microbial community shifts accompany divergent soil carbon recovery after aquaculture-pond restoration across China's coastal wetlands
papers.abstract: Aquaculture-pond restoration may rebuild coastal soil carbon, but gains in soil organic carbon (SOC) do not necessarily indicate lower lability or uniform microbial responses. We compared aquaculture ponds and adjacent restored wetlands at 10 sites across temperate, subtropical, and tropical China. SOC, microbial biomass carbon (MBC), dissolved organic carbon (DOC), and easily oxidizable carbon (EOC) were measured at 0–15 and 15–30 cm in 160 samples, and carbon pool management index (CPMI) components were calculated. Surface-soil bacterial communities and FAPROTAX-inferred functions were characterized at three sites. Restoration increased SOC at most sites and surface MBC at five, but carbon-pool responses differed among regions. Operationally non-labile carbon (C SS = SOC − EOC), an operational estimate of less-labile carbon rather than a directly measured persistent carbon pool, increased at Yancheng, Minjiang River Estuary, Zhanjiang, and Dongzhai Port. Caofeidian, Hangzhou Bay, Zhangjiang River Estuary, and Beilun River Estuary had high carbon pool activity indices, producing CPMI values of 239.78–363.74% and indicating labile-carbon enrichment rather than uniform stabilization. Bacterial community structure was dominated by geographic separation: pond and restored samples remained close within sites, whereas alpha diversity decreased at Caofeidian, changed little at Minjiang River Estuary, and increased at Dongzhai Port. Restoration also altered dominant genera and inferred functions, including greater representation of plant-polymer degradation functions in some restored soils. DOC accounted for 46.25% of the fitted variation in the 10 dominant genera and was positively associated with Sulfurimonas , SOC, and C SS . Pond-to-wetland restoration therefore followed multiple carbon-recovery trajectories, ranging from labile-carbon pulses to accumulation of a less labile fraction. Assessments should integrate SOC quantity, carbon lability, and microbial associations.

papers.title: Cold-season grazing better sustains ecosystem multifunctionality than warm-season grazing in Tibetan alpine steppe
papers.abstract: Grazing season profoundly shapes vegetation and soil properties in alpine grasslands, yet its effects on ecosystem multifunctionality (EMF) remain poorly understood. Here, we compared grazing exclusion (GE), moderate-intensity warm-season grazing (WG), and herder-managed cold-season grazing (CG) in a cold-season pasture of the alpine steppe on the Tibetan Plateau to evaluate how seasonal grazing influences species diversity, community biomass, soil physicochemical properties, and EMF. Relative to GE, WG reduced grass dominance but increased sedge and forb proportion, while also decreasing plant height and aboveground biomass (AGB), and lowered EMF. By contrast, CG was associated with higher plant diversity and significantly elevated soil total carbon (TC) while maintaining AGB at levels comparable to GE. Effect-size analysis showed that WG significantly reduced EMF relative to GE whereas the reduction under CG did not reach significance. Correlation and path analyses further indicated that, under WG, multifunctionality was chiefly associated with the biomass pathway, which was positive but insufficient to counterbalance the direct negative effect of grazing, whereas no significant plant diversity or soil nutrient pathway was detected. Under CG, EMF was jointly associated with plant biomass, plant diversity and soil nutrients. These findings highlight the critical role of grazing season in maintaining ecosystem multifunctionality in alpine steppe, suggesting that, in cold-season pastures of the central Tibetan Plateau, cold-season grazing represents a more sustainable strategy than warm-season grazing for balancing forage production and ecological conservation.

papers.title: Function-based and PCA-derived soil health assessments reveal convergent land-use responses and functional trade-offs in Brazilian drylands
papers.abstract: Drylands are highly vulnerable to soil degradation, yet soil-health assessments remain limited for agroecosystems in the Brazilian semi-arid region, and the consistency between diagnoses produced by different assessment frameworks remains poorly understood. This study compared two soil-health assessment methods and evaluated land-use effects on soil health across Brazilian dryland agroecosystems. Soil health was assessed using (i) a soil-function framework integrating chemical, physical, and biological indicators into five functional domains and a multifunctionality metric and (ii) a variance-weighted soil health index (SHI) derived from principal component analysis (PCA). Measurements were obtained from the 0-30 cm layer across three semi-arid sites of Brazil (Sobral-CE, Betânia do Piauí-PI, and Petrolina-PE). Across sites, several diversified agroecosystems showed soil-health scores comparable to native vegetation at the time of sampling and, in some cases, higher scores for specific soil functions. The two frameworks captured similar land-use patterns but differed in indicator contributions: the PCA-derived SHI emphasized chemical variation, whereas the soil-function framework highlighted function-specific strengths and limitations. Soil health interaction functional trends showed that management effects were often expressed as functional trade-offs rather than uniform gains across all functions. Together, the results indicate that the two frameworks provide convergent overall diagnoses but complementary information, with the function-based assessment offering additional resolution for interpreting functional strengths, limitations, and trade-offs. These findings provide a consistent basis for improving soil-health assessment strategies and supporting sustainable land-use management across environmentally vulnerable dryland agroecosystems.

papers.title: Variance-based global sensitivity analysis of a stochastic Collision Risk Model: how wind turbine parameters impact seabirds
papers.abstract: To achieve the United Nation's goal of net-zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2050, we must create a world powered by renewable energy. This will rely on large-scale infrastructure projects, which must be developed with consideration for the natural environment. Offshore wind farms (OWFs), in particular, must balance the collision risk that turbines pose to seabirds with green energy targets. Within the UK and most of Europe, collision risk modelling (CRM) is a required component of Environmental Impact Assessments (EIAs) and integral for developers and regulators to gauge the risk an OWF development poses to seabird populations. Despite this, how different combinations of OWF parameters may impact collision risk estimates is poorly quantified. We assess the sensitivity of the stochastic CRM to seven key OWF parameters. Using variance-based global sensitivity analysis methodologies, we quantify results for six seabird species deemed at high risk of turbine collision. We find that the estimate of annual bird-turbine collisions is most sensitive to variation in the number of turbines and the distance between blade tip height and highest astronomical tide (air gap), whereby increasing turbine number and decreasing air gap contributed to increased collision rates. A smaller number of large turbines with greater energy output (larger rotor radius) reduced collision risk per unit energy output. These results quantify the impact of OWF parameter variation on seabird collision risk, which could be used to inform design envelopes, focusing the number of turbine scenarios that developers consider within EIAs and maximising cost-effectiveness whilst minimising seabird collision risk.

papers.title: Expansion toward risk: China's urban growth reshapes population exposure to compound environmental pressures
papers.abstract: Rapid urban expansion is altering the distribution of environmental benefits and risks. As cities grow outward, newly developed areas may face elevated exposure to multiple environmental pressures, raising concerns about whether urbanization is inadvertently exposing population toward more adverse environmental conditions. To investigate this, we use population-weighted exposure model to quantify three key environmental exposures in China's newly built-up areas from 2000 to 2018: blue-green space exposure (BGE), PM 2.5 exposure (PME), and heat stress exposure (HSE). By integrating SOM–K-means clustering and Bayesian Networks, we identify the evolution of typical environmental exposure combinations and examine their conditional dependencies. Results show that, from 2010 to 2018, BGE slightly improves, PME shows greater balance but persistent risks, while HSE intensified significantly. Clustering analysis identifies three distinct environmental exposure types: Ecological Deficiency (ED), High Environmental Cost (HEC), and Eco-Advantaged under Heat (EAH). In 2010, ED is the most prevalent type (1133 counties; 55.5%), followed by HEC (792 counties; 38.8%) and EAH (115 counties; 5.6%). By 2018, EAH increases to 386 counties (18.4%), while ED and HEC decline to 1052 (50.1%) and 664 (31.6%) counties, respectively. Notably, 466 ED counties transition to HEC, making ED-to-HEC the largest single transition. 146 counties transition from ED to EAH, indicating ecological improvement accompanied by greater heat stress. Together, these changes reveal a pattern of urban expansion toward risks. Bayesian Networks further reveal a reconfiguration in the conditional dependency structure of environmental exposures, moving from a relatively constrained dependency pattern toward a more interconnected configuration, with BGE becoming more centrally embedded in the network. This study contributes a novel integrative framework for understanding how urban expansion reshapes population exposure to compound environmental pressures and provides insights to inform risk-aware and equitable urban governance.

papers.title: SHAP-based interpretable sparse autoencoder-neural network framework for electric vehicle energy consumption forecasting
papers.abstract: Accurate energy consumption (EC) prediction for different road conditions is critical for battery management, regenerative braking control, and range estimation in battery electric vehicles (BEVs). However, conventional models trained on raw telemetry data often fail to capture complex driving dynamics due to noise and redundancy in high-dimensional inputs. To address these issues, this study proposes a novel hybrid interpretable framework that combines the sparse autoencoder, neural networks, and SHAP (Shapley additive explanations) (SAE-NN-SHAP), which effectively enables denoising, features extraction, reduces dimensionality, captures complex nonlinear characteristics and interpretable EC estimation, utilizing a real-world BEV dataset from a downloadable dynamometer database. Firstly, the enhanced SAE compresses the input space into 25 compact yet essential and meaningful information-dense latent features. Secondly, this representation is then fed into a Bayesian-optimized NN regressor. Both instantaneous (kW) and trip-level (Wh/km) EV-EC were estimated using the meaningful latent features. Thirdly, the proposed SAE-NN achieves the highest R 2 (0.991) and lowest root mean squared error (RMSE) (1.270) and mean absolute error (MAE) (0.930) among all evaluated models, reducing error by 96.67% relative to a conventional NN trained on raw features and by 14.19% relative to the strongest baseline; at the trip level, predicted and actual EC differ by less than 1% across unseen trips’ driving conditions. Finally, the innovative end-to-end SHAP-based interpretability method, combined with SAE-NN encoder weights and latent feature mapping, identifies the specific driving-dynamics factors influencing EC, including speed, regeneration, braking, torque, battery dynamics, etc. The findings provide physically meaningful explanations and actionable insights for an accurate EC and range estimation, proactive and intelligent energy management approach.

papers.title: How can new energy vehicle adoption affect urban ecological resilience? Evidence from a double/debiased machine learning method
papers.abstract: New energy vehicles (NEVs) are increasingly regarded as a driver of energy transition. However, few scholars have conducted quantitative research on the impact of the large-scale adoption of NEVs on urban ecological resilience (UER). Based on the Pressure-State-Response framework adopted to assess UER, this study utilizes panel data from 294 cities in China from 2017 to 2023 and applies a double/debiased machine learning approach to analyze the impact of NEV adoption on UER and the mechanisms driving this effect. The findings yield four main conclusions. First, the adoption of NEVs significantly increases UER. A 1% rise in NEV stock leads to a 0.0132% increase in UER, and this outcome remains stable through multiple robustness tests. Second, the mechanism exploration demonstrates that the adoption of NEVs improves UER through three channels: industrial structure upgrading, boosting green technological innovation capabilities, and raising public environmental awareness. Third, heterogeneity analysis reveals that NEV adoption has a stronger effect on UER in western cities, non-resource-based cities, and cities with stricter environmental regulations. Fourth, sub-dimensional analysis indicates that the adoption of NEVs mainly improves the state criterion and response criterion of UER, while improvements in the pressure criterion occur only in non-resource-based cities and cities with stricter environmental regulations. This study offers empirical evidence demonstrating how NEV adoption contributes to UER and drives sustainable development, emphasizing that this process requires participation from multiple stakeholders including governments, enterprises, and the public.

papers.title: Land‐Use Thresholds and Spatial Regulation Oriented Toward Ecosystem Service Supply–Demand Balance: A Case Study of Jiangxi Province
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Imbalances between ecosystem service (ES) supply and demand constrain ecological governance and sustainable development. While spatial patterns of these imbalances have been widely studied, less attention has been paid to the land‐use thresholds and regulatory mechanisms needed to maintain ES balance. Using Jiangxi Province as a case study, we developed a threshold‐based spatial regulation framework integrating ESs supply–demand ratio (SDR) analysis, key land‐use type identification, and management zoning. We quantified the spatiotemporal supply and demand of four ESs—carbon sequestration (CS), habitat quality (HQ), water yield (WY), and soil conservation (SC)—from 2003 to 2023. By combining boosted regression tree and segmented regression, we identified key land‐use types affecting ESs balance and their proportional thresholds, and used segmented regression breakpoints for differentiated spatial zoning. The results showed that although the supply of ESs generally exceeded demand, the imbalance intensified over time, particularly for WY and HQ, accompanied by significant spatial heterogeneity. Built‐up land, cropland, and forest land are the dominant land use types affecting the balance of ESs. Built‐up land negatively affected CS and HQ, cropland positively affected WY, HQ, and SC, forest land supported CS and WY, and water area promoted SC. Although land use in Jiangxi remained within the overall balance threshold, some areas approached critical points, with WY showing the smallest balanced area (75.39%). Based on current land‐use structure and ESs thresholds, three ESs management zones and 27 integrated zones were delineated, and differentiated land‐use regulation strategies were proposed, providing a scientific basis for ESs‐oriented spatial governance.

papers.title: Carbon emission and health impacts of remote working: A case study of the Helsinki capital region
papers.abstract: Remote working can reduce commuting-related carbon emissions but may also lower population physical activity levels. This study examines these trade-offs in the Helsinki Capital Region by modelling changes in commuting and worktime travel under three scenarios: no remote work, current levels, and full potential uptake. We combine demographic data, the Finnish National Travel Survey, public transport schedules, and official transport demand models to estimate impacts on CO 2 emissions and active travel. Commuting volumes are taken from demographic data containing home and workplace information of workers, and worktime trips are modelled using an agent-based synthetic population model. Under the full remote work scenario, commuting-related emissions decrease by approximately 72.9 tonnes per day, a 16.7% reduction compared to current levels. However, rebound trips during working hours offset 71.3% of these potential savings, even after accounting for reduced workplace-based trips. Health impacts were assessed using the WHO Health Economic Assessment Tool. Compared to a baseline with no remote work, current remote working levels are associated with approximately 42 additional premature deaths annually due to reduced physical activity, with a further 31 deaths under full remote work conditions. Conversely, if commuting time were repurposed for walking or cycling, up to 71 premature deaths could be avoided under current conditions and 137 under full remote working. The findings highlight the interrelationship between environmental and health dimensions of remote work. While remote working involves clear trade-offs, integrated policy approaches that combine emission reduction strategies and promotion of physical activity while limiting rebound travel are needed to achieve substantial co-benefits.

papers.title: Contested spatialities of renewable energy expansion—Introduction to the theme issue
papers.abstract: Renewable energy increasingly complements fossil fuels in meeting rising global energy demand. Yet its rollout is neither even nor free of conflict. This theme issue foregrounds the spatialities and scales of renewable energy infrastructures and examines the deeply contested nature of energy transition efforts. Drawing on case studies from Morocco, Jordan, Namibia, Mexico, Brazil, Peru and Ecuador, the contributions offer insights into recent regional developments and highlight transregional and cross-scalar interrelations. They connect place-based research on contested energy projects in political ecology, geography and anthropology with nation-focused analyses of energy transition policy, and approach scale as an unfolding field of contestation. In doing so, they challenge notions of a homogeneous “local” in analyses of energy conflict and move beyond methodological nationalism while still recognizing the significance of the national scale. Together, the theme issue demonstrates the value of relational approaches for disentangling and understanding the contested geographies of contemporary renewable energy expansion.

Their recommendations focused heavily on safeguards, evaluation, and governance of AI models and systems, largely overlooking the risks that arise from the interactions of AI with people and institutions. AI safety needs to be addressed at the level of the human–AI system, not the AI model alone.

Thermodynamic origin of the phonon Hall effect in a honeycomb antiferromagnet
papers.abstract: The underlying mechanism of the thermal Hall effect generated by phonons in a variety of insulators is yet to be identified. In this work, we report on a sizable thermal Hall conductivity in nickel phosphorus trisulfide (NiPS 3 ), a van der Waals stack of honeycomb layers with a zigzag antiferromagnetic order. The longitudinal (κ aa ) and the transverse (κ ab ) thermal conductivities peak at the same temperature, and the thermal Hall angle, at this peak, respects a previously identified bound. The amplitude of κ ab is extremely sensitive to the amplitude of magnetization along the b axis but is not correlated with the phonon mean free path, which points to an intrinsic origin.

papers.title: Wireless electrocatalytic closed-loop system for drug-free management of diabesity
papers.abstract: Lifestyle-related type 2 diabetes and associated obesity (diabesity) affect >2.5 billion people worldwide and impose nearly $3 trillion in annual health care costs. We developed an implantable, wirelessly powered electrocatalytic closed-loop health optimization (ECHO) device containing platinum-decorated gold nanoclusters embedded in graphite felt that enabled selective, electrically tunable oxidation of blood glucose to renally cleared gluconate. In type 2 diabetic mice, wireless, low-power activation (0.75 volts, 10 milliamperes) restored glucose homeostasis within 1 hour, shifted metabolism from glucose to lipid utilization, reduced body weight and triglycerides, and increased circulating free fatty acids and ketone bodies without detectable hypoglycemia or adverse physiological, inflammatory, or behavioral effects during 6 weeks of treatment. Coupling this ECHO device to a commercial continuous glucose monitoring system enabled autonomous, smartphone-controlled, drug-free closed-loop management of experimental diabesity.

papers.title: Visualizing symmetry-broken Chern insulators and their quantum melting
papers.abstract: In the presence of a magnetic field, electronic states of moiré quantum materials develop a Hofstadter spectrum that provides a distinctive setting for studying the interplay between band topology and strong electron-electron interaction. Using scanning tunneling microscopy, we studied Hofstadter’s states in bilayer graphene aligned with hexagonal boron nitride and directly visualized the formation of interaction-driven symmetry breaking Chern insulators. Our measurements revealed the formation of phases that double, triple, or quadruple the moiré unit cell at fractional filling of the Hofstadter bands as well as states with complex intra–unit cell wave functions. We visualized two distinct quantum phenomena in different Chern states, including quantum melting driven by the appearance and proliferation of topological defects and a quantum transition co-occurring with phase competition and separation.

papers.title: BAK and BAX form a multiprotein complex to drive mtDNA efflux and caspase-independent cell death
papers.abstract: The apoptotic regulators BAX and BAK, once activated, form homo-oligomers to trigger mitochondrial outer membrane permeabilization (MOMP), activating the apoptosome and caspases. Activation of BAX-BAK without apoptosome activation triggers sustained efflux of mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) and caspase-independent cell death. However, the molecular basis of mtDNA efflux remains unclear. We purified a macromolecular complex comprising BAK, BAX, activator BH3-only molecules, voltage-dependent anion channels 1 and 2 (VDAC1 and VDAC2), and prohibitins that released mtDNA from mitoplasts. BAX-BAK activation resulted in VDAC closure, mitochondrial calcium influx, and mtDNA efflux. Loss of VDAC1, VDAC2, or prohibitins prevented BAX-BAK activation–induced mtDNA efflux and caspase-independent cell death without affecting MOMP or mitochondrial inner membrane herniation. These findings support differential regulation of cytochrome c and mtDNA efflux by distinct BAX-BAK complexes.
