By identifying limitations in prevailing experimental practices and aligning equilibrium characterization, kinetic modeling, and sorbent evaluation with application-relevant conditions, this review provides a framework for generating mechanistically grounded sorption data to support material selection and translate laboratory-derived sorption data into process design parameters for pilot- and full-scale TrOC treatment systems.

papers.title: No Significant Elimination of Perfluoroctanesulfonate and Other Common Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances by Adult Fathead Minnows, Pimephales promelas
papers.abstract: Abstract Bioaccumulation dynamics of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) remain poorly understood, and kinetic-based information is lacking across environmental gradients, particularly for Cyprinidae, the largest and most diverse fish family. We examined the influences of pH (6.5, 7.5) and salinity (0.3 g/L, 3.0 g/L) on uptake and elimination kinetics of 19 PFAS, which were selected at low concentrations not eliciting standardized adverse outcomes, in the common Cyprinidae, Pimephales promelas. These PFAS consisted of short- and long-chain perfluoroalkyl carboxylic acids (PFCAs) and perfluoroalkyl sulfonates (PFSAs), a sulfonamide, and fluorotelomer sulfonates. Water, whole-body tissue, and plasma were collected over time, and samples were analyzed via liquid chromatography tandem mass spectrometry. Rapid uptake was observed in tissue, reaching pseudo-steady-state conditions within 24–96 h of exposure initiation; uptake rates increased with chain length but were not influenced (p > 0.05) by pH or salinity. During four separate experiments, no significant (p > 0.05) elimination was observed for PFDA, PFDoDA, PFTeDA, total PFOS, PFOSA, and 8:2 FTSA. Kinetic-based bioaccumulation factors (BAFs) increased with chain length for PFCAs and PFSAs, and exceedances of BAF cutoff values were identified. No significant (p > 0.05) elimination of these PFAS indicates that Cyprinidae should be considered during future bioaccumulation studies.

papers.title: Economic Potential of Nuclear Power in the Transportation Sector: Analysis of E-Fuels as An Alternative Fuel for Total Cost of Ownership and Vehicle Emissions
papers.abstract: Abstract Advanced nuclear reactors could expand U.S. nuclear energy beyond electricity generation into transportation by supplying heat and power for hydrogen and synthetic hydrocarbon fuel production. We evaluated nuclear-enabled hydrogen for fuel cell electric vehicles (FCEVs) and nuclear-derived electro-fuels (e-fuels) for internal combustion engine vehicles (ICEVs) and hybrid vehicles across selected light-, medium-, and heavy-duty classes. Economic performance was assessed using total cost of ownership (TCO), and environmental performance was evaluated using life-cycle emissions. We then estimated carbon abatement costs for alternative fuel/vehicle pathways relative to conventional gasoline and diesel systems. Our findings indicate that conventional ICEVs fueled by gasoline or diesel generally remain the lowest-cost options in 2035. For small sport utility vehicles (SUVs), however, hybrid vehicles using nuclear-based e-fuels and battery electric vehicles (BEVs) with home charging increase TCO modestly relative to gasoline vehicles, while e-fuels achieve the lowest emissions among the alternatives. In long-haul trucking, hydrogen and e-fuels show potential, with marginal TCO increases relative to conventional systems and relatively low abatement costs. Although hydrogen and e-fuels produced with advanced nuclear reactors remain relatively expensive, continued advances in reactors, electrolysis, and fuel synthesis, together with scale economies, could improve competitiveness, diversify transportation fuel options, and reduce emissions.

papers.title: Evaluating Emergency Emission Controls During an Unprecedented Regional Haze Event Using Causal Machine Learning
papers.abstract: Abstract Emergency emission controls are widely implemented to mitigate severe haze, yet their effectiveness is difficult to disentangle from meteorological variability and concurrent changes in activities. Here, we develop a three-step evaluation approach integrating air quality meteorological normalization, augmented synthetic control, and machine-learning prediction to causally quantify intervention-attributable changes in local emission strength and ambient pollutant concentrations. Applied to Shijiazhuang’s unprecedented 45-day “Sharp Sword to Cut Haze” campaign in 2016, the approach revealed that local emission strengths of PM2.5, PM10, SO2, NO2, and CO were reduced by 4.3%, 4.8%, 15.8%, 5.8%, and 15.3%, respectively. Corresponding concentrations fell by 42.1 (14.8%), 47.4 (12.4%), 13.8 (16.6%), 15.8 (15.5%) μg·m–3, and 0.9 mg·m–3 (19.6%). Observation-based PM2.5 source apportionment results independently supported these estimates: contributions from vehicle emissions, steelmaking, and coal combustion were 4.1%, 11.0%, and 21.7% lower, respectively, than during the corresponding period in 2017. Despite stringent controls, PM2.5 averaged 243.2 μg·m–3 during the intervention period. Thus, stringent local controls substantially reduced emissions, but regional transport and unfavorable meteorology partly offset the resulting air quality benefits, highlighting the need for coordinated regional mitigation.

papers.title: Root-associated microbial community dynamics in tobacco following topping: implications for nicotine degradation
A physics-guided grey-box residual framework for cleaner production and energy-efficiency optimization in aluminum electrolysis
Assessing the circular transition progress across Pakistan's textile supply chain: Empirical evidence from the field
Digital economy-driven resilience enhancement in the global food supply chain
papers.abstract: The global food system is undergoing significant changes due to the digital economy, but the specific impact of this on the resilience of the food supply chain remains unclear. This study examines the impact of the digital economy on the resilience of food supply chains in 106 countries between 2013 and 2023. The findings show that although the digital economy is growing internationally, its development is still unequal, especially in terms of digital market and digital governance. Food trade networks are becoming more interconnected; trade in plant-based foods is more geographically diverse, while trade in animal-based foods is more closely linked. Resilience patterns reveal significant disparities, with high-income countries continuing to have a distinct edge. For animal-based food supply chains, digital technology is the main source of resilience (35.6% of total feature importance); for plant-based food supply chains, on the other hand, GDP is the most important factor (54.2%). The degree to which different digital economy factors affect resilience is determined by threshold effects. Critical levels usually fall between 36 and 74 on the digital economy index, depending on the food type and digital dimension. These results highlight the necessity of category-specific approaches to help create more resilient and sustainable global food supply chains.

papers.title: Predictive energy management for hybrid amphibious vehicles integrating operating condition recognition and condition-matched speed prediction
papers.abstract: The substantial differences between land and water operating conditions, abrupt power-demand variations, and multi-objective optimization conflicts pose significant challenges to real-time energy management for hybrid amphibious vehicles. This study proposes a coordinated predictive energy management strategy integrating online operating-condition recognition and speed prediction to improve power response, fuel economy, and battery safety. A switchable hybrid powertrain operates in series mode on land and parallel mode on water. Representative operating conditions are identified offline using kernel principal component analysis (KPCA) and K-means++ clustering, and the resulting labels are used to train a long short-term memory (LSTM) network for online recognition. A dual-path condition-dependent adaptation mechanism is established: discrete condition labels select the corresponding condition-matched variational mode decomposition–radial basis function (VMD-RBF) speed predictors, while continuous distances to cluster centers adaptively adjust the power-response and fuel-economy weights of the predictive equivalent consumption minimization strategy (ECMS). Real-vehicle tests show that the proposed strategy reduces the mean 0–100 km/h acceleration time on land by 14.9% compared with the conventional predictive strategy, avoids the engine-overload shutdown observed in six of ten rule-based tests, and reduces the mean 0–60 km/h acceleration time on water by 9.2% compared with the rule-based strategy. The proposed framework provides an effective approach for coordinated energy management across amphibious operating domains.

A mechanistic-data fusion framework for lifetime prediction of PEMFCs under cross-temperature condition
papers.abstract: The performance degradation of proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs) has always been a key issue restricting their large-scale commercial application. As PEMFCs are increasingly used in heavy-duty vehicles, the demanding load conditions widen the operating temperature range of stack and lead to cross-temperature operation conditions. Under these conditions, the degradation behavior of PEMFCs becomes highly nonlinear, posing significant challenges to the accuracy of existing lifetime prediction models. Therefore, this study conducts cross-temperature durability experiments and proposes a mechanistic-data fusion framework named Freq-PEANet (Frequency-based Period-wise & Exogenous-Endogenous Association Network). It hierarchically couples a Frequency Filter Block and a Times Block to capture nonlinear degradation dynamics by jointly modeling the global trend and multi-period temporal variations. A Cross-Attention Block is further introduced to fuse recovery features derived from distribution of relaxation times (DRT) analysis and operating variables as exogenous inputs for assisting the endogenous target. This block assigns time-varying weights to exogenous variables at each time step, improving information utilization of exogenous variable. Compared with best-performing benchmark models, the proposed framework reduces the root-mean-square error by 26.74% on the static dataset and by a significantly higher 42.73% on the cross-temperature dataset. This method provides a new interpretable framework to predict PEMFC lifetime under cross-temperature conditions.

papers.title: A Deep Reinforcement learning approach for Profit-Maximizing and robust control of hybrid CSP-PV plants with Power-to-Heat integration

Application of Organic Superabsorbent Cellulosic Polymers ( OSCPs ) and Cyanobacteria on Reduction of Aeolian Losses
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Establishing biocrusts on sandy surfaces in harsh desert environments presents significant challenges due to extreme ecological conditions. To address these challenges, this study examined the effects of two organic superabsorbent cellulosic polymers (OSCPs)—carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC) and guar gum (GUA)—on the establishment of cyanobacterial crusts on aeolian sands, specifically using a consortium of Nostoc sp. and Microcoleus vaginatus . The optimal concentrations of GUA and CMC for maximum cyanobacterial growth were determined through preliminary optimization assays. The resulting suspensions, combining OSCPs and cyanobacteria, were applied to sandy substrates. After 60 days of inoculation, the cyanobacterial crusts were analyzed for exopolysaccharide (EPS) accumulation, chlorophyll a content, physical and chemical properties, shear strength, and compressive strength. Additionally, wind tunnel tests were conducted to measure aeolian mass flux under the different treatments. Results indicated that the cyanobacteria + CMC treatment outperformed all others, increasing chlorophyll a by 114% and EPS production by 108% to 280% depending on the EPS fraction. This treatment also enhanced organic carbon and nitrogen accumulation, crust thickness (~21 mm), shear strength (51.39 kPa), and available water capacity (+110%). Furthermore, it raised the wind erosion threshold velocity from 11.5 to 19.7 m s −1 , reducing aeolian mass flux by over 98% at wind speeds up to 19.7 m s −1 . In contrast, GUA alone resulted in the lowest compressive strength and mass flux rates. These findings suggest that combining cyanobacteria with OSCPs, particularly CMC, is an effective strategy for promoting biocrust formation and mitigating soil erosion in arid environments.

papers.title: Public support for regulatory research on the potential ecological effects of RF-EMF
“Aging-out” of the out-of-home care system: What young people and carers say helps and hinders this transition
How Peer Working Hours Shape Individual Preferences: Experimental Evidence From Germany
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines how colleagues' working hours influence individual working hours preferences. We conducted a representative survey experiment among German employees in 2024, in which participants received randomized information about colleagues' working hours. We combine the survey experiment with quantitative and LLM‐based text analysis of an open‐ended question. Colleagues' hours causally influence stated preferences, yet respondents' explanations focus on personal reasons. This shows that social factors influence working time preferences alongside the individual considerations that respondents most frequently identify. Our findings highlight the importance of collective action for working‐time policy and reveal methodological considerations for studying labor supply preferences.

Trihalomethane Exposure, Seminal Plasma Metabolomics, and Semen Quality in Healthy Men: A Meet-in-the-Middle Approach
papers.abstract: Abstract Exposure to trihalomethanes (THMs) has been linked to reduced human semen quality, but the critical windows of vulnerability and underlying biological mechanisms remain unclear. We therefore measured untargeted seminal plasma metabolomics to identify metabolic biomarkers and biological pathways linking blood THM concentrations to repeated measurements of semen quality (4146 measurements over a 3 month follow-up period) among 762 healthy Chinese men. We found inverse associations between blood THM concentrations (i.e., chloroform, bromodichloromethane, and chlorinated THMs) and semen volume and total sperm count (all P values <0.05), which were most pronounced for exposure measured 70–90 days prior to semen collection (corresponding to the early stage of spermatogenesis). Metabolome-wide association analyses identified 90 metabolites that were simultaneously associated with blood THM concentrations and sperm-quality parameters. Mediation analyses further revealed that 44 metabolites, enriched in the pathways of unsaturated fatty acid biosynthesis, steroid hormone biosynthesis, arachidonic acid metabolism, linoleic acid metabolism, pantothenate and CoA biosynthesis, and β-alanine metabolism, mediated a considerable proportion (8.1–41.3%) of the inverse relationships between THM exposure and semen quality. Our results suggest that THM exposure during the early stage of spermatogenesis is associated with reduced human semen quality, potentially driven by perturbations in lipid metabolism, steroid hormone synthesis, and antioxidant-related metabolisms.

papers.title: Linking Protist-Bacteria Trophic Interactions to Organic Matter Chemodiversity: Insights from a Coal Mine Ecological Restoration Chronosequence
papers.abstract: Abstract Restoring soil biota and dissolved organic matter (DOM) is essential for sustainable ecological restoration of coal mine sites. Protists, as key microbial predators, are recognized as regulators of multiple belowground processes, yet their roles in shaping DOM during ecological restoration remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated a field-scale coal mine ecological restoration chronosequence using vegetation surveys, ultrahigh-resolution Fourier-transform ion cyclotron resonance mass spectrometry (FT-ICR-MS), and high-throughput Illumina sequencing. Restoration increased plant diversity, coverage, and aboveground biomass, which are key resources for soil organic matter inputs. Soil DOM shifted toward more thermodynamically stable compounds, with enhanced chemodiversity during the restoration process. Protistan diversity, particularly of phagotrophic taxa, increased with restoration age, potentially exerting top-down control that increased bacterial diversity but suppressed fungal diversity. Co-occurrence network analysis and random forest modeling revealed that plant biomass was positively linked with phagotrophic diversity, which might influence DOM composition through direct transformation of organic matter (OM) or indirect regulation of bacterial transformation of OM, contributing to the accumulation of recalcitrant molecules with high stability. Together, these findings uncover a previously unrecognized trophic cascade linking protists to DOM chemodiversity at the molecular level, highlighting the importance of integrating protistan regulation into soil ecological restoration strategies for mine sites.

papers.title: Winter and Summer Differences in Oxylipin Responses to Ambient Particles: Roles of Sizes and Constituents
papers.abstract: Abstract Ambient fine particulate matter (PM2.5) has been associated with increased mortality risk, but whether it is more harmful on colder or warmer days is unclear. Here, we investigate seasonal variations in PM2.5 mass, sizes, constituents, and their association with oxylipin changes in humans. In a panel study of 123 adults in Beijing, we measured 27 PM2.5 metrics and five circulating lipoxygenase-derived oxylipins (i.e., leukotriene B4 [LTB4], 5-, 8-, 12-, and 15-hydroxyeicosatetraenoic acid [HETE]) across winter and summer. PM2.5 exposure was associated with peak oxylipin increases at lag 0–1 days. Across particle size fractions and constituents, oxylipin increases ranged from 3.3% to 114.2%, with the most robust associations for ultrafine particles, accumulation mode particles, organic carbon, and chloride. Furthermore, an exposure-response relationship between UFP and oxylipins was observed only in summer. An IQR increase in UFP was associated with oxylipin changes of 12.9–97.7% in summer and −7.7 to 18.8% in winter. Conversely, oxylipin increases associated with accumulation mode particles and organic carbon were greater in winter. These findings suggest that the sizes and constituents of PM2.5 may partially explain the seasonal difference in the health effect of PM2.5 exposure, helping identify components associated with stronger biomarker responses in specific seasons.

papers.title: Root-applied taurine reduces grain cadmium and improves rice yield by decreasing Cd transport and increasing Cd retention in roots
Dormant and green-up season mowing maximizes productivity-derived vegetation carbon input potential in coastal wetlands
papers.abstract: Managing coastal Phragmites australis wetlands through seasonal mowing can alter belowground C input potential and soil CO 2 and CH 4 fluxes. However, how mowing timing affects vegetation structure and belowground C input potential across phenological stages remains poorly resolved. To address this management gap, we conducted a long-term randomized-block experiment in the Yellow River Delta, comparing an unmown control (CK) with annual mowing at green-up (March, 3M), peak growth (July, 7M), and dormancy (December, 12M). We quantified vegetation structure and production, estimated belowground net primary productivity (BNPP) using ingrowth cores, operationally estimated heterotrophic respiration ( R h ) using root exclusion and derived autotrophic respiration ( R a ) as the difference between total soil respiration and R h , measured soil CH 4 flux, and conducted scenario-based regional scaling of BNPP-derived belowground C input potential using the remotely mapped P. australis area. BNPP-derived belowground C input potential was greatest under December mowing, intermediate under March mowing, and lowest under July mowing. Targeted regressions showed positive associations of shallow coarse-root biomass with R a and shallow fine-root biomass with R h , whereas plant height was negatively associated with soil CH 4 flux. Under the full-coverage scenario, additional regional BNPP-derived belowground C input potential reached 0.170 ± 0.018, 0.100 ± 0.036, and 0.043 ± 0.017 Tg C yr −1 under 12M, 3M, and 7M, respectively. December mowing therefore produced the largest BNPP-derived belowground C input potential among the tested timings, whereas March mowing showed an intermediate response. Scenario-scaled C input potential should not be interpreted as realized ecosystem C sequestration or net climate benefit.

papers.title: Plant-derived high-C:P amendments enhance legacy phosphorus utilization in phosphorus-enriched greenhouse soil via stoichiometric regulation and microbial functional coupling
papers.abstract: Long-term intensive fertilization has accumulated large legacy phosphorus (P) pools in greenhouse vegetable soils, while substituting chemical fertilizers with livestock manure may exacerbate soil P loading. We evaluated pakchoi growth and legacy P utilization in an acidified, P-enriched greenhouse soil, comparing an unfertilized, unamended control (CK) with equal-carbon inputs of low-C:P, high-P chicken manure (OF) and high-C:P, low-P plant-derived amendments: alkali lignin (AL), straw (ST), and alkali-lignin-modified straw (AST). Compared with the OF, shoot dry weight was 47.0% and 12.4% higher under ST and AST, respectively, while shoot P uptake increased by 80.2% and 76.8%. OF produced an apparent P surplus, whereas ST and AST generated negative apparent P balances, indicating current-season amendment P inputs could not offset shoot P removal and supporting enhanced legacy P utilization without further accumulation of available or labile inorganic P. Plant-derived amendments increased soil C:P and pH, generally enhanced C- and N-acquiring enzyme activities, and reduced ecoenzymatic vector angles, alleviating relative microbial P-acquisition limitation. Metagenomic and random forest analyses showed that enhanced P acquisition was not primarily linked to a single P-cycling process, but more closely associated with resource stoichiometry and soluble N status, alongside coordinated restructuring of microbial C degradation, N transformation, and P-cycling functions. Overall, AL most strongly ameliorated acidity but elicited weak plant responses; ST produced the strongest biomass response, while AST maintained comparably high P acquisition and markedly improved soil pH. These high-C:P amendments provide a low-P alternative to high-P manure inputs, offering a strategy for reduced-P management and legacy P utilization.

papers.title: Honeycomb monolith-based multichannel reactor for methane bioconversion into ectoine
papers.abstract: A novel gas-liquid multichannel bioreactor based on cordierite honeycomb monoliths was engineered and operated under internal gas and liquid recirculation for methane bioconversion into ectoine. The assessment of the volumetric gas-liquid mass transfer coefficients for O 2 ( k L a O 2 ) in this novel bioreactor showed values up to 1472.7 ± 111.6 h −1 , representing an increase of one order of magnitude over conventional bubble column reactors. Bubble measurements were consistent with a flow regime compatible with Taylor-flow operation, suggesting that liquid-film renewal was likely a major contributor to mass-transfer enhancement. During diluted-methane bioconversion into ectoine, stable operation at relatively high gas and liquid recirculation rates was achieved after gradual enrichment of the halotolerant mixed methanotrophic culture, potentially because of the associated hydrodynamic shear stress. After inoculum adaptation, methane bioconversion efficiencies and capacities of up to 72.9% and 45 g m 3 h −1 , with an ectoine concentration of 32.1 mg gVSS −1 , were achieved when operating with a gas residence time of 30 min, and gas and liquid recirculation of 40 L min −1 and 25 L min −1 , respectively (corresponding to a k L a O 2 of 679.5 ± 57.3 h −1 ). Process performance was supported by a well-adapted inoculum dominated by Methylophaga , Methylonatrum and Methylotuvimicrobium , which accumulated 44% of the relative abundances. Monoliths as microchannels in high gas-liquid mass transfer reactors represent a promising platform for methane valorisation, but further optimisation of operational parameters is required to intensify ectoine production from methane.

papers.title: A multi-scale framework for long-term prediction of algal bloom occurrence using satellite-derived mapping and catchment-scale drivers
From data to carbon efficiency: Data as a production factor and corporate carbon intensity
Does an invasive aquatic plant influence lakefront property values? Revisiting the impact of Eurasian watermilfoil using an event study analysis
Spatial prediction of coastal groundwater nitrate using combined feature selection and explainable machine learning
papers.abstract: Groundwater nitrate contamination is an important issue affecting groundwater quality and safety. Accurate prediction of groundwater nitrate concentrations and identification of key influencing factors are of great significance for groundwater pollution prevention and water resource management. Taking the lower reaches of the Huangshui River as the study area, 452 groundwater samples collected in July 2023 were used to predict groundwater NO 3 − -N concentrations by integrating Spearman correlation analysis, self-organizing map (SOM)-Boruta feature selection, Random Forest (RF), Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), RF-XGBoost stacking modeling, SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), and geographic information system (GIS)-based spatial mapping. The dataset was divided into 361 training samples and 91 independent test samples, and model robustness was further assessed through cross-validation and 1000 repeated resampling runs. The SOM-Boruta method selected eight key variables: TDS, SO 4 2− , TH, Cl − , NH 3 -N, COD, F − and pH. All three models showed good predictive ability, with the RF-XGBoost stacking model yielding the most favorable test-set performance (R 2 = 0.881, RMSE = 13.266 mg/L, MAE = 9.284 mg/L).SHAP analysis identified TDS as the predictor with the highest contribution to model predictions across the three models. GIS-based RF-XGBoost prediction showed groundwater NO 3 − -N concentrations ranging from 5.31 to 59.83 mg/L, with higher values in the north, lower values in the south and transitional values in the central area. These findings support groundwater nitrate spatial identification, water quality assessment and regional groundwater resource protection.

papers.title: Spatial differentiation and urban environmental associations of avian co-occurrence network roles: Evidence from Guangzhou, China

Insight into the urine progression and DOM transformation mechanism for sustainable nitrogen-water synergistic recovery in space stations
papers.abstract: Urine represents a critical water resource for closing the water and nitrogen loop in life support systems during manned space exploration. This work focuses on the impacts of pretreatment agents on urine progression and dissolved organic matter (DOM) transformation during long-term storage, with a perspective towards technology innovation for nitrogen-water synergistic recovery from urine in space. Urea hydrolysis, driven by microbial activity, was identified as the primary driver of urine variation, initiating rapid changes within 8 h of storage. The time point of significant DOM variation was prior to urea hydrolysis, and fresh humic-like substance from recent biological activity, which were dominated the variations of DOM. Meanwhile, the increasing NH 4 + -N and pH can resulted in precipitation, such as MgNH 4 PO 4 , which showed potential risks to the urine transport and treatment devices. Both H 2 SO 4 and CrO 3 showed excellent urine stabilization performance with urea hydrolysis rates of 0.10∼0.17 within 336 h. However, there have divergent DOM transformation pathways and sediment components: H 2 SO 4 influenced the fresh DOM by microbial inhibition through acidic environment, and uric acid and CaSO 4 were the main sediments; CrO 3 could enhance the degradation of protein-like substances by strong oxidation, and generate Cr-containing dense sediments. Therefore, the selection criteria for technologies and pretreatment agents on urine recovery are proposed, which encourage the integration of membrane separation and biosynthesis. This work reveals the dynamic variation and the mechanism of pretreatment agents during urine storage, which offers the basis for innovation in urine recovery for deep space exploration.

papers.title: A sensitivity-informed correlation-based framework for detecting runoff pollutant hotspots in grazed catchments: Implications for precision cattle grazing to improve water quality
papers.abstract: Cattle grazing is a known source of water pollution. Identifying areas within grazinglands where cattle activity contributes most to downstream water quality impairment is important for effective management. This study presents a framework to detect these runoff pollutant hotspots. The framework is based on Pearson correlation coefficients between cattle presence across the catchment and water quality at the outlet. Cattle locations were recorded at 5–60 min time intervals using Virtual Fencing (VF) technology in three experimental catchments located in north-central Oklahoma, USA, two under rotational grazing and one continuously grazed. Escherichia coli (E. coli) , total Kjeldahl nitrogen (TKN), and total phosphorus (TP) were measured during runoff events between March 2022, and June 2024. The spatial and temporal scales at which runoff quality was most affected by cattle presence were determined through a sensitivity analysis of grid cell size (GCS), time interval ( Δ T ) between consecutive cattle Global Positioning System (GPS) records, and pollutant half-life (HL) representing manure decay. The strongest grid cell-scale correlations between water quality parameters and cattle presence ranged from 0.48 to 0.83 for E. coli , 0.70 to 0.86 for TKN, and 0.67 to 0.90 for TP. These hotspots were detected using grid cell sizes ranging from 70 m × 70 m to 100 m × 100 m, and half-life values ranging from 3 to 12 days for E. coli , 3–23 days for TKN, and 3–20 days for TP. Compared to the continuously grazed catchment, hotspots in rotationally grazed, VF-managed catchments with cattle exclusion from riparian buffers were fewer, diffused, and located away from streams. Significant positive spatial autocorrelation was observed in five hotspot maps. Hotspot identification was influenced by pollutant persistence and grazing management, with rotational grazing showing fewer and more diffuse hotspots than continuous grazing.

Patently peculiar: Patents and innovation in the United Kingdom of the Netherlands
papers.abstract: Abstract We study the patent system of the United Kingdom of the Netherlands (1815–30), a post‐Napoleonic state which brought together an early industrializing region that subsequently became Belgium with a later‐industrializing one comprising what is now the Netherlands. The system formally distinguished between patents of invention and patents of importation, protecting both domestic inventions and the introduction of foreign technologies. It also granted administrators considerable discretion over patent fees, terms, and conditions. Using a new hand‐collected dataset covering all patent applications, including those granted, withdrawn, and rejected, we analyse application outcomes across sectors, regions, and patent types. We show that administrators systematically differentiated between patents of invention and importation in ways consistent with a technology policy that encouraged the domestic introduction of useful foreign technologies. We also find that administrative decisions reflected assessments of novelty, utility, and applicant characteristics, without evidence of systematic discrimination. Despite high fees, the system remained broadly accessible across social classes. Patents of invention were more commonly associated with technically skilled inventors, whereas patents of importation were more often sought by commercially oriented applicants. Overall, the regime combined accessibility with substantive screening and illustrates how discretionary patent administration could support technology transfer during a formative period of industrialization.

papers.title: Demographic Ageing and the Reshaping of Global Processed Food Trade
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines how demographic ageing shapes global processed food trade by estimating trade‐income elasticities (IEs) that incorporate the influence of the aged population share, within a structural gravity model. The findings indicate that ageing amplifies IEs for processed food imports in both developed and developing economies while dampening them for domestic processed foods in developing economies. Import IEs in developed economies remain above unity, while those in developing economies are projected to rise from about 0.6 to nearly 1.3 in coming decades. Country‐ and product‐level estimates reveal substantial heterogeneity, with pronounced increases in import IEs for major economies and for processed meat, fish, fruit and vegetables, cocoa and sugar confectionery, and drinks. The contrasting responses of imported and domestically supplied processed foods may partly reflect differences in product composition. These findings highlight the importance of accounting for demographic ageing and product‐level heterogeneity when assessing future processed food trade.

papers.title: Reverse auctions for drought‐responsive water buybacks: Evidence from co‐designed lab and field experiments
papers.abstract: Abstract Protecting endangered aquatic species while sustaining farming communities can require water buyback programs that are both cost‐effective and responsive to the variability and unpredictability of drought conditions. Working in close partnership with The Nature Conservancy and the Georgia Water Planning and Policy Center, we co‐design parallel laboratory experiments and high‐stakes framed field experiments to evaluate alternative reverse auction designs. The framed field experiments involved over $650,000 in real payments to irrigators making decisions about their own fields. Results from this lab‐to‐field experimental framework show that streamflow‐based targeting improves cost‐effectiveness relative to acre‐based targeting, and that flexible contracts linking irrigation suspension to actual streamflow conditions outperform rigid contracts when commitments must be made before drought conditions are known. This study demonstrates how integrated lab and framed field experiments can be embedded within real‐world institutional settings to generate policy‐relevant evidence for agri‐environmental programs.

papers.title: The Effects of Promotion Patterns Within Audit Firms on Audit Adjustments: Insights Into Promotion Speed and Flexibility
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT This study investigates how promotion patterns within audit firms impact audit adjustments. Using detailed data on partner promotions in Chinese audit firms, we measure firm‐level promotion speed and promotion flexibility and examine their effects on audit adjustments. We find that auditors in audit firms with faster and more flexible promotion patterns are more likely to make audit adjustments. Additional analyses show that firmwide promotion speed and flexibility are positively associated with the likelihood of both upward and downward adjustments, as well as the magnitude of audit adjustments. Cross‐sectional analyses indicate that the effects of promotion patterns on audit adjustments are more pronounced in larger audit firms, with the effect of promotion speed being stronger among lower ranked auditors facing greater promotion incentives. Additionally, fast and flexible promotion patterns improve audit efficiency. Organizational reform also shapes promotion patterns, as the adoption of the limited liability partnership (LLP) structure is associated with faster partner promotion. Overall, this study provides initial evidence of the effect of promotion patterns on audit outcomes.

papers.title: Between history and ideology. The Middle Ages and Medievalism in Italian economic thought on corporations
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the relationship between corporatist economic thought and medieval guilds (here: corporations), exploring whether and how medieval ideas influenced various strands of Italian corporatism, and how concepts from the Middle Ages were received and transformed. The study focuses on how those concepts – in particular corporation-based economic structures – were reinterpreted to legitimise modern economic visions. After defining mediaevalism and corporatism, it classifies different forms of Italian corporatism and highlights the influence of Giuseppe Toniolo on the Catholic strand of corporatist thought, the only one explicitly shaped by historical studies on the Middle Ages. Ultimately, it assesses how references to the Middle Ages served ideological purposes, rooting novel economic visions in a selectively reconstructed medieval past.
papers.journal_name: The European Journal of the History of Economic Thought

papers.title: Measurement Error, Manipulation, and the Value of Short‐Term Performance in Job Retention
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT This paper studies how the accuracy of a short‐term performance measure affects its value when a principal decides whether to retain or fire an agent, who can manipulate that measure. Compared with ignoring performance and never firing the agent, the performance measure is valuable when the savings in the expected cost of the retention error is more than the expected cost of the firing error. A more accurate performance measure can have a non‐monotonic effect on its value: Greater accuracy improves the principal's ability to correctly identify the agent, which increases efficient firing, but it causes the incompetent agent to increase manipulation to avoid being fired, which increases inefficient retention. With a less accurate performance measure, the incompetent agent has weaker incentives for manipulation, and an increase in accuracy increases its value due to the identification effect. With a more accurate performance measure, the manipulation effect dominates, and an increase in accuracy decreases its value. The results imply that the principal prefers an imperfect performance measure when the agent can choose the level of manipulation.

papers.title: ‘I'm Not Smoking; I'm Just Vaping’: Deciphering the Reasons for and Against Vaping and Intention to Quit Among Young Consumers
papers.abstract: Abstract Vaping has become a defining feature of youth culture and a fast‐expanding consumer practice, yet little is known about how young people rationalize their continued use despite awareness of health risks and social controversy. Drawing on behavioral reasoning theory (BRT) and insights from social identity theory (SIT), this study examines how young consumers construct, compare and prioritize reasons for and against vaping under conditions of uncertainty, thereby deciphering their intention to quit. Using a mixed‐methods design, it combines 21 in‐depth interviews with a survey of 804 young adult vapers in the UK. The findings indicate that conspiracy beliefs, scepticism and perceived uncountability are positively associated with relative disadvantage, which in turn predicts ambivalence and subsequently intention to quit. Ambivalence, in turn, is linked with stronger intention to quit, particularly among individuals with a strong future time perspective, whereas fear of social exclusion appears to weaken the effect of relative disadvantage on ambivalence. The study advances BRT by using evaluability as a conceptual lens to explain why certain reasons become more salient. By integrating cognitive reasoning with social identity, it offers theoretical and policy insights for enhancing health communication and fostering more informed behavioural engagement among young consumers.

papers.title: Sustaining Circular Economy Practices: Comparing Supply Chain Resilience, Well‐Being, and Technology Adoption in SMEs Across the United Kingdom and France
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Small and medium‐sized enterprises (SMEs) face increasing pressure to adopt the circular economy ( CE ). However, prior research often treats CE as an outcome rather than as an ongoing organizational process. This study adopts a Strategy‐as‐Practice perspective to examine CE as a set of routines through which strategy is carried out in daily activities. We analyze how supply chain resilience, technology adoption, and organizational well‐being support CE and how these factors relate to economic, environmental, and social performance. Using survey data from 175 SMEs in France and the United Kingdom and partial least squares modeling, we find that technology adoption consistently supports CE, whereas resilience and well‐being have more context‐dependent effects. CE is conceptually shared across countries but differs in practice. It is consistently associated with environmental performance, whereas its links to economic and social performance vary. The study shows how organizational routines and institutional context shape CE practices and performance.

papers.title: Too much of a good thing? Knowledge transfer and scientists’ job satisfaction
papers.abstract: Abstract Universities and research organisations increasingly expect scientists to expand their roles beyond research and teaching through various forms of knowledge transfer. As these activities extend scientific work across organisational and institutional boundaries and embed scientists in heterogeneous role expectations, they may enrich scientists’ work while also creating integration strain. Despite extensive research on the antecedents and outcomes of knowledge transfer, little is known about how engagement in knowledge transfer activities is associated with scientists’ job satisfaction. Given the relevance of job satisfaction for individual performance, collaboration, productivity and retention, this study addresses this gap by examining associations between seven specific knowledge transfer categories and job satisfaction using cross-sectional survey data from 1,658 scientists in German universities and research organisations. The findings provide the clearest evidence of an inverted U-shaped association for cooperative knowledge development, although evidence for a decline at high engagement is less robust across alternative specifications. Continuing education is positively associated with job satisfaction. Curvilinear associations for several other knowledge transfer categories emerge in separate models but do not persist in the joint model, while technology transfer exhibits an exploratory U-shaped pattern contrary to our expectation. Taken together, our findings reveal heterogeneous and partly nonlinear associations between knowledge transfer engagement and job satisfaction and highlight the importance of accounting for scientists’ broader knowledge transfer portfolios.

papers.title: Leveraging digital capabilities for supply chain recovery and renewal: the mediating roles of spontaneous and creative improvisation
papers.abstract: Purpose Building on the dynamic capability view (DCV) and supply chain (SC) literature on digitalization, improvisation and resilience, we examined how different digital capabilities influence different post-disruption SC resilience outcomes (recovery and renewal) through distinct forms of improvisation in cross-border SCs. Design/methodology/approach Our sample comprises 217 matched Chinese supplier–buyer dyads, with buyers located in 66 countries. Confirmatory factor analysis and multiple regression were used to test the measurement model and hypothesized relationships, respectively. Robustness and endogeneity tests were also performed. Findings We find that digital market orientation is positively associated with creative improvisation, while its relationship with spontaneous improvisation is non-significant. In contrast, digital process innovation is positively associated with spontaneous improvisation, while its relationship with creative improvisation is non-significant. Furthermore, spontaneous improvisation is positively associated with SC recovery, while creative improvisation is positively associated with SC renewal. Creative improvisation mediates the relationship between digital market orientation and SC renewal, while spontaneous improvisation mediates the relationship between digital process innovation and SC recovery. Originality/value This study reveals distinct paths through which different digital capabilities contribute to post-disruption SC resilience. By differentiating digital capabilities, improvisational capabilities, and resilience outcomes, the study extends DCV-based SC resilience research by explaining how the adaptive potential embedded in these digital capabilities is translated through distinct improvisational capabilities into post-disruption SC resilience outcomes in cross-border SCs.
papers.journal_name: International Journal of Operations & Production Management

papers.title: Peer benchmarking and digital upgrading: Field experiments on business websites
papers.abstract: Can low-cost comparative information trigger firms to improve the performance of a digital asset they already own? Using two large-scale randomised controlled trials with approximately 7000 UK firms in the distilling and retail sectors, we study whether peer benchmarking of website performance prompts measurable improvement. Firms receiving benchmarked website metrics and targeted recommendations exhibit modest average improvements, with more favourable effects among initially underperforming firms, consistent with partial convergence towards the industry frontier. The catch-up dynamic is strongest on mobile metrics, including as a spillover in the first experiment, in which reports contained desktop metrics only, a pattern consistent with firms focusing improvement efforts where performance gaps are greatest. Treated firms also show suggestive report-aligned increases in the adoption of mobile-optimisation and content-delivery technologies. These patterns are consistent with comparative performance information helping firms identify and respond to performance shortfalls. The findings position peer benchmarking as a scalable, low-cost instrument for narrowing the digital divide among SMEs: informational aspiration cues generate more favourable responses among firms furthest behind than among firms nearer the frontier.

papers.title: Population Aging and Citizen Preferences for Automation and Immigration: A Cautionary Tale for Advanced Aging Economies?
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Extensive research highlights public apprehension toward immigrants and robots, but few studies examine how demographic challenges, particularly population aging, influence these perceptions. The public may not naturally consider population aging when evaluating immigration or automation policies, as these issues are often discussed in silos. We thus hypothesize that priming the public to consider population aging will lead them to view automation and immigration more favorably. Using pre‐registered survey experiments in three countries—Japan, South Korea, and France—we investigate whether providing factual information about population aging alters attitudes toward immigration and automation. We find that in Japan, the world's most aged country, such information generates more favorable attitudes toward both immigration and automation. In Korea, the fastest‐aging country, it improves only immigration attitudes. In France, where the elderly population is average for the EU, we find no significant effect. We find, however, that these positive effects in Japan and Korea do not persist when respondents consider automation and immigration policies alongside other options like adjusting the retirement age. These findings suggest that the public's policy preferences in response to population aging are subject to country‐specific contexts, as well as to different issue linkages activated in policy discussions.

Toward net-zero building: an optimisation methodology for passive and active retrofits with renewable integration – a UK office building case study
papers.abstract: Existing commercial buildings account for a large share of energy use and carbon emissions, highlighting the need for net-zero retrofit strategies. This study develops an integrated framework for building retrofits, combining calibrated building energy simulation with multi-source renewable energy system design and optimisation to reduce energy demand, maximise on-site renewable generation, and enable cost-effective decarbonisation. A calibrated energy model was created in DesignBuilder to evaluate retrofit measures, while renewable energy systems and storage were optimised for maximum renewable fractions using HOMER Pro. A two-stage MATLAB-based Pareto front and TOPSIS multi-criteria optimisation evaluated and ranked retrofit configurations. The framework was applied to a UK office building case study (hot-summer, cold-winter climate), identifying the optimal configuration, which combines lighting upgrades, office equipment improvements, a water-to-water ground-source heat pump, carport-mounted solar PV, and rooftop horizontal-axis wind turbines. The retrofit reduces annual energy demand by 38.4% and achieves an average renewable fraction of 66.3%, reducing net grid energy import by 91.53%, with on-site generation exceeding demand during peak summer months. Annual CO 2 emissions decrease by 39.0% after retrofitting and by 86.1% after the integration of renewables compared to the baseline model of the case-study building. Economic analysis shows strong financial viability, with a levelized cost of £0.172/kWh and a payback period of 6.48 years. Sensitivity analyses confirm the solution remains optimal under varying energy prices and stakeholder priorities, demonstrating robustness for commercial deployment. The results highlight the framework's ability to guide transferable, multi-criteria retrofit planning and support deep operational decarbonisation across diverse building types.

A review of the effects of photovoltaic (PV) systems on thermal conditions in the built environment
papers.abstract: The thermal effect of photovoltaic (PV) systems on the built environment is an ongoing research field. An up-to-date review integrating indoor and outdoor effects as well as their influencing factors within a unified framework remains lacking. Therefore, this paper presents a literature review on the thermal effects of PV systems based on heat-transfer mechanisms, covering evidence from both experimental and simulation-based evaluation methods. This review aims to identify research gaps and support decision-making in this growing research field; hence, it examined 181 publications from 2003 to 2026. The findings show the potential of PV systems to improve indoor and outdoor thermal conditions, with more pronounced cooling effects observed indoors during summer daytime. Roof PV systems have more significant indoor thermal effects, whereas façade and window PV systems exert more direct effects on outdoor thermal conditions at the pedestrian level. Thermal effects vary with contextual factors, including diurnal and seasonal cycles, climatic conditions and urban morphology, and design factors related to PV modules, PV systems, and the building surfaces to which they are attached. These factors alter the heat-balance components of absorbed solar irradiance, electricity generation, convection, long-wave radiation, and conduction, resulting in different thermal effects under case-specific conditions. Future research should prioritize annual measurements across diverse climates, meso-scale experimental studies, and integration with machine learning.

papers.title: Plant Oxidative Stress Mediates the Synergistic Transformation of Benzotriazole Ultraviolet Stabilizers in Rhizosphere Soil: Insights from Dual Exposure Pathways
papers.abstract: Abstract Benzotriazole ultraviolet stabilizers (BUVs) are widespread emerging contaminants in soil. However, their transformation in the rhizosphere and the regulatory effects of plant oxidative stress on rhizosphere remediation remain unclear. The objective of this study was to investigate these effects using molecular simulations and rhizosphere and foliar exposure experiments. The removal efficiency of the four BUVs was 15–46% higher in the rhizosphere of Helianthus annuus than under natural soil degradation. The plant rhizosphere promoted BUV desorption from soil and induced hydroxylation as a specific transformation pathway. Direct rhizosphere exposure triggered oxidative stress and accelerated reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation in soil. Rhizosphere ROS contributed approximately 31.2%–42.7% to BUV transformation. Foliar exposure experiments suggested that plant oxidative stress is an important contributor to rhizosphere ROS generation. Under BUV stress, plant oxidative stress regulated the composition of dissolved organic matter (DOM) and the selective enrichment of bacteria, including Acidobacteriota, Actinomycota, and Bacteroidota. Multivariate correlation network analysis suggested that foliar exposure resulted in more complex interactions among rhizosphere microenvironmental characteristics than did direct rhizosphere exposure. This study provides insights into BUV transformation in the rhizosphere and establishes a framework for plant signal-guided rhizosphere remediation strategies.

papers.title: Exploring the Influence of Chemical Exposures on Breast Cancer Disparities: High-Throughput Transcriptomic Analysis of Normal Breast Cells from Diverse Donors
papers.abstract: Abstract Racial disparities in the incidence of, and mortality from, aggressive breast cancers are a pressing public health issue. Many factors have been investigated in these inequities; however, the role of toxicant exposures is not well characterized. We and others have identified substantial inequities in chemical biomarker concentrations by race. The goal of this study was to test the hypothesis that exposure to these chemicals is linked to biological changes relevant to aggressive breast cancers, such as dysregulation of the Hallmarks of Cancer. We used high-throughput transcriptomic profiling of normal primary human breast epithelial cells from diverse donors (n = 6) to test the effects of 8 chemicals (cadmium, lead, arsenic, copper, PFNA, BPA, BPS, and p,p’-DDE) with documented exposure disparities by race/ethnicity across 3 concentrations (100 nM, 1 μM, and 10 μM). Across chemicals, we identified that pathways related to cell cycle regulation and protein secretion were commonly affected. Through bioinformatic estimation of cell-type proportions, we found that metals like lead and cadmium induced cell-type shifts, consistent with the dysregulated cellular plasticity cancer hallmark. Lead- and arsenic-response genes were enriched for genes associated with poor breast cancer survival in the Cancer Genome Atlas. Integrating concentration–response modeling and chemical biomonitoring data, BPA, p,p’-DDE, copper, and lead elicited expression changes at concentrations relevant to the US population. Finally, we identified substantial interindividual heterogeneity in response to chemical classes, with heavy metals producing the largest dose-responsive transcriptional effects. These findings highlight the value of high-throughput transcriptomics as a new approach methodology (NAM) in quantifying how common exposures may impact aggressive breast cancer-associated biological processes.

papers.title: From Molecular Topography to Ozone Pollution: Species Sources and Photochemical Kinetics of Individual Organic Peroxyl Radicals
papers.abstract: Abstract Ground-level ozone (O3) poses significant threats to global public health and climate change. Organic peroxyl radicals (RO2) serve as crucial intermediates in atmospheric O3 formation. Although individual RO2 species exhibit distinct reactivities, the quantification and source attribution of individual RO2 species remain poorly understood. Here, we address the challenge by integrating high-resolution field observations with fundamental theoretical kinetics within a novel hybrid receptor-kinetic modeling framework. The concentration and composition of RO2 species exhibit significant seasonal and diurnal dependencies. In summer, the 19 RO2 pool was characterized by a substantial contribution from biogenic sources (29%), particularly isoprene-derived species (ISOPOBO2). Conversely, the wintertime RO2 composition shifts, dramatically dominated by industrial emissions (41%), notably ethylene-derived species (HOCH2CH2O2). Source apportionment via the RO2+NO pathway further demonstrates that O3 photochemical formation potentials align closely with the kinetics of RO2 production. A data-driven machine learning model effectively captures the contribution of individual RO2 species to O3 formation in summer, but it shows significant deviations from kinetic simulations in winter. The framework establishes a dynamic framework to support daytime O3 mitigation by quantifying the high-time-resolution RO2 radical pool from field VOCs measurements.

papers.title: Relative Humidity Modulates Nitration and Ring Fragmentation during Heterogeneous Oxidation of Catechol by Nitrate Radicals
papers.abstract: Abstract Catechol is an important biomass-burning-derived phenolic compound and a precursor to secondary organic aerosols (SOAs). Although nitrate radicals (NO3) are recognized as major nighttime oxidants, the influence of the aerosol water content on heterogeneous NO3 oxidation of phenolic compounds remains poorly understood. Here, we investigate the impact of relative humidity (RH = 0–90%) on the heterogeneous oxidation of catechol thin films by nitrate radicals generated from the reaction of O3 and NO2. Product formation was characterized using Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy, UV–visible spectroscopy, electrospray ionization mass spectrometry (ESI-MS), ultrahigh-pressure liquid chromatography coupled with mass spectrometry (UHPLC–MS), and ion chromatography–mass spectrometry (IC–MS). Under dry conditions, oxidation favored nitration and oligomerization pathways, producing mono-, di-, and trinitrocatechols together with catechol dimers and trimers. These products exhibited enhanced absorption in the 300–500 nm region, characteristic of brown carbon chromophores. Increasing RH progressively suppressed the relative nitration capacity of the NO3/N2O5 system while promoting oxidative ring-opening reactions, leading to the formation of dicarboxylic acids, including cis,cis-muconic acid, 2,3-dihydroxymaleic acid, and oxalic acid. Product distributions revealed a transition from functionalization-dominated chemistry at low RH to fragmentation-dominated chemistry at high RH. These results indicate that RH strongly controls nighttime nitrate radical oxidation of biomass-burning phenolics by shifting product formation from light-absorbing nitroaromatic brown carbon toward highly oxygenated fragmentation products. The findings provide new mechanistic insights into the role of aerosol water in governing the chemical aging and optical evolution of biomass-burning aerosols.

papers.title: Electrification, Lightweighting, and Materials Supply: A Dynamic Life Cycle Assessment of the U.S. Light-Duty Vehicle Fleet
papers.abstract: Abstract Electrification and lightweighting are reshaping vehicle designs and materials demand, with uncertain net effects on life cycle greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. Most existing fleet studies treat material choices, materials markets, and vehicle adoption separately, without capturing feedbacks between design, supply chains, and consumer behavior. This study develops an integrated system dynamics–life cycle assessment (SD–LCA) framework to explore these interactions for the U.S. light-duty vehicle fleet from 2000 to 2060. The model extends an established powertrain diffusion framework by endogenizing vehicle body material selection, battery capacity evolution, and materials market responses, linking these dynamics to a bottom-up life cycle assessment of fleet GHG emissions. Scenario analysis shows that increasing aluminum use in lightweight gasoline vehicles improves their utility and market share, largely offsetting use-phase GHG savings and yielding only modest reductions in total fleet emissions. In contrast, faster battery electric vehicle adoption raises cradle-to-gate emissions but more than compensates through lower use-phase emissions, reducing total fleet GHGs. Shifts in vehicle material demand also generate transient imbalances in steel and aluminum markets, temporarily lowering recycled fraction and increasing cradle-to-gate emissions. The SD–LCA framework demonstrates how feedbacks between vehicle design, materials supply, and consumer adoption shape fleet decarbonization pathways.

Synchrotron micro-XRF and micro-XANES characterisation of metal entrapment in anthropogenic tufa
papers.abstract: Anthropogenic tufa deposits forming in hyperalkaline environments near legacy industrial waste sites can act as passive sinks for toxic metals offering potential for nature-based remediation. To unravel the distribution and mechanisms of metal incorporation in tufa we investigated two tufa samples from a stretch of slag-contaminated stream near Consett (N.E. England) using synchrotron-micro-X-ray fluorescence (μ-SXRF) and micro-X-ray absorption near edge structure (μ-XANES). Analyses revealed that metal content were significantly higher in the upstream sample compared to the downstream sample for As, Fe, Mn, Pb and Zn. Element maps revealed metals distributed heterogeneously as diffuse enrichments, linear features and discrete concentrations between calcite growths. Prominent bands of Cu, Fe, Mn, Ti and Zn were also observed between laminates. Statistical analysis of whole images and transects along the direction of tufa growth in the upstream sample gave notable correlations ( p < 0.005) between: Mn and Zn ( R = 0.66); Fe and Zn ( R = 0.64); Fe and Mn ( R = 0.55); and Cu and Fe ( R = 0.61). Linear combination fitting (LCF) of μ-XANES spectra indicated that Pb micro-sized particles might contain phases of galena (PbS), Pb(II)oxides, cerussite (PbCO₃) and/or crocoite (CrPbO 4 ), while sorbed phases of Pb were not favoured in the LCF fit. These LCF results raise questions about transport and transformation of Pb from the weathered slag and the stability of Pb trapped within tufa. The highly alkaline stream conditions (pH 10.3–11.3) favour metal co-precipitation with CaCO 3 whilst incorporating atmospheric carbon. Overall, these findings highlight the potential of tufa as a natural attenuation material for trapping metals in contaminated post-industrial landscapes. Further study is required to help understand how these tufa metal capturing processes could be harnessed.

papers.title: Post-Paris agreement GHG emissions of 208 countries and territories: A 54-year descriptive trajectory classification relevant to SDG 13.2.2 monitoring (1970–2024)
Human rights impact assessment in Sápmi: a methodological framework
papers.abstract: Emerging due diligence laws aim to ensure responsible resource extraction but leave companies with considerable discretion. In this paper, we explore the role of human rights impact assessment (HRIA) as an arena for clarifying corporate accountabilities, and provide a novel framework based on a synthesis of research, international law, and good practice standards. We focus on the example of Indigenous Sámi reindeer herding in Sweden: this is a high-risk context for human rights violations, and the mining industry has a growing interest in the large mineral resources located on traditional Sámi lands. The criteria-based framework defines six preconditions that must be protected to ensure that herding communities can enjoy their collective rights to land and culture, notably the cultural practice of natural grazing-based herding and its seasonal migration. As a case study we examine state-owned mining company LKAB’s proposed Per Geijer project – notably, the project’s application for a concession permit on the traditional lands of Gabna reindeer herding community. The study is based on collaborative research with members of the community, guided by principles from participatory action research and Indigenous methodologies. The analysis demonstrates how LKAB’s project entails a significant risk of violating the Indigenous rights of the members of Gabna. In so doing, we provide one of the few evaluations of the human rights risks of mining on Sámi lands in Sweden. Finally, because of the challenges of using HRIA tools to build cross-cultural understanding, we consider how innovative methods could help us develop rights-based approaches with Indigenous communities.

papers.title: A systematic methodology for PTO sizing and hydrodynamic optimization of OWC systems in high-energy Atlantic environments
papers.abstract: This study presents a systematic methodology for the hydrodynamic optimization and power take-off sizing of an L-shaped oscillating water column wave energy converter for high-energy Atlantic environments. While standard oscillating water column designs, such as the Mutriku wave power plant (18.5 kW per unit), serve as a global benchmark, this research demonstrates that such configurations lead to significant energy underutilization in more energetic sea states. The proposed methodology combines multi-criteria site assessment, hydrodynamic resonance tuning, and time-domain numerical simulations. It is validated through a case study on Tenerife (Canary Islands, Spain), where an optimal chamber geometry was identified, matching the dominant wave period (T p = 12.5 s). A key contribution of this work is the optimization of the power take-off capacity. Sensitivity analysis revealed that increasing the rated power to 60 kW effectively mitigates clipping losses, increasing the annual energy production by 105.66% to 138.48 MWh/year compared with the 18.5 kW reference. Furthermore, the capture width ratio improved from 12.16% to 22.51%, highlighting the importance of hydrodynamic–pneumatic impedance matching. Comparative results show that the Tenerife site is 60.61% more energetic than the Mutriku wave power plant, achieving 2308 full-load hours and a capacity factor of 26.45%. These findings provide a transferable engineering methodology for designing resource-optimized oscillating water column systems in high-energy coastal environments. • Systematic four-stage framework for OWC design and PTO optimization. • Hydrodynamic resonance maximized through chamber geometry tuning. • PTO sizing mitigates clipping losses in energetic wave environments. • Optimized PTO increases annual energy production. • Framework transferable to high-energy breakwater-integrated OWC systems.

Research on the nonlinear mechanism of environmental regulations on China's industrial green total factor productivity: Evidence from a dynamic panel threshold model
papers.abstract: Environmental regulations (ERs) are effective in balancing industrial economic benefits with ecological protection. The study aimed to explore how ERs combine with R&D expenditure, human capital, industrial structure, and ownership structure to promote industrial green total factor productivity (GTFP) growth in China's industrial sector. Utilizing input-output data from the industrial sector covering 30 provinces and obtained between 2003 and 2021, the Meta-frontier Malmquist-Luenberger (MML) index is employed to measure GTFP. Then, a dynamic panel threshold model is constructed to empirically examine the nonlinear dynamic effect of different types of ERs on GTFP from the perspectives of R&D expenditure, human capital, industrial structure, and ownership structure, with the objective being to reveal the economic conditions under which ERs generate a “strong” Porter effect. The results indicate that: (1) GTFP is significantly enhanced during the observation period, yet it displays pronounced spatial disparities. Technological progress is the main source of GTFP growth. (2) The results of the benchmark model indicate a significant U-shaped relationship between ERs and GTFP. The stimulation effects driven by market-incentive environmental regulation (MIER) and public participation environmental regulation (PPER) are far stronger than those motivated by command-and-control environmental regulation (CCER) and performance-based environmental regulation (PBER). (3) The dynamic relationship between ERs and GTFP depends on R&D expenditure, human capital, industrial structure, and ownership structure. Speciﬁcally, ERs exert a stronger positive effect on GTFP in the region with lower degrees of nationalization and higher levels of R&D expenditure, human capital, and industrialization. MIER has the greatest positive effect. However, in the region with a higher degree of nationalization and lower levels of R&D expenditure, human capital, and industrialization, ERs exert a weaker positive effect or even a significant negative effect on GTFP.

Visible-light-driven removal of bisphenol A using a Bi12SiO20/Bi2O3 S-scheme heterojunction: Performance and charge-transfer mechanism
papers.abstract: Efficient removal of the emerging organic contaminant bisphenol A (BPA) remains an important challenge for sustainable water treatment. Herein, a series of BSO-Bi 2 O 3 heterojunction composites were synthesized via a facile in situ precipitation strategy to enhance visible-light photocatalytic degradation of BPA. Structural characterizations confirmed intimate interfacial contact between two components, facilitating strong electronic coupling across the BSO-Bi 2 O 3 interface. Among all as-prepared samples, the composite BSO-5%Bi 2 O 3 exhibited the highest photocatalytic performance, achieving nearly 90% BPA removal within 80 min, significantly outperforming pristine Bi 2 O 3 and Bi 12 SiO 20 . The enhanced photocatalytic performance was mainly attributed to extended visible-light absorption, accelerated charge separation, and efficient interfacial charge transfer. Trapping experiments and ESR analyses revealed that superoxide radicals (·O 2 − ) and holes (h + ) were the dominant reactive species involved in the degradation process. Electrochemical measurements combined with density-functional theory (DFT) calculations further revealed favorable interfacial charge redistribution and enhanced charge-transfer kinetics, supporting an S-scheme charge-transfer pathway that preserves charge carriers with strong redox capabilities. Moreover, the composite BSO-5%Bi 2 O 3 maintained excellent recycling stability and structural integrity after repeated use. This work provides an effective strategy for constructing efficient bismuth-based S-scheme photocatalysts for the photocatalytic removal of emerging organic contaminants.

Seaweed-based blue carbon potential of eco-engineered coastal structures
papers.abstract: Natural coastal ecosystems hold substantial capacity for blue carbon storage, but habitat replacement with harbour and shoreline infrastructure has severely diminished their potential to mitigate climate change. Enhancement of topographic complexity on coastal infrastructure through eco-engineering can increase biota abundance, such as the standing stock of long-lived seaweeds, thus positively impacting carbon capture and mitigating the carbon footprint of concrete-based infrastructure. However, ecosystem services of eco-engineered structures remain largely unquantified. Here, we assessed the seaweed biomass on a large-scale, eco-engineered seawall and show that topographically complex panels supported up to 19-fold greater blue carbon storage than flat surfaces. However, estimated panel CO 2 emissions exceeded CO 2 captures by 3- to 64-fold, after two years of seaweed growth. No retrofitted panel was realistically expected to achieve carbon neutrality within its 20-year design life, despite seaweed turnover and sequestration supporting long-term blue carbon potential. Predictive calculations, using six topographic designs, four concrete mixtures, two installation scenarios, and two detritus sequestration rates, suggested that the most efficient topography for seaweed growth, produced from low-carbon concrete and integrated during the construction phase, may achieve carbon neutrality within 15-32 years. Less effective or less sustainable scenarios were expected to require 52-277 years until carbon neutrality. An active transition towards low-carbon, integrated designs is necessary to align biodiversity-focused thinking in green infrastructure design with broader principles of sustainability and climate change mitigation.

Key account managers' relational identity and identification forms: When interpersonal meets intergroup within intra- and interorganizational contexts
papers.abstract: Key account management (KAM) is a strategic priority for many business-to-business (B2B) organizations. In KAM, key account managers play a central role, as they serve as the liaison between the supplier company and one or more key account customers. Existing research highlights the importance of identity (i.e., who a key account manager is) and identification (i.e., with whom a key account manager identifies) in understanding key account relationships. This research builds on the concepts of relational identity and identification, both of which define the self through relationships with others rather than solely through individual distinctiveness or group membership. These concepts are particularly relevant for key account managers and their role in nurturing B2B relationships. Specifically, this research examines how key account managers' relational identity and identification (i.e., interpersonal or intergroup), within both intra- and interorganizational contexts, influence the nature of the relationships they develop with their customers. It then formulates four research propositions on how specific forms of relational identity and identification of key account managers can lead to the development of either a strategic or relational partnership. This research has broad implications for collaborative B2B relationships.
