Inclusion of low-income consumers in global consumption dynamics: a socioeconomic framework for sustainable international marketing
papers.abstract: Purpose Despite the growing interest in sustainable marketing over recent decades, research in this area remains limited relative to the needs and scope of the field, in supporting low-income consumers situated at the bottom of the pyramid across international markets. There is an inadequate knowledge of how marketers can precisely reflect on international low-income consumers' needs, to adapt market offerings to serve them profitably. Addressing this lack of research, we aim to develop a novel socioeconomic framework of sustainable international marketing to help marketers enhance low-income consumers' inclusion in global consumption dynamics. Design/methodology/approach Following the realist approach, a systematic literature review (1975–2025)was conducted, using Web of Science, on low-income consumers; equity, diversity and inclusion; and sustainable marketing, published in generalized and international marketing and business journals, to determine the implications of the reviewed literature for international marketing and low-income consumers. Findings The literature review suggests that both sustainability concerns and low-income consumers bring opportunities for international marketing. Findings present eight key socioeconomic constructs and fifty-two underlying factors to design a sustainable international marketing framework (Figure 1), reflecting on the values important to low-income consumers in cross-border markets. We have coined a novel matrix (Figure 2) to help international marketers implement our framework. Practical implications Considering the socioeconomic constructs of our framework are supported by extant empirical literature, the framework helps design sustainable international marketing strategies, which consider the needs of low-income consumers and their socioeconomic settings, whilst offering positive business outcomes. Social implications Our framework and matrix help to inform sustainable marketing strategies, which enable marketers to enhance low-income consumers' inclusion in global consumption dynamics, whilst generating profit responsibly in international markets. Originality/value Given the importance of low-income consumers across international markets and the scarcity of effective frameworks in extant research, we present an initial framework and matrix to pragmatically design sustainable international marketing strategies.

papers.title: Actions Speak Louder Than Words: Behavioral Versus Textual Credibility Signals in Tourism Review Platforms
papers.abstract: Online reviews are central to traveler decision-making, yet their credibility is increasingly challenged by manipulated and strategically generated content. This study compares textual signals, or what reviewers say, with behavioral signals, or how reviewers act over time and across businesses. Drawing on more than five million Yelp reviews, the findings show that behavioral patterns, especially temporal activity and reviewer-business structure, provide more reliable indicators of manipulation likelihood than textual features alone. A late-fusion model combining behavioral and textual evidence offers the strongest overall assessment, while category-level results show that manipulation risk is unevenly distributed across tourism contexts. The study advances tourism research by framing review credibility as a multi-signal assessment problem and by highlighting behavioral consistency as a foundation of trust. Practically, platforms should prioritize behavioral monitoring, review-velocity tracking, and reviewer-business pattern analysis while using text-based detection as a complementary governance layer.

papers.title: A Perspective on the Development of Novel In Situ Remediation of Contaminated Sediments Using Black Carbon
papers.abstract: Abstract The field of contaminated sediment remediation was disrupted two decades ago by the emergence of a new way to reduce risk in situ through the amendment of black carbon sorbents─activated carbon and specialized biochars. This required a paradigm shift from a focus on reducing pollutant mass to reducing exposure through bioavailability control. Sorbent amendment technology has advanced from laboratory and pilot field demonstrations to full-scale applications at many sites and has recently been incorporated in USEPA records of decision at Superfund sites. This perspective summarizes critical points in advancing the new technology: 1) accurate problem definition recognizing that sediment pollutant mass reduction does not necessarily lead to risk reduction, 2) breakthroughs in bioavailability science and unraveling the role of native black carbon in sediments, 3) demonstration of pollutant bioavailability reduction with strong sorption, 4) quantitative descriptions of the process, 5) addressing the challenges of mercury, 6) understanding unintended consequences, and 7) development of freely dissolved concentrations as a key bioavailability metric with regulatory and stakeholder engagement. The lessons learned in this journey from early science through technological maturity can help inform other technologies that are in development to address evolving threats to the environment.

papers.title: Environmentally Persistent Free Radicals on Aged Polyamide Microplastics Drive Neurotoxicity in Eisenia fetida via a Glutamate-Centered Cascade
papers.abstract: Abstract Nitrogen-containing microplastics (N-MPs) are widespread in soil and often exhibit distinct environmental behaviors and effects owing to their unique elemental composition and molecular structure. However, their toxicity to soil organisms remains poorly understood. To address this knowledge gap, the toxicity of pristine and aged polyamides (PA) was evaluated in earthworms (Eisenia fetida), a representative soil invertebrate. At 0.01% (w/w), aged PA increased the magnitude of body-weight loss, MDA levels, and AChE activity by 24.4%, 11.6%, and 24.1%, respectively, relative to pristine PA-MPs. Greater accumulation of aged PA-MPs was accompanied by enhanced oxidative damage and neurotoxicity. Integrated multiomics, quantitative real-time PCR, and biomarker analyses revealed that oxidative stress-mediated membrane damage promoted glutamate accumulation, receptor overactivation, Ca2+ overload, synaptic injury, and ultimately neurotoxicity. Pharmacological interventions and transmission electron microscopy of the ventral nerve cord provided functional and morphological support for this cascade. Radical quenching and comparative leachate bioassays further supported the important contribution of environmentally persistent free radicals in aged PA-MPs to neuronal damage. These findings define a mechanistic pathway for aged microplastic-induced neurotoxicity and provide a basis for assessing the ecological risks of aged N-MPs in soils.

Synthesizing Information-Driven Insider Trade Signals
papers.abstract: Abstract We propose a novel approach to synthesize presumably information-driven insider trading signals for the cross section of stocks. We find that the resulting straightforward composite strategy can often forecast returns in a global sample. This predictability is strongest in equal-weighted portfolios, short holding periods, and insider-buying signals, and it improves further with global diversification. Cross-country analysis reveals that varying insider trading restrictions between countries have limited explanatory power for the performance of the composite strategy. Overall, the results are consistent with a short-term informational advantage of insiders, which might be due to the skillful interpretation of non-private news.

papers.title: Craft and Industrialization: Uncovering the Plasticity and Frontier of Craft
papers.abstract: Abstract Craft as an approach to work has been proposed as an alternative to industrial mass production. While industrialization has led to the replacement of craft logic with industrial logic to create uniformity and scale operations, the role of craft in industrialization remains ambiguous. Building on the analysis of engineering work performed at an R&D laboratory in the pulp and paper industry, we explore how and why craft enables industrialization. Our findings reveal how elements of craft manifest in engineering work by helping to transform ideas into useful objects, balancing scientific accuracy with practical usefulness, and fostering a sense of community and identity within the engineering field. These findings point to the plasticity of craft logic , suggesting that elements of craft can be transferred into new contexts and reinterpreted to address new objectives. Considering that these activities took place in an R&D laboratory that drove industrialization, they also reveal the existence of a craft frontier that escapes standardization by providing a context for crafting candidates for future standards. Craft frontier enables the coexistence of craft and industrial logics, where craft can contribute to industrialization by establishing foundations for managerial control without being absorbed into it.

papers.title: Conceptual search: A generative view of entrepreneurial imagination
papers.abstract: Abstract Research Summary Entrepreneurs cannot pursue ventures they never imagine. This article develops a generative view of entrepreneurial imagination as the construction of an evolving candidate set through generation, provisional evaluation, and revision. Conceptual search represents venture concepts as text, transforms them through interpretable operations, and compares their promise. A large language model prototype demonstrates complementary modes: local refinement lifts a concept from sixteenth to third among 30 ventures under a validated evaluator, while global recombination reaches distant possibilities that refinement makes competitive. The framework shows how search architecture determines what enters, survives, and develops, and how AI may broaden imagination within firms while producing correlated imagination across firms. By making imagination programmable, auditable, and experimentally tractable, conceptual search opens a research program on how entrepreneurial possibilities are constructed. Managerial Summary Entrepreneurs can pursue only the ventures they imagine, and valuable ideas routinely go unbuilt because nobody thinks of them. AI makes imagining cheap: it can draft, critique, and rewrite venture concepts in seconds, so developing ideas becomes a process that can be designed, run, and audited. I demonstrate a system that evolves real venture concepts: step‐by‐step refinement lifted a middling concept to third place among 30 real ventures, as ranked by an AI judge shown to predict fundraising, while recombining distant ideas created novel concepts that refinement made competitive. The entrepreneur's job shifts from generating a few ideas to governing many: choosing what to search, keep, and test in the market. One caution: rivals using the same AI will imagine similar ventures; advantage comes from proprietary problems, data, and evidence.

papers.title: Building Eco‐Innovation in SMEs Through Circular Economy Capability: Revisiting the Role of Green Transformational Leadership
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Resource‐constrained small and medium‐sized enterprises (SMEs) often struggle to translate sustainability ambitions into eco‐innovation because environmental initiatives must also support economic survival. Although green transformational leadership (GTL) is widely recognized as a driver of eco‐innovation, little is known about how it enables SMEs to develop the organizational capabilities needed to achieve both environmental and economic objectives. Drawing on the Resource‐Based View (RBV), this study examines whether circular economy capability (CEC) mediates the relationship between GTL and eco‐innovation and whether innovative climate (IC) strengthens this relationship. A repeated cross‐sectional design was employed among emerging‐economy SMEs (Study 1, n = 335; Study 2, n = 302), with each study adopting a three‐wave, multi‐source survey design with temporal separation between measurements. The hypotheses were tested using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS‐SEM). The findings show that GTL is positively associated with eco‐innovation primarily by developing CEC, with CEC partially mediating the leadership–innovation relationship across both study periods. Although IC has no direct effect on eco‐innovation, it significantly strengthens the positive influence of CEC on eco‐innovation. The replication of these relationships across the two study periods, alongside stronger capability‐related associations in Study 2, indicates the robustness of the proposed relationships across temporally separated samples. By extending the RBV, this study demonstrates that the strategic value of green leadership lies in developing capabilities that reconcile environmental sustainability with operational efficiency and firm competitiveness, offering important implications for SMEs pursuing sustainable innovation under resource constraints.

papers.title: Under Pressure: Building Relational Water Stewardship Capability in Buyer‐Driven Agri‐Food Chains
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Buyers increasingly demand water stewardship, yet it is hard to operationalize because water risk is place‐based, collective and only partly auditable. We develop Relational Water Stewardship Capability (RWSC), the relational capacity through which buyers, exporters and intermediaries align incentives, produce credible evidence and test water‐saving practice while protecting yield and quality. Evidence comes from an abductive multiple‐case study of the Tunisian date sector: 32 interviews, 15 days of observation and 190 documents. Three mechanisms generate RWSC: reframing water as a threat to supply continuity, cofinanced field trials that yield locally credible evidence and boundary spanning to producer organizations and agronomists. Contrasting cases show RWSC fails where buyer power lacks recognition and investment and where shared objectives meet no capital at producer level. We specify three pathways from dyadic capability to collective resource and find the fiscal one binding. Over a fossil aquifer, the process slows depletion without reversing it.

papers.title: Bankability as a Mechanism for Sustainability Implementation in Public–Private Partnerships
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Infrastructure public–private partnerships (PPPs) may formally incorporate sustainability commitments while lacking the financial capacity required to support their implementation over long concession horizons. This paper examines project‐level financial architecture as a structural condition shaping that capacity. Using an analytical single‐case study of a Mediterranean port redevelopment PPP, we combine project finance simulation with sensitivity and scenario analyses. The findings analytically illustrate how a project may be economically profitable yet remain below a minimum analytical financeability threshold, thereby creating financial pressure on non‐revenue‐generating sustainability components and increasing their exposure to potential deferral or renegotiation. Sensitivity analyses identify debt tenor and cost of debt as threshold parameters, while scenario analyses indicate that dependence on a dominant revenue stream may create incentives to prioritize commercial activities over non‐revenue‐generating commitments. The study contributes to sustainability strategy research by conceptualizing bankability as an enabling financial condition—rather than a guarantee—of sustainability delivery and by framing commercial drift as a potential structural risk associated with concentrated revenue architectures. The implications for public authorities, environmental, social, and governance (ESG) investors, and development finance institutions are framed as conditional implications requiring comparative and longitudinal testing.

papers.title: Driving Greater SME Engagement With Stakeholder Support for Environmental Sustainability: The Role of Resources, Barriers and Dependency Activation Strategies
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT External stakeholders are critical in enabling SMEs to achieve environmental sustainability. Yet, despite the growing availability of sustainability support, SME engagement remains limited. This article addresses significant gaps in the SME sustainability literature by mapping the support ecosystem and explaining why available sustainability resources are so underutilized. Drawing on resource dependence theory (RDT) and institutional theory (IT), we analyse 47 interviews and two focus groups with UK SMEs and support providers, revealing (i) latent and reverse dependencies, (ii) institutional and structural barriers and (iii) strategic inaction weakening engagement. Our findings advance RDT by shifting attention from dependency formation to the mechanisms that hinder it, offering a novel conceptual lens on how support relationships can be activated. This study combines academic rigour with practical relevance, providing actionable insights for policymakers and intermediaries seeking to strengthen SME–stakeholder interactions and accelerate sustainability adoption and carbon reduction efforts in line with the net‐zero agenda.

papers.title: Strategic Sustainability Evaluation of Industrial Symbiosis Partners for the Textile Industry: A Robust Fuzzy Decision Analytics Approach
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Technological advancements have transformed production processes, revealing the inadequacy of traditional resource management approaches. This necessitates redesigning industrial systems based on collaborative models. Industrial symbiosis (IS) aims to create a sustainable production ecosystem by generating economic and environmental value. However, decision‐making models addressing uncertainties in IS partner selection under advanced fuzzy approaches remain limited. This study supports IS implementation and sustainable resource management in the textile industry by identifying the most suitable symbiotic partner under uncertainty. The evaluation considers cement and ready‐mixed concrete, ceramics, packaging and recycling, agriculture and greenhouse cultivation, chemical and industrial chemicals, and construction sectors. The study proposes the fuzzy skewness impact through distributional evaluation (F‐SITDE) and fuzzy multiple normalization rating analysis (F‐MUNRA) model, an integrated fuzzy multicriteria decision‐making (MCDM) framework for uncertainty handling. F‐SITDE determines criterion weights, while F‐MUNRA evaluates alternatives. The results show the packaging and recycling sector performs best. Comparative analysis confirms robustness. The framework offers a systematic methodology for decision‐making and contributes to SDGs 9, 12, and 13.

papers.title: Climate, Nature, and the Uneven Expansion of Financial Governance
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Financial authorities have developed extensive climate‐related policies, but nature‐related financial policy remains less widespread. Using data on individual policy instruments across 116 jurisdictions from 2000 to 2025, this paper compares the adoption, policy areas, binding status, and source of climate‐ and nature‐related policies. Nature‐related policies appear in 27 jurisdictions, compared with 60 for climate‐only policies. National nature adoption is positively associated with a larger existing body of climate and environmental financial policies, mainly through the broader environmental component rather than climate‐specific policy. Climate‐only policies are used more frequently in prudential supervision and credit allocation than policies that combine nature with climate or broader environmental concerns. Nature‐related policies have a higher mandatory share over the full period but a lower share than climate‐only policies in 2023–2025. In the European Union, broad EU‐level coverage coexists with limited national issuance. The paper contributes a common framework for comparing climate and nature policies and distinguishes EU‐level coverage from national policy development. The results show that the climate‐nature gap concerns not only adoption, but also where policies are used, how binding they are, and which level of authority issues them.

papers.title: Translation in State Governance. By DongshengRen, LinJiao, and SanjunSun, Cambridge, UK: Cambridge University Press, 2026. 72 pp. US $68.33(hbk). ISBN: 978‐1‐00‐965981‐9; US $23.75 (ebk), ISBN: 2633‐6480
From Policy to Sustainability: The Evolution of Sustainability in Public HRM in Aotearoa/New Zealand in the SDG Era
papers.abstract: This study examines how sustainable human resource management (SHRM) has been incorporated into public sector HRM policy in Aotearoa/New Zealand before and after the introduction of the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Drawing on a longitudinal qualitative analysis of HRM policies from 10 local councils between 2010 and 2021, it explores how sustainability concerns across social, economic, and environmental domains were integrated into public HRM. The findings show that sustainability entered public HRM primarily through incremental layering onto existing HRM frameworks rather than transformational change. Following the SDGs, policy attention to equity, diversity, and wellbeing increased; however, broader social justice commitments remained uneven, while environmental sustainability received limited attention. By examining HRM policies as organizational signals, the study contributes to public HRM and SHRM scholarship by showing how sustainability priorities are communicated before implementation and may remain constrained by institutional logics of compliance, efficiency, risk management, and organizational performance.

papers.title: Extended oxygenation control of endogenous contaminants induced by load fluctuations in bio-trickling filters treating decentralized sewage
Eroding Confidence in Gully Location Risk Prediction in Mine Pit Rehabilitation
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Understanding how rehabilitation measures, such as landform shaping, and surface finishes impact gully erosion risk could assist in designing less erosive rehabilitation. In this study we use high resolution digital elevation models of rehabilitated mine pits to explore risk factors for gully formation. We determine features that pre‐dispose rehabilitated mining pits to gully formation, how topographic features vary across these areas, and generate a binomial regression and a random forest model relating surface features to erosion risk. These models are benchmarked against the ‘topographic threshold’. We found topographic features, like hillslope gradient and curvature, which concentrate and accelerate runoff were overrepresented at gully heads, while at the mine pit level, erosion risk can be predicted by surface area and average pit hillslope gradient, providing a high‐level risk screening tool. The topographic threshold, applied with high resolution accumulation data, outperformed the random forest and logistic regression models in predicting risk from topographic features alone. Despite being based on post‐erosion data, the topographic threshold performs well to predict erosion risk across rehabilitated mining areas. The method balances data requirements with prediction accuracy and is a conservative approach to highlighting risk areas within rehabilitated pits. The random forest and regression approaches underpredicted gully locations, in contrast with the topographic thresholds over prediction, which limits their utility without additional inputs. Operators have opportunities to collect additional data during rehabilitation that could build better predictive models. Informed rehabilitation design offers the opportunity to avoid, where possible, features that occur more commonly in conjunction with erosion.

Price Gouging and the Monopoly Option
papers.abstract: Abstract We investigate a dynamic oligopoly model with two phases: a normal phase where an essential input is available, and a disruption phase where firms must rely on inventories. Disruptions create an overcutting pricing incentive arising from the option to forgo sales and monopolize the market once rivals stock out. This monopoly option causes the price to jump to a supracompetitive level at the advent of the disruption and to remain above the competitive price path throughout. Price caps raise welfare, but reduce inventory investment. Government reserves reduce prices and raise buffer stocks, as do reserve mandates when financially feasible.

papers.title: The effect of prime brokers’ balance sheet constraints on hedge fund performance: Evidence from the GSIB surcharge
Bismarck’s Welfare State and the Socialists
Failures of contingent reasoning in screening decisions
papers.abstract: Abstract Screening decisions—choosing a costly action that reveals information about an unknown quality—can be crucial in various situations, such as hiring workers or designing policies. Choosing whether to screen can be difficult because it requires recognizing and trading off the benefits of information with the costs of getting it. We investigate whether people recognize when the benefits of screening dominate its costs and what causes them to choose otherwise. Our online experiment simulates a hiring scenario with an initial trial task. Participants can first reveal candidates’ quality at a small cost and then choose which candidate to hire. Most participants choose the dominated task that does not reveal the candidates’ quality, and this mistake persists even with experience and feedback. We show that this insufficient screening is driven by failures to anticipate inference and plan the full strategy.

papers.title: Speaking With One Voice: Shareholder Collaboration on Activism
papers.abstract: Abstract I study how an activist shareholder organizes a cost-sharing coalition with active shareholders while seeking support from passive shareholders outside the coalition. A larger coalition shifts more of the campaign cost to members, allowing the activist to pursue lower-value proposals. Observing a larger coalition therefore lowers passive shareholders’ posterior expectation of proposal value. The activist chooses the largest coalition that preserves support from pivotal passive shareholders, endogenizing coalition size. Consequently, coalition size need not be a monotone measure of activist influence, and activism frequency depends on passive shareholders’ preferences. Coalition building strengthens the proxy-fight threat and can increase prevote settlements. (JEL G34, G23, D83)

papers.title: Fixing the cryptofinance conundrum: the politics of crypto-assets regulation in the EU
Pricing Geopolitical Risk: Closed-Form Valuation of Futures and Options on the GPR Index
papers.abstract: On July 31, 2026, the European Central Bank (ECB) published the results of its thematic reverse stress test on geopolitical risk, in which 110 directly supervised banks identified scenarios severe enough to deplete CET1 capital by 300 bps. The exercise delivered narratives but not probabilities: without a market price of geopolitical risk, it has no quantitative anchor. This article closes that gap by applying the Grünbichler–Longstaff (1996) square-root, mean-reverting state-variable model directly to the Caldara–Iacoviello Geopolitical Risk (GPR) index, yielding closed-form prices for GPR futures and European options. Exact maximum-likelihood estimation on the monthly series from 1985 to June 2026 delivers a mean-reversion half-life of about two months toward a long-run mean of approximately 104, with the Feller condition satisfied with substantial slack, so the non-central chi-square pricing structure applies without modification. Applied to the ECB exercise, the framework converts the supervisory threshold into a tail-probability statement. Under the physical measure, the 12-month exceedance probability is approximately 12%—the answer a historical-simulation stress test would report. Under the risk-neutral measure it lies between 29% and 79% across the range of the market price of geopolitical risk motivated by analogy to inflation-swap risk premia—a bandwidth that is wide precisely because no traded GPR instrument yet identifies this parameter. Because the modeling techniques are deliberately standard, the article’s contribution is the practical layer: specification tests grounding the process choice in the data, confidence intervals around the physical anchor, a sensitivity analysis over the loss-channel mapping, and an explicit model-risk map organized for supervisory validation. The wedge between the physical probability and the risk-neutral band is the geopolitical risk premium, and a single observed transaction price on a cash-settled GPR contract—exchange-listed in the VSTOXX/VIX mold or OTC in the inflation-swap mold—would collapse the bandwidth to a point.

papers.title: “The Minimum Wage Is the Maximum Wage”: How Goal Replacement Perpetuates Means–Ends Decoupling
papers.abstract: This research examines how organizations contribute to the perpetuation of means–ends decoupling (MED) within issue-based fields organized around societal problems, under conditions of heightened field scrutiny. In such settings, organizations often profess commitment to field goals and visibly comply with institutionally prescribed practices to satisfy monitoring, reporting, and public evaluation requirements. However, many adopted goals remain underachieved, raising questions about how compliance without progress endures and how claims of commitment remain credible under transparency regimes intended to spur substantive goal pursuit. Our data came from 75 interviews with 68 brands, suppliers, and third-party organizations pursuing worker well-being in global fashion supply chains. We unveil auditability-based goal replacement as an organizational-level mechanism through which actors rhetorically foreground compliance as public evidence of commitment while narrowing internal goal pursuit to auditable thresholds that serve their core goals, thereby allowing shortfalls to persist. Self-silencing about this substitution and the instrumentalizing of shortfalls close the configuration into a self-reinforcing loop. The study advances MED scholarship by (i) showing how organizations leverage field conditions and appropriate the existing scrutiny infrastructures to advance their core goals while reproducing the means–ends gap, (ii) problematizing the authenticity of commitment claims, and (iii) explaining how goal-ineffective compliance prevails as a credible substitute for adopted goals. It also extends research on organizational responses to institutional complexity and calls for greater attention to institutional impact—that is, the realized advancement of the societal aim an institution emerged to address.

papers.title: Sustainability in marketing: A systematic analysis and future research agenda
papers.journal_name: Journal of the Academy of Marketing Science

papers.title: Common ownership and consumer welfare
papers.abstract: Abstract Rival firms with shared institutional investors (i.e., common owners) may compete less aggressively, potentially harming consumer welfare. Yet, research on common ownership has primarily focused on firm performance, often overlooking welfare outcomes or revealing contradictory results. This paper adopts a strategic network perspective to examine how common ownership affects firms’ service quality and pricing levels, which directly impact consumer welfare, and how customer and competitor factors that alter the focus of competitive strategy moderate these effects. To test the hypotheses, the authors analyze a rich, multi-market dataset of U.S. airline firms from 1995 to 2025. Findings reveal that competing firms with higher common ownership tend to have lower service quality and set higher prices. However, this effect is attenuated for firms with high customer-asset value and amplified among rivals competing across multiple markets. The findings demonstrate common ownership’s influence on firms’ marketing mix strategies and offer actionable insights for managers, policymakers, and investors.
papers.journal_name: Journal of the Academy of Marketing Science

papers.title: The Equity Market Implications of the Retail Investment Boom
papers.abstract: We quantify the equilibrium impact of retail traders on the U.S. equity market within a structural model of asset demand. Estimating investor-specific demand curves, we find that Robinhood traders are fundamentally distinct from all other investors, including other households: their demand is the most elastic and tilts most strongly toward volatile and microcap stocks. Each dollar invested through Robinhood generates more than five dollars in aggregate equity repricing, exceeding hedge funds, other households, and all other investor types. We decompose the cross-sectional variation in stock returns during Robinhood’s growth surge in 2020 into investor-specific components and find that shifts in Robinhood traders’ latent demand drove 11% of small-cap return volatility despite their negligible aggregate wealth share. To explain these demand shifts, we show that Robinhood traders are the only investor group whose latent demand is well explained by attention proxies: their demand exhibits a V-shaped response to past returns and rises sharply with trading volume. Our findings suggest that the growth of retail trading platforms represents a fundamental shift in the composition of equity demand with equilibrium consequences disproportionate to retail investors’ share of aggregate wealth. This paper was accepted by Lukas Schmid, finance. Funding: P. van der Beck acknowledges financial support from the Swiss National Science Foundation. Supplemental Material: The data files are available at https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2025.04854 .

papers.title: Corporate Pension Risk-Taking in a Low Interest Rate Environment
papers.abstract: We examine how funding deficit pressures shape the risk-taking of U.S. corporate defined-benefit pension plans and how targeted regulatory relief can mitigate these incentives. Using the 2012 Moving Ahead for Progress in the 21st Century Act reform, which temporarily eased funding pressure by revising discount rate calculations, we show that plans receiving greater relief significantly reduced their equity allocations and shifted toward safer assets. This derisking was most pronounced among active plans and those sponsored by more financially constrained firms. Our findings demonstrate that targeted regulatory relief can curb risk-taking incentives even without altering underlying economic conditions or financial reporting standards and shed light on the likely (and unlikely) frictions driving such behavior. This paper was accepted by Bo Becker, finance. Funding: R. Pinto acknowledges financial support from the Lancaster University Management School Pump Prime Program. Supplemental Material: The online appendix and data files are available at https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2025.02928 .

papers.title: Qualitative Research in the Age of AI: Considerations, Critiques, and Craft
papers.abstract: publishersversion

papers.title: Thank You, Now What? How Donors Respond to Calls to Action
Testing a moderated mediated model through intellectual capital of smart circularity and brand loyalty in Saudi Arabia
Brave new cities? Governance configurations for sustainable city logistics
papers.abstract: Purpose Despite extensive research and policy efforts, there is still no consensus over the aspects that must be influenced to mitigate the environmental and social impact of city logistics. Existing approaches have primarily focused on optimizing urban freight operations but have struggled to generate lasting and systemic improvements. Building on recent supply chain management (SCM) calls to conceptualize supply chains as socially embedded systems, this study aims to investigate why cities implementing broadly similar collaborative governance initiatives produce different sustainable city logistics outcomes. Design/methodology/approach A qualitative configurational analysis was conducted across twenty French city logistics initiatives. Drawing on Furnari et al.’s (2021) configurational theorizing toolkit, governance conditions were iteratively identified and combined to explain variation in sustainable city logistics outcomes. Findings The analysis identifies five governance configurations. Rather than depending on collaborative governance alone, high-impact outcomes emerge from the interaction among governance structure, stakeholder representation, structural commitment and intervention scale. Research limitations/implications The governance configurations identified are grounded in French city logistics initiatives and should be further strengthened through fieldwork, and then examined in other institutional contexts. Future research should investigate how governance configurations evolve over time and across different socially embedded supply chains. Practical implications Managers and public authorities should focus less on replicating individual governance practices and more on assembling governance configurations that combine broad stakeholder representation, collaborative decision-making, structural commitment and coordinated ecosystem-level interventions. Originality/value The study advances SCM research by reconceptualizing sustainable city logistics as a governance and coordination challenge embedded within socially embedded supply chains. By doing so, it further demonstrates how configurational theorizing explains wicked sustainability problems in SCM by shifting attention from isolated governance mechanisms toward governance configurations as the appropriate unit of analysis.
papers.journal_name: Supply Chain Management: An International Journal

papers.title: Color lightness as a sensory marketing cue: implications for guest decision-making
papers.abstract: Purpose The comfort of sleep-related hotel amenities plays a critical role in shaping guests’ perceptions and booking intentions. Although prior research suggests that color lightness influences perceived comfort, existing studies have primarily focused on manufactured goods. Given the fundamental differences between goods and hospitality services, this study aims to examine how bedding color lightness influences hotel guests’ perceptions and behavioral intentions in the service context. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on Accessibility-Diagnosticity Theory, this research uses one pretest and two experiments to examine the effects of bedding color lightness on perceived comfort, brand image and willingness to pay, as well as the underlying mechanism explaining the relationship between color lightness and willingness to pay. Findings Compared with light-colored bedding, dark-colored bedding significantly enhances perceived comfort, brand image and willingness to pay. Brand image and perceived comfort serially mediate the relationship between color lightness and willingness to pay. Research limitations/implications Color lightness serves as an accessible and diagnostic cue shaping consumer responses. The findings provide practical insights into how hotel businesses can leverage color lightness in bedding design and visual marketing communication to enhance guests’ perceptions and behavioral intentions. Originality/value Prior research in manufacturing contexts suggests a direct association between light colors and perceived comfort. However, this study shows that, in hospitality settings, darker colors can enhance perceived comfort, as experiential comfort is shaped through brand-level perceptions. Such critical insights highlight how the underlying mechanism of color lightness operates differently in service contexts, reflecting the unique characteristics of hospitality settings.
papers.journal_name: International Journal of Contemporary Hospitality Management

papers.title: When robots take the initiative: how robotic service proactivity shapes customer experience of hospitableness
papers.abstract: Purpose Drawing on social response theory, this research aims to examine whether, how and when robotic service proactivity fosters customer experience of hospitableness. Design/methodology/approach A multistudy design consisting of three scenario-based experiments and one field validation survey was used to test the proposed conceptual model. Findings Customers reported a more intense experience of hospitableness when service robots displayed higher levels of proactivity. Automated social presence accounted for this effect, and the effect was amplified when robots possessed a more human-like appearance. Practical implications This research presents actionable insights for optimizing the coordinated management of robotic behaviors and appearances to enhance customer-robot interaction experiences. Originality/value This research extends research on service robots from static design to dynamic behavior, positioning robotic service proactivity as a key driver of customer experience of hospitableness. From the perspective of customer social responses, this study reveals automated social presence as the socio-emotional mechanism. It further establishes humanoid appearance as a moderating factor, demonstrating that proactive behavior yields greater benefits when robot form and behavior are aligned. These findings advance research on service robot form–behavior consistency and offer novel implications for robot design.
papers.journal_name: International Journal of Contemporary Hospitality Management

papers.title: How could fun activities motivate informal field-based learning?
papers.abstract: Purpose As the motivational mechanisms through which workplace practices activate employees’ informal field-based learning (IFBL) remain underexplored, this study aims to address this gap by examining how fun activities (FA) influence IFBL in hotel contexts. Design/methodology/approach Three-wave survey data were collected from 424 frontline and backstage employees in Chinese hotels and analyzed through the AMOS and Macro PROCESS in SPSS. Findings The results showed that the interaction between FA and individual playfulness influenced IFBL through two distinct mediators: harmonious passion (HP) and obsessive passion (OP), depending on employees’ playfulness. FA activated HP only among employees with high playfulness, whereas among those with low playfulness, FA activated only OP. Practical implications Organizations should design FA that genuinely meet employees’ needs, thereby satisfying psychological needs such as autonomy and activating HP to promote IFBL. Importantly, employees should be given greater flexibility in choosing the form and frequency of their participation in FA according to their level of playfulness. Originality/value This research advances understanding of the organizational antecedents of IFBL and explores the motivational mechanisms that stimulate hotel employees’ IFBL by integrating organizational- and individual-level research on fun and play.
papers.journal_name: International Journal of Contemporary Hospitality Management

papers.title: Can Academia Ethically Use Tools of Techno-Colonial Extraction? The “Problem” of GenAI
papers.abstract: Debates on generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) in qualitative research focus on methodological utility versus epistemological harm. We reframe the issue from conditions of use to conditions of production , arguing GenAI’s foundation in exploitative digital labor and geopolitical inequality presents a more fundamental ethical challenge for business and society scholars, who risk complicity in these extractive systems. We outline several pathways through which scholars and institutions can engage GenAI more responsibly.

papers.title: From clearance to capital: regulatory timing, financing conditions, and observability limits in medical-device commercialization
papers.abstract: Abstract An authorized medical device may still need outside capital before its sponsor, the firm responsible for it, can manufacture and launch it. The paper asks what public U.S. records can show about whether authorization timing relates to access to that capital, and what a credible test needs. It does not estimate a financing or commercialization effect. The data combine 52,910 successful authorizations for submissions received in 2008–2024, a monthly capital-market measure, and a prototype match of 510(k) applicant names to Form D notices of private securities offerings. Among submissions received through 2022, the longest tenth accounts for 49.4–57.4 percent of days above the pathway median. Receipt-to-decision durations include applicant-response periods and do not measure unexpected or agency-caused delay. The market measure takes similar values in neighboring months. Its nine high periods, runs of two or more high months, last two to nine months; its relevance to individual sponsors is untested. As an observability diagnostic, the Form D prototype shows how name linkage can mislead. Records in the longest-duration quartile less often have a notice within a year (2.1 versus 3.1 percent in the shortest). Their applicant names, however, also appear less often among issuers (8.7 versus 14.4 percent), and among records with a name found, the notice share is not lower. About 11 percent of outcome windows are incomplete, and amendments count as notices. The contribution is to document these measurement requirements and to specify a sponsor-level test with validated identities, decision-date forecasts at receipt, and dated capital events.

papers.title: It is all about digitalization: investigating antecedents and effects of digital transformation
papers.abstract: Abstract Digital transformation is increasingly recognized as a vital driver of competitiveness, yet the precise organizational factors that most strongly influence its success remain ambiguous. This study addresses this gap by examining how strategic, operational, organizational, and cultural factors jointly relate to digital transformation outcomes, and by uncovering the mediating role of innovation success in shaping overall company success. Drawing upon data from 279 organizational key informants in Germany with substantive involvement in digital transformation, this study develops a holistic framework that not only identifies key organizational factors relevant for digital transformation success but also compares their associations with transformation success when considered simultaneously. The findings reveal numerically larger associations for cultural and operational factors, whereas strategic and organizational factors exhibit smaller coefficients, with the organizational-domain association only marginally significant ( p < 0.10). Although bootstrap-based parameter-difference tests do not support a statistically established ranking of the four domains, the results underline the relevance of all four domains while suggesting that cultural and operational conditions may warrant particular attention depending on firms’ specific transformation context. Furthermore, the results reveal a significant indirect association between digital transformation success and company success through innovation success, accounting for around 60% of the total association in the specified model. Hence, organizations seeking to maximize the returns on their digital initiatives should consider cultural and operational conditions alongside the strategic and organizational foundations of digital transformation. Taken together, these insights offer actionable guidance for businesses aiming to allocate their resources strategically, consider cultural and operational conditions as important diagnostic starting points, and harness the full potential of digital transformation through a concerted emphasis on innovation.

papers.title: Going green but seeing red: Tensions in initiating collective market shaping for sustainability
papers.abstract: Empirical research on market shaping for environmental outcomes remains rare in business marketing research, and existing studies are largely biased towards successful cases while overlooking the challenging “front end” of collective market shaping. This study examines how actor-perceived tensions emanating from the business context influence efforts to initiate a collective market-shaping process for improved environmental outcomes. Drawing on a real-time qualitative case study of a European cruise shipbuilding network, we focus on the phase in which a shared market vision and coordinated action have yet to emerge. Our findings show that accumulated tensions hinder the microprocesses required for initiating collective market shaping. These tensions manifest as conflict, scattered activity and inactivity, delaying progress towards collective market shaping. Shifting attention from successful outcomes to early-stage tensions, this study contributes to market-shaping research by uncovering why collective market-shaping efforts for sustainability may fail to take shape in complex industrial networks.

papers.title: How do monetary rewards impact free knowledge contribution? – business implication for Q&A platforms
How employees appropriate AI in the workplace: Effects of task characteristic and organizational culture
Who's ready for AI? The strategic leader–employee confidence divide and its economic and cultural contexts
Mindful consumption: how social media shapes fashion choices and brand pride
papers.abstract: Purpose Fashion brands increasingly use social media to promote sustainability, but different social media marketing activities may not shape mindful consumption in the same way or have the same influence across cultural contexts. This study aims to examine how social media marketing activities (entertainment, electronic word-of-mouth, trendiness, interactivity and personalisation), consumer knowledge and environmental concern influence mindful consumption. It also examines the relationships between mindful consumption, sustainable consumption and brand pride, comparing consumers in the UK and Malaysia. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on attitude–behaviour–context theory, the study collected survey data from 468 fashion consumers (UK, n = 245; Malaysia, n = 223) and tested the proposed model using partial least squares structural equation modelling. Multi-group analysis was conducted to compare results between the two countries. Findings The results indicate that interactivity and personalisation significantly predicted mindful consumption among British consumers, but not among Malaysian consumers. Entertainment, electronic word-of-mouth and trendiness had no significant effect in either country. In contrast, environmental concern and consumer knowledge were significant predictors in both markets. Mindful consumption significantly predicted sustainable consumption in both countries, while sustainable consumption significantly predicted brand pride, with a stronger effect in Malaysia. Research limitations/implications This research extends the sustainable consumption literature by addressing the literature gap and responding to the call of a recent study to explore antecedents and consequences of mindful consumption of sustainable fashion. It also provides novel insights into how social media marketing, consumer knowledge and environmental concerns have different effects on mindful consumption among Malaysian and British consumers, which leads to improving brand pride. Practical implications This paper provides practical implications for fashion brands on the differences in using social media marketing to improve their connection with consumers through enhanced mindful consumption among Malaysian and British consumers. Originality/value The study provides actionable insights for fashion brands on which social media marketing activities shape mindful consumption across different markets, while highlighting the consistent importance of consumer knowledge and environmental concern in both the UK and Malaysia. It also shows that mindful consumption is linked not only to sustainable consumption but also to brand pride, extending understanding of its outcomes from sustainable behaviour to consumers’ emotional responses towards brands. This provides a broader understanding of the value of mindful consumption across different cultural settings.

papers.title: Zero price or token price? The impact of bundle promotional format on promotional attractiveness and value discounting
papers.abstract: Purpose This study aims to explore the relative attractiveness of freebie (e.g. “buy one, get one free”) and token-price (e.g. “buy one, get the second one for only 1¢”) promotions in the short run and value discounting effect for the separate items in the long run. Design/methodology/approach Two imaginary-scenario and two incentive-compatible experiments test the hypotheses. Findings Token-price promotions are more attractive than freebie promotions no matter if the supplemental item is identical to the focal item or not. Moreover, when the two items are identical, consumers who encounter a token-price (vs freebie) promotion express stronger value discounting for the focal item. This effect reverses when the items are nonidentical. Research limitations/implications Future research should examine whether the bundle promotional format effect differs with the amount of the token price and the complementarity of the focal and supplemental items. Practical implications Practitioners can draw on the findings to determine when to use freebie or token-price promotions and how to adjust bundle promotional strategies according to the type of the supplemental item. Originality/value This study improves understanding of the effects of freebie and token-price promotions, especially over the long-term. Based on mental accounting theory, the authors build a comprehensive framework that explains how the bundle promotional format influences promotional attractiveness and value discounting.

papers.title: Talking or typing? How GenAI modality, product type, and multitasking shape recommendation response behaviour
papers.abstract: Purpose This research aims to explore how generative AI (GenAI) recommendation modality (text vs voice) influences consumer recommendation adoption and how this effect further interacts with product type (search vs experience), processing fluency and multitasking to shape consumers’ behavioural responses to recommendations. Given that GenAI recommendation systems increasingly support interactive consumer decision-making, the authors examine modality as a key design feature shaping how GenAI-generated recommendations are delivered to consumers. Design/methodology/approach Across five studies, the authors examine how GenAI recommendation modality influences consumers’ recommendation adoption. The preliminary field study uses actual customer interactions in a natural commercial environment to establish the practical relevance of the phenomenon. Study 1 replicates the core modality effect in a controlled Chinese experiment. Study 2 examines the moderating role of product type. Studies 3 and 4 investigate processing fluency and multitasking as the underlying mechanism and boundary condition, using behavioural measures across all studies. Findings The findings demonstrate that GenAI recommendation modality affects consumers’ recommendation adoption, with text-based recommendations outperforming voice-based recommendations. The modality also interacts with product type and this effect is mediated by processing fluency: text-based recommendations elicit stronger behavioural responses for search products, whereas voice-based recommendations are more effective for experience products. Multitasking further moderates this pattern, favouring voice-based recommendations under high cognitive load across product types. Research limitations/implications The findings are based on controlled experimental settings and future work could examine additional contextual or individual-level moderators to enhance external validity. Practical implications Marketers should tailor GenAI recommendation modalities based on product type and anticipated multitasking environments. Text-based interactions are more suitable for detail-oriented search products, whereas voice-based interactions better suit experience products and multitasking contexts. Originality/value This research contributes to the GenAI literature by identifying recommendation modality as a critical yet understudied design feature of GenAI recommendation systems. The findings show that recommendation modality plays a central role in shaping consumer responses to GenAI-generated recommendations and extend processing fluency theory and task–technology fit by integrating product type and multitasking as key boundary conditions.

papers.title: Mobile coupon-clicks inside vs outside a mall: implications for location-based targeting
papers.abstract: Purpose This paper considers mobile coupons issued outside and inside a shopping mall with multiple stores. It aims to study the implications of coupon-click effects on optimal location-based mobile coupon targeting (LBMCT) strategy. Design/methodology/approach The study first empirically examines the effect of consumers’ coupon-click behaviors on purchases and find that coupon clicks made outside the mall are associated with a stronger purchase response than inside-mall clicks for experiential-product stores, a pattern consistent with a traffic-conversion mechanism overlooked in prior literature. Then the study builds a mathematical model to investigate whether, when and where to issue coupons for different types of stores. Findings The analytical results identify the conditions regarding two new decisions – whether a store should issue coupons, and if so, where to target the coupons. The study shows that cross-store traffic spillovers from outside-mall coupons can induce free-riding and coordination failure, such that stores may choose not to issue coupons even when mutual couponing would make them better off. Research limitations/implications Future research could examine whether the findings generalize to other geographic and cultural contexts, to settings with multiple stores or malls, and to competitive conditions that influence coupon effectiveness. Practical implications Marketers should evaluate LBMCT by considering not only direct sales conversion but also traffic spillovers across stores. Because outside-targeted coupons can benefit neighboring stores, mall managers should coordinate coupon programs or design incentives when spillovers are strong, thereby reducing free-riding and overcoming coordination failure. Originality/value To the best of the authors’ knowledge, this study is among the first in the LBMCT literature that develops an empirical analysis motivated game model to investigate retail stores’ mobile coupon issuing and targeting strategies for inside and outside of a shopping mall, and considers two coupon effects and two product types.

papers.title: Navigating scarcity: sustainable supply network archetypes for water stress
papers.abstract: Purpose This study examines how firms configure sustainable supply networks (SNs) under water scarcity. It explains how water dependence shapes capability-configuration bundles and introduces transformational capability as the capacity to orchestrate capabilities for architecture-level redesign of SNs. Design/methodology/approach An abductive multiple-case study compares 13 multinational manufacturers across four sectors. Evidence from 23 interviews, site observations and secondary sources was analysed using Gioia-inspired coding and cross-case pattern matching. Findings Three contingent sustainable SN archetypes emerge: (1) “Stable”, (2) “Continuous Improvement”; and (3) “Progressive”. They differ in the scope of water dependence, the breadth of capabilities and the scope for reconfiguration. Static capabilities support routine monitoring and efficiency; dynamic capabilities renew existing processes and relationships; transformational capabilities orchestrate combinations of the five capability clusters to alter product and material choices, sourcing, governance, location, infrastructure or network structure. This is most evident in the “Progressive Sustainable SN” archetype. Research limitations/implications The qualitative study focuses on multinational manufacturers. Future research in other sectors, such as energy, should test the archetypes and transitions across smaller firms, services and other contexts of natural resource scarcity. Practical implications Managers can diagnose water dependence, distinguish incremental adaptation from transformational reconfiguration and align capability investments with changes across operations, sourcing, products, governance and network design. Social implications The developed framework can inform decisions on industrial location, catchment stewardship and shared water resilience. Originality/value The study advances a contingency-informed SN configuration perspective through a nested framework of sustainable SN archetypes. The archetypes are theorised as distinct configuration–capability combinations rather than as descriptive groupings of known adaptation practices. It establishes transformational capability as a distinct sustainable SN capability, rather than a synonym for dynamic capability, and explains when capabilities trigger architecture-level redesign under water scarcity.
papers.journal_name: International Journal of Operations & Production Management

papers.title: Lobbying Priorities in Agenda‐Setting: Agenda Breadth, Direction, and Responsiveness Across Economic and Citizen Groups
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Interest groups are key actors in shaping political agendas. Yet, we know surprisingly little about how they determine their lobbying priorities at the earliest stage of the policy process. This study advances a novel conceptual framework for studying interest groups' issue prioritization in the agenda setting stage along three complementary dimensions: agenda breadth, agenda direction, and agenda responsiveness. Drawing on original survey data from 630 EU level interest groups, our results show that issue prioritization is driven primarily by the type of constituents a group represents. Economic interest groups tend to pursue broader lobbying agendas, focus on defending the policy status quo, and are more responsive to internal member pressures when prioritizing undesired issues. Citizen groups, by contrast, typically adopt narrower agendas, prioritize challenging the status quo, and respond more strongly to external issue salience when determining their lobbying priorities. Overall, the study advances our understanding of how interest groups navigate competition for political attention and contributes to broader debates on agenda‐setting in contemporary democracies.

papers.title: An Analytical Comparison of Latent Growth Curve, Cross-Lagged Panel, and Latent Difference Score Modeling for Longitudinal Mediation Analysis
papers.abstract: Latent growth curve, cross-lagged panel, and latent difference score models are widely used for longitudinal data analysis. Relationships among those models have been analytically investigated in the extant literature for the univariate and bivariate contexts. However, mathematical connections among these models where three time-varying variables (i.e., input, mediator, outcome) are involved in longitudinal mediation analysis have not been previously studied. To fill in the research gap, we analytically derived the mathematical connections between latent growth curve mediation models and latent difference score mediation models (LDSMMs), as well as those between cross-lagged panel mediation models and LDSMMs for longitudinal mediation analysis. The equivalence relationships among the longitudinal mediation models provided new insights into the connections and interpretations of these models. We provided numerical examples using both simulated and real longitudinal data to illustrate the equivalence relationships, and shared the data and code online. Implications for longitudinal mediation modeling were discussed.
papers.journal_name: Structural Equation Modeling: A Multidisciplinary Journal

papers.title: Improving the Validity of Post-Selection Inference in Lasso-Regularized Structural Equation Modeling for Model Respecification
papers.abstract: Regularization is increasingly used in structural equation modeling (SEM) to search for potential post hoc model modifications, yet the validity of statistical inference after selecting parameters/models via regularization has received limited attention. We propose selective discrepancy inference for lasso-regularized SEM, particularly when the lasso is used for model respecification. The framework views regularization not simply as selecting SEM parameters, but as selecting Jacobian-defined covariance-change directions along which a constrained model may fail to reproduce the covariance structure. The inferential target is therefore a selected covariance-discrepancy coefficient, which quantifies how much the misfit left by the constrained model is explained by the selected modification direction after accounting for other selected directions and baseline parameter readjustment. A simulation study shows that the resulting confidence intervals achieve target coverage rates. An empirical example regarding measurement invariance testing illustrates how the approach evaluates lasso-selected model modifications. Example R code is provided.
papers.journal_name: Structural Equation Modeling: A Multidisciplinary Journal

papers.title: Interpreting prior-dependent precision in renal tumor growth estimates
Multimorbidity clustering and implications for clinical trials in low-resource settings
Associations between types of residential greenspace and depressive symptoms in older adults: the Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis
papers.abstract: Residential greenspace may prevent older-adult depression, but it is unclear whether this depends on type of greenspace and population subgroup. We examined associations between six greenspace measures and depressive symptoms among 6,799 U.S. older adults in the Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis (1-3 observations per participant in 2000-2012). Depressive symptoms were assessed using the Center for Epidemiological Studies Depression scale. Time-varying residential address-linked exposures included street-view-based vegetation (grass, trees, other, and total), satellite-based Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI), and park access. In fully adjusted mixed-effects Poisson models, overall associations were null (symptom count ratios [CRs], 0.98-1.03 per SD increase). Associations varied by site, race/ethnicity, neighborhood socioeconomic status, and population density. In site-stratified analyses, fewer symptoms were associated with NDVI in New York, NY (CR=0.96, 95% CI: 0.92, 0.99), park access in Winston-Salem, NC (CR=0.95, 95% CI: 0.92, 0.99), and grass in Minneapolis, MN (CR=0.87, 95% CI: 0.79, 0.97). The greenspace metric most strongly associated with fewer symptoms differed across racial/ethnic groups. Greater street-level greenspace was associated with more symptoms in high-density areas. Greenspace-depression associations may therefore depend on greenspace type and context, suggesting that mental-health-oriented greenspace interventions should be tailored to local populations and environments.

Odds of culpability associated with the presence of drugs in injured drivers
papers.abstract: Responsibility analysis was conducted on almost 10,000 drivers injured over a 10-year period in Victoria, Australia as a result of a vehicular collision and in whom comprehensive toxicology testing in blood was conducted. Multivariable logistic regression models were fitted to compute unadjusted (OR) and adjusted odds ratios (aOR). In the multivariable model, adjustments were made for gender, age group, vehicle type, and whether the crash occurred in metropolitan or rural areas. The psychoactive drug-free driver was the control group. Drivers with ethanol (alcohol) present at any concentration (>0.01 % BAC) confirmed the well-known large increases in OR that occur with rising blood ethanol concentration, with an aOR of 16.4 (95 %CI 11.1–24.2). Drivers positive to methamphetamine and no other psychoactive drug also showed a large increase in the odds of culpability (aOR 17.2, 95 %CI 10.2–29.2). Drivers with Δ 9 -tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) in blood showed a modest increase in odds when all concentrations (> 1 ng/mL) were assessed (aOR 1.5, 95 %CI 1.1–2.0) that trended to a possible increased aOR 2.1 (95 %CI 0.9–4.9) when concentrations were 10 ng/mL or higher. Benzodiazepines in drivers also showed a significant increase in odds (aOR1.8, 95 %CI 1.2–2.8), as well as antidepressants (aOR 1.3, 95 %CI 1.0–1.6). Opioids such as codeine and oxycodone showed no measurable increase in the odds of culpability, whereas combinations of ethanol with methamphetamine or THC gave aOR of 22.6 (95 %CI 3.0–168) and 20.0 (95 %CI 7.3–54.5), respectively, as well as drivers positive to both THC and methamphetamine (aOR 14.6, 95 % CI 5.9–36.4). Drivers positive to one or more illicit drug, or a larger selection of psychoactive drugs in the absence of ethanol both gave similarly large increase in odds (aOR 4.0, 95 %CI 3.3–5.0). This study contributes to a better understanding of risks associated with driving in the presence of common psychoactive drugs.

papers.title: From not being parented to not being a parent: Reproductive outcomes following early institutional psychosocial deprivation
papers.abstract: Background: Severe psychosocial deprivation, reflecting a lack of stable and responsive caregiving, can have long-term developmental consequences, yet little is known about its relation to later family formation and parenthood. Participants and Setting: This study examined reproductive outcomes among 174 individuals placed in Swiss infant care institutions in the 1950s and compared them with 196 non-institutionalized individuals from the same region and period (overall M age = 67.52, range = 62.87–71.39). Institutionalized children experienced severe psychosocial deprivation, with documented caregiver interaction amounting to less than one hour per 24-h period. Method: Using a convergent mixed-methods design, several regression models investigated the differences in the likelihood of becoming a parent, age at first parenthood, and number of children, while qualitative content analysis of biographical interviews explored individual experiences of non-parenthood among formerly institutionalized individuals. Results: Results showed that formerly institutionalized individuals were significantly less likely to become parents than the non-institutionalized cohort ( OR = 0.53, 95% CI [0.33, 0.83], p = .006). Flexible parametric survival models revealed that formerly institutionalized individuals had a lower average hazard of entering parenthood ( HR = 0.78, 95% CI [0.61, 0.997], p = .047). Among participants who became parents ( n = 260), linear regressions showed that formerly institutionalized individuals did so on average 1.3 years earlier than the comparison group (β = −0.23, 95% CI [−0.46, −0.008], p = .04). Number of children did not differ between cohorts ( OR = 0.71, 95% CI [0.44, 1.15], p = .17). Qualitative findings indicated that childlessness was linked to relational instability, structural and fertility-related constraints, and self-determined or protective decisions not to have children. Discussion: Together, the findings suggest that early psychosocial deprivation, as a severe disruption of early caregiving, may have lasting implications for family formation, primarily by reducing the likelihood of having children.

papers.title: Advancing a Model of Mindful Sexual Communication: Testing Sexual Communication as a Mediator of the Association Between Sexual Mindfulness and Sexual Satisfaction
papers.abstract: Mindfulness and communication have powerful implications for sexual health. Sexual communication and sexual mindfulness - the ability to be aware and non-judgmental during sexual activity - are two constructs often associated with sexual satisfaction. To further explore these relationships, a model of mindful sexual communication was advanced. More specifically, a moderated mediation model was tested to explore the indirect effect of sexual mindfulness on sexual satisfaction through sexual communication, as well as the potential moderating role of interoceptive awareness (i.e., trusting the body and self-regulation). Data were collected from 205 young adult college students in a variety of relational contexts that had a recent sexual interaction. The results indicated that sexual mindfulness awareness was indirectly associated with sexual satisfaction via frequency and comfort of sexual communication, whereas sexual mindfulness non-judgment was only indirectly associated with sexual satisfaction via sexual communication comfort. Additionally, two moderated mediation models were supported for participants in committed relationships: trusting the body and self-regulation moderated the indirect effect of sexual mindfulness non-judgment on sexual satisfaction via sexual communication comfort. The results reveal that different aspects of sexual mindfulness function uniquely together with aspects of sexual communication and interoceptive awareness to predict sexual satisfaction, revealing preliminary support for a new theoretical model of mindful sexual communication. These findings and their implications for sexual communication and mindfulness are discussed along with practical applications for individuals and professionals.

papers.title: More Than Just a Happy Ending? The Role of Orgasm Consistency for Sexual Satisfaction, Relationship Satisfaction, and Emotional Intimacy in Mixed-Gender Romantic Relationships
papers.abstract: Orgasm consistency is defined as the frequency with which individuals achieve orgasm during sexual encounters with a partner, while orgasm discrepancy is defined as the difference between the orgasm consistency of two partners. Orgasm consistency has been linked to sexual and relational well-being, yet little is known about how orgasm discrepancy in partners were associated with these factors. This study examined whether orgasm consistency as well as orgasm discrepancy in couples was associated with sexual satisfaction, relationship satisfaction, and emotional intimacy. Data from 327 couples were analyzed using Dyadic Response Surface Analysis. Higher orgasm consistency was associated with greater sexual satisfaction and relationship satisfaction, particularly among men, and with higher emotional intimacy among women. Contrary to expectations, couples with higher levels of orgasm discrepancy reported higher relationship satisfaction than couples with lower levels of orgasm discrepancy. Findings suggest that higher orgasm consistency may serve as a sexual reward, while orgasm discrepancy may not be perceived as a cost. Gendered sexual scripts likely shape these patterns. Overall, models explained limited variance, indicating that other factors beyond orgasm consistency are critical for sexual and relational well-being.

Turning the Tide. Studying the Impact of People Management on Teacher Turnover Intentions: The Mediating Roles of Role Ambiguity and Emotional Exhaustion
papers.abstract: Teacher turnover poses a significant challenge to educational quality worldwide, with turnover intention serving as a critical precursor to actual turnover. This study explores how people management—defined as the integration of the implementation of human resource management practices and leadership behavior—affects teachers’ intentions to leave their positions. Grounded in conservation of resources theory, we examine how people management can serve as a crucial resource in reducing turnover intentions by alleviating role ambiguity and emotional exhaustion, two key issues in the teaching profession. Role ambiguity arises from the increasing demands placed on teachers, while emotional exhaustion exacerbates intentions to leave. Our results show support for the (serial) mediating role of role ambiguity and emotional exhaustion, providing new insights into how people management impacts teacher retention. The findings contribute to the understanding of how people management activities can effectively support teachers, reducing turnover intentions and ultimately enhancing overall education quality.

Learning control policies from heterogeneous multi-horizon time series in battery energy management systems
papers.abstract: This paper introduces Representation-to-Decision (R2D), an end-to-end imitation learning framework that maps heterogeneous multi-horizon time-series inputs directly to battery control decisions through modular Temporal Feature Extractors (TFEs) and a shared latent representation, without an explicit load and PV forecasting step. While accurate forecasting improves prediction quality, optimal control performance remains unguaranteed in prediction-then-optimization pipelines; standard Reinforcement Learning (RL) lacks the long-horizon temporal awareness due to short-window observations, even when forecast signals are available as additional inputs. R2D offers a different perspective: rather than forecasting first and deciding second, it learns to decide directly from raw temporal inputs, with control optimality anchored by an aging-aware Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) expert through Behavior Cloning (BC). Benchmarked against six controllers on a high-fidelity electro-thermal battery simulation across five industrial sites, R2D achieves 62--77\% of the global clairvoyant optimum, outperforms the tested Model Predictive Control (MPC) and RL benchmarks, and yields battery degradation nearly identical to its MILP teacher across all five sites. Comprehensive ablation studies over temporal backbone, model size, expert formulation, aging-cost weighting, and horizon configuration confirm that an LSTM encoder with a 15-minute single-step control horizon provides the most robust and deployment-ready configuration, and cross-site and single-factor out-of-distribution tests show that generalization to unseen profiles is profile-dependent, with policies trained on high-activity sites transferring most reliably.
