Angular solar absorption and thermal energy storage seasonally modulate radiative cooling
papers.abstract: Passive daytime radiative cooling materials (RCs) maintain low surface temperatures under sunlight and can reduce building cooling loads and urban overheating. However, RCs with static optical properties overcool in cold seasons, and adaptive RCs proposed to date rely on temperature/humidity to switch their optical/radiative properties. Further, they address either daytime or nighttime response and are subject to ageing and to false switching on mild sunlit winter days. Here, we propose a system to seasonally modulate RCs with angular solar absorption, achieved with L-shaped fins, and with thermal energy storage (TES), implemented with phase change materials (PCMs) and concrete mass. The L-shaped fins have solar-absorptive, equator-facing walls shaded by horizontal eaves, enabling high direct solar absorption only at the low solar elevations of winter, with RC film on all other surfaces. Coupled with TES, the system is an angular-dependent thermal-mass-enhanced radiative cooler (ATMRC). In field campaigns in Western Sydney, the finned RC samples reached winter daytime surface temperatures 6–9 °C above the static RC and up to 11 °C above the unfinned RC + TES, resolving the daytime overcooling that TES alone introduces. The ATMRC with the 8 °C PCM reduced winter dew and frost durations by 56% and 73%, respectively, relative to the static RC. The summer daytime penalty against the static RC was 2 °C. Ray-tracing yields seasonal absorbed fractions of 37% in winter and 21% in summer in Sydney. Effective adaptive RCs therefore require both TES against night overcooling and angular-dependent solar absorption for daytime modulation.

Can the European recycling target for plastic packaging be met? A scenario analysis for Finland
papers.abstract: The European Union’s plastic packaging recycling target for 2025 is unlikely to have been met by most member states, so to achieve the more ambitious 55% target for 2030 will require significant changes to existing waste management and recycling practices. This study examines the factors affecting plastic packaging waste recycling and assesses, using 13 waste collection and recycling efficiency scenarios, the conditions under which Finland could meet the 2030 target. The findings indicate that the target is a multidimensional challenge shaped by multiple factors along the plastic value chain. At present, a substantial proportion of packaging waste is incinerated instead of material recovery. Priority should be given to business packaging by substantially improving the separate collection rates, with material recovery from mixed waste streams as a complementary measure. The paper also suggests targeted policies and interventions for improving plastic packaging recycling in Finland and beyond.

papers.title: Microplastics Are Prevalent in Striped Bass and Shiner Surfperch Tissues across San Francisco Bay, California
papers.abstract: Abstract The ingestion of microplastics by fish is widely documented, but the drivers of contamination and the movement of particles within organisms are still not well understood. We investigated microplastic contamination in sport fish caught from San Francisco Bay in California, USA. We compared microplastic contamination in striped bass (Morone saxatilis) and shiner surfperch (Cymatogaster aggregata). We observed an average of 5.9 ± 5.6 (Std Dev) microplastics per fish, with significantly higher overall contamination in striped bass but higher concentrations (microplastics/gram of tissue) in shiner surfperch. For each, we considered contamination relevant to their consumption by recreational anglers. For striped bass, where only the fillet is typically ingested, we found that contamination among tissues differed significantly (on average 3.8 ± 3.1 microplastics/fish fillets). Shiner surfperch, which are typically consumed whole, had an average body burden of 9.1 ± 1.2 microplastics/fish. Contamination varied significantly (p-value < 0.0001) among sampling locations for shiner surfperch, with the highest amounts observed near urban centers (no significant spatial pattern was observed for striped bass). Our findings show microplastics in tissues beyond the gastrointestinal tract, posing concerns for fish health and suggesting that fish caught from San Francisco Bay are a pathway for human consumption of microplastics.

papers.title: Arsenate Adsorption by Amorphous Titanium (Hydr)Oxides: Governing Roles of Medium-Range Ordering and Surface Disorder
papers.abstract: Abstract Amorphous metal (hydr)oxides are used for oxyanion removal from water, yet the structural features responsible for their adsorption performance remain poorly understood. This paper systematically investigated how the ordering range and associated structural characteristics of amorphous titanium (hydr)oxides influence the adsorption of arsenate, used here as a model oxyanion. Six materials were synthesized with ordering ranges spanning approximately 4 to 43 Å. As the ordering range increased, a transition from microporous–mesoporous structures to predominantly mesoporous architectures was observed. Characterizations revealed progressive structural ordering with increasing synthesis aging temperature. The most amorphous sample exhibited stronger water binding, providing indirect evidence of fewer surrounding hydration clusters than in more ordered samples. However, despite possessing the highest specific surface area, the most amorphous material did not exhibit the highest arsenate uptake. Instead, the material aged at 140 °C achieved the greatest adsorption capacity, exceeding that of the fully amorphous material by >20%. This adsorption maximum coincided with an intermediate ordering range, a transitional structural state, and a mesopore-dominated pore architecture. The results indicate that arsenate adsorption is not governed by surface area alone. Instead, the ordering range provides a useful descriptor linking atomic-scale structure, pore architecture, hydration behavior, and adsorption performance in amorphous metal (hydr)oxides.

papers.title: Emerging Contaminants Are Associated with Seasonal Variations in Phytoplankton Community Diversity in a Eutrophic Lake
papers.abstract: Abstract Emerging contaminants (ECs) are increasingly detected in eutrophic lakes, yet their ecological contributions to phytoplankton community variation relative to conventional environmental factors remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated the spatiotemporal occurrence of typical ECs and associated phytoplankton community variation in Taihu Lake, China. Phytoplankton abundance was significantly correlated with water temperature and total phosphorus (P < 0.05). Among the EC groups, organochlorine pesticides (37.7%), per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (16.7%), and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (16.1%) showed strong associations with the spatiotemporal variation in phytoplankton community composition. Organochlorine pesticides explained 18.8% and 25.9% of the α-diversity variation in spring and summer, respectively, and interaction analyses suggested potential combined effects among contaminant groups. Water quality factors and ECs jointly explained 67.9% of the community variation, with stronger associations observed in summer than in spring. Higher dominance of Cryptomonas ovata in Gonghu Bay during spring and Microcystis sp. in Western Bay during summer was associated with reduced phytoplankton community diversity under combined gradients of eutrophication and ECs. These findings highlight the covariation of phytoplankton communities with eutrophication and ECs and provide new insights into ecological risk assessment and algal bloom management in shallow eutrophic lakes.

papers.title: Dynamic Hydrogen-Bonded Hydration Networks Mitigate Organic–Inorganic Fouling in Nanofiltration
papers.abstract: Abstract Hydration layers are widely recognized as the molecular basis of antifouling membrane interfaces, yet their role is still largely viewed through a static barrier picture. The dynamic response of hydrated membrane–water interfaces to approaching foulants, particularly under organic–inorganic mixed fouling conditions, remains poorly understood. Here, using poly(sulfobetaine methacrylate) (pSBMA)-modified nanofiltration membranes as a model zwitterionic interface, we reveal that fouling reversibility is strongly influenced by the dynamic stability of hydrogen-bonded hydration networks at the membrane–water interface. Molecular simulations combined with sum-frequency generation spectroscopy demonstrate that pSBMA sustains a strongly hydrogen-bonded interfacial water structure with preferential water dipole orientation under silicate and alginate perturbation, thereby suppressing long-lived foulant residence near the membrane surface. Real-time surface plasmon resonance measurements further confirm weakened irreversible foulant anchoring and enhanced interfacial reversibility. As a result, pSBMA-modified nanofiltration membranes reduced flux decline during mixed-foulant filtration to ∼6% and achieved >91% flux recovery after physical cleaning, accompanied by lower organic and inorganic foulant residuals. Repeated filtration–cleaning tests with real secondary effluent further confirmed nearly complete flux recovery in complex water matrices. These findings revisit zwitterionic antifouling by shifting the focus from static surface hydration to the dynamic stability of hydrogen-bonded hydration networks, providing a mechanistic basis for understanding and regulating fouling reversibility.

papers.title: Mechanistic Understanding of Breath-Borne Bacterial Inactivation Kinetics in Oxidant-Rich and Natural Air
papers.abstract: Abstract Bioaerosols play a central role in respiratory infection transmission, but how atmospheric oxidants affect their viability, especially in human respiratory fluids, remains unexplored. Here, we investigated the inactivation of five bacterial species with distinct cell envelope architectures (Escherichia coli, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Bacillus subtilis, Staphylococcus aureus, and Mycobacterium smegmatis) suspended in human exhaled breath condensate (EBC) droplets exposed to gas-phase hydroxyl radicals (•OH) produced by ultraviolet irradiation of H2O2. Compared with the other three exposure conditions, the •OH-generating (H2O2+UV) treatment caused the greatest viability loss, with 4-h survival ranging from 24.3% (E. coli) to 63.0% (M. smegmatis). Gram-negative bacteria were sensitive to both H2O2 and •OH, whereas Gram-positive species resisted H2O2 but were inactivated by •OH. M. smegmatis showed the highest tolerance. Inactivation accelerated in smaller droplets, and the size-dependent kinetics were characterized using Weibull and first-order models incorporating surface-area-to-volume ratio. Morphological, biochemical, and metabolomic analyses indicated that the observed inactivation differences were associated with bacterial envelope types and surface characteristics. •OH preferentially degrades outer membrane glycolipids in Gram-negative bacteria and oxidizes cytoplasmic membrane lipids in Gram-positive bacteria, while all species shared a core signature of nucleic acid oxidative damage. These findings provide a molecular understanding of bacterial inactivation kinetics in human EBC droplets and may inform the assessment of bioaerosol transmission risks.

papers.title: Near-Complete Decomposition of Soil Microplastics over Transient Electrical Heating and Associated Benefits
papers.abstract: Abstract Soil serves as a significant sink for microplastics, posing considerable risks to both the ecological and human health. The diverse composition and dynamic transformation of microplastics present major challenges for remediation as conventional strategies often fail to achieve efficient and complete decomposition. In this study, biochar was applied to microplastic-contaminated soil as a conductive material to initiate transient electric heating under a low-power input. This approach facilitated near-complete decomposition of soil microplastics (>95.0%) across the tested soil and microplastic types while preventing soil hardening. Specifically, electric heating enhanced interactions between soil microplastics and the biochar conductor, leading to the formation of highly aromatic carbon (HAC). The resulting HAC not only improved soil microecology but also supported the growth of pak choi (Brassica campestris L. ssp.). The newly formed HAC was found to upregulate the expression of auxin-responsive gene families, including Aux/IAA and GH3, in the roots. HAC enriched tryptamine in the rhizosphere, and tryptamine abundance was positively correlated with the relative abundance of Sphingomonas, a genus with a reported capacity to convert tryptamine-derived intermediates toward indole-3-acetic acid (IAA) biosynthesis. These findings demonstrate that transient electric heating offers a sustainable strategy for decomposing diverse soil microplastics and that the remediated soil remains safe and conducive for agricultural production.

papers.title: Unveiling Phase-Dependent Fe–O Bond-Guided Nitrate Reduction at Biocathodes: Balancing Interfacial Reactivity and Iron Bioavailability
papers.abstract: Abstract Iron oxides are widespread in anoxic water environments, yet how their structures regulate microbial nitrate reduction remains unclear. Here, we reveal that phase-dependent Fe–O bond characteristics guide denitrification in bioelectrochemical system (BES) by balancing lattice-iron bioavailability and interfacial electrochemical reactivity at biocathodes. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations revealed that surface Fe–O bond covalency was associated with the thermodynamic barrier to lattice-iron release. α-Fe2O3, with the most negative ICOHP, exhibited the strongest Fe–O bonding and restricted iron release, thereby limiting microbial iron acquisition and downstream Fe–S cluster assembly. In contrast, γ-Fe2O3 and γ-FeOOH exhibited higher surface electroactivity but suffered from structural instability, evidenced by phase transformation, cell encrustation, and elevated microbial mortality. With mixed valence and balanced Fe–O bonding characteristics, Fe3O4 achieved the highest denitrification efficiency (17.8-fold enhancement over its abiotic control), which enabled direct Fe(II) uptake via the FeoAB system, bypassing siderophore-dependent acquisition and simultaneously activating both TonB-mediated iron acquisition and Fur-flavin-regulated respiratory pathways. This dual-pathway activation supported enhancement in biomass growth, intracellular electron transfer, and Fe–S cluster-dependent enzymatic activity. These findings help establish Fe–O bond characteristics as a key structural factor for Fe–N coupling and offer a structural perspective for rational design of iron-oxide-based nitrate-removal technologies.

AI-driven granular LCA for apparel: Quantifying product-specific GHG emissions for sustainable design and circularity
papers.abstract: Product-specific Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) for apparel is hindered by generalized data, failing to quantify unique environmental burdens crucial for sustainable production and consumption. This study addresses this challenge by proposing and validating an automated methodology using a Vision-Language Model (VLM) to extract product-specific details (e.g., fabric composition) from unstructured User-Generated Content (UGC) on consumer-to-consumer (C2C) platforms and subsequently calculate corresponding product-specific greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. The study seeks to demonstrate the significance of AI-enabled product-specific information as a tool for deriving insights into sustainable production, cleaner manufacturing, and resource efficiency. Applying this framework to 3500 apparel listings from a major C2C marketplace, our VLM demonstrated high accuracy in extracting physical attributes like garment size (92.3%) and fabric composition (81.6%). The subsequent LCA quantified an average emission of 11.9 kg-CO 2 eq/item. More importantly, by analyzing the product-related parameters required for these computations, we attempted to extract and structure data on product attributes and user behavior from unstructured UGC, enabling more effective estimation of product-specific GHG emissions. Although challenges remain in precisely inferring complex user behaviors from unstructured data, the successful granularization of material composition highlights the significant impact of material selection, providing actionable insights for sustainable eco-design and circularity. Ultimately, by significantly enhancing information transparency across the value chain, our work directly aligns with emerging global policies like the EU Digital Product Passport (DPP), fostering data-driven decision-making for cleaner production goals.

Impact of process configuration on flexibility–cost trade-offs in amine-based post-combustion carbon capture systems
The use of biochar in agricultural soils: Impacts on vineyard productivity and the potential for carbon capture and sequestration
papers.abstract: Background Viticulture is increasingly exposed to water deficit, heat and soil degradation, prompting interest in biochar as a soil amendment that may simultaneously improve productivity and sequester carbon. Methods This integrative review used a documented Scopus search (June 2026), targeted searches (September 2026), explicit eligibility criteria and a PRISMA-style flow diagram. All vineyard field trials were tabulated, meta-analyses were reported with effect and sample sizes, and each conclusion was graded by level of evidence. Results Significant yield gains were confined to three Tuscan vineyards amended with the same 500 °C orchard-pruning biochar on acidic to neutral, carbon-poor, non-irrigated soils (+16% to +67% per harvest, persisting ten years after application), and eight site-level comparisons, six in humid-temperate, cool or calcareous-alkaline settings, showed no significant yield response, whereas increases in soil water and topsoil organic carbon were more consistent. The most robust climate outcome is the persistence of the biochar carbon (inert fraction unchanged after 15 years, 65–89% remaining after 100 years), whereas N2O and CH4 reductions are not robust at field scale and remain undetected in vineyards. The previously cited 7.5 Mg CO2-eq ha-1 yr-1, the mean of all soil‑carbon practices in vineyards, rests on very few biochar observations, whereas a single 16.5 t ha-1 (dry) application stores 31–42 Mg CO2-eq ha-1 over 100 years before life-cycle emissions. Without a yield response, the break-even carbon price for biochar costing €200–500 t-1 is €90–243 per t CO2-eq, against a carbon-removal index of €135 (2026), and a single application requires 22–48 years of a vineyard's own prunings. Conclusions Carbon storage in the biochar itself is well supported, agronomic benefits are demonstrated only for a narrow pedoclimatic domain and require independent replication, and greenhouse-gas co-benefits, long-term microbial effects, economic viability and large-scale carbon farming remain plausible but poorly documented or speculative.

Regulatory quality, energy consumption, and environmental sustainability in a developing economy: Evidence from a Bayesian vector error correction model
papers.abstract: Sustainable management of the environment is among the primary objectives of sustainable development. Although environmental regulation is widely studied in advanced economies, its effectiveness in developing nations like Nigeria, characterized by weak regulatory and enforcement institutions, remains underexplored. Based on the Stochastic Impacts by Regression on Population, Affluence, and Technology framework, and using ecological balance (EB) and carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) emissions (COEs) as environmental indicators, this article investigates the impact of environmental regulations on environmental sustainability in Nigeria in an augmented framework that includes renewable energy consumption and gross domestic product as additional regressors. Using annual time series data from 1990 to 2022, the study employs the novel Bayesian Vector Error Correction Model, which improves the robustness of the parameter estimates by utilizing the Inverse Wishart Prior distribution. Robust postsimulation is conducted using the Gibbs sampling technique to generate 5000 iterations. The posterior mean estimates indicate that a one-standard-deviation improvement in regulatory quality (RQ) is associated with a decrease of 0.027 units in ecological deficit and a decrease of 0.111 units in COEs, though the credible intervals for the latter include zero. The results also show that higher RQ is associated with a decreased deficit between ecological footprint and biocapacity (i.e. improved EB) and CO 2 , indicating that effective regulatory frameworks may lead to more sustainable environmental outcomes. The results also demonstrate that the effect of regulating the environment is stronger on COEs compared to EB, implying that more stringent environmental regulations are necessary to promote EB than to reduce COEs. Nigeria's weak enforcement institutions amplify the urgency of reforms; hence, there is a need to improve RQ to ensure the efficient administration of environmental legislation in Nigeria. Relevant policy inferences and recommendations have been provided in the paper.

papers.title: Exploratory geoplay in metaverse fieldwork: Avatar movement as learning data for geographic understanding
papers.abstract: Geogames are increasingly recognized as playful systems based on real-world geographic data and spatial reasoning, yet open-ended geographic play remains underexplored. This study examines immersive virtual fieldwork as exploratory geoplay, where participants engage with geographic environments through autonomous observation, movement, and interaction rather than scores, competition, or fixed missions. We developed a multiplayer metaverse environment based on a life-scale 3D reconstruction of the Byobugaura Sea Cliff in Japan. Sixty-two participants explored it in two rounds: one unguided and one supported by light interpretive prompts. Avatar positions were recorded using the YAIBA behavior-logging system and analyzed through space-time clustering, PCA, trajectory-grid aggregation, and cluster-duration analysis. During unguided exploration, participants clustered around geomorphologically significant areas, while interpretive supports shifted visits toward breakwater and terrace zones. Cluster durations increased in the smaller sub-instance but remained stable in the larger main instance. Questionnaire responses reflected positive experiences and perceived behavioral changes. By framing avatar movement as learning data, while recognizing that movement does not directly measure knowledge acquisition, this study proposes exploratory geoplay as a model for studying locational attention and geographic inquiry within immersive environments.

papers.title: Salinization and Development,
papers.abstract: Abstract Climate change-intensified seawater intrusion creates a dual shock of transitory freshwater shortages and lasting soil degradation. We study its impacts on agricultural production in the Vietnamese Mekong Delta, a major rice exporter. Combining river salinity observations and detailed canal network data to map localized hydrological shocks, we find that salinity reduces rice yields but generates disproportionately larger declines in output and revenue. These losses are driven by a contraction in land under cultivation and limited substitution toward salt-resistant crops, pointing to constrained short-run adaptation. Using household and firm data, we further document reductions in own-farm employment alongside minimal transition to non-agricultural sectors, suggesting frictions in labor adjustment. Beyond income effects predicted by Engel curves, households reallocate expenditures toward healthcare and children’s schooling. The increase in schooling spending is driven by higher participation and may reflect shifts in opportunity costs, though we cannot rule out forward-looking responses.

papers.title: The Effects of Health Shocks on Time Spent in Home Production
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT This paper examines the causal impact of health shocks on time spent in home production among retired individuals. Two channels with opposite predictions motivate the analysis: health shocks may tighten household budgets, inducing substitution toward home‐produced goods (income effect), or they may reduce the physical and functional capacity to perform domestic tasks (impairing effect). Using longitudinal data from the Health and Retirement Study, I estimate condition‐specific causal effects of ten health conditions on home production in a staggered difference‐in‐differences design. Conditions that impair functional capacity, such as psychiatric conditions, depression on the Center for Epidemiological Studies Depression (CES‐D) scale, and adverse self‐reported health, reduce home production substantially. Psychiatric conditions reduce weekly home production by 3.2 hours, a 16% decline; CES‐D depression and self‐reported health shocks each reduce it by approximately 1 hour per week. Conditions that raise out‐of‐pocket medical costs but impose modest functional limitations produce no increase. The evidence therefore supports the impairing effect and gives no support to the income effect. The decline is not fully offset by increased help utilization or by spending on market substitutes such as housekeeping services, prepared meals, and yard work. Health shocks thus impose welfare costs beyond what monetary measures alone capture, with direct implications for the design of home‐ and community‐based support services for retirees.

papers.title: How Green Work Characteristics Drive Pro‐Environmental Behavior: The Mediating Role of Green Self‐Efficacy Among Hotel Employees
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines the influence of green work characteristics on hotel employees' pro‐environmental behavior and the mediating role of green self‐efficacy. Drawing on the job demands–resources (JD‐R) model and social cognitive theory (SCT), this study conceptualizes green work characteristics as comprising green job demands, green job autonomy, green supervisor support, and green coworker support. Data were gathered from 374 hotel employees in two waves with a 1‐month time lag and were analyzed using consistent partial least squares–structural equation modeling. Results indicate that green job autonomy and green coworker support positively influence green self‐efficacy, whereas green job demands and green supervisor support have no significant effects. Green self‐efficacy is a strong predictor of pro‐environmental behavior and mediates the effects of green job autonomy and green coworker support but not those of green job demands or green supervisor support. These results highlight the importance of green self‐efficacy as a psychological mechanism that links green work characteristics to employees' pro‐environmental behavior. This research contributes to the literature by integrating the JD‐R model and SCT into a comprehensive framework and by demonstrating that different dimensions of green work characteristics do not operate through a common motivational pathway in promoting employees' pro‐environmental behavior.

papers.title: Do ESG‐Oriented Common Institutional Investors Reduce ESG Strategic Dissimilarity? Evidence From Multinational Firms
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines whether ESG‐oriented common institutional ownership reduces strategic dissimilarity among multinational rival firms. Prior research primarily examined common ownership in relation to competition, firm performance, ESG disclosure, and ESG ratings, with limited attention to its role in shaping strategic ESG convergence among commonly owned firms. Using a global sample of 7766 listed firms and 110,490 firm‐dyad‐year observations from 2010 to 2024, we employ a dynamic panel system GMM approach to investigate this relationship. The findings show that ESG‐oriented common institutional ownership significantly reduces ESG strategic dissimilarity, indicating that such ownership promotes convergence rather than differentiation in firms' ESG strategies. This convergence effect is stronger in industries with high ESG materiality, where ESG issues are more visible, financially relevant, and reputationally sensitive. Furthermore, additional analyses show that reputational risk avoidance and ESG disclosure coordination explain this convergence effect, while cross‐national distance shapes the effectiveness of ESG coordination across countries. This study contributes to common ownership, institutional investors, and ESG strategy research by showing that ESG‐oriented common institutional ownership serves as a portfolio‐level governance mechanism that promotes ESG coherence among multinational rivals.

papers.title: Environmental, Social, and Governance Performance as a Driver of Green Innovation: Evidence from Green Patent Data
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines the relationship between environmental, social, and governance (ESG) performance and firms' green innovation (GI), positioning ESG as an organizational context potentially conducive to sustainable technological transformation. Using a patent‐based methodology, GI is measured through firms' granted green patent outputs, providing a tangible indicator of green technological innovation. Based on 3314 firm‐year observations from 17 countries over 2002–2021, baseline estimations use OLS models with multiple fixed effects, complemented by count‐data and alternative specifications. The findings show a positive and statistically significant relationship between ESG performance and GI, which remains consistent across alternative specifications. The environmental, social, and governance dimensions are each positively associated with green patent output, with the environmental dimension exhibiting the largest coefficient in the baseline estimates. Additional mechanism analyses indicate that R&D intensity and analyst coverage serve as significant partial mediating channels. R&D intensity represents a firm‐internal innovation input, whereas analyst coverage captures external information and monitoring environment. Overall, the findings provide cross‐country evidence that ESG performance is associated with tangible green technological outcomes and suggest that this relationship may operate through both internal resource allocation and external information and monitoring channels.

papers.title: Profit, Purpose and the ‘Price of Change’: Evidence From Benefit Corporation Transitions
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT This study investigates the short‐term financial consequences of transforming into a benefit corporation, a hybrid organisational form that embeds a dual mission of profit and public benefit. Drawing on the Social Resource‐Based View and sustainability‐oriented change management, we argue that the transition entails a reconfiguration of organisational priorities and resource allocation, which may temporarily affect firms' financial performance. Using a longitudinal event study on Italian firms, we compare transformed benefit corporations with a matched sample of non‐benefit firms. The results reveal lower performance in revenues, more tentative evidence on total assets, together with a reconfiguration of the debt structure following the transformation. Rather than signalling structural weakness, these dynamics may reflect transitional adjustment costs associated with the development of social and relational capabilities. The study contributes to research on hybrid organisations by clarifying the financial implications of benefit transformation and offers managerial insights on the need for careful financial planning during the transition process.

papers.title: How Are Strategic Orientations Related to Environmental Performance? Empirical Evidence From Moroccan Manufacturing Firms
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT In an era of intensifying competition, escalating environmental uncertainties, and heightened regulatory and societal pressures, firms, particularly in developing economies, face significant challenges in improving their environmental performance (EP). Grounded in the relational view and dynamic capabilities perspectives, this study examines how market orientation (MO) and entrepreneurial orientation (EO) are associated with EP. It tests a model in which supply chain integration (SCI) serves as a key mediator and organizational ambidexterity (ABX) acts as a crucial moderator. The empirical analysis draws on survey data from 275 Moroccan industrial businesses using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS‐SEM). The findings show that SCI significantly mediates the positive relationships between MO and EP, as well as between EO and EP. Furthermore, ABX significantly moderates the SCI‐EP nexus. This study supports the proximity argument of MO while emphasizing the crucial role of collaborative relationships and capabilities for achieving environmental outcomes in developing countries.

papers.title: Advancing Circular Economy Measurement in Agri‐Food: An Updated Dashboard of Indicators
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The increasing relevance of the circular economy in the agri‐food sector highlights the need for systematic tools to assess environmental, economic and social performance. Despite the proliferation of studies, literature still presents fragmentation and lacks comprehensive sets of indicators across certain thematic areas. This study develops an updated version of the Dashboard of circularity indicators for the agri‐food sector, reflecting recent advances in research and policy and addressing previously identified gaps. The methodology builds on prior work through a systematic literature review on the Scopus database, covering publications from 2020 to 2025. Out of 44 retrieved articles, 18 were selected for full‐text analysis, leading to the extraction of 156 indicators, harmonised into a final list of 116. Indicators were classified into eight thematic scopes, of which seven are populated with indicators, three spatial dimensions and the three pillars of sustainability. Further categorisation distinguished product and organisation‐level indicators, while also identifying cross‐linked and cross‐sectional metrics. Findings reveal significant quantitative and qualitative expansion, particularly in the economic and social domains, largely due to the integration of Common Agricultural Policy indicators. Nonetheless, gaps persist in air, water, knowledge and innovation. The updated dashboard provides a more coherent and multidimensional framework, supporting evidence‐based decision‐making and advancing the circular transition.

papers.title: From intra-disciplinary synthesis to problematizing theorization: Rethinking MNE sustainability in local markets
papers.abstract: This study conducted an intra-disciplinary review exploring how multinational enterprises (MNEs) contribute to sustainability in local markets within the fields of international business (IB) and strategy.It comprehensively examines four key themes of corporate social responsibility, economic (regional) development, social performance, and environmental sustainability of MNEs.By doing so, it seeks to consolidate fragmented findings from existing independent studies while broadening understanding through problematizing assumptions made in research.In addition, it sheds light on the complexities that MNEs face to address sustainability challenges, and how to strategically integrate economic, social, and environmental goals while adapting to global and local pressures.In turn, we propose new research directions and draw implications for MNEs in addressing grand challenges.Overall, this study contributes to deepening sustainability research in IB and strategy fields, and provides valuable insights for MNEs' sustainable business practice.

papers.title: Cultural intermediation through indigenous values-based accountability: the case of Bangarra Dance Theatre
papers.abstract: Purpose This paper examines how Indigenous values shape the accountability practices governing cultural intermediation. It investigates how accountability enables Indigenous relational governance to be sustained as Indigenous cultural knowledge circulates through cultural intermediation while remaining aligned with Indigenous custodial authority. Design/methodology/approach The study draws on a qualitative, longitudinal case study of Bangarra Dance Theatre, an Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander organisation operating as a cultural intermediary in Australia. Data were collected over twelve years through a combination of participant observation, semi-structured interviews, and documentary materials. Findings The analysis identifies Indigenous Values-Based Accountability as a set of interconnected accountability practices through which Indigenous relational governance is sustained. Through permission seeking, cultural observation, creative obligation, and return and renewal, IVBA organises Bangarra's continuing accountability as Indigenous cultural knowledge circulates across public and cross-cultural domains while sustaining Indigenous custodial authority. The findings further demonstrate how IVBA structures participation in cultural circulation by making engagement by sponsors, partners, and other external actors conditional upon Indigenous custodial authority. Originality/value This paper advances Indigenous accounting and accountability research by conceptualising accountability as a culturally embedded governance arrangement through which Indigenous values are enacted beyond Indigenous organisational and community settings. It demonstrates how Indigenous relational governance organises authority, reciprocity, and custodial responsibility as cultural knowledge circulates across public and cross-cultural domains. The paper further positions cultural intermediation as a distinctive accountability setting that, in our case, involves Bangarra remaining accountable to recognised custodians while Indigenous authority structures participation, representation, and engagement with non-Indigenous actors.

Data-driven approach to estimate ambient ammonia concentrations
papers.abstract: The Netherlands experiences significant environmental impacts from reactive nitrogen, particularly ammonia (NH 3 ), whose long-term deposition harms soil, water, and biodiversity. NH 3 is emitted mainly from agriculture and its levels can be very high and variable in intensive livestock areas. Although monitoring stations are set up across multiple locations, data gaps may still arise due to issues with measurement instruments. Therefore, there is a need for models that can reliably fill in these missing observations. In this study, we first applied Linear Regression, Random Forest, and Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) models to predict one day ahead NH 3 concentrations at six sites (De Zilk, Valthermond, Vredepeel, Wekerom, Wieringerwerf, Zegveld) in the Netherlands. All models captured daily NH 3 trends, with Random Forest initially performing best (R 2 up to 0.59 at Valthermond). Predictions were strongly driven by lagged NH 3 values with wind speed and precipitation contributing moderately. After correcting for prediction lag caused by autocorrelation, the linear regression performed best at most sites (with best performance observed at Zegveld with R 2 of 0.84) and was used for gap filling. It maintained reasonable accuracy despite sparse observations (every 2–7 days), with most sites (De Zilk, Valthermond, Vredepeel, Wekerom, Zegveld) exhibiting a significant correlation of almost or more than 0.5 even at 7 days measurement gaps. Additionally, we noted that historical data from existing sites could be effectively used to fill gaps at newly established locations that exhibited similar distributions of NH 3 .

Potential influence of landscape structure on water quality and phytoplankton community in highly degraded urban lakes: Implications for restoration
papers.abstract: Urban lakes are of particular concern in urban landscapes, as they provide ecological, social and economic benefits, but are under strong human pressure. The current study examined eleven urban lakes that differ in their morphometric and hydrological characteristics and were located across various macroregions of Poland. The aim was to examine potential relationships among landscape structure, water quality, and phytoplankton communities across three buffer zones (10 m, 100 m, and 1000 m), selected to reflect different spatial scales of land use/land cover (LU/LC). The urban lakes were characterised by different phytoplankton biomass, with a maximum of 181.3 mg/l. Most of them were dominated by toxic or potentially toxic cyanobacteria. Land use/cover explained the greatest percentage of variability (24.3%) in phytoplankton composition in the 100 m buffer zone. However, this relationship was only suggestive and did not reach the conventional level of statistical significance. In contrast, LU/LC explained little of the variation in physicochemical parameters across three spatial scales, accounting for up to 0.6% in the 10 m buffer zone, but with no statistically significant relationships. Phytoplankton play a more important role than other water quality parameters and can serve as a more sensitive indicator, providing complementary information for assessing the impact of landscape structure. Despite the large proportion of forest and seminatural areas, the urban lakes were classified as highly degraded, exhibiting poor or bad water quality, which can be more related to historical pollution than to current landscape structure. Our results indicate that a 100 m wide buffer zone may be a useful study-specific spatial scale for considering shoreline and surrounding LU/LC management. They can be prioritised for protection and restoration activities, as well as for planning future spatial development. Restoring natural vegetation within this zone may reduce the nutrient inflows and slow the process of cultural eutrophication. However, further studies with a larger number of lakes are needed to confirm these relationships.

A national dataset of downtown business district boundaries for pre-automobile U.S. cities and towns
papers.abstract: The downtown business district is a fundamental unit of analysis in urban revitalization research, yet no nationally consistent, publicly available dataset of downtown boundaries exists for small and mid-sized U.S. cities and towns. This paper introduces an open data product containing 6,551 downtown polygons for pre-automobile-era places spanning 47 contiguous states. The dataset is constructed from a fully reproducible, open-source R workflow: a national universe of historically significant places is assembled using historical census records, contemporary population data, and metropolitan classification criteria; points-of-interest data from the Overture Maps Foundation are collected within each place boundary; and a kernel density estimation algorithm identifies the highest-concentration commercial cluster as the downtown core. The resulting boundaries are validated against Main Street program districts, which the polygons cover at high rates in the two states examined. The polygons are deposited at Harvard Dataverse under a CC0 1.0 license, with all R code available on GitHub. The dataset supports research on downtown revitalization, Main Street commercial activity, and the economic geography of small and mid-sized American cities.

Optimal avoidability in cross-border minimum taxation
papers.abstract: Many tax regimes collect revenue to the extent that other governments do not. This paper develops a theory of how such cross-border minimum taxes should be designed, focusing on choices that affect avoidance of the regime. Making a minimum tax more difficult to avoid retains more firms within the regime but weakens competition among tax havens. Havens then raise their rates toward the minimum, reducing the top-up tax rate on shifted profit. As a result, an avoidable minimum tax can raise more revenue for the governments that impose it than an unavoidable one.

papers.title: Pricing climate risks: Evidence from wildfires and municipal bonds
papers.abstract: How are public finances affected by climate-driven changes in wildfire risk? Using high-resolution meteorological forecasts, land use data, and US municipal bond spreads, we find that municipalities facing greater future wildfire exposure already incur higher borrowing costs: A one standard deviation increase in future wildfire risk is associated with a 7 (8) basis point rise in primary (secondary) market spreads—over 15% of the sample mean. Impacts appear larger in areas with higher minority populations and greater reliance on local revenue. Our study contributes to the broader literature by introducing a new approach to evaluating the capitalization of evolving physical climate risks.

papers.title: The impact of preference programs in public procurement: Evidence from veteran set-asides
Geopoliticizing the Firm: Embraer, Corporate Nationality, and the Geopolitical Constitution of Contracts, Capabilities, and Markets
papers.abstract: Transnational corporations (TNCs) drive fast-changing global economic geographies amid fraught geopolitical relations. However, three influential theoretical accounts of the firm, the nexus of contracts, the resource-based view, and Global Production Networks 2.0, still underspecify how corporate nationality and home–host state geopolitical agendas constitute TNCs’ formation, operations, and strategic management. This omission creates a gap in explaining the connections between geopolitical conditions and TNC operations. This article addresses this gap by geopoliticizing the firm. To this end, it integrates key aspects of the three theoretical accounts into a novel conceptual framework that comprises three analytical mechanisms: geopolitical agenda alignment, territorially defined capability formation, and territorially differentiated product development. Empirically, the article primarily draws on twenty-two interviews with elites across different firms and institutions to examine how Embraer, an aerospace producer, evolved following its establishment in 1969 as an integral part of Brazilian state developmentalism. After privatization in 1994, Embraer simultaneously (dis)engaged with multiple state geopolitical agendas to straddle US–China geopolitical tensions and compete internationally. Such proactive geopolitical (dis)engagement augmented Embraer’s ability to secure contracts, create capabilities, and capture markets across multiple countries. Through this case study, the article demonstrates the importance of conceptualizing the entwinement of TNC activities with both corporate nationality and variegated geopolitical contexts.

papers.title: The Weight of Compliance: Anti-Money Laundering Enforcement, Banking Sector Composition, and Lending
papers.abstract: Abstract We examine how strengthened anti-money laundering (AML) enforcement affects the U.S. banking sector. Heightened enforcement disproportionately raises compliance costs for small banks, especially in counties more exposed to money laundering. In these areas, small banks contract while large banks expand, increasing standardized, government-supported, and secured lending. While aggregate county-level credit does not decline differentially, local outcomes improve. Small establishments grow, non-tradable employment and wages rise, and real estate prices increase. The evidence is consistent with a reallocation mechanism in which AML enforcement shifts activity toward large banks, potentially improving intermediation quality through changes in the composition of local financial intermediation.

papers.title: A Century of Stock Market Liquidity and Trading Costs
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT I assemble and examine an annual time series of bid–ask spreads on Dow Jones stocks from 1900 to 2000 and average commission rates for trading NYSE stocks since 1925. Spreads are cyclical, especially during periods of market turmoil. The sum of half‐spreads and one‐way commissions, multiplied by annual turnover, estimates the aggregate cost of trading and drives a wedge between gross and net equity returns. This difference explains only a small part of the observed equity premium, though I show that the gross equity premium is perhaps 1% lower today than it was early in the 1900's. Finally, I find that the transaction cost measures (spreads and turnover), which serve as a proxy for liquidity, predict stock returns 1 year or more ahead and dominate traditional measures such as the dividend yield. The evidence suggests aggregate liquidity is a determinant of expected stock market returns.

papers.title: The Impact of Early Investments in Urban School Systems in the United States
papers.abstract: Cities in the United States dramatically expanded spending on public education after WWI, with the average urban school district increasing per pupil expenditures by over 70 percent by 1924. We provide the first evaluation of these unprecedented investments in public education using a new dataset and plausibly exogenous growth in school spending generated by anti-German sentiment. We find that school resources significantly increased educational attainment and wages later in life, particularly for less advantaged children. Increases in expenditures can explain about 40 percent of the sizable increase in educational attainment of cohorts born between 1895 and 1913. “Every great war in which the United States has played a part has been followed by educational developments of supreme national importance…Although the United States was engaged in the World War less than two years, the effects upon education resulting from this brief period of warfare will perhaps prove to be as far-reaching and as important as those growing out of any previous war…Undoubtedly the World War was the most important factor in awakening the American public to the inadequacy of its educational provisions and in arousing the States to vigorous efforts to improve educational conditions.” —Fletcher Harper Swift, Biennial Survey of Education 1920–1922, Volume 1, (1924, pp. 1–2).

papers.title: School timing, sleep, and adolescent behavior: Evidence from lottery-assigned start times
Revisiting the price elasticity of charitable giving: Meta-analysis of tax incentives and matching donations
papers.abstract: This paper presents the first quantitative meta-analysis of the price elasticity of charitable giving under both rebate and matching schemes. We compile 137 elasticity estimates from 26 experimental papers and synthesize them using random-effects and multilevel models. Charitable giving is highly price-responsive: the pooled meta-analytic mean elasticity of total donations is −1.75, indicating that lowering the effective price of giving substantially increases charitable revenue. Although we observe considerable between-study heterogeneity and some evidence of publication bias, bias-adjusted estimates remain negative. Furthermore, elasticity is substantially more negative under matching (−2.44) than under rebate (−0.73), contradicting the theoretical prediction of equivalence but aligning with the original experimental findings in this literature. The rebate-matching difference is attenuated when moving from laboratory to field settings, although it persists.

papers.title: Human rights economics
papers.abstract: This article proposes a theoretical framework that systematically integrates human rights and economic analysis, addressing gaps in previous attempts linking theory and policy. Rather than developing a new theoretical approach, we work within a standard social planner setting in which a social welfare function embeds both fiscal constraints and rights-based valuations, ensuring Pareto-efficient outcomes while guaranteeing minimum rights. Conceptually, we link principles, policy instruments, and outcomes, highlighting shared structures across disciplines and enabling policy design that balances efficiency, equity, and transparency. Empirically, a case study of universal social protection strategies in South Africa illustrates how economic, human rights, and integrated approaches produce different priorities: targeted basic income maximizes fiscal efficiency, the universal transfer maximizes equality and rights, and the integrated perspective favors the expansion of the existing system as the second-most rights-consistent and most cost efficient option. This fully integrated framework demonstrates that human rights economics is not a slogan, nor merely the economics of human rights or rights within economics, but a true integration of both—practically applicable, context-sensitive, and offering a pathway to fiscally sustainable, socially inclusive, and administratively feasible policies.

papers.title: Economic impacts of pasture degradation at the municipal level: Evidence from Minas Gerais, Brazil
Government positions and climate change: paradigmatic conflict versus consensus in environmental performance
papers.abstract: Historically, environmental policy was framed as a fundamental trade-off between economic growth and ecological preservation. Since the mid-1980s, however, this dichotomy has been largely replaced by the paradigm of ecological modernization, expressed in concepts like “green growth” and “sustainable development,” which hold that economic growth and environmental protection are mutually reinforcing. This shift was accompanied by the assumption that a broad political consensus on reconciling economic growth and environmental protection would lead to superior environmental outcomes. Yet, the persistent gap between climate targets and actual emission trends necessitates a critical re-evaluation of this “consensus” approach and of whether the original antagonism between environmental protection and economic growth has genuinely been overcome. To assess this claim, this study tests six distinct conceptualizations of government ideology and policy focus, analyzing government positions across 35 advanced democracies from 1990 to 2021. The findings show that neither the focus on technocratic environmental issues, nor the classic left-right divide, nor the newer, more encompassing green-alternative versus traditional-authoritarian dimension predicts emissions performance. Instead, emissions decline where governments adopt growth-critical positions and even more where environmental ideology contrasts growth-oriented productionism with growth-critical environmental protection. This suggests that the depoliticization of climate policy may be part of the problem: ideological contestation over growth itself, not environmental consensus, emerges as the more effective driver of decarbonization.

papers.title: The effects of R&D tax credit and market competition policies on firms’ zero-leverage behaviour
papers.abstract: Abstract Motivated by the characteristics of R&D and its co-movement with the rising prevalence of zero-leverage firms over the past four decades, we investigate the effects of US R&D tax incentive and import tariff policies on zero-leverage behaviour. We find that the number of R&D-intensive firms has increased since the introduction of the R&D tax credit in 1981, and that zero-leverage firms are disproportionately concentrated among R&D firms. Both the increase in R&D investment and the rising sensitivity of leverage decisions to R&D contribute to this pattern. In addition, intensified market competition driven by tariff reductions significantly increases the likelihood of zero leverage among R&D firms, but not among non-R&D firms. Overall, our findings suggest that R&D tax incentives and trade liberalisation policies have played important roles in shaping the long-term trend of zero-leverage behaviour in the United States.

papers.title: Emerging Research Frontiers in Business Cycle Synchronization: A Review of Measurement, Evolution, and Driving Forces
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Offering new evidence on business cycle synchronization (BCS) has received special attention in recent decades owing to the structural shifts witnessed in the world economy. Hence, this study provides a survey of the literature on business cycle synchronization. The study aims to understand: (a) the definition, (b) measurement, (c) evolution, (d) determinants/driving forces, and (e) propose future research directions. This study highlights that correlation, dynamic correlation, the concordance index, the absolute growth differential, the decoupling index, and the network approach are the key measures of synchronization. While trade integration, financial integration, specialization, and policy similarity have emerged as key drivers, other factors, such as the global financial cycle, geographical proximity, and political factors, also drive synchronization. To track the evolution, this study delves into historical evidence, conventional wisdom, the world business cycle, sectoral and regional business cycles, the financial crisis perspective, the euro area, and the decoupling hypothesis. Finally, this study reveals that although economies are broadly synchronized during a specific period, they exhibit distinct synchronization patterns across different economies and groups at various time periods. Given the long‐standing and unsettled literature, these findings are highly relevant for policymakers, and the suggested research directions open avenues for future research.

papers.title: Review of Literature on Corporate Cash Holdings and Future Research Agenda in an ESG Framework
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT This study synthesizes the literature on corporate cash holdings under an ESG framework and develops a theoretically grounded future research agenda. Based on a systematic review of 116 studies screened from Scopus and Web of Science Core Collection, the literature is categorized into five streams: impacts of aggregate ESG, environmental, social, and governance factors on cash holdings, and reverse effects of cash holdings/financial slack on ESG‐related outcomes. ESG reshapes three established cash‐holding motives: the insurance value of liquidity, the financing wedge between internal and external funds, and agency costs of retained cash. The E, S, and G pillars present distinct mechanisms tied to environmental commitments, stakeholder/labor claims, and liquidity governance. Stronger ESG can reduce cash by lowering risk, financing frictions, or agency costs, while strategic liquidity needs, stakeholder commitments, and adverse ESG shocks may increase cash demand. Reverse evidence shows accumulated liquidity funds ESG investment and supports employment resilience, forming a dynamic bidirectional ESG‐cash relationship. Methodologically, OLS and fixed‐effects regressions dominate the literature, while quasi‐experimental, structural, and machine‐learning approaches remain rare. Future research could explore nonlinear, co‐determined ESG‐cash dynamics via E‐DSGE modeling, real‐options analysis, AI‐enabled liquidity management, and ESG contagion in strategic alliances.

papers.title: Mitigating time-varying buyer power through farmer commodity storage
papers.abstract: Abstract Buyer market power is a significant concern in many agricultural product procurement markets. Research almost exclusively treats such buyer power as a static element of agricultural market structure, despite evidence that buyer power varies across the marketing season for many commodities and locations. We study buyer power as a time-varying phenomenon and analyze the role of commodity storage in mitigating such power and increasing farmer incomes. Data-driven simulations show that strategic storage can generate significant farm income gains and risk reduction. Key factors determining welfare impacts are magnitudes and expected changes in buyer power and farmers’ storage efficiency and risk preferences.

papers.title: Corridors in Shallow Lakes: The Case of Intermediate Pollution
papers.abstract: Abstract We study optimal management of the standard shallow lake model with special attention to the damage caused by the accumulated phosphorus in the water of the lake. The occurrence of a tipping point leads to a stronger increase in the damage after moving from the low-damage to the high-damage regime, because of the loss of ecosystem services. We modify the standard quadratic damage function by introducing a jump in marginal damage when moving from the low-damage to the high-damage regime. Connecting the lower and the higher marginal damage functions yields a continuous piecewise linear marginal damage function with a strong increase around the jump. In addition to the well-known oligotrophic and eutrophic steady states, we find that a third steady state can occur, separated by two Skiba points. This implies that a corridor or a basin of attraction arises between these two Skiba points where optimal management of the lake stabilizes the amount of phosphorus somewhere in the middle instead of either moving to the low-damage or to the high-damage regime, as is the result in the standard knife-edge case with one Skiba point.

papers.title: A Cross‐Country Study of Carbon Risk and Financial Constraints: The Role of Carbon Disclosure Quality
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT We examine whether firm‐level carbon risk affects financial constraints and whether the quality of carbon disclosure moderates this relationship. Using 16,274 firm‐year observations from 50 countries from 2007 to 2023, we find that higher carbon risk is associated with greater financial constraints. The result is robust to entropy balancing, Heckman correction, instrumental variables and a quasi‐natural experiment based on the 2013 UK carbon disclosure regulation. High‐quality disclosure weakens this association, suggesting that transparency reduces financing frictions by lowering information asymmetry. Additional analyses show that governance, monitoring and institutional context shape the financing consequences of carbon risk.

papers.title: The Effect of a Miscarriage Compared to a Completed Pregnancy on Mental Health Care Use, Labour Market and Family Outcomes
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Miscarriages occur in about 15% of recognised pregnancies and often cause grief and stress. We investigate the effect of a miscarriage on mental health care use, labour market and family outcomes of women and their partners using an event study framework applied to Dutch linked administrative data. After a miscarriage, women's use of mental health care temporarily increase compared to before the miscarriage, while their partner's use is unaffected. Furthermore, miscarriages affect labour market trajectories and reduce the probability of living together. Results are similar when comparing the effects of a miscarriage with the effects of having a child using a matched sample of women with a completed pregnancy.

papers.title: Do Tax Incentives Enhance Entrepreneurship? Evidence from Value‐Added Tax Reform in China
papers.abstract: Abstract This paper investigates the causal effect of tax incentives on entrepreneurship. Using a staggered Value‐Added Tax (VAT) reform in China as an exogenous shock to conduct difference‐in‐differences estimation, we find that tax cuts have a considerable positive effect on local entrepreneurship. A plausible mechanism driving our findings is the ease of financial constraints. Our results are robust to a battery of endogeneity and robustness tests. We find that regions with high levels of institutional quality, trust, or a commercial culture undergo greater entrepreneurship after the VAT reform. Overall, this study provides a timely policy evaluation of the importance of tax incentives in promoting entrepreneurship in a typical emerging market.
papers.journal_name: Journal of Money, Credit and Banking

papers.title: The Tipping Point: Interest Rates and Financial Stability
papers.abstract: Abstract This paper studies the impact of interest rates on bank stability in a standard bank‐run model. Banks invest in long‐term assets, whose value decreases with interest rates, and set deposit rates to optimally insure depositors' liquidity risk. Liquidity‐risk insurance implies banks earn interest margins, which increase with interest rates. Hence, interest rates have two countervailing effects: they reduce the value of banks' long‐term assets while widening their margins. First, the paper characterizes the parametric condition under which an effect dominates. The condition implies interest‐rate risk is captured by banks' maturity mismatch adjusted for deposits' effective duration. Second, the paper solves for the interest‐rate level that tips banks into instability. Quantification points to the possibility of a negative effective maturity mismatch, making the tipping point a lower bound on interest rates.

papers.title: Color me aroused while keeping the cool
papers.abstract: Abstract Drawing on visual complexity theory and the arousal properties of color, this paper challenges the prevailing assumption that only warm (longer wavelength) or highly saturated colors can induce arousal in consumers. Instead, we propose a novel pathway: multicolor logos with cool hues can elicit arousal through triggering curiosity. Across a total of eight experiments (seven preregistered with a total of 1,724 participants recruited), of which six experiments are reported in the main text, including a behavioral lab study employing biometric measures (eye tracking, galvanic skin response, pupil dilation), and three studies utilizing real product choices, we consistently find that multicolor cool logos are more arousing than single cool color designs. This heightened, curiosity-driven arousal subsequently impacts marketing outcomes, including willingness to pay and choice. These findings offer marketers alternative strategies for inducing arousal in brand communications and provide actionable guidelines for effectively designing logos.
