papers.title: EXPRESS: Incentive Design for Sales Managers: Impact on Resource Allocation and Performance
papers.abstract: Many firms struggle to design effective incentives for sales managers . Yet despite a vast literature on salespeople’s incentives, little theoretical or empirical research has examined managers’ incentive structures. The authors address a common dilemma that firms face: Should managers’ incentives be based on achieving an aggregate target ( Aggregate Target Scheme , ATS) or instead be linked to the target achievement of each individual territory or salesperson ( Individual Target Scheme , ITS)? A quasi-experiment reveals that, despite ATS’s flexibility and apparent alignment with firm objectives, an ATS-to-ITS transition improved performance , with larger gains among lower-performing and higher-span territories. A scenario-based experiment with sales managers suggests that these effects may stem from the reallocation of resources from high to low performers but provides no evidence of an increase in managers’ overall resource investment. A survey of sales leaders indicates that a sales star bias —a managerial tendency to overallocate resources toward high performers relative to their marginal returns—likely drives suboptimal resource allocation under the flexible ATS. Finally, a supplementary field study documents that, following an ATS-to-ITS transition, managers increased joint fieldwork , especially with the lowest performers, and performance again improved. These results provide insights into managerial incentive design and offer guidance for firms.

papers.title: Unpacking the micro–macro transmission mechanism: how home-country culture selectively shapes cognitive orientations in entrepreneurial internationalization
papers.abstract: Abstract International business accounts treat national culture as a country-level antecedent that shifts average export propensity uniformly, leaving the individual-level mechanisms producing within-country heterogeneity in internationalization intensity unspecified. We address this micro–macro transmission gap using social cognitive theory, examining how individualism versus collectivism and risk avoidance versus tolerance selectively recalibrate three cognitive orientations in entrepreneurial export decisions: perceived self-efficacy, perceived opportunity availability, and fear of failure. Our multilevel analysis of 40,529 observations across 41 countries spanning 2010–2019 reveals divergent rather than uniform moderation: individualism amplifies self-efficacy and opportunity availability beliefs through the social validation pathway, while risk avoidance constrains opportunity availability beliefs and fear of failure through the anticipatory self-regulation and outcome expectancy pathways. Fear of failure’s directional relationship with internationalization is contingent on the expectations of failure costs that the home-country cultural environment establishes through the outcome expectancy pathway, rather than being uniformly inhibitory as prior frameworks assume. These findings advance international business microfoundations theory by specifying the observable transmission pathways through which national cultural dimensions produce heterogeneous export intensity outcomes within the same national context. For policymakers, the findings imply that interventions to strengthen self-efficacy or opportunity awareness work best when calibrated to a country’s cultural profile.

papers.title: Correction: National identity rhetoric under bilateral geopolitical tensions: evidence from Taiwanese MNEs
Generative AI use in entrepreneurship: An integrative review and the Empowerment–Entrapment Framework
papers.abstract: Abstract Research Summary Despite the growing use of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) in entrepreneurship, research on its impact remains fragmented. To address this limitation, we provide an integrative, entrepreneur‐centered review of how GenAI influences entrepreneurs at each stage of the entrepreneurial process: (1) opportunity recognition and ideation, (2) opportunity evaluation and commitment, (3) resource assembly and mobilization, and (4) venture launch and growth. Based on our review, we propose the Empowerment–Entrapment Framework, which not only catalogs GenAI's benefits and costs throughout the entrepreneurial process but also identifies potential trade‐offs underlying GenAI's double‐edged role. For example, GenAI may improve venture idea quality yet produce hallucinations and biases; boost entrepreneurial self‐efficacy yet heighten overconfidence; increase functional breadth and self‐sufficiency yet reduce prosociality; and enhance productivity yet diminish cognitive engagement, learning, and memory. We also identify features of GenAI that underlie these empowering and entrapping effects. Moreover, we explore boundary conditions that moderate GenAI's effects, including entrepreneurs' expertise, approaches to GenAI use, and personal traits and values. Beyond these theoretical contributions, our review and framework offer practical guidance for entrepreneurs seeking to use GenAI strategically while managing its risks. Managerial Summary We review how GenAI influences entrepreneurs at each stage of the entrepreneurial process: opportunity recognition and ideation, opportunity evaluation and commitment, resource assembly and mobilization, and venture launch and growth. Based on this review, we propose the Empowerment–Entrapment Framework to help entrepreneurs understand GenAI's trade‐offs at each stage. The future of entrepreneurship will depend less on whether entrepreneurs use GenAI than on how they use it. Used thoughtfully, GenAI may empower entrepreneurs by expanding their capabilities to engage in entrepreneurial activities. Used uncritically, GenAI may entrap entrepreneurs by restricting or eroding those capabilities. Entrepreneurs should therefore verify what GenAI produces, calibrate GenAI use to their expertise and task demands, and decide which tasks to delegate to GenAI while retaining human judgment for consequential decisions.

papers.title: The Signaling Role of Seemingly Myopic Investment Behavior
Navigating the Rugged Data Landscape: The Impact of Data-Extrapolation Technologies on Knowledge Production
papers.abstract: Data-extrapolation technologies enable progress by importing and applying empirical patterns from one domain to another. Their reliance on empirical patterns, however, is also their limitation: these tools can only be applied where data are abundant. Using the setting of structural biology, I investigate the impact of a data-extrapolation technology on innovation. I exploit the variation in prior data availability to compare areas in which the tool was usable to those in which it was not. I find that the tool increased the quantity of research in data-rich areas: the resulting output yielded limited biological insights but was methodologically rigorous and contributed to downstream research. This paper was accepted by Toby Stuart, entrepreneurship and innovation. Supplemental Material: The online appendix and data files are available at https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2023.04115 .

papers.title: Selection into Financial Education and Effects on Portfolio Choice
papers.abstract: We study the impact of a financial education program on portfolio choices in a setting that allows us to examine both participation decisions and differences in program benefits across individuals. We directly elicit willingness to pay for financial education and show that individuals with higher financial literacy, greater confidence in applying new knowledge, and higher expected returns are willing to pay more. Using incentivized portfolio allocation tasks, we develop outcome measures tailored to individual risk preferences and show that financial education improves decision quality along these dimensions. The program increases the share of participants who experience an improvement by 20 percentage points, corresponding to average gains of 3.2 percentage points of initial wealth. Individuals with the highest willingness to participate benefit disproportionately from the program, with important implications for the design and evaluation of financial education initiatives. By isolating a specific investment skill in a setting with voluntary participation, our design sheds light on how selection into financial education shapes measured program effects and informs the assessment of broader workplace and public training programs. This paper was accepted by Marie Claire Villeval, behavioral economics and decision analysis. Funding: The authors thank the Pension Research Council of Wharton School at the University of Pennsylvania, as well as the Retirement and Savings Institute at HEC Montréal, for generous research funding. Supplemental Material: The online appendices and data files are available at https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2024.08268 .

papers.title: The Efficiency Trap of Agentic AI in Human Resource Management
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Agentic AI transforms HRM from data‐driven support to autonomous execution. Organizations deploy these recursive workflows to eliminate human implementation variance, yet we challenge the assumption that such alignment remains optimal. Drawing on Weick's theory of loose coupling, we argue that delegating HR execution to agentic AI creates algorithmic tight coupling. While this generates immediate hyper‐fit, the removal of strategic slack leads to structural calcification, compromising organizational resilience during polycrises. Human line managers provide a critical buffer, enabling the sensemaking necessary to absorb systemic shocks. In contrast, agentic AI workflows governed by instrumental rationality lack the value rationality required for complex organizing. We propose a governance framework to reconcile machine‐driven consistency with the human stewardship required to preserve long‐term organizational adaptability.

papers.title: Machine Learning Instrument Variables for Causal Inference
papers.abstract: A machine learning framework for constructing strong instrumental variables from weak exogenous data achieves semiparametric efficiency with applications to advertising and demand estimation.

papers.title: Do PCAOB Inspection Deficiencies Related to Management Review Controls Affect Financial Reporting Decisions? Evidence From Goodwill Impairments
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT We examine whether PCAOB inspection deficiencies related to management review controls (MRCs) affect financial reporting decisions. Using the goodwill impairment setting, we find that firms are more likely to record goodwill impairments when their auditors have received more PCAOB inspection deficiencies related to goodwill MRCs. The association is stronger when inspection deficiencies are more likely to lead to changes to the design or implementation of an internal control (repeat deficiencies and deficiencies related to MRC precision). We observe some evidence that MRC inspection deficiencies increase the likelihood of goodwill impairment even when unrelated to goodwill, indicating that improving the audit of MRCs can broadly affect financial reporting. Our findings provide evidence that PCAOB inspections affect not only auditor behavior but also the financial reporting behavior of audit clients. Specifically, inspection feedback appears to influence reporting outcomes through changes in the audit and evaluation of MRCs, identifying a channel through which regulatory oversight affects issuers. The results have implications for audit firms seeking to remediate inspection deficiencies, for management and audit committees responsible for overseeing significant estimates and impairment analyses, and for regulators evaluating the broader effectiveness of the PCAOB inspection process.

papers.title: Do Audit Committee Characteristics Influence Climate‐Related Disclosure? Evidence From Italian Listed Firms
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Research concerning the determinants of corporate climate disclosure has primarily focused on the board of directors, whereas evidence regarding the audit committee (AC), whose oversight directly influences the reporting process, remains limited and inconclusive. Drawing on agency and stakeholder theories, this study examines whether AC characteristics explain the extent of climate‐related disclosure. We hand‐code a 13‐item Climate Disclosure Index aligned with the Task Force on Climate‐related Financial Disclosures from the 2024 non‐financial reports of 211 Italian‐listed firms and estimate hierarchical regressions. AC gender diversity and meeting frequency are positively and significantly associated with disclosure extent, whereas AC size and independence are not; firms in environmentally sensitive industries (ESI) exhibit a greater disclosure extent than non‐ESI firms. Results hold across several robustness tests, including Tobit regression, regional controls, and entropy balancing. These findings provide implications for managers and policymakers, highlighting the need to promote AC activism and gender diversity as essential internal mechanisms to enhance corporate accountability in response to the climate crisis.

papers.title: Boards of Directors and Voluntary Carbon Disclosure: Evidence From Italy
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines whether Italy's concentrated ownership environment alters the effectiveness of board‐level governance mechanisms as drivers of voluntary carbon disclosure quality, in line with the institutional theory, challenging the assumptions of standard agency and stakeholder theories. Using a sample of 60 Italian listed non‐financial companies over 2015–2023, we employ the Carbon Disclosure Project scores as a measure of disclosure quality. The presence of a corporate social responsibility committee is the only governance mechanism consistently associated with the disclosure quality across all specifications. Board independence exhibits a significant negative effect, consistent with the symbolic compliance hypothesis, according to which independent directors in blockholder‐dominated firms may function as compliance figures rather than effective monitors. Board size, gender diversity, and CEO duality are not significantly associated with disclosure quality. Further analysis shows that the CSR committee effect is stronger in carbon‐intensive industries and weaker in family‐controlled firms. Family ownership also attenuates the negative effect of board independence, suggesting that concentrated ownership selectively conditions, rather than uniformly suppresses, governance effectiveness. Results are robust to alternative estimators, lag structures, and endogeneity tests. Overall, the findings provide novel evidence that governance–disclosure relationships documented in dispersed ownership settings do not readily extend to blockholder‐dominated environments, with important implications for governance reforms in similar institutional contexts.

papers.title: Decoupling Sustainability Reporting and Social Media Communication After a Sustainability Scandal: Strategic Silence, Selective Disclosure and Legitimacy Stabilisation
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines how corporate sustainability disclosure evolves across a legitimacy‐threatening event by analysing the interaction between formal sustainability reporting and social media communication. Using a qualitative, longitudinal, event‐centred single‐case design, the study investigates a major Italian organic meat producer over the 2021–2024 period through formal sustainability reporting, Facebook content and stakeholder interactions, regulatory and contextual documents and selected economic indicators. Findings reveal a marked divergence across corporate‐controlled disclosure channels. Formal sustainability reporting remained active and progressively expanded, whereas sustainability‐related Facebook communication sharply contracted after the scandal despite continued overall platform activity. Stakeholder interactions shifted from predominantly routine and positive before the scandal to markedly critical during it, before progressively normalising in 2024. The study contributes to the literature by conceptualising strategic silence as topic‐specific avoidance within active communication, identifying multi‐channel communication fragmentation and showing how post‐scandal dynamics may involve delayed and selective acknowledgement alongside legitimacy stabilisation without comprehensive legitimacy repair.

papers.title: Capability Configurations Linking Circular Economy Practices to Sustainable Supply Chain Performance: A Theory‐Building Systematic Literature Review
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Circular economy ( CE ) practices do not automatically result in sustainable supply chain performance (SSCP), indicating the need for a conceptual explanation of how capabilities support the translation of CE practices into SSCP. This study employed a Scopus‐based theory‐building systematic literature review followed by cross‐study conceptual synthesis. The synthesis identified three complementary capability configurations with different yet interrelated functions: Information‐Digital‐Adaptive and Relational‐Integration primarily serve enabling roles by supporting information processing, analytics, visibility, collaboration, and coordination, whereas Operational‐Adaptive serves a transmitting role by translating enabling resources and CE requirements into coordinated and adaptive supply chain responses. The effectiveness of these configurations is context‐dependent and may vary with industry dynamism, supply chain integration, technological readiness, institutional and stakeholder pressures, and firm and resource characteristics. The proposed framework extends Dynamic Capability Theory by shifting attention from individual capabilities toward capability complementarity, differentiated functional roles, and contextual cross‐capability mechanisms.

papers.title: The Rise of Carbon Finance: A Bibliometric Perspective
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Carbon finance has emerged as a critical mechanism for mobilizing capital toward climate change mitigation and supporting the transition to low‐carbon economies. However, its intellectual development remains fragmented across environmental economics, financial economics, sustainability, and climate policy. This study provides a comprehensive bibliometric assessment of carbon finance research, examining its growth trajectory, intellectual structure, collaboration patterns, thematic evolution, and emerging research frontiers. Using 1610 Scopus‐indexed publications from 1993 to 2026, the study integrates performance analysis, citation impact, science mapping, network analysis, thematic visualization, Bradford's law, Lotka's law, journal quality indicators, and life cycle analysis. The findings reveal substantial growth, particularly following the Paris Agreement, alongside a concentrated intellectual structure in which China leads publication productivity, whereas the United States, the United Kingdom, and Japan demonstrate strong citation influence. Collaboration networks indicate increasing internationalization, although research remains concentrated among a limited number of authors and institutions. Thematic evolution demonstrates a shift from carbon markets, emissions trading, and environmental regulation toward green finance, sustainable investment, climate‐related financial risk, renewable‐energy financing, ESG integration, and digital finance. The study contributes by extending the temporal coverage of previous bibliometric reviews, integrating multiple analytical approaches, and explicitly tracing the progressive financialization of carbon finance. It reconciles divergent patterns in productivity, citation influence, collaboration, and development across countries and disciplines. By identifying structural patterns, emerging themes, and underexplored research frontiers, the study provides an evidence‐based agenda for future research and informs policymakers, standard‐setters, investors, and practitioners seeking to advance sustainable financial systems and climate transition strategies.

papers.title: Bio In, Garbage Out? A Review of Paradoxes and Trade‐Offs in the Circular Bioeconomy
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The circular bioeconomy (CBE) is increasingly presented as a promising way to advance corporate environmental sustainability by combining the use of renewable, bio‐based resources with circular economy principles of resource efficiency and lifecycle management. However, despite growing interest in the CBE, limited attention has been paid to the tensions that emerge in its implementation across the value cycle. This gap matters, as the transition to the CBE requires substantial technological, organizational, regulatory, and market changes that create competing yet interdependent demands for firms and other stakeholders. Drawing on paradox theory as a detective theoretical lens, this study systematically reviews 58 articles to identify and map the tensions characterizing the CBE. In doing so, we distinguish between trade‐offs and paradoxes, examine where these tensions are located, and assess how they concentrate across the CBE value cycle. Our findings indicate that tensions arise unevenly—with the highest concentration occurring during the procurement and processing of raw materials—and that issues related to resource availability, technological development, supply chain adaptation, and regulatory uncertainty are particularly significant. By providing a systemic account of tensions within the CBE, this study extends research on sustainability transitions and offers a foundation for understanding the contradictory demands that firms must navigate as they pursue circular bio‐based strategies.

papers.title: Smart Industry and Ecological Sustainability: Industry 4.0 Technologies, Renewables, and the US Production Ecological Footprint
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The United States ranks 5th globally in terms of the per capita ecological footprint (ECF) and 2nd in terms of the total ECF and is responsible for intensive energy consumption, resource exploitation, and carbon‐intensive industrial production. However, achieving sustainable industrial development requires understanding which ecological modernization pathways are associated with reducing environmental pressures in the long run. Our study evaluates the long‐term associations of AI and eco‐innovation, supply chain efficiency, industrial renewable energy consumption, GDP growth, and foreign direct investment with the ECF in the United States. In terms of methodology, the study employs autoregressive distributed lag (ARDL) using US data from 1990 to 2023. The long‐run ARDL estimation suggests that AI and eco‐innovation, supply chain efficiency, and industrial renewable energy consumption are statistically significant and negatively associated with the ECF in the country over the long run. In contrast, GDP growth and foreign direct investment are significant positive ECF drivers within long‐run dynamics. However, supply chain efficiency shows the largest estimated negative long‐term association with ECF among the modernization pathways examined. Nevertheless, this result is model‐specific evidence rather than proof of universal superiority in comparison with other modernization pathways. Alternative long‐run estimators provide additional support for the baseline associations, although the alternative‐indicator specifications reveal sensitivity to variable measurement. In addition, the Toda–Yamamoto Granger causality results suggest that FDI follows unidirectional predictive precedence toward ECF. Overall, the findings suggest that ecological modernization in the United States operates through innovation capability, operational efficiency, and energy transition, each of which is associated with ECF through a different mechanism. Federal policymakers may consider prioritizing these ecological modernizers as long‐term complementary pathways and set combined policy actions to reduce ECF in the country.

papers.title: Sustainable Dreams, Overlooked Realities: Closing the Design–Outcome Gap in Sustainable Business Models
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Sustainable business models (SBMs) are enablers of the circular economy ( CE ) and sustainability. However, its adoption does not always improve environmental performance. This study investigates the conditions under which SBM design does (or does not) produce the expected environmental benefits. We conducted a secondary cross‐case analysis of three use‐oriented product–service–system (PSS) business model (BM) implemented by three distinct Swedish companies that previously had been assessed using business model life cycle assessment (BM‐LCA). Across the cases, environmental performance outcomes were not primarily determined by BM main property (i.e., reuse, sharing, or rental) as such, but by a set of conditions (e.g., product return rates, enabling infrastructure, location, and consumer behavior). Overall, the results show that sustainability benefits are not inherent to SBM archetypes. A key learning is that the singular design focus, institutional pressure to “show” sustainability, and lack of quantitative assessment contribute to the poor environmental performance of the SBM in the studied cases. We also show that the absence of empirical validation can foster a wishful thinking that well‐intentioned environmental efforts are enough. The study contributes by specifying conditions that shape SBM's environmental performance, clarifying when and why environmental performance outcomes of SBMs can diverge from their design expectations. We further show how BM‐LCA can be integrated into SBM analysis to operationalize and test the sustainability assumptions embedded in BM design. This positions BM‐level, life cycle–based assessment as a structured decision‐support and learning tool for assessing and refining SBMs.

papers.title: Regulatory Governance and Sustainable Logistics Performance in India: The Conditional Role of Operational Capabilities
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Logistics performance is critical to economic competitiveness and resilient supply networks, particularly in emerging economies facing technological, infrastructural, workforce, environmental, and institutional constraints. However, limited attention has been given to how regulatory governance conditions the effects of these operational factors on logistics performance. This study examines the determinants of sustainable logistics performance in India's transportation sector, focusing on the moderating role of government policies and regulatory compliance. Drawing on Institutional Theory, the Technology Acceptance Model, and Innovation Diffusion Theory, an integrated framework links transportation infrastructure, technology adoption and automation, system integration, supply chain (SC) coordination, environmental factors, and driver shortage and turnover to logistics performance. The proposed relationships are examined using partial least squares structural equation modeling with moderation analysis. The findings indicate that transportation infrastructure, technology adoption and automation, system integration, SC coordination, and environmental factors are positively associated with logistics performance, whereas driver shortage and turnover are negatively associated. Government policies and regulatory compliance moderates two relationships: They mitigate the negative association between driver shortage and logistics performance but attenuate the positive association between SC coordination and performance. The findings highlight the need for regulatory frameworks that address workforce constraints without limiting coordination and operational flexibility. The study contributes to sustainable logistics research by demonstrating that regulatory governance can condition, rather than uniformly determine, the performance effects of operational capabilities.

papers.title: Antecedents, Mediators, Moderators and Outcomes of Circular Business Models: A Systematic Literature Review
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Circular business models (CBMs) have gained increasing scholarly attention as organisations seek to transition toward more sustainable and regenerative economic systems. Despite this growing body of research, the literature remains fragmented across disciplines and lacks an integrated understanding of the drivers, mechanisms, contextual conditions and outcomes associated with CBM implementation. To address this gap, this study conducts a systematic literature review of 477 peer‐reviewed articles published between 2017 and 2024 spanning business, management, environmental science and sustainability disciplines. Through an inductive synthesis of recurring patterns, four higher‐order dimensions were identified: antecedents, mediators, moderators and outcomes. These dimensions form the basis of the AMMO framework, a causal model that links organisational and ecosystem‐level drivers to sustainability outcomes through mediating mechanisms and moderating contextual conditions. By consolidating dispersed insights into a coherent explanatory model, this study advances CBM theorising, outlines a structured research agenda for future research and provides practical guidance for managers and policymakers seeking to identify key drivers, mechanisms and boundary conditions for circular transitions.

papers.title: Emotional labor in the age of service robots: Comparing hospitality and other service sectors through service robot support, ego depletion, and service performance
Interpretable machine learning for customer satisfaction optimization
papers.abstract: Purpose Understanding how dining experiences are transformed into customer satisfaction judgments is central to hospitality competitiveness. Using high-dimensional user-generated content on tourism dining experiences, this study aims to examine whether shared three-factor classifications coexist with segment-specific differences in satisfaction relationships. Design/methodology/approach The authors analyze 82,105 Yelp restaurant reviews from nine market segments based on price level, cuisine type and restaurant category. Bidirectional encoder representations from transformers-based aspect mining and clustering extract attribute–sentiment pairs. Ensemble models estimate nonlinear predictive relationships, and SHAP decomposes their predictions to support attribute classification, segment-specific satisfaction functions and diagnostic prioritization. Findings Empirical results reveal a basic-dominant pattern together with segment-level variation in estimated penalty–reward magnitudes, satisfaction-function shapes and diagnostic priorities. This pattern remains largely stable under alternative impact asymmetry thresholds and the procedure based on penalty-reward contrast analysis. Categorical stability can therefore coexist with segment-contingent differences in evaluative weight and relationship form. Practical implications Theoretically, the findings highlight the value of extending attribute classification with segment-specific satisfaction-function analysis, because segment heterogeneity is expressed within, and not only between, three-factor categories. Practically, managers can use the framework to diagnose service attributes with higher marginal predictive utility and develop more targeted, segment-specific improvement priorities. Originality/value This study refines the categorical interpretation of three-factor theory by showing that a shared attribute classification does not imply an invariant satisfaction relationship. Segment heterogeneity can occur within a shared category through differences in penalty–reward magnitude and satisfaction-function shape, not only through category shifts.
papers.journal_name: International Journal of Contemporary Hospitality Management

papers.title: The role of leadership on employee mental ill‐health through workplace disruption: A systematic review and meta‐analysis of longitudinal research
papers.abstract: Abstract As socio‐global events more frequently disrupt workplaces, understanding leadership's dynamic and context‐sensitive role in shaping employee wellbeing during periods of uncertainty has become increasingly important. Drawing on the Conservation of Resources Theory, this study synthesized current longitudinal evidence on the association between leadership and mental ill‐health (i.e. stress, burnout, psychological distress). We systematically reviewed 106 longitudinal studies, and meta‐analysed 191 time‐lagged effect sizes, to compare direct leadership associations and the moderating role of workplace disruption. Twenty‐four studies reported a disruptive workplace context, identified by the novelty, criticality or discontinuity of the event. Meta‐analytic results revealed that leadership styles differed in the magnitude of their peak observed association with employee mental ill‐health outcomes. Servant Leadership showed the strongest negative association with burnout across all leadership styles, although evidence was mixed across other outcomes. Destructive/Abusive Leadership styles had consistently strong effects across all mental ill‐health outcomes. Workplace disruption weakened the negative association of Supportive Leadership and stress, but further amplified the positive association between Autocratic Leadership and psychological distress. Statistical analyses and narrative commentary identified key opportunities to improve future longitudinal leadership research. Organizations can leverage these findings to promote sustainable leadership behaviours that enhance mental health generally and through adversity.
papers.journal_name: Journal of Occupational and Organizational Psychology

papers.title: Different strokes for different folks: how firms’ language complexity influences Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) rating divergence?
The evolving role of organisational foresight: Implications for the food service industry
papers.abstract: This article examines the evolving role of organisational foresight (OF), by integrating economics of innovation and managerial economics perspectives. The analysis investigates the interplay between foresight practices, coordination of routines and innovation, and how OF can be adopted to address mounting environmental and social challenges in the underexplored context of Small and Medium-sized Enterprises (SMEs) of the food service industry (FSI). Hypotheses were tested using partial least squares structural equation modelling on data collected from 204 managers of Brazilian FSI firms via an online questionnaire, complemented by a subsequent qualitative investigation. The results reveal that OF positively affects coordination of routines and innovation of firms. Innovation also positively affects green corporate social responsibility (GCSR) and sustainable performance (SP) of firms. Coordination of routines plays a mediating role that strengthens the association between OF and innovation. Furthermore, innovation mediates the relationship between OF and GCSR, as well as between OF and SP. In the context of FSI SMEs, foresight appears as a more informal, experiential sense-making capability. Although OF is a systematic process of thinking strategically about the future, OF per se is not enough. Firms should integrate a selection of dynamic capabilities into OF to strengthen their innovation, GCSR, and sustainable performance. The formalisation of additional management capabilities related to the coordination of routines, can make this process more effective. OF can shift from a theoretical exercise towards more socially- and environmentally-oriented actions which should be embedded into the culture of FSI firms.

papers.title: Beyond a Name: The CAPE Framework for Names, Nicknames, and (Nick)Naming in Marketing
More to gain, less to lose? Chinese firms’ US patenting strategies amidst decoupling
papers.abstract: US-China geopolitical tensions have produced decoupling policies that restrict Chinese firms’ access to most assets within strategic industries in the US. Yet Chinese firms in strategic industries can still legally obtain patents in the US, though doing so poses political risks and even this access may be restricted in the future. How do Chinese firms seek assets abroad in this new geopolitical environment? Drawing on the Attention-Based View, we argue that decoupling redirects attention of managers at Chinese firms in strategic industries to significantly increase US patenting because restrictions on alternative assets heighten patents’ relative value, reduce the perceived costs of exploiting them aggressively, and create urgency to secure them before access is potentially restricted. In contrast, managers with lived experience in the US or politically similar markets are theorized to perceive greater political risks of this strategy, leading their firms to increase patenting less. Using a difference-in-differences approach analyzing USPTO patent filings by publicly-listed Chinese firms from 2013–2023, we find support for our hypotheses. Robustness checks, including tests showing no comparable increase in patenting by the Chinese firms in other major foreign markets, corroborate these results. Further, supplementary analysis indicates that the increase in patenting is associated with fewer claims per patent — a pattern consistent with the strategic use of patents, potentially as weapons and transactable assets, rather than proportionally greater inventiveness. Our findings highlight how geopolitical decoupling intensifies firms’ pursuit of still-accessible assets in host markets, tempered by managers’ attention to political risks.

papers.title: Media Framing, Solidarity, and Tourism in Wartime
papers.abstract: This study examines how the framing of newspaper articles shapes place solidarity and associated tourism implications during the Russia-Ukraine war, and how these framing effects vary according to national values of the countries in which the articles were published. Drawing on framing theory, Hofstede’s national values, and the place solidarity concept, we analyze 379 newspaper articles from 46 countries using quantitative content analysis and categorical principal component analysis. Justice- and threat-focused frames in newspapers are associated with place solidarity, which is linked to media-represented tourism implications such as willingness to visit Ukraine, hospitality toward Ukrainians, and perceived tourism spillovers. Several national values moderate these relationships, indicating contingent framing effects. The study advances understanding of how media narratives construct solidarity during crises and how cultural contexts influence tourism outcomes.

papers.title: How the European Union Fell Out of Love With Open‐Source Software
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT This article explains why the European Commission diluted the 2004 European Interoperability Framework's provisions favoring open‐source software and open standards when it revised the framework in 2010. Using an extended Multiple Streams Framework with a technology stream, the study shows how pro‐openness policy entrepreneurs secured the 2004 provisions and why incumbent advocacy became more effective during revision. Drawing on annotated drafts and expert interviews, the study traces actors' lobbying strategies across the problem, politics, and policy streams and examines how technology‐stream developments altered the feasibility and political salience of competing solutions. The analysis shows how changing standards and licensing dynamics, incumbent advocacy, and declining political support for the earlier pro‐openness package enabled a new coupling around business‐model neutrality and licensing flexibility, diluting the 2004 provisions. Beyond the European case, the study informs debates on open‐source artificial intelligence and advances theory on institutional dynamics in regulatory governance.

The Prediction and Mediating Role of Lifetime and Daily Aggressive Sexual Fantasies: An Experience-Sampling Study
papers.abstract: Aggressive sexual fantasies (ASF) have consistently been associated with different sexual-aggression measures and mediated the effects of other risk factors on sexual aggression. Little, however, is known about the predictors of ASF and whether they should be considered as an independent risk factor for sexual aggression or rather an expression of aggression-related sexual interests. The present study, therefore, assessed lifetime ASF cross-sectionally (N = 422; Mage = 28.14; SD = 9.76) and over a 14-day experience-sampling period (n = 230; Mage = 27.38; SD = 9.08). Of the participants, 87% reported to have experienced ASF at least once in their lives; 11% reported ASF during the experience-sampling period. Psychopathy, violent pornography consumption, sexual interest in sexual sadism, and the interactions between hypersexuality and sexual-abuse experiences, Machiavellianism, and sexual interest in sadism were associated with higher lifetime ASF. Sexual interest in sadism positively predicted ASF during the experience-sampling period, but only in men. Lifetime ASF were the strongest predictor of sexual aggression and mediated the cross-sectional associations between sexual interest in sadism, hypersexuality, and violent pornography consumption and sexual aggression. These findings support the notion that ASF are an important cognitive risk factor for sexual aggression, partially independent from sexual interest, and require stronger attention by research and practice.

papers.title: Consensual Unwanted Sex and Body Dissatisfaction Among Cisgender Heterosexual Women and Queer Women/Gender Expansive Individuals
papers.abstract: People (especially women) often consent to unwanted sexual activity (especially with men). Reasons for consenting to unwanted sex include facilitating desired and avoiding undesired outcomes, and both positive and negative outcomes are common. Much of this research has focused on cisgender women’s experiences consenting to unwanted sex with cisgender men and associated relationship and emotional outcomes. Building on existing work, we examined how consenting to unwanted sex was associated with body-related harms among samples of cisgender heterosexual (cis/het) women (N = 491) and Queer women and gender expansive individuals (N = 529). Using survey data, we examined whether self-objectification explained the relationship between consensual unwanted sex (yes/no) and body dissatisfaction, and whether sexual/gender identity moderated those relationships. We also explored reasons for consenting to unwanted sex and how those reasons were associated with self-objectification and body dissatisfaction. Results found 70% of participants had ever consented to unwanted sex, and that consenting to unwanted sex was more common among Queer women/gender expansive individuals than cis/het women. There was a significant indirect effect of consensual unwanted sex on body dissatisfaction via self-objectification for both cis/het and Queer participants. Moreover, the frequency of different reasons for consenting to unwanted sex were similar for cis/het women and Queer women and gender expansive individuals. Only avoidance reasons were associated with greater self-objectification and body dissatisfaction. Overall, consenting to unwanted sex was associated with body-related harms, and such harms were experienced by both cis/het women and Queer women/gender expansive individuals.

papers.title: Prevalence of Sexual Acts and Materials Provided for Financial Compensation Among Young Adults in the United States
papers.abstract: Providing in-person (e.g., sex) and virtual (e.g., photos) sexual acts for pay or financial compensation (SAMP) is underreported due to stigma and substantial measurement issues. Prior research using a single item may have underestimated the prevalence and associated characteristics. This study sought to determine lifetime SAMP prevalence and associated characteristics of SAMP in a nationally representative sample in young adults (18–34 years old) in the United States. We administered a cross-sectional web-based survey through the National Opinion Research Council (N = 2,935). We used the validated, behaviorally specific, 10-item SAMP index to assess prevalence and circumstances, standardized measures of health and childhood experiences, and demographics. Over one-third (36%) of participants reported providing SAMP. Of those, 22% first provided SAMP as minors and 65.5% reported coercion. Prevalence differed by gender, sexuality, race, education, employment, income, and parenthood. Participants who provided SAMP had higher odds of depression, PTSD, problematic substance use, rape victimization, childhood adversity, discrimination, and lower social support. Findings suggest that SAMP is more common than previously assumed. Significant differences among those reporting SAMP underscore the need for harm reducing public health approaches to address health disparities, systemic social issues, diverse experiences, and SAMP’s spectrum of agency and victimization.

papers.title: Childhood Physical Abuse Perpetrators: Australian National Survey Data on Prevalence and Perpetrator Types
papers.abstract: = 2,623 experiencing childhood physical abuse), we estimated prevalence by perpetrator type and examined age of onset, cessation and duration. The overwhelming majority of physical abuse occurred within family settings. Lower prevalence estimates among younger cohorts suggest physical abuse may be becoming less common in more recent generations. Physical abuse most commonly began before 10 years of age, particularly when both parents were identified as perpetrators. These findings show that a substantial proportion of physical abuse occurs during children's formative years when they are unlikely to have networks outside of their family to turn to. The predominance of familial perpetration highlights the central role of family environments in the occurrence of physical abuse and the critical need for policies and programs that can target physical abuse within the home.

papers.title: Recruiting for SDGs-Oriented Profiles: Unpacking Drivers of Employer Attractiveness in Hybrid Organizations
papers.abstract: Recruitment is critical for equipping public service organizations with the competencies required to advance the sustainable development goals (SDGs). This is particularly salient for public utilities, hybrid organizations mandated to contribute to the SDGs through essential services in water, waste, and energy management. This study examines employer attractiveness for profiles considered critical to SDG implementation in Italian utilities. Drawing on self-determination theory, we combine semi-structured interviews with HR and Employer Branding managers from 16 utilities with two discrete-choice experiments involving STEM and vocational-technical students and professionals. Salary and competence-related opportunities are consistently important across both groups. Remote work does not significantly affect STEM respondents’ choices, whereas workplace proximity is the strongest driver for vocational-technical respondents. Relatedness, operationalized as environmental and community impact, is not a significant differentiating attribute, suggesting that in organizations whose public value mission is already highly visible, social and environmental impact may function as a baseline expectation.

papers.title: Governance of a Party‐State: Corruption, Law, and the Modus Operandi of the Chinese Communist Party. By LingLi, Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 2025. 358 pp. £110.00/$140.00 (hardcover). ISBN: 978‐1‐00‐927500‐2
The benefits of concentrating solar hybrid systems: A unified benchmarking framework
Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy for proton exchange membrane fuel cells: From implementation to application
papers.abstract: Proton exchange membrane fuel cells play a vital role in achieving a hydrogen-powered, carbon-neutral society. Although they have been deployed in stationary and transportation applications, their limited durability and reliability still restrict large-scale commercialization. Assessing internal health states is critical to overcoming these challenges by preventing operational faults and minimizing degradation rates. However, hydrogen fuel cells are highly nonlinear, multiscale, and multiphysics systems, hindering the estimation of system health states. This review investigates a nondestructive and in situ characterization technique, electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS), to characterize the health states of hydrogen fuel cells. The variation in internal health states is directly reflected in the impedance spectrum, which can be assessed through proper interpretation. Nevertheless, developing EIS for hydrogen fuel cells is a nontrivial task. Implementing and applying EIS requires interdisciplinary studies in signal processing, control theory, and machine learning in particular cases. This review systematically discusses the implementation, interpretation, and application of EIS for hydrogen fuel cells. The onboard applicability and short measurement time are key factors in EIS implementation. Model-based and DRT-based interpretation approaches are reviewed for efficiently extracting valuable health states. Based on these methods, the applications of EIS in performance characterization, fault diagnosis, degradation analysis, and prognostics are discussed. Four perspectives regarding general, non-electrical, localized, and multiphysics-integrated EIS, are proposed to highlight and guide EIS-related studies in hydrogen fuel cells. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the deployment and application of EIS in hydrogen fuel cells and offers insights into addressing durability and reliability challenges.

papers.title: Global soybean markets and land-use emissions: Evidence from the China–Brazil soybean trade relationship
Financing models, energy diplomacy, and strategic dependency in nuclear power projects: A comparative analysis of Akkuyu and El Dabaa nuclear power plants
The complexities and failures of Australia’s East Coast Gas Market
papers.abstract: Australia's East Coast Gas Market (ECGM) presents a policy paradox. Despite abundant gas reserves, households, businesses and industry continue to face high energy costs. These outcomes are commonly linked to the ECGM's integration with the international gas and oil markets. However, market structure alone does not explain why more structural forms of regulatory intervention remain politically constrained. This Perspective examines three recurring claims in Australia's gas policy debate: that increasing gas supply will lower domestic prices, that renewable energy is unreliable without continued reliance on gas, and that government intervention can correct problems within the gas market. Existing research has raised questions about each of these propositions. This paper, therefore, focuses on the political work they perform and argues that the claims circulate and reinforce one another by sustaining increased gas supply in response to affordability concerns, positioning gas as necessary for energy reliability, and providing reassurances that market problems can be managed through regulation. In doing so, they help to maintain an export-oriented gas market while narrowing the political space for structural intervention. The analysis highlights how market structure and political framing interact to constrain domestic energy governance and complicate energy transition in fossil-fuel-exporting economies.

papers.title: The impacts of the 2022 energy crisis on heating in German households - An empirical before-and-after examination of energy relevant concepts
Microplastic-Derived Dissolved Organic Matter Regulates Reactive Bromine Species Formation by Modulating the Photochemistry of Seawater Dissolved Organic Matter
papers.abstract: Abstract Microplastic-derived dissolved organic matter (MP-DOM) is emerging as a non-negligible organic input to marine systems, yet how its interactions with seawater DOM (S-DOM) regulate the photochemical formation of reactive bromine species (RBS) remains unclear. In this study, the RBS formation potential of poly(vinyl chloride) (PVC)-derived MP-DOM, S-DOM, and their mixed systems was systematically investigated under simulated solar irradiation. MP-DOM input exerted a nonlinear ratio-dependent regulatory effect on S-DOM-mediated RBS formation. At relatively low MP-DOM proportions (5–20%), the formation rate constant of 4-bromo-3,5-dimethyl-1H-pyrazole (Br-DMPZ), which represents the RBS formation potential, increased relative to S-DOM alone, reaching a maximum enhancement of 47.4% at 20% MP-DOM under seawater halide ion conditions (540 mM Cl– + 0.8 mM Br–). This enhancement was associated with increased quinone-/carbonyl-related redox-active structures, electron exchange capacity, and tannin-like components, which could facilitate photoinduced charge separation, electron transfer, and Br– oxidation. In contrast, higher MP-DOM proportions (40–50%) promoted hydrophobic lipid-like mixed assemblies, enhancing excited-state quenching and suppressing electron transfer and RBS photogeneration. These findings demonstrate that MP-DOM is not an inert byproduct of microplastic aging but rather an important regulatory factor in S-DOM-mediated halogen photochemistry in plastic-impacted marine waters.

papers.title: Suspect and Non-Targeted Analysis of Organophosphate Esters in Plastic Consumer Products via Ion Mobility Spectrometry-Mass Spectrometry
papers.abstract: Abstract Organophosphate esters (OPEs) are widely used as plasticizers and flame retardants in plastic products, posing critical environmental and human health risks. Traditional liquid chromatography-high resolution mass spectrometry (LC-HRMS) approaches face trade-offs between comprehensive coverage and spectral purity. This study established an advanced multidimensional identification framework utilizing LC coupled with cyclic ion mobility spectrometry and quadrupole time-of-flight mass spectrometry (LC-cIMS-QTOF). An integrated screening workflow merging targeted analysis, suspect screening, and nontargeted analysis (NTA) was deployed to characterize the OPEs in consumer plastics. A total of 63 OPEs were successfully characterized across seven polymer types, with 10, 22, and 31 compounds identified via targeted, suspect, and NTA workflows, respectively. Notably, 14 OPEs were traced back to the transformation products of phosphite antioxidants, ethoxy-linked OPEs constituted another predominant class with 22 congeners. This comprehensive characterization enriches current knowledge regarding the diversity of OPEs within plastic products, providing critical target lists for future migration and exposure assessments. Methodologically, the benefits of IMS, including providing cleaner mass spectra, discriminating isomers, and improving confidence levels, were demonstrated throughout the OPEs identification workflow. This established multidimensional screening strategy serves as a robust and efficient tool for uncovering OPEs contaminants in both plastic matrices and broader environmental media.

papers.title: Mn(II)-Mediated Abiotic Humification via Synergistic Interactions with Molecular Oxygen
papers.abstract: Abstract Terrestrial organic carbon (OC) dynamics critically influence the global carbon budget. Humification is a key pathway for stabilizing OC by transforming labile compounds into macromolecular polymers. High-valent manganese oxides (e.g., Mn(IV)O2) are well-known as efficient catalysts of abiotic humification, whereas the role of Mn(II) in OC transformation remains poorly understood. Here, dissolved Mn2+ drives oxidative polymerization and nitrogen-enriched humic-like product formation in the presence of common soil precursors─catechol, glycine, and glucose─through a synergistic interaction with molecular oxygen (O2). Mechanistically, Mn2+ mediates sequential single-electron transfers from catechol to O2, forming reactive intermediates that potentially couple with Maillard precursors to yield nitrogen-enriched macromolecules. FT-ICR-MS reveals that CHON species in lignin-like and highly condensed aromatic regions collectively account for 75.6% of total product relative abundance. This process is accompanied by the generation of reactive oxygen species (ROS), which could further enhance molecular diversity. Across 14 soil and freshwater DOM samples, 13.1–54.7% of assigned product formulas overlap with those in the corresponding DOM samples. Collectively, these shared formulas account for 78% of the total relative abundance of product formulas, indicating molecular-formula-level compositional similarity. These findings provide mechanistic and molecular-level insight into the underexplored role of Mn2+ in abiotic humification.

papers.title: Modeling to Plan the Future Cities We Desire
papers.abstract: W hat transformational changes are needed to create the future cities people desire�ones that are sustainable, resilient, and equitable�and what modeling tools do we need to support action toward this goal?Many decision-support tools for urban infrastructure, from energy to transportation to water systems, are designed for incremental planning and management over the next months or years�and for use by technical experts.This focus is appropriate for ensuring safe and reliable service provision but not longer-term, transformative, community-driven changes, such as phasing out fossil fuels, moving away from autocentric mobility, and achieving universal access to affordable, clean water.Existing tools are often used defensively, taking the present as a point of departure to identify and avoid potential vulnerabilities.However, a model grounded in the status quo embeds current worldviews, priorities, and power structures, potentially reproducing, or even widening, existing inequities. 1 For instance, if demand forecasting is based on existing user patterns, without taking into account households that are already structurally underserved, underinvestment will continue.In this Viewpoint, we explore possibilities for broadening modeling tools and processes�and the goals, levers, and actors they represent�to support collaborative decisions toward more transformative urban futures.We see an opportunity to orient models, and the planning processes that use them, toward desired futures, 2 not just predicted or plausible ones.3 Visions of what is a desired future are necessarily plural and will vary across contexts, values, and worldviews.This multiplicity is part of their power.Widening the framing of the future to explicitly include plural and diverse aspirations, and not just what is most likely to happen, can create space for more transformational possibilities, particularly for groups whose perspectives are currently marginalized in dominant planning processes.For instance, Afro and Indigenous futurisms often exemplify this stance, imagining futures around Black and Indigenous flourishing rather than the extension of present harms.4,5 Critically, starting with desired futures allows us to center a question that predictive framings can elide: what are the goals Viewpoint pubs.acs.

papers.title: Biochar Application Enhances Photochemical Reactivity of Dissolved Organic Matter to Stimulate CO2 Emissions in Paddy Water
papers.abstract: Abstract Dissolved organic matter (DOM) plays a pivotal role in regulating photochemical reactivity and carbon turnover in flooded paddy systems. While biochar (BC) is recognized as a promising strategy for soil carbon preservation, its impact on DOM evolution and photochemical carbon cycle in paddy water remains unknown. Here, we demonstrated that BC amendment continuously enhanced the photogeneration of hydroxyl radicals (•OH) and low-energy excited triplet-state DOM (3DOM*-L) in paddy water, increasing CO2 emissions by an average of 35.5% while playing a minor role in CH4 formation over a 34-day incubation. The enhanced photoactivity was associated with the enrichment of the photoactive molecular pool characterized by highly aromatic compounds and polyphenols with higher aromaticity, unsaturation, and oxygenated degrees. The proposed mechanisms in enriching photoactive DOM of paddy water depended on soil types, i.e., BC facilitated the biotic reprocessing of inert, highly recalcitrant aromatics into metabolites associated with photoactivity in sandy soil, whereas abiotic processes, including BC-induced dissolved black carbon release and mineral-associated organic carbon desorption, likely played more important roles in loam soil. Enhanced anaerobic fermentation further supplied photolabile substrates for amplifying mineralization. Extrapolation estimations suggested that BC-enhanced photochemistry may release an additional 3.56–15.47 Tg CO2 yr–1 globally, potentially offsetting ∼0.7–7.0% of BC’s CO2 mitigation potential. The findings revealed a previously unrecognized photochemical pathway of BC-involved carbon loss across the soil-water continuum, with implications for evaluating the net climate benefit of biochar as a carbon management strategy.

papers.title: Event-Scale Deposition of Atmospheric Microplastics in Snowfall of the Sierra Nevada in North America
papers.abstract: Abstract Atmospheric deposition of microplastics (MPs) at an event-scale resolution can be measured in snowfall events, as snow scavenges atmospheric MPs and the snowpack serves as a repository for MP accumulation. We monitored MP deposition in freshly fallen snow, the snowpack, and dry deposition over the course of 6 months in the Sierra Nevada of North America. Average microplastic concentrations in fresh snow ranged from 11.8 to 37.5 p/L at remote sites, which were significantly less than the 68.3 to 92.9 p/L MP concentrations found at the anthropogenically impacted site. Average bulk deposition rates were estimated to be 267 to 3190 p/m2/day at remote sites, significantly lower than the 3242 to 7480 p/m2/day at the anthropogenically impacted site. HYSPLIT back-trajectory modeling characterized the potential regional transport of MPs from upwind regions that were predominantly agricultural and suburban areas, as well as localized anthropogenic activities that could significantly affect MP deposition rates in snowfall. This study introduces high-throughput FTIR analysis methods with a highlight on fiber spectroscopy, demonstrates the value of estimating MP fluxes at the meteorological event scale, reports MP deposition rates in a critical water resource, and provides a basis for future long-term atmospheric MP monitoring.

papers.title: Recombinase Polymerase Amplification Coupled with Graphene Oxide Nanomaterial-Assisted Purification and Target Signal Selection for Highly Sensitive and Rapid Harmful Algae Detection
papers.abstract: Abstract Harmful algal blooms (HABs) pose serious ecological and health risks, creating an urgent need for rapid, sensitive, and accurate detection of harmful algae. Here, we developed a graphene oxide (GO)- and Mg2+-regulated recombinase polymerase amplification assay (G-M-RPA) for rapid and ultrasensitive detection of Heterosigma akashiwo, Prorocentrum minimum, and Akashiwo sanguinea. Using conserved internal transcribed spacer sequences, we designed species-specific primers labeled with 6-carboxyfluorescein for fluorescence readout. Innovative one-step purification of RPA products was achieved using self-synthesized GO-wrapped magnetic nanocomposites instead of traditional purification kits, reducing purification time from 15 to 2 min (∼86.7%). The fluorescence resonance energy transfer property of the GO nanosheets was applied to quench the fluorescence of excess single-stranded primers, significantly lowering background levels. Mg2+ further enhanced primer–GO interactions, likely through electrostatic screening and Mg2+-mediated interactions. The entire detection process was completed within ∼30 min, achieving a genomic DNA detection limit of 3.3 fg/μL, corresponding to ∼7 cells/mL for H. akashiwo. The assay also showed reliable performance in mixed-DNA and seawater matrices, with favorable reproducibility and short-term stability. Overall, the proposed G-M-RPA strategy provides a rapid, sensitive, and practical platform for multispecies harmful-algae detection, nearshore environmental monitoring, and early warning of HABs.

Soil Heating from Fire Induces Bidirectional Changes in Dissolved Organic Matter Release and Organic Sulfur Speciation
papers.abstract: Abstract Soil heating from fire influences dissolved organic matter (DOM) release but has unknown effects on organic sulfur (S) speciation, with implications for S and metal cycling in aquatic environments. Here, low and high organic carbon soils (4.80 versus 50.4%) were heated at environmentally relevant temperatures and durations (75–300 °C, 0.25–4.0 h) and subject to leaching experiments that quantified DOM and inorganic anion release, and changes in organic S speciation via S X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) spectroscopy. In both soils, heating between 75 and 200 °C increased dissolved organic carbon (DOC) and inorganic sulfate (SO42–) release (by up to 24- and 88-fold, respectively) while decreasing the % highly reduced S in DOM (e.g., thiols), indicating thiol oxidation to SO42–. Soil heating at 300 °C decreased DOC release and increased SO42– release, with step increases in DOM aromaticity and % heterocyclic reduced S species (e.g., thiophenes). Across treatments, DOM aromaticity positively correlated with DOM % heterocyclic reduced S, interpreted to reflect organic S cyclization during heating. The observed bidirectional changes in organic S speciation in DOM due to soil heating, with thiol oxidation at ≤200 °C and S cyclization at 300 °C with SO42– releases, provide mechanistic insights that improve the prediction of fire effects on S, C, and metal cycling in aquatic environments.

papers.title: Correction to “Nitrous Oxide Emissions from Urban Green Spaces Substantially Offset Their Carbon Sequestration Benefits”
Observation-Based Emission Estimates of the Potent Greenhouse Gas HFC-23 for Article 5 and Non-Article 5 Country Groups under the Montreal Protocol
papers.abstract: Abstract The Kigali Amendment to the Montreal Protocol requires parties to destroy, to the extent practicable, HFC-23 generated as a byproduct during the production of controlled hydrochlorofluorocarbons and hydrofluorocarbons. Global total HFC-23 emissions estimated from reported abatement and known sources (bottom-up) agreed with those inferred from atmospheric observations (top-down) before 2015, but have been substantially lower since then. Here, we show that during 2011–2013, bottom-up estimates of global total HFC-23 emissions were right for the wrong reasons: bottom-up estimates for the non-Article 5 (mainly developed) country group were lower than top-down estimates (1.7 ± 0.2 vs 3.1 ± 0.5 Gg yr–1 on average), while those for the Article 5 (mainly developing) country group were higher (11.8 ± 0.4 vs 9.7 ± 1.0 Gg yr–1), resulting in a cancellation at the global scale. We further show that during 2015–2023, while the underestimation of global bottom-up emissions was dominated by the Article 5 country group, the non-Article 5 country group also contributed in 2023 [bottom-up (byproduct emissions reported to UNEP plus other known sources) vs top-down: 0.5 ± 0.2 vs 1.3 ± 0.6 Gg yr–1]. Our results underscore improvement of emission accounting and mitigation for both country groups under the Kigali Amendment.

Upcycling whey permeate into a clean-label bio-preservative via fermentation: Metabolomic insights and application in sponge cake
Deep eutectic solvent processing of seagrass biomass from beach wrack for sustainable polypropylene composites in large format additive manufacturing
papers.abstract: Seagrass-rich beach wrack collected from the Bay of Cádiz (Spain) was valorized as a reinforcement for polypropylene (PP) composites manufactured by large-format additive manufacturing by fused granular fabrication (LFAM-FGF). Two delignification approaches were investigated with NaOH (SG-NaOH) and a deep eutectic solvent (DES) based on lactic acid and choline chloride (SG-DES). While SG-NaOH achieved greater lignin removal, SG-DES yielded a cellulose-rich material with higher crystallinity and a distinctive nanofibrillar morphology. When incorporated into PP at 15 wt%, untreated seagrass (SG-UT) and SG-NaOH resulted in a marked reduction in tensile strength and ductility. In contrast, composites reinforced with SG-DES exhibited a significant increase in Young's modulus while maintaining tensile strength comparable to neat PP and preserving high elongation at break. Thus, despite its lower delignification efficiency, the DES treatment produced the most effective reinforcement among the investigated formulations, highlighting that extensive lignin removal is not necessarily required to achieve high composite performance. In addition, all seagrass-filled formulations showed improved dimensional stability during LFAM-FGF printing, effectively suppressing the warping commonly observed in neat PP, enabling the fabrication of large-scale demonstrator parts which maintained their structural integrity after more than one year of outdoor exposure.

Changes in the fire resilience of black pine in response to Mediterranean climate variability over the past 300 years
papers.abstract: Elucidating the resilience of trees to wildfires remains a critical issue for forest conservation. The potential changes in tree resilience over time in response to the combined changes in fire regime and climate remain unknown. We hypothesised that tree resilience was influenced by mean fire-return intervals (MFI) and by their interactions with atmospheric conditions over the past 300 years, particularly during drought and hot years. This hypothesis was tested by analyzing tree-ring widths following past fires, using growth during fire-free periods as baseline, and atmospheric values (annual and seasonal temperature and precipitation, drought index and CO 2 concentration). The study focused on black pine ( Pinus nigra ) as a model species to investigate long-term ecological responses to fires in natural forests of Corsica, a western Mediterranean island. The study is based on 180 cross-dated black pines from four Corsican mountain sites. 54 fires were recorded between 1719 CE and 2012 CE. Four contrasted periods, defined according to MFI and atmospheric records are used to assess the black pine responses to fire events, MFI period, and climate. The fire resistance and resilience of trees have gradually declined since about 1850, independently of the MFI and increased atmospheric CO₂ levels. Post-fire radial growth recovery lengthened over time, indicating a decline in resistance. Concurrently, tree-ring responded more positively to precipitation and negatively to drought intensity. In isolation, fire does not compromise tree resilience. But the combined effects of drought and wildfires thus threaten black pines by shrinking their resilience mainly since 1971, which underscores the increasing vulnerability of this Mediterranean tree to fire in an increasingly dry climate.
