To determine which effect dominates, we analyse 9606 US firm‐years (2006–2023) with 543 documented breaches and find that increased digitalization, measured through 10‐K business descriptions, significantly raises the likelihood of future cyber breaches. A one‐standard‐deviation increase in digitalization corresponds to up to a 10 percentage point higher breach probability, driven primarily by organizational rather than technological dimensions. Expert auditors and cybersecurity disclosure reduce breach likelihood, but their protective effect attenuates as digitalization rises; that of board and C‐suite technology expertise instead strengthens. These findings qualify the protective role of conventional monitoring in highly digitalized firms and point to a repositioning of cybersecurity governance from external monitoring towards digital expertise embedded in strategic decision‐making.

papers.title: How Assumptions About Time Divide and Connect Epistemic Communities in Business and Management
papers.abstract: Abstract Business and management studies comprise distinct epistemic communities that frequently do not interact or collaborate. While this has been explained as paradigm incommensurability, construct ambiguity or the variance–process, this CrossRoads article sets out a less commonly invoked source of difference: how our theories conceptualize time. This includes assumptions about whether the future is determined or open (temporal openness), whether and how change takes place (temporal directionality) and the appropriate timescales and detail for analysis (temporal duration). To illustrate the importance of these three temporal dimensions, influential traditions in strategy, entrepreneurship, institutional theory, process studies, population ecology, real‐options and scenario planning are mapped. The mapping demonstrates that many temporal differences between epistemic communities are differences of degree that may offer productive tensions for collaborative approaches, even though some may remain difficult to reconcile. Through a set of diagnostic questions, this CrossRoads piece offers a framework for interdisciplinary temporal brokerage within and beyond business and management.

papers.title: Harnessing Power Through External Collaborative Innovation: How Incumbent Inventors Navigate Rising Talent Influx in Developed‐country MNE Subsidiaries
papers.abstract: Abstract This paper examines how, and under what conditions, the increasing presence of highly skilled local employees (HSLEs) within subsidiaries of developed‐country multinational enterprises (DCMNEs) influences incumbent local inventors’ external collaborative innovation. Adopting a power dependence perspective, we propose that incumbent local inventors are more likely to engage in external than internal collaborative innovation in response to the increasing presence of HSLEs. Successful external collaborative innovation enhances incumbent local inventors’ bargaining power by enabling them to gain stronger positions within external networks critical to DCMNEs’ innovation and to access alternative employment opportunities. We further contend that the positive relationship between the increasing presence of HSLEs and incumbent local inventors’ external collaborative innovation is strengthened by the boundary‐spanning characteristics of the management hierarchies, such as cross‐cultural CEOs and interlocking directors. Our analysis of DCMNE subsidiaries operating in China provides empirical support for these predictions. This research offers novel and important insights into collaborating‐by‐hiring, highlighting the increasing presence of HSLEs as a competitive mechanism for interorganizational collaborative innovation and emphasizing the strategic importance of externally leveraging the knowledge and expertise of incumbent inventors.

papers.title: Responsible Management Education and Its Potential as an Epistemic Object of Change
papers.abstract: Abstract This study examines whether and how RME can be performed as an epistemic object to broaden business schools’ education on climate change. The research builds on a qualitative case study involving 10 Finnish business schools. The analysis reveals that RME is performed as both an epistemic object and a boundary object, with different implications for its embeddedness within institutions. Our findings show how accreditations have introduced RME as a boundary object enforcing performativity around sustainability themes yet enabling disciplines to maintain their distinct or limited roles. At the same time, RME is met with both resistance and compliance, depending on how well the object fits with disciplinary boundaries and career trajectories. Lastly, as an epistemic object, RME encourages co‐reflexivity, which is essential for climate‐proofing business schools. We discuss the possibilities of a hybrid orientation of RME as both a boundary object and an epistemic object for enforcing climate‐orientation in management education.

papers.title: Anchoring Corporate Climate Action: Credible Commitments and the Internal Governance of Private Standard‐Setters
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Corporate climate commitments depend partly on the credibility of the institutions that define and validate them. This article examines the Science Based Targets initiative as a key private standard‐setter in polycentric climate governance. A mechanism‐based analysis informed by Basic Formal Ontology reconstructs SBTi's governance from documented entities, functions, authority relations and decision effects, examining how this structure operated during the 2024 Scope 3 controversy and subsequent standard revision. The Technical Council exercises technical approval and procedural gatekeeping. Scientific criteria, specialised advisory input and expectations of expert integrity support its deliberations but do not constitute an autonomous imperative constraint because the Board retains final appointment and adoption authority. This arrangement creates a structural vulnerability when scientific judgement, organisational strategy and stakeholder pressures diverge. By extending credible commitment theory from firms to standard‐setters, the article offers a framework for assessing the internal credibility of key institutions in polycentric climate governance.

papers.title: ESG Disclosure Intensity and Financial Performance: Text‐Mined Evidence from Vietnam's Manufacturing Sector
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Environmental, social, and governance disclosure (ESGD) increasingly forms part of firms' communication with external capital providers. However, its association with financial performance remains unclear, especially in emerging markets where reporting formats, assurance practices, and enforcement mechanisms remain uneven. Using annual reports of 201 listed manufacturing firms in Vietnam over 2016–2024, this study constructs a dictionary‐based measure of ESG disclosure intensity, expressed as dictionary‐matched ESG occurrences per 1000 n ‐grams, and examines its association with return on assets (ROA), return on equity (ROE), and Tobin's Q . The central finding is a negative association between ESG disclosure intensity and ROE. This is the only association that retains the same direction across the baseline two‐way fixed‐effects and supplementary dynamic system GMM specifications. The baseline models also show a weakly positive association with ROA and a positive association with Tobin's Q , but neither positive association is corroborated by the dynamic specifications. The results therefore show that the financial associations of ESG disclosure intensity depend on the performance outcome examined and on model specification. For corporate sustainability strategy, the findings suggest that higher ESG disclosure intensity should not be interpreted as uniformly associated with stronger financial performance. Rather, the financial relevance of sustainability reporting depends on the outcome against which it is assessed. The negative ROE association, which runs against the prediction of the monitoring argument, raises a specific theoretical puzzle concerning the relationship between disclosure, shareholders' capital, financing, and the timing of returns.

papers.title: Tail Risk and Earnings Management: The Role of Gender Diversity and Environmental–Social Reporting in International Banking
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT We examine the impacts of earnings management on the tail risks of banks using a dataset of 3297 bank‐year observations across 157 publicly traded commercial banks from 12 countries, covering 2002–2022. Our findings suggest that banks engaging in earnings management activities exhibit higher tail risks. However, this relationship is moderated by two critical factors: board gender diversity and environmental–social (ES) reporting. Specifically, our analysis indicates that the elevated tail risks associated with higher levels of earnings management can be mitigated by stronger female representation on boards or through higher ES ratings. These insights provide important financial implications and policy guidelines for multiple stakeholders engaging with the international banking sector and ES seeking to strengthen governance framework structures while mitigating risk‐taking.

papers.title: Beyond the Liability of Origin: Multidimensional Legitimacy and ESG Strategies of Emerging Market Multinationals
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Drawing on a multidimensional legitimacy perspective, this study examines how internationalization shapes the ESG performance of emerging market multinational enterprises (EMNEs). EMNEs face not only external legitimacy pressures in host‐country markets but also internal legitimacy pressures in the home‐country institutional environment. These internal pressures are especially salient for state‐owned EMNEs because of their stronger political embeddedness and closer alignment with state priorities. Using panel data on 16,342 firm‐year observations from Chinese listed firms covering 2009–2022, the findings show that greater geographic breadth of internationalization is positively associated with ESG performance. This relationship is stronger for state‐owned EMNEs, suggesting that their ESG strategies are shaped by the need to maintain legitimacy both abroad and at home. Board overseas experience further strengthens this effect, indicating that internationally experienced directors help firms reconcile competing home‐ and host‐country expectations during international expansion. By integrating external and internal legitimacy into the analysis of EMNE ESG strategies, this study extends research on internationalization, legitimacy, and corporate governance and highlights the role of board‐level international experience in translating legitimacy pressures into stronger ESG engagement.

papers.title: Local institutional quality, firm size, and innovation: evidence from Italy
papers.abstract: Abstract This paper investigates whether local institutional quality is associated with firm-level innovation from an economic geography perspective. Focusing on Italian manufacturing firms, we examine whether cross-province differences in institutional quality are related to firms’ patenting activity and whether this relationship varies by firm size. Drawing on a longitudinal dataset of more than 125,000 manufacturing firms observed from 2011 to 2019, we combine firm-level patent data with a province-level measure of institutional quality. Our results show that higher local institutional quality is positively associated with firms’ patenting activity. Moreover, the relationship varies across firms and institutional dimensions, as improvements in control of corruption, government effectiveness, regulatory quality, and voice and accountability are associated with larger increases in patenting among smaller firms. By contrast, we find no evidence that the association between the rule-of-law dimension and patenting varies by firm size.

papers.title: Should I stay or should I go: intentions to freelance across 16 countries
papers.abstract: Abstract A substantial literature explores workers’ transitions into entrepreneurial business ownership, while freelance, on-demand self-employment, a distinct and increasingly prevalent mode of labour market participation, remains comparatively understudied. Using an original large survey conducted in 16 countries, we investigate the determinants of workers’ intentions to leave their main salaried job to engage in freelance, on-demand self-employment. We find that socio-demographic characteristics, job conditions, and behavioural traits are systematically associated with these intentions, though several patterns diverge from those documented in the entrepreneurship literature. A detailed heterogeneity analysis substantiates variation across occupations, task types, and individual characteristics. Workers in more vulnerable positions exhibit higher intentions to transition into freelance, on-demand self-employment, a form of work often associated with lower protection and higher income risk.

papers.title: Early-life autonomy imprint as a driver of the learning advantage of newness in international new ventures
papers.abstract: This study examines how the learning advantages of newness (LAN) emerge from organizational structures and strategic behaviours, and from entrepreneurs acting as learning agents. Despite extensive research on LAN, research on how formative childhood experiences shape the learning foundations of new ventures is limited. This study draws on imprinting theory to investigate how early experiences of autonomy leave enduring cognitive and behavioural imprints on entrepreneurs, fostering a disposition that supports the development of LANs. The study relies on an exploratory multiple-case study of ten early internationalizing technology firms, supported by 11 narrative-informed interviews with entrepreneurs and an abductive research strategy. Its findings identify childhood autonomy as an important antecedent of LAN development. Autonomy imprints operate through four organizational learning mechanisms: selective attention to novelty, distributed authority routines, psychological safety norms, and boundary-spanning searches. These mechanisms translate early-life experiences of autonomy into venture-level learning capabilities. The analysis further shows that resource slack strengthens those mechanisms by enabling broader exploration, experimentation, and knowledge development. This study extends imprinting theory by demonstrating that childhood autonomy constitutes a formative imprint with enduring consequences for organizational learning and international venture development. It also contributes to the learning advantages of newness literature by identifying a previously unexplored antecedent of LAN and revealing the organizational learning mechanisms through which founder imprints shape its emergence in international new ventures. Finally, this study offers practical insights for entrepreneurs by illustrating how formative experiences can be leveraged to cultivate sustainable learning advantages in global markets.

papers.title: Microbusiness and place-based change: New insights into the aggregate nature of small-scale entrepreneurial action
papers.abstract: Entrepreneurship research increasingly recognises that place is shaped by the everyday actions of economic actors. Yet, we still know relatively little about how the small-scale actions of individual microbusinesses reshape local places. Starting from a relational conception of place as process, this article examines how microbusinesses contribute intentionally and in harmony to the transformation of local places. We combine Emirbayer and Mische’s temporal-relational conception of agency, which recognises entrepreneurial action as a contextually embedded process, with constitutive approaches to performativity that highlight how microbusiness actions gradually remake place. The findings of our 18-month ethnographic study of a small town in the United Kingdom, which combines interviews, diaries and field observations, show how visible, materially grounded microbusiness practices operate performatively, signalling aspirational futures and reshaping expectations for local places. Underpinned by processual theories of temporal-relational agency and performativity, our analysis identifies an entrepreneurial process, through which mutually reinforcing effects of individual, projective entrepreneurial actions by microbusinesses accumulate over time and space to transform the town. Theorising this process as ‘aggregate agency’, we contribute to place-based entrepreneurship research by revealing how microbusinesses make incremental transformative contributions to local places through uncoordinated yet, converging individual actions, commanding a processual understanding of both entrepreneurship and place.
papers.journal_name: International Small Business Journal: Researching Entrepreneurship

papers.title: The dark side of people management: a systematic literature review of nonlinear effects of HRM and leadership
papers.abstract: This paper systematically examines the dark side of people management, that is, the combination of HRM and leadership. We conceptualize the ‘dark side’ as the nonlinear effects of people management and its components: we focus on instances in which higher levels of HRM and leadership do not result in better outcomes, which contradicts the assumption underlying most HRM and leadership research. Studying these nonlinear relationships is a research avenue that is gaining significance but contains theoretical and methodological challenges. In response, this study systematically maps the existing literature (N = 71 empirical articles) on nonlinear effects of people management, its components and outcomes. In doing so, we explore: 1) evidence for nonlinear relationships between people management and outcomes, and 2) theoretical explanations for the direct and mediated nonlinear relationships, and 3) moderators for these nonlinear relationships. This review shows that nonlinear effects of people management and its components have been observed in both HRM and leadership studies. Further, the findings showed that the theoretical underpinning of nonlinear relationships is wanting and that a coherent theoretical foundation is lacking. We present a research agenda to further facilitate the development of this emerging research avenue from infancy to a consolidated area of study.
papers.journal_name: The International Journal of Human Resource Management

papers.title: Carbon accounting in the supply chain: investigating its antecedents and consequences for organizations
papers.abstract: Over the past decade, stakeholder attention to carbon accounting has intensified, with particular emphasis on greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from firms’ direct operations (Scope 1) and purchased energy use (Scope 2). However, a substantial portion of emissions occurs beyond these boundaries, and firms continue to struggle to identify, measure, and manage emissions embedded in their supply bases. Limited data availability, voluntary disclosure, and supplier heterogeneity significantly impede accurate assessment of supply chain emissions. This paper addresses these challenges by (a) identifying the key drivers of GHG emissions in a firm’s supply base and (b) developing a novel empirical approach to measure supply base emissions. Using data from 1,142 firms and drawing on transaction cost and network theory, we show that greater geographical and industrial diversity significantly increases supply base emissions, and that buyer network influence and supply base interconnectedness moderate these effects.

papers.title: Acoustic–semantic equivalence: A trimodal framework for B2B sales communication effectiveness and training allocation
papers.abstract: This study documents acoustic–semantic equivalence as the empirical finding that voice delivery and message content have comparable predictive power for sales outcomes under duration-matched conditions. In 5183 authentic Finnish business-to-business (B2B) sales calls, acoustic and semantic features predict outcomes with nearly identical accuracy, challenging traditional content-centric training approaches. A trimodal framework that integrates acoustic, semantic, and linguistic dimensions yields improved predictive performance, with gains arising from complementary information across modalities. These results suggest that sales training may benefit from balanced attention to how salespeople speak and what they say, within the way they structure their conversations. The study contributes to multimodal communication research and offers practical guidance for redesigning sales training and developing AI-assisted coaching systems.

papers.title: Effective empowerment or institutional paradox? An investigation into the impact of industrial policy on corporate digital transformation
Bittersweet Minds, Better Selves: How Mixed Emotions Shape Preferences for Self‐Improvement Products
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Bittersweet mixed emotion—the simultaneous experience of happiness and sadness—is a common but underexplored form of mixed emotion. This research examines how bittersweet emotion shapes consumers' preferences for self‐improvement products. Across five complementary studies, including three laboratory experiments and two secondary data analyses, we show that bittersweet emotion increases preferences for self‐improvement products relative to single emotional states of happiness or sadness. We further identify perceived self‐discrepancy as the underlying mechanism: bittersweet emotion heightens awareness of the discrepancy between the actual self and the ideal self, thereby strengthening preferences for self‐improvement products. In addition, this effect is moderated by consumers' beliefs in self‐malleability. These findings advance the mixed emotions literature by highlighting the constructive role of bittersweet emotion in consumer decision making and offer practical implications for the marketing of self‐improvement products and services.

papers.title: AI Appreciation for Rejection: How Advice Source Shapes Consumers' Responses to Rejection Versus Endorsement Advice
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Offering product recommendations based on AI or human analysis is common in contemporary marketing practice. Beyond endorsing an option to choose (recommend‐for; RF advice), platforms increasingly provide rejection‐oriented advice that discourages specific alternatives (recommend‐against; RA advice). We propose that consumers respond differently to these two advice types depending on the advice source. Across five studies (including a supplementary study), we show that consumers are more likely to adopt RA advice when it is generated by AI rather than human advisors, whereas acceptance of RF advice does not differ by source. This AI appreciation for rejection is driven by consumers' perceptions of the advice source's filtering ability and is attenuated when the filtering procedures underlying advice generation are made transparent. These findings contribute to the literature on rejection and consumer responses to AI, while also offering managerial implications for how firms can effectively leverage AI and advice framing to facilitate consumer decision making.

papers.title: Detecting Careless Responding: A Comparison of Norm Group-Based Mahalanobis Distance and Norm Group-Based Person-Total Correlation with Their Sample-Based Counterparts
papers.abstract: Detecting careless responding in self-report questionnaires has gained considerable attention. Different detection methods have been proposed, with implicit methods offering clear advantages over explicit ones. Mahalanobis distance (MD) and person-total correlation ( r pbis ) are among the most promising implicit detection methods. However, previous research has suggested that MD and r pbis are less accurate indicators of careless responding when the percentage of careless respondents in the sample is high and that norm group-based (NGB) MD and r pbis might be more accurate alternatives under that condition. In two simulation studies and a reanalysis of real data, we examined whether NGB MD and NGB r pbis indeed outperform their sample-based (SB) counterparts in a variety of careless responding patterns. The three main findings were as follows: (1) NGB MD outperformed SB MD in most conditions in three studies, (2) both MD indices (but not r pbis indices) were ineffective when simulated scale-midpoint invariant and full straightlining careless responding had to be detected, and (3) NGB r pbis almost never outperformed SB r pbis . We therefore recommend using NGB MD instead of SB MD, and using SB r pbis instead of NGB r pbis when screening data for careless responding.

papers.title: When Humans Still Matter: Consumers’ Responses to Automation in Loyalty Program Preferential Treatment
papers.abstract: The recent introduction of automated complimentary upgrades reflects the emerging role of artificial intelligence (AI) in making symbolically meaningful decisions in tourism. We explore consumers’ responses using a thematic analysis of online comments and open-ended survey responses, followed by a quantitative survey to validate findings. Paradoxically, the qualitative analysis reveals that both unbiased decisions and personalization are valued. The quantitative study further shows that lay beliefs about AI are associated with preferences, through procedural and interactional fairness. Only procedural fairness fully mediates the lay beliefs’ association with intention to negotiate out of dissatisfying upgrade decisions. Moreover, desire to be treated as a unique customer weakens the lay beliefs’ association with interactional fairness and the indirect association with preferences. We contribute by revealing how consumers respond when automated agents make symbolically meaningful decisions in the automated preferential treatment context. Firms should prioritize the procedural legitimacy and symbolic framing of automated decisions.

papers.title: Reconfiguring external and internal networks for resilience, agility and ambidexterity under geopolitical volatility
papers.abstract: Purpose Geopolitical tensions and economic policy volatility are compelling multinational firms to redesign both external supply chain networks and their intra-organisational networks of plants, subsidiaries and governance. This study examines how intra-organisational networks are redesigned in response to geopolitically induced reshaping of external supply chain networks and how this redesign enables resilience, agility and ambidexterity. Design/methodology/approach The study uses a qualitative multiple-case design with three longitudinal focal cases and five supporting cases. The data comprise 58 semi-structured interviews, supplemented by secondary documents to reconstruct case trajectories over time. Findings Geopolitically driven external network reshaping heightens dependence and power asymmetry through concentrated bottlenecks, low substitutability, and compliance-gated access. Firms respond through buffering, bridging, and selective internalisation, but these moves become effective only when internal decision rights, subsidiary mandates, and integration capacity are redesigned. Originality/value The study conceptualises external and intra-organisational network restructuring as a coupled, dependence-driven process under geopolitical volatility. It extends Resource Dependence Theory by showing that dependence-management strategies require internal re-architecture to become executable, thereby reframing resilience, agility, and ambidexterity as outcomes of organisational redesign rather than static capabilities.
papers.journal_name: International Journal of Operations & Production Management

papers.title: Shared Stakes, Shared Brains: Common Ownership and Inventor Mobility Along Supply Chains
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Research Question/Issue This study investigates the influence of common ownership on inventor mobility along supply chains and examines its role in shaping the interfirm governance conditions for human‐capital reallocation within portfolios. Research Findings/Insights Using Chinese listed supplier–customer pairs from 2012 to 2023, we find that inventors are more likely to move along supply chains when common owners hold larger stakes in both suppliers and customers. Through mechanism tests, we reveal that common owners increase the likelihood of such flows by facilitating collaboration and information exchange. This effect is more evident when common owners are long‐term, institutional, or state‐owned, and when supply chains have a weaker collaborative culture, less efficient management, or a poorer legal environment. Finally, such flows mainly increase incremental innovation and enhance innovation performance of both supply‐chain partners. Theoretical/Academic Implications This study extends research on inventor mobility from competitors to collaborators and identifies common ownership as a governance determinant of supply‐chain human‐capital flows. It also reframes common ownership's labor‐market effects from horizontal anticompetition to vertical human‐capital reallocation and highlights inventor mobility along supply chains as a person‐level channel for complementary knowledge recombination, rather than another collaboration‐style outcome. Practitioner/Policy Implications Our findings suggest that investors can leverage common ownership to enhance portfolio competitiveness by strengthening the governance conditions that support inventor mobility. For policymakers, particularly those in emerging markets, our results demonstrate that common ownership can fill institutional voids and alleviate supply‐chain frictions, suggesting that regulatory frameworks should recognize its benefits in supporting human‐capital reallocation and supply‐chain resilience.

papers.title: Corporate Ethical Dilemma under Judicial Pressure: Environmental Judicial Enforcement and Corporate Biodiversity Risk Exposure
Hushed Whispers or Watchful Eyes? How Employees’ Source of Misconduct Information Differentially Affects Employees’ Whistle-Blowing and Managers’ Corrective Actions
papers.abstract: Internal whistleblowing begins with employees becoming aware of ethical misconduct in their organization. While current research focuses on observation or direct evidence of wrongdoing as primary sources of knowledge of wrongdoing, it overlooks an important source of awareness: employees may also learn about misconduct, indirectly, by hearing about it from others. Drawing on cognitive appraisal theory, we investigate how employees’ source of knowledge (observing vs. hearing about the wrongdoing) influences both employees’ whistleblowing tendencies and managers’ willingness to take corrective actions. Across a critical incident study, a two-wave field study, an immersive behavioral experiment, and a scenario experiment, we find that employees are less likely to report misconduct they hear about than misconduct they observe. Managers, however, are equally willing to take corrective action regardless of whether a report originates from an employee who observed the misconduct or heard about it. We further find that the effect of knowledge source on taking action is mediated by anticipated guilt, even after accounting for felt obligation, perceived futility, and fear of retaliation. Together, our findings identify an important asymmetry in the whistleblowing process: indirect knowledge substantially reduces employees’ willingness to report misconduct, even though it does not diminish managers’ willingness to act on those reports.

papers.title: A systematic and causal review of the link between leader-driven psychological safety and work outcomes
papers.abstract: Leader-driven psychological safety has attracted growing organizational investment and a rapidly expanding empirical literature, yet the causal quality of the evidence underpinning the performance case, that is, the claim that leader behavior improves work outcomes through psychological safety, has never been systematically evaluated. This review takes a critical and methodological stance, conducting the first systematic causal audit of 47 articles published in highly ranked peer-reviewed journals between 1990 and January 2026. Applying a diagnostic protocol that evaluates concepts, measures, and study design, we find that 82% of coded entries operationalize the leader antecedent through follower ratings, rendering the evidence causally indeterminate at the point of measurement. No observational study employs a design-based identification strategy, and no study provides causal evidence for the full theoretical chain from leader behavior through experienced psychological safety to work outcomes. Ninety percent of coded entries are diagnosed as implausible causal inference. Only 10% of coded entries reach partial causal evidence, establishing a credible estimate for the antecedent-to-mediator link and leaving the mediator-to-outcome relationship descriptive only. The associations reported across the literature therefore neither confirm nor refute the theoretical argument. We offer theoretical and methodological recommendations for future research, provide a prescriptive roadmap with five pathways toward a more causally rigorous research program, and introduce a diagnostic flowchart to help scholars and practitioners assess the trustworthiness of available evidence.

papers.title: Effects of HRM Gaps on Exploratory Innovation in the Context of Digital Transformation: Based on Institutional Logic Theory
papers.abstract: Against the backdrop of accelerating digital transformation, emerging market firms are undergoing profound structural adjustments. However, existing studies paid insufficient attention to how the gaps between human resource management implementation and employee perceptions affect exploratory innovation within the context of digital transformation. Drawing on institutional logic theory, we employ the multilevel polynomial regression and response surface analysis to examine the effect and mechanism of the human resource management gaps on employees’ exploratory innovation, with dataset collected from 83 companies in the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei region of China. We show that: (a) the significant human resource management gaps directly influence employees’ exploratory innovation; (b) the “high implementation-high perception” scenario yields the strongest employees’ exploratory innovation; (c) when the gaps are significant, its relationship with employees’ exploratory innovation follows an inverted U-shape; (d) uniqueness of human capital mediates the relationship between the human resource management gaps and employees’ exploratory innovation; (e) corporate digital maturity negatively moderates the relationship between the human resource management gaps and employees’ exploratory innovation. These findings provide a theoretical foundation for designing management policies that encourage exploratory innovation in the context of digital transformation.

papers.title: The effects of national security assessments in public procurement on competition, sustainability, innovation, and critical technology procurement
papers.abstract: By strategically leveraging public procurement, governments can harness market competition to drive business innovation and sustainable development. It remains unclear, however, how this premise is affected by heightened security awareness due to increasing geopolitical tensions. Focusing on European Union (EU) member states, we examine how security-oriented practices in public procurement affect tender outcomes. Using data from a recent pan-European survey of 1613 procurement projects, coupled with data from the EU's tender platform Tender Electronic Daily, we test the effect of using national security assessments (NSAs) during tender preparation on competition, innovation, sustainability, and critical technology procurement. We find that conducting such assessments has positive effects on innovation and on critical technology procurement, but only for tenders won by domestic suppliers. NSAs can thus create urgency and mobilize resources to innovate through public procurement, but possibly in a way that reinforces national rather than EU-wide technological development. We identify a tension between the need for research and coordination of NSA development at the EU level to avoid market distortions arising from uncontrolled NSA proliferation versus a heightened bureaucratic burden for suppliers. We also argue that stimulating joint cross-border innovation procurement, particularly of critical technologies, is key to fully leveraging the benefits of the EU internal market when pursuing strategic policy goals.

papers.title: Dueling Political Fictions and Public Administration and Democracy in an Era of Populism and Authoritarian Impulses
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The political fictions used in political discourse, during the English Civil War period, remain relevant to contemporary public policy and administration. Mainstream public administration discourse has too often employed the fiction of a singular and unbounded popular sovereignty that emerged during this period, leaving public administration ill‐equipped to deal with the authoritarian impulses of contemporary populist governments. What is needed in public administration discourse, in dealing with these authoritarian impulses, is not an ethic of administrative neutrality, such as has traditionally dominated much of our field, but an ethic of constitutionalism that draws on the fiction of the individual that was also articulated during the English Civil War period by the English Levellers and subsequently by the founders of the American Constitution.

papers.title: Form Before Capability? AI Governance Adoption, Functional Capability, and the Limits of Index‐Based Evidence in the Global South
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Governments across the developing world have adopted artificial intelligence governance instruments at high speed, though the relationship between formal adoption and the capability to operate those instruments remains poorly understood. This article asks whether the expansion of AI governance architecture across the Global South has been matched by the functional capabilities on which regulatory effectiveness depends, and what explains the answer. Drawing on panel data for 82 countries across five Global South regions and six waves of the Government AI Readiness Index, it reports that within the period of stable index architecture (2020–2024) measures of regulatory form rose by 20.3 points on a 0–100 scale while measures of functional capability rose by 0.4 points, a within‐country differential present in 90% of sample countries and surviving removal of the single step‐scored indicator of national strategy adoption. The pattern of the differential discriminates among explanations: formal adoption rose four times faster in states in the top quartile of administrative capacity than in the bottom quartile, where capability fell; the most aid‐dependent states adopted least; and the differential is unrelated to regime type. This is inconsistent with the view that legislation is simply quicker to produce than infrastructure and with the view that adoption is decoupled from performance for external audiences, and consistent with adoption conditioned on administrative capacity, in which capability in the weakest states erodes while capability in stronger states grows more slowly than the instruments that depend on it. Vietnam and India are developed as confirming and deviant cases. Cross‐national dispersion widened on both dimensions, and patterns that appear only when the 2025 wave is included cannot be separated from the redesign of the index in that year.

papers.title: Roger Detels, 14 October 1936 to 25 July 2026
Discrimination in Bureaucratic Recruitment Under Civil Service Exams
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Meritocratic recruitment is a central tenet in Weber's theory of bureaucracy, which states that employees should be hired based on merit. However, extensive research has shown evidence of hiring discrimination against minorities, breaking with basic principles in bureaucratic selection. This paper examines whether ethnic and racial minorities are discriminated against when bureaucratic organizations use civil service exams to assess candidates' merit and fitness for positions. Drawing on data from the local government of New York City and a candidate list fixed effects approach, we find that Black and Hispanic candidates are slightly more likely to be hired than White candidates with similar exam scores, suggesting that these ethnic minorities hold a small advantage in bureaucratic selection. However, examining the starting compensation levels of new hires, we show that minorities are hired at lower salaries and are compensated less for high exam scores than comparable White hires. Our findings suggest that civil service exams might be an important lever for securing fair and unbiased bureaucratic selection but also that they do not prevent discrimination in later steps of the recruitment process.
papers.journal_name: Journal of Policy Analysis and Management

papers.title: Participation in the smart city: disability and autonomous public transport in Singapore
papers.abstract: Amidst the increasing interdependency between bodies and technology in smart city space, this article examines the extent to which disabled people can participate in the development and discursive construction of smart city technology. While citizen participation in urban planning and decision-making processes is ostensibly a key pillar of the smart city concept, the actual and meaningful capacity for citizens – especially disabled citizens – to translate their interests into smart city technology systems remains limited. In this article, we focus on the weaving of autonomous vehicle technology into Singapore’s city space as autonomous public transport is situated as an integral part of the country’s imagined future as a ‘driverless vehicle city.’ Findings from a qualitative content analysis of 86 newspaper articles about autonomous public transport, published from August 2013 to August 2025, and a series of online focus group discussions with 20 people with ambulatory disability indicate few opportunities for disabled people to democratically participate in autonomous public transport development and hold a stake in Singapore’s smart, driverless future, as well as a disappearance of disability from public communication about the technology. Reading technology communication and design as critical mediums that concretise standards for citizenship in smart city space in both material and symbolic ways, we emphasise the need for meaningful citizen participation, informed by disability, to develop smart city technologies in line with more democratic and emancipatory agendas.

papers.title: The making of cloud computing: an antecedent of scalability
papers.abstract: This paper offers a historically situated analysis of cloud computing. Cloud computing is a paradigm for provisioning computing infrastructure that now has enormous reach. It is defined by its unique scalability. This unique scalability has proven to be enormously impactful in the digital economy and beyond, shaping the emergence of platform ecosystems, the development of AI, and the process of digitalization in the 21st century. As important as it is to grapple with this scalability, it is easy to reify. This paper examines emergent sociotechnical practices that sought to make the computer more flexible. The study focuses on specific efforts within the Research Department of a major US technology company. The analysis of scalability I offer is based on interviews with former engineers in this Lab as well as archival material. I trace projects and practices as teams forayed into making a relatively fixed machine more dynamic and more scalable. This paper advances emerging literatures on cloud computing and digital infrastructure by offering a grounded analysis of scalability-in-the-making.

papers.title: Correction to: Caution in handling switchers in pharmacoepidemiologic studies estimating treatment effects: the example of dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitors and inflammatory bowel disease
papers.abstract: CorrectionCorrection to: Caution in handling switchers in pharmacoepidemiologic studies estimating treatment effects: the example of dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitors and inflammatory bowel disease

papers.title: Causal Inference with Missing Exposures and Missing Outcomes
What matters in pre-crash driving behavior modeling? An evaluation of state representations via imitation learning
Is greater engagement with a gamified app associated with greater improvements in safe driving behaviour? A naturalistic study from the i-DREAMS project
Configuring hidden and visible camera enforcement for risky driving deterrence
papers.abstract: Road rule violations such as speeding and mobile phone use while driving remain major contributors to road crashes worldwide. Camera-based enforcement is widely implemented to address these behaviours, yet the relative and combined effects of overt and covert enforcement remain insufficiently understood. This investigation develops and tests a deterrence-based framework for identifying the perceived effectiveness of hidden and visible camera enforcement, focusing on key mechanisms including perceived certainty of apprehension and punishment avoidance. A cross-sectional, scenario-based survey was conducted with 1,167 licensed drivers in Australia. Participants evaluated four enforcement configurations (no enforcement, covert cameras, overt cameras, and combined covert and overt cameras). Outcomes included deterrence perceptions, willingness to engage in offending behaviours, and attitudes towards enforcement. Ordinal random forest models were used for variable selection, followed by cumulative link mixed-effects models to estimate effects while accounting for repeated measures. Covert enforcement was associated with higher perceived certainty of apprehension, whereas overt enforcement reduced punishment avoidance and willingness to offend. Punishment avoidance emerged as a central behavioural mechanism, showing stronger associations with willingness than perceived certainty. Combined enforcement aligned these mechanisms, increasing perceived certainty while reducing opportunities for undetected violations. Visible enforcement was also associated with more positive attitudes, indicating a complementary role in supporting legitimacy. The findings demonstrate that deterrence is not a property of individual enforcement mechanisms, but an emergent outcome of how enforcement is configured. Effective strategies should therefore balance uncertainty, visibility, and communication across the road network. These results extend deterrence theory by showing that key mechanisms are co-produced through enforcement configurations and provide practical guidance for designing more effective and publicly acceptable enforcement systems.

papers.title: Reactive safety-critical scenario generation for autonomous driving via interaction-adaptive diffusion
The relationship between child protection training and teachers' self-reported contact with authorities
Youth Engagements with Pornographic Stereotypes: A Systematic Scoping Review
papers.abstract: Pornography is a pervasive influence on young people’s understandings and experiences of sexuality, raising critical questions about how they engage with its stereotypical portrayals. While most research approaches this issue from an “effects” perspective, far less is known about the more agentic, interpretive, and contextual ways in which youth make sense of and position themselves in relation to pornographic stereotypes. To address this gap, this systematic scoping review synthesizes empirical insights into how youth (aged 16–25) in OECD countries interpret and navigate such stereotypes. Following the PRISMA-ScR framework, a systematic search across eight academic databases identified 27 studies relevant to our research question. The findings show that youth engagement with pornographic stereotypes is heterogeneous, ranging from uncritical adoption of stereotypical scripts to various forms of detachment and transformation. These modes of engagement reveal both a capacity for evaluative reflection and the relational character of sexual socialization, with transformation, in particular, emerging through dialogue and boundary setting within peer and intimate relationships. By integrating dispersed findings, this review advances scholarly debates on media and sexuality while offering practical insights for interventions such as porn literacy programs.

papers.title: Beyond fossil fuels: ensuring food and energy security in low-and-middle-income countries amid recurring geopolitical tensions
papers.abstract: Abstract The increasing dependence of smallholder agriculture on fossil fuels not only constitutes an energy challenge but also a structural threat to domestic food security in world’s low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), where a majority of the rural population still relies on small-scale agriculture for food and income, yet rapid urbanization has increased food and energy demand. Recurring geopolitical crises, such as the recent Strait of Hormuz crisis, expose one fundamental vulnerability of the food systems in the LMICs: their dependence on imported fossil fuels. Such a dependence leaves both agricultural production and food security vulnerable to energy supply and price shocks. In this Opinion article, we argue that these crises actually could open the ways to, and accelerate, a strategic transition toward renewable-energy-powered agri-food systems. Renewable energy offers proven pathways to enhance domestic food security. Success, however, requires coordinated actions from governments, NGOs, research institutions, and global development stakeholders guided by a systems view, translated in economic terms by comprehensive benefit–cost frameworks, which account for long-term public benefits (e.g. increased food-system resilience, reduced fossil fuel dependence, and environmental footprints), in addition to short-term private benefits.

papers.title: Fish production improves food security of householders in rural Ethiopia
Field-calibrated surrogate prediction and uncertainty-aware decision diagnostics for multi-unit geothermal organic Rankine cycle plants
Balancing-aware observability and joint state estimation for unmanned aerial vehicle battery packs
Modeling the electricity system in integrated assessment models - a time-series clustering approach for diverse futures
papers.abstract: The growing role of variable renewable electricity calls for high time resolution when modeling the electricity sector. However, this can be computationally too expensive for models that combine different sectors and run over long timeframes, such as Integrated Assessment Models (IAMs). The computational burden can be reduced by, e.g., timeslicing or time-series clustering. Clustering approaches have the benefit of maintaining chronology and thus enabling electricity storage modeling; however, which hourly-level features clustering should capture for the diverse long-term scenarios calculated with IAMs have remained unclear. This paper makes a two-fold contribution to address these challenges. First, we propose an hourly-resolution electricity sub-model that links to the annual level of a suitable IAM, and uses time-series clustering to reduce the hourly dimension to a small number of representative periods. Second, we propose a new clustering approach – the multi-scenario clustering – that functions robustly across a range of future scenarios that might be calculated with an IAM. In this approach, outputs from multiple model runs covering different future scenarios are used in clustering to define representative periods. Our results show that this approach produces a clustering that works for a wide range of future scenarios nearly as accurately as a-posteriori clustering tailored for each scenario individually. Therefore, the multi-scenario clustering approach provides a robust way to save on computational burden while offering a relatively good level of accuracy in comparison to using the full, multi-year, hourly time-horizon, which would be prohibitively costly to use in IAMs.

papers.title: Terrain-aware end-to-end deep learning for temporally flexible rooftop photovoltaic potential assessment
A city-scale modelling framework for equitable EV charging station planning using the comprehensive charging duration metric
Land consolidation in the context of linear infrastructure projects: Adverse outcomes from southern Poland

Effects, spatio-temporal evolution, chain transmission mechanism and precision governance of farmland resource curse in China: Based on Farmland Resource Curse Index and multi-scale raster data with causal identification
Towards European hydrogen market design: Perspectives from transmission system operators
papers.abstract: Despite hydrogen being central to Europe's decarbonisation strategy, only a small share of renewable hydrogen projects reached final investment decision. A key barrier is uncertainty about how future hydrogen markets will be designed and operated, particularly under Renewable Fuels of Non-Biological Origin requirements. This study investigates the extent to which future hydrogen market design can be adapted from existing natural gas markets, and the challenges it must address. The analysis was based on a survey on future hydrogen market design targeting European gas transmission system operators, the stakeholder group responsible for operating the network and implementing the Network Codes. The survey provided an assessment of mechanism transferability and identified challenges for the early development of the hydrogen market. Core market design principles and trading frameworks are broadly transferable from natural gas markets, as entry-exit systems and virtual trading points. Capacity allocation requires targeted adaptation to improve coupling with electricity markets. Tariffs require adaptation through intertemporal cost allocation, distributing infrastructure costs over time to protect early adopters. Balancing regimes should be revisited to reflect hydrogen's physical characteristics and different linepack flexibility usages. Key challenges for early hydrogen markets include: temporal mismatches between variable renewable supply and expected relatively stable industrial demand, limited operational flexibility due to scarce storage and reduced pipeline linepack, fragmented regional hydrogen clusters, and regulatory uncertainty affecting long-term investment decisions. These findings provide empirical input to the hydrogen Network Codes and offer guidance to policymakers designing hydrogen market frameworks.

papers.title: Understanding demand-side flexibility characterisation and barriers to effective deployment: A Dutch case study
papers.abstract: Demand response is a critical component of future energy systems, as it provides a significant contribution to the cost-optimal integration of renewable energy. However, a variety of barriers inhibit its deployment and utilisation. While the research on barriers to demand response is wide and varied, it is often unsystematic and incomplete, with studies focusing on parts of the demand response ecosystem such as specific sectors, technologies or stakeholders. To bridge this gap, this study builds upon existing literature to develop a consistent and comprehensive framework for systematically identifying, classifying and analysing barriers across the demand response ecosystem, with the aim of providing input for the design of policy incentives. We develop an integrated framework that is based on the underlying nature of the identified barriers. We identify four overarching categories: technical, economic, regulatory and behavioural, along with multiple sub-categories and elements. This framework is tested on the Dutch energy system. We find that the most significant technical barriers faced by the Dutch energy sector are process and operational constraints and network limitations; the main economic barriers are financial uncertainty and distorted market signals due to taxes and tariffs; the main regulatory barriers are policy ambiguity and information insufficiency; and the main behavioural barriers are lack of expertise and incompatible individual preferences.

papers.title: Decommissioning and repowering of utility-scale solar photovoltaic systems: A review of policy, economics, technology, environment and social dimensions
papers.abstract: The rapid global expansion of solar photovoltaics (PV), rising to nearly 3 TW in 2025, has outpaced planning for end-of-life (EoL) management. The first wave of large-scale solar farms, commissioned in the early 2010s, is now in its second decade of operation, making EoL decisions increasingly urgent. Existing literature has focused primarily on panel recycling, overlooking balance of system components, civil works, grid infrastructure, and regulatory and contractual obligations. In mature industries such as oil and gas, decommissioning frameworks and financial assurance were developed over decades after environmental harms became visible, and liabilities such as abandoned wells remain unresolved. Solar PV is younger and growing rapidly, and can establish EoL frameworks before most of its fleet reaches EoL. This review provides the first cross-domain synthesis of EoL pathways for utility-scale PV systems, spanning policy, economics, technical practices, environmental impacts, and social dimensions. Drawing on 85 sources and 36 case studies, it examines decommissioning and repowering as the primary EoL strategies. The literature reveals fragmented regulatory frameworks, inconsistent cost estimation methods, and limited empirical evidence. While repowering offers economic benefits, it presents environmental trade-offs, while social impacts are underexplored. The evidence is concentrated in the U.S. and Europe and limited to English language sources, so findings on costs, incentives and permitting may not transfer to other regions. No framework exists to compare EoL options across these factors. These findings highlight the need for structured, site-specific decision frameworks, and for evidence from more regions, to support transparent and consistent EoL planning.

papers.title: Electrostatic precipitators for particulate matter emission control in flue gas: A review of experimental and multiphysics studies with optimization perspectives
Comparative analysis of heat pumps coupled with thermal energy storage systems: Performance improvement, flexibility, sustainability assessment, and future perspectives
Dust-induced degradation of wind turbines: A comprehensive critical review of research trends, knowledge gaps, aerodynamic degradation, structural implications, and mitigation strategies
Geospatial optimization and life cycle assessment of structural steel reuse hubs
Environmental-social hotspots and sourcing trade-offs in global material supply chains for NCM 622 batteries manufactured in China
Lipophilic Redox Mediators Reprogram Intracellular Electron Flow to Promote Arsenic Methylation in Soil Fermentative Bacteria
papers.abstract: Abstract Anaerobic arsenic (As) methylation by fermentative microorganisms, particularly Clostridium-related populations, controls As speciation, mobility, and volatilization in flooded paddy soils, yet the mechanisms promoting this process remain poorly understood. Here, we reveal that phenazine- and phenoxazine-like redox mediators can enhance anaerobic As methylation via reshaping the intracellular electron allocation in a representative As-methylating fermentative bacterium. We integrated As speciation analysis, metabolite profiling, proteomics, and metabolic-flux modeling to determine how resazurin, as a represenative lipophilic redox mediator, reshapes fermentative metabolism and methylated As (MeAs) formation. The membrane-permeable redox mediator resazurin increased the apparent rate constant of MeAs formation by up to fourfold relative to the hydrophilic mediator anthraquinone-2,6-disulfonic acid (AQDS). Unlike AQDS, resazurin enhanced dimethylarsine formation while establishing a more reducing intracellular environment by diverting electrons from hydrogen evolution, indicating altered intracellular electron disposal. At the proteomic level, resazurin induced coordinated increases in As(III) methyltransferase (ArsM) and proteins involved in S-adenosylmethionine (SAM) biosynthesis, representing the primary molecular responses associated with enhanced As methylation. Proteins involved in amino-acid-fueled energy conservation and redox homeostasis were also enriched, potentially creating favorable cellular conditions for SAM-dependent As methylation. In a paddy-soil-derived fermentative consortium, resazurin likewise enhanced MeAs production and increased transcript levels of Clostridium-associated arsM and the SAM synthetase gene (metK). These findings identify lipophilicity-dependent, redox-compound-mediated intracellular electron flow reprogramming as a previously underappreciated control on anaerobic As methylation and provide a mechanistic basis for predicting MeAs formation in flooded soil environments.

papers.title: Industrial Solid Wastes Recycling from Steel and Power Sectors Delivers Climate and Net Societal Benefits
papers.abstract: Abstract Sectoral decarbonization can substantially reshape the quantity and composition of industrial solid waste and its associated resource recovery potential, yet how these changes evolve along decarbonization pathways remains poorly understood. Here, we develop a sectoral transition framework linking future waste generation, recycling technologies, life cycle environmental impacts, and societal benefits. We focus on the steel and power sectors, which represent major industrial solid waste sources and distinct decarbonization pathways across six major producing regions from 2025 to 2050. By 2050, steel sector wastes remain at 0.61–0.78 Gt, whereas power sector wastes decline from 1.11 Gt in 2025 to 0.17–0.50 Gt. Under four scenarios, cumulative mitigation ranges from 25.68 to 53.39 Gt CO2-eq, with discounted net societal benefits of USD 11.24–23.81 trillion. Steel sector benefits are sensitive to recycling technology shares, whereas power sector benefits are more strongly shaped by transition-driven changes in the waste generation and composition. These findings highlight the importance of integrating evolving waste flows and technology choices into long-term decarbonization and circular economy strategies.

papers.title: Proteomic Profiling for In Situ Exposure in a Sentinel Freshwater Species to Describe the Crustacean Reproductive Effects of Aquatic Contamination
papers.abstract: Abstract Complex mixtures of contaminants can affect aquatic organisms through diverse modes of action, making extrapolations of laboratory findings to field conditions complex. Here, we show that proteomics combined with active biomonitoring may inform about reprotoxic effects in the sentinel species Gammarus fossarum. Proteomic responses provide information on the diversity of underlying mechanisms and may serve as a sensitive early warning signal of reprotoxicity. Females were exposed in situ in 18 French surveillance sites and analyzed for reproductive end points and proteomic levels in the caeca and the ovaries. This study aimed to assess links between reproductive impairment and molecular responses, using the complementary information provided by both tissues. Protein coexpression analysis identified protein clusters associated with organ functions, reproductive impairments, or field exposure. Several modules were significantly associated with field condition or females’ physiological integrity. Interestingly, we identified a large diversity of biological pathways modulated in impacted females exposed to reprotoxic sites, with reproduction-related proteins as potential early biomarkers of reprotoxicity. These results highlight the relevance of considering field conditions and individual physiology within the eco-exposome framework and demonstrate the value of integrating omics and active biomonitoring to uncover diverse molecular signature behind field-induced reprotoxicity in this sentinel species.

papers.title: Unregulated Disinfection Byproducts from de facto Water Reuse: Molecular Evidence for EfOM-Induced Redirection of Chlorination Pathways
papers.abstract: Abstract Unplanned potable reuse introduces effluent-derived organic matter (EfOM) into drinking water sources. While conventional coagulation partially removes EfOM, the residual fraction undergoes chlorination and may form toxic disinfection byproducts (DBPs) that escape current monitoring. However, the molecular mechanisms by which EfOM alters DBP formation pathways remain poorly understood. Here, we combine ultrahigh-resolution mass spectrometry with reaction network analysis to reveal that EfOM significantly redirects chlorine pathways. Compared to EfOM-free surface water, the presence of 20% EfOM decreases direct halogenation pathways (addition and substitution) from 4.2% to 1.8% of total transformation events. This shift occurs because EfOM introduces reduced, high-molecular-weight, heteroatom-rich molecules that cannot be directly halogenated; they require HOCl-driven oxidative fragmentation to generate halogenation-susceptible intermediates. Consequently, chlorinated finished water accumulates sulfur-containing DBPs (CHOS compounds, with relative intensity increasing from 35% to 60%) and complex “orphan” DBPs lacking identifiable precursors (with molecular features linked to elevated toxicity). These findings highlight an urgent need to update DBP monitoring frameworks to include unregulated sulfur-containing and orphan byproducts in de facto reuse scenarios.

papers.title: Enhancing sustainability in greenhouse agriculture through chemical analysis–driven characterization of boiler biogas fuel strategies
papers.abstract: Greenhouses can enhance sustainability and productivity by integrating renewable energy and CO 2 enrichment, which improves photosynthesis and reduces environmental impact. However, existing studies on biogas and methane combustion have not addressed how combustion-derived CO 2 can be strategically managed to meet the coupled thermal and photosynthetic demands of greenhouse crops. In this context, the present study is the first to conduct a parametric analysis of biogas utilization for greenhouse applications, offering a proposed adaptive fuel management strategy hypothesized to support both environmental and economic benefits. To achieve this, a counterflow flame configuration is employed to investigate the combustion characteristics of a greenhouse boiler operating with various methane–biogas fuel mixtures. The detailed Gas Research Institute Mechanism (GRI-Mech 3.0), comprising 53 species and 325 reactions, is utilized to model the reaction kinetics. Detailed thermophysical and transport properties based on fundamental thermodynamics are integrated to accurately capture flame structure and species transport. The model was validated against experimental methane/air flame data, demonstrating good agreement and confirming its predictive accuracy. The effects of (1) CO 2 enrichment, (2) operating pressure, and (3) strain rate on flame temperature and species concentrations (CO 2 , CO, NO, and NO 2 ) are systematically investigated. Findings demonstrate the potential of biogas as a sustainable fuel under characterized conditions: Biogas substitution lowers peak in-flame NO x and CO concentrations while increasing peak CO 2 concentration, highlighting its potential for CO 2 enrichment. A pressure-sensitivity analysis (1–10 atm) and a proposed adaptive diurnal fuel-switching strategy are also presented. Practical guidelines are proposed to support greenhouse growers in enhancing thermal efficiency and environmental performance.

papers.title: Village and farm ponds differ in contaminant retention and mobility: Implications for sustainable management of rural agricultural landscapes
Consumer willingness to pay and farmers’ adoption intentions for pesticide-reducing technologies in European orchards
papers.abstract: Reducing synthetic pesticide use remains an EU sustainability objective, yet uptake of pesticide-reducing technologies remains limited in high-input orchard systems. This study examines whether information on consumer willingness to pay (WTP) for products with reduced pesticides is associated with farmers' adoption intentions. We focus on four pesticide-reducing innovations: smart mapping variable rate (VRA) application systems, robotic weeders, bio-based solutions with low sulphur and copper formulations, and cover crops. Evidence is drawn from a structured survey experiment involving 354 olive and vine growers across five European Union countries. Using a within-subject design with randomised presentation order and a Cheap Talk script to mitigate hypothetical bias, we compare farmers' adoption intentions before and after exposure to estimated consumer WTP premiums for wine and olive oil produced with reduced pesticide use. Non-parametric tests and multinomial logit models indicate that consumer WTP information is positively associated with both partial and full adoption intentions across all four technologies, with stronger associations for smart mapping VRA and robotic weeders than for bio-solutions and cover crops. Farm structure and behavioural factors, including perceived costs, subjective norms, and perceived effectiveness of existing pest management practices, exhibited technology-specific associations with adoption intentions. Although the study design does not permit causal inference, the findings suggest that consumer-driven market signals could complement existing policy approaches to support the transition towards more sustainable agricultural production.

papers.title: Major olive mill aqueous effluents as industrial sources of hydroxytyrosol, 3,4-dihydroxyphenylglycol and tyrosol for circular valorisation
papers.abstract: The selective recovery of valuable chemicals from waste streams is a central objective of Green Chemistry, particularly when waste prevention and the use of renewable feedstocks can be combined. In two-phase olive oil extraction systems, several aqueous effluents are generated that are commonly treated as waste despite their significant organic and phenolic content. In this work, four industrial effluents—olive washing water (OWW), hopper drip water (HDW), vertical centrifuge water (VCW) and oil decanting water (ODW)—were systematically characterised in six olive oil mills over two consecutive production seasons to evaluate their potential as sources of bioactive phenolic compounds. HDW exhibited the highest phenolic concentration, reaching up to 3.5 g/L, together with elevated sugar contents, identifying it as the most promising stream for the recovery of hydroxytyrosol (HT) and 3,4-dihydroxyphenylglycol (DHPG). VCW, although more diluted, was generated in the largest volumes and contained substantial amounts of both compounds, while ODW showed an unusual predominance of DHPG over HT, enabling selective recovery. An industrial chromatographic process was optimised to maximise phenolic retention and HT purity in the most concentrated streams. Based on national production data, the valorisation of these effluents could enable the recovery of up to 80 t/year of HT and 56 t/year of DHPG. Overall, this study highlights the potential of phenolic recovery to support waste valorisation strategies and facilitate subsequent wastewater management within a circular-economy framework.

papers.title: Future hydrogen demand in Europe’s steel and chemical sectors: A site-specific assessment
Physics-based deep reinforcement learning for adaptive BOG management under dynamic voyage conditions and carbon regulations on LNG carriers
A novel Solar-Driven Molten-Salt methane pyrolysis system with direct Particle-to-Reactor-Wall heat Transfer: Design and Techno-Economic assessment
papers.abstract: This study proposes a solar-driven methane pyrolysis system in which a particle-based concentrating solar power (CSP) plant supplies heat directly to an array of molten-salt (MnCl 2 –KCl) bubble-column reactors through the reactor wall, without an intermediate heat-transfer fluid or electric heating step. An hourly-resolved CSP model over a full year, comprising a heliostat field, a free-falling particle receiver, and two-bin thermal energy storage, is coupled to a reactor model that includes reaction kinetics, bubble hydrodynamics, particle-to-salt heat transfer, and equipment sizing. The integrated plant is assessed through a techno-economic analysis for a site in Daggett, California. At the baseline design (hot and cold particle temperatures of 1100 and 950 °C, 14 h of storage), the bulk salt temperature is 936 °C, the plant reaches a capacity factor of 69% and a single-pass methane conversion of 45%, and it produces about 6700 t/yr of hydrogen at a levelized cost of hydrogen (LCOH 2 ) of $3.87/kg without carbon credit and $3.52/kg with credit for the co-produced carbon. Raising the reactor temperature increases the cost of solar heat but lowers LCOH 2 through faster kinetics and fewer reactor modules, so the CSP and reactor subsystems must be designed jointly. Natural gas accounts for about 54% of LCOH 2 , and the particle-to-wall heat transfer coefficient is the most influential design parameter. At an assumed hydrogen price of $4/kg, the project has a positive 30-year net present value of $53 M with the carbon credit and without Section 45 V or LCFS policy support. At a gas price of $6/GJ and a hot-particle temperature of 1200 °C (bulk salt temperature of 1021 °C), approaching the conditions of earlier studies, LCOH 2 falls to $1.9–2.3/kg depending on the carbon credit. The configuration is a conceptual design: experimental validation of the particle-to-wall heat transfer, corrosion, creep, thermal cycling, abrasion, and liner compatibility in molten chloride is required.

papers.title: Multi-seasonal assessment of soil contamination and metal mobility following the Jagersfontein tailings storage facility failure event in South Africa
papers.abstract: The failure of the Jagersfontein tailing storage facility (TSF) in South Africa on 11 September 2022 released ~5.8 million m 3 of kimberlite tailings into a semi-arid wetland, representing one of the largest such spillages in history. This study investigates the chemical evolution of the deposited tailings and their impact on soil geochemistry over three seasons (18 months). Geochemical and statistical analyses identified two broad elemental groupings: Group 1 elements (B, Na, Mg, Cr, Mo, Co, and Ni) were primarily introduced into the landscape by the tailings, whereas Group 2 elements (V, Mn, Cu, Zn, As, Sn, Cd and U) were mainly enriched through landscape-driven processes, particularly groundwater discharge, and material redistribution during flood events. Sodium migrated rapidly through the soil profile, contaminating soils down to bedrock, and showed no signs of recovery even where surface tailings had been removed. In contrast, Mg, Cr, Co and Ni migrated primarily via colloidal-facilitated transport, resulting in the progressive enrichment of the upper soil horizons. The tailings' sodic and metal-laden nature is particularly problematic in an environment naturally enriched in Na, B, As and Mo. Chemical mass transfer analyses indicate that pedogenic processes are unlikely to reverse contamination within ecologically meaningful timescales. Immediate remediation, including tailings removal, is recommended to mitigate long-term environmental and health impacts. Overall, the findings demonstrate that environmental impacts extend far beyond surface contamination, revealing complex subsurface enrichment pathways that offer new insights into contaminant behaviour following large-scale tailing failures in dryland environments.

papers.title: A 4000-year record of parallel collapse in the ecological niche of Black Sea top predators
papers.abstract: Marine ecosystems face multifaceted threats stemming from historical overexploitation and environmental degradation. Despite existing research, there are notable gaps in understanding the long-term dietary dynamics of marine organisms in the context of anthropogenic impacts. To address these gaps, we utilized stable isotope analysis as a proxy for dietary niche and examined changes in the Black Sea over a 4000-year period, focusing on ancient and contemporary samples from cetaceans ( Phocoena phocoena , Delphinus delphis , Tursiops truncatus ) and fish ( Scophthalmus maximus ). Among the ancient samples, the isotopic data from all four species revealed a wide and generally overlapping average dietary niche. In contrast, contemporary cetacean and fish samples exhibited niche compression, indicative of a fundamental shift in the Black Sea marine ecosystem from Antiquity to the present day. Our analyses provide ecologically significant temporal perspectives, shedding light on critical trends and changes essential for conservation efforts aimed at addressing contemporary ecological challenges in degraded marine systems.

papers.title: Experimental assessment of rotational speed stability in a micro turbojet engine for unmanned aerial vehicles based on fuel physicochemical properties, engine performance, and vibration analysis
papers.abstract: This study investigated the rotational speed stability of a micro turbojet engine operating with three different fuels through physicochemical fuel characterization, engine performance testing, and vibration-based stability analysis. Experiments were conducted on a micro turbojet engine used in unmanned aerial vehicle applications under five steady-state operating regimes. Key performance parameters—including thrust, turbine inlet temperature, fuel flow rate, and specific fuel consumption—were investigated. Engine stability was evaluated using two triaxial accelerometers installed near the compressor and turbine bearing planes, while rotational speed variations were analyzed from vibration signals and encoder measurements using short-time Fourier transform, root mean square, and kurtosis indicators. The results showed that diesel fuel containing 5 vol% lubricating oil provided engine performance comparable to Jet A containing 5 vol% lubricating oil, with thrust and fuel flow variations generally below 3%. In contrast, biodiesel containing 5 vol% lubricating oil increased the specific fuel consumption by up to 17%. For all tested fuel–lubricating-oil formulations, kurtosis values remained below 3, indicating no pronounced impulsive or shock-like behavior in the measured vibration signals. However, at high operating regimes (approximately 110000 rpm), biodiesel and diesel fuel containing 5 vol% lubricating oil produced slightly higher vibration amplitudes than Jet A containing 5 vol% lubricating oil.
