Estimating economy-wide mineral commodity consumption using hybrid input-output modeling: a case study of fluorspar
Barriers to Addressing Biodiversity Conservation in Multinational Companies and Strategies to Overcome Them
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Corporate initiatives supporting biodiversity conservation in multinational companies (MNCs) face limited commitment despite biodiversity's multiple benefits. Although reasons associated with MNCs' commitment are documented and include increased profits, stakeholder pressure, or reputation, those preventing it remain unclear. This study investigates the decision‐making processes related to biodiversity issues in a sample of 16 multi‐sectoral MNCs, uncovering how information is managed internally. It identifies barriers experienced by all 16 companies and explores their underlying drivers. We find that biodiversity issues follow ill‐suited organizational routines, characterized by insufficient slack resources, and rely on tools that lack operational relevance—including the current double materiality assessment. Our results also highlight the limited influence of stakeholders, supply‐chain interdependencies, and tensions between individual and collective scales that hinder organizational adaptation. Finally, we reveal how external factors beyond corporate control shape these barriers and suggest strategies to overcome them, advocating for systemic change and deeper community engagement.

papers.title: Political Corruption, Foreign Investment and Industrial Environmental Performance: Developing Countries' Perspective
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The debate on the environmental impact of foreign direct investment (FDI) continues to evolve; however, it is widely shown that FDI worsens environmental pollution in developing countries due to their institutional deficiencies. Currently, there is limited evidence on the synergistic effect of political corruption, which is corruption across the executive, legislature and judiciary, and FDI on industrial environmental performance in developing countries. This study, therefore, addresses this research gap by investigating the impact of political and public sector corruption and FDI on industrial environmental performance, measured by industrial carbon emissions, relying on a panel dataset from 112 developing countries for the period 1980–2022. Contrary to the pollution‐haven hypothesis (PHH), our results demonstrate that FDI flows to developing countries are significantly associated with a reduction in industrial emissions. Also, a higher level of public sector corruption and overall political corruption, especially executive corruption, significantly leads to higher industrial emissions, while less judicial and legislative corruption lessens industrial emissions. Also, contrary to the dominant view based on PHH, our results demonstrate that FDI reduces industrial emissions in developing countries with higher political and public sector corruption; however, FDI has a weak effect on industrial emissions in developing countries with less political and public sector corruption. These findings are important as they provide contradictory evidence to the widely held view that FDI flows to developing countries worsen environmental pollution due to their institutional deficiencies.

papers.title: Regenerative Business Between Normative Ambition and Managerial Practice: A Systematic Review Through the Integrated Management Model
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT As the regenerative rhetoric spreads across research and practice, management literature remains fragmented, with no coherent account of how regenerative principles are defined, governed, and enacted at the organizational level. This systematic literature review synthesizes 36 peer‐reviewed articles (2017–2025) through the lens of the Integrated Management Model, structuring regenerative business along normative, strategic, and operational levels. The analysis shows that the field's coherence is unevenly distributed: it converges on a shared normative core of ecological worldview, systemic purpose, and net positive contribution to socio‐ecological systems, while the strategic mechanisms and measurement systems that would translate that core into practice remain comparatively undeveloped. Regenerative business thus emerges less as an accomplished paradigm shift than as a discourse defined by the shift it pursues. We identify central tensions and propose a research agenda to close the distance between its normative ambition and its managerial means.

Distributed small-reservoir pumped-storage hydropower in Europe: a GIS screening under drawdown and karst constraints
papers.abstract: Continental pumped-storage hydropower (PSH) atlases omit schemes built from small reservoirs, although such sites could provide distributed flexibility. We screen this resource across 37 European countries, detecting closed depressions and water bodies and pairing upper and lower reservoirs under land-use, protection and grid-distance constraints. The reproducible workflow uses open pan-European data, a hybrid terrain stack (FABDEM; national lidar in Norway and Sweden) and an explicit allowable water-level variation for lake volume. At a 5-km grid distance and 1-m drawdown, exact maximum-weight matching gives an all-size screened bound of 2.57 TWh; excluding mapped-karst footprints for purpose-built reservoirs and sites above 2500 m leaves 0.58 TWh, of which a 21 115-site portfolio capped at 100 MWh per site stores 0.40 TWh (0.24 TWh, EU-27). Replacing FABDEM by national lidar cuts Norway’s and Sweden’s screened energy with 72% each (328.7 to 92.1 and 67.3 to 18.5 GWh): usable lake volume barely moves ( − 0.4 %), but pairs containing a dry basin collapse because that basin binds. A Sobol analysis makes maximum pair distance and karst treatment the joint controls (total effects 0.49 and 0.48). This is an exploratory first screening, not deployable capacity: it ranks where national feasibility studies should look, and their constraints can only reduce it.

papers.title: Identifying administrative villages for rural revitalization: A case study in the loess hilly and gully region of China
Managing load shedding in Ukraine: rationing rules, exemptions and price caps
papers.abstract: Ukraine’s power infrastructure has been a primary target of Russian attackssince the start of the full-scale invasion in February 2022. The country wasonce an energy exporter, but its generation capacity has regularly fallenshort of domestic demand since early 2024 due to intensified attacks. Administrativebodies safeguard the power system and protect households andcommercial customers by repairing and rebuilding generation and transmissioncapacity, supporting decentralised generation, expanding imports, andregulating wholesale and retail markets — including adjusting price caps.However, due to capacity shortages combined with market interventions, demandfor electricity often exceeds supply, necessitating outages to preventunmanageable blackouts. These load-shedding measures include a sophisticatedsystem of pre-announced, block-wise outages called hourly outageschedules that are difficult for customers to understand, costly to manage,and likely economically inefficient. This paper describes the load sheddingprocess in Ukraine (including exemptions), the regulated price caps for endconsumers, and the implications of both. We also provide actionable long andshort-term advice for improving how outages are handled.

papers.title: Self-powered electrochromic smart windows: Energy-conversion pathways, energy–device matching, and building integration
In Situ Reconstruction-Directed Electrocatalyst Design Enables Low-Energy Anodic Oxidation for Water Purification
papers.abstract: Abstract Anodic oxidation reactions (AORs) hold promise for degrading persistent organic pollutants, yet practical deployment is constrained by inadequate anode stability and sluggish kinetics under low-bias operation. Prussian blue analogues (PBAs) feature cyanide-bridged metal frameworks with efficient intermetallic electron transfer, yet their surfaces inevitably undergo uncontrolled reconstruction during electrolysis, producing outcomes that range from beneficial activation to detrimental degradation. Here, we reported a first-ever paradigm shift from suppressing reconstruction to actively directing it, demonstrating that the intrinsic instability of FeMn PBA could be harnessed as a design lever. Through an in situ self-reconstruction process, we discovered that the morphology and surface coordination environment were spontaneously reorganized into FeMn nanoflowers grown on carbon paper (FeMn@CP), a configuration never before achieved from this precursor. This reconstruction-guided pathway uniquely yielded a 201-fold increase in electrochemically active surface area (ECSA) over pristine FeMn PBA, alongside markedly enhanced electrochemical stability, synergistic gains not attainable by conventional stabilization strategies. Capitalizing on this reconstructed architecture, FeMn@CP achieved efficient phenolic pollutant degradation at low bias, with robust reusability, broad matrix adaptability, and substantially reduced effluent toxicity. Continuous-flow experiments further verified its sustained performance under practical conditions. This study unveils, for the first time, that catalyst reconstruction, when rationally exploited, serves as a decisive and generalizable strategy to concurrently boost AOR activity and stability, opening an unexplored avenue for designing next-generation electrocatalytic water purification systems.

Acute autonomic and cardiovascular responses to walking in natural versus urban environments: A systematic review and three-level meta-analysis
Functional divergence of biochar and nano-Fe3O4 in microbial chain elongation: Adsorptive regulation as an overlooked equilibrium driver

BTCA/Ca2+-reinforced sodium alginate/chitosan/MWCNT aerogel for sustainable remediation of herbicide-contaminated water: Adsorption performance and molecular insights
A wireless and passive RFID-based sensing system for the detection of Cd2+ in soil: A novel approach for onsite detection of hazardous metals
Bridging wildfire risk science and forest management: a modular integrated framework for loss estimation and economic–environmental trade-off analysis
Mapping the beyond GDP field: Canonical concentration and insular invisibility in three decades of multidimensional prosperity measurement (1995–2026)
papers.abstract: Three decades after the Stiglitz Commission's call to measure “beyond GDP”, multidimensional prosperity frameworks have proliferated, yet cross-linguistic mappings of their paradigmatic and territorial composition remain scarce; existing reviews rely on English-only searches. This article characterises the conceptual, methodological and territorial structure of multidimensional prosperity frameworks published between 1995 and 2026, and tests the robustness of the resulting patterns to alternative definitions of the review scope. Following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA 2020), we searched Web of Science and Scopus in English, Spanish, French, Italian and Portuguese, retrieving 23,048 unique records. Title-and-abstract screening used a deterministic rule-based classifier specified and refined by the two reviewers, who adjudicated every record it passed forward at full text, yielding 583 included studies. Paradigm was coded at two levels — the identity of the framework referenced and the analytical framing of the study deploying it — because the two do not coincide. Robustness was assessed across three nested corpora ( n = 583, 551, 503). The Human Development Index (HDI) of the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) and the Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) of the Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative (OPHI) jointly account for 46.3–50.4% of the corpus. Frameworks with a social paradigmatic identity account for 79.0%, ecological for 8.9%, holistic for 8.3%, economic for 2.2% and two-dimensional hybrids for 1.6%. Insular contexts represent 1.0% of studies, and paradigm is not associated with territorial scale (Monte-Carlo p = 0.39), so the concentration is field-wide rather than confined to any territorial tier. Framework paradigm and study-level analytical framing diverge for 73.2% of the studies in which both are determinable: 184 of the 348 studies invoking a social-paradigm instrument (52.9%) are framed economically. Among the 162 bespoke frameworks, 58 integrate all three substantive dimensions but only one imposes an explicit biophysical boundary. All patterns are stable across the three corpus definitions. Three decades after the Beyond GDP critique, the field remains concentrated on a narrow canon of capability-based instruments that are predominantly deployed within income- and growth-centred analytical framings, while ecological-paradigm frameworks and insular territories remain marginal. Paradigmatic plurality appears to require editorial and institutional intervention rather than further conceptual elaboration.

papers.title: CEO power and stock price crash risk: moderating effect of environmental practices
papers.abstract: Abstract This paper investigates the influence of CEO power on corporate stock price crash risk in developed market context, and further examines the moderating impact of corporate environmental practices. Two environmental practices are examined: greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions and Sustainable Development Goal 13 (SDG-13 supporting climate action). Analysing data from publicly listed firms in the G7 nations from 2006 to 2021, empirical results show that firms led by more powerful CEOs are generally exposed to lower crash risks. Additionally, results show that companies implementing stronger environmentally friendly practices, particularly, supporting climate actions - SDG-13, see a further reduced crash risk. This pattern is especially evident in non-crisis period, non-financial firms, and firms with high environmental and social (ES) scores, i.e., Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) performance. The findings are validated by various robustness tests using alternative estimation models, alternative measures, and additional tests. Our findings provide practical implications for firms, investors, regulators, and policymakers.
papers.journal_name: Review of Quantitative Finance and Accounting

papers.title: Globalization and the Benefits of Education: Evidence From the Double Burden of Malnutrition
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT This paper investigates how rising women's education and exposure to economic and social globalization jointly shape the Double Burden of Malnutrition (DBM), defined as the coexistence of maternal overweight and child stunting within the same household. Drawing on Demographic and Health Surveys (DHS) spanning 1992–2017 across 38 low‐ and middle‐income countries, we first apply a sub‐national (DHS region) bivariate statistical decomposition framework that teases apart two forces: “structure effects”, which capture changes in how household characteristics relate to DBM while holding their distribution fixed, and “composition effects”, which isolate how shifts in the distribution of household characteristics affect DBM while holding their association with DBM constant. In a second‐stage analysis, structure effects show that as social globalization deepens, the protective role of women's education against DBM is attenuated and becomes positively associated with DBM, especially in more urbanized regions. Composition effects further reveal that where economic globalization is already advanced, gains in women's education are associated with higher DBM prevalence. Taken together, this empirical evidence suggests that women's education alone may be insufficient to counteract the nutritional risks linked to globalization, underscoring the need for complementary institutional, regulatory, and dietary interventions.

papers.title: A Structural Volatility Surface Under Stress and Low Liquidity Conditions
papers.abstract: This article presents the Kinetic Equation for Volatility Analysis (K-EVA), a primarily conceptual framework for the structural interpretation of implied volatility surfaces under stress conditions and low liquidity. Rather than treating the volatility surface as a uniformly continuous and continuously deformable object, the proposed approach considers the possibility that the surface may consist of maturity-dependent structural regions connected through either continuous or discontinuous transitions. K-EVA integrates structural reparameterization, geometric interpretation, and structural fractures into a unified representation. Under this perspective, the implied volatility surface is interpreted not only as the result of calibration but also as a structural system whose geometry reflects different information environments associated with market uncertainty, liquidity conditions, and scheduled or unexpected informational events. A mathematical definition of structural fractures is introduced on the basis of changes in the information set associated with neighboring option maturities. This distinction naturally leads to a structural interpretation of market regimes and volatility dynamics, in which transitions between latent, normal, and turbulent market conditions are represented by changes in the geometric configuration of the implied volatility surface rather than by latent stochastic states. The proposed parameterization preserves desirable properties commonly associated with Stochastic Volatility Inspired–based formulations, including parsimony and smooth extrapolation. It also introduces a set of geometrically interpretable structural coefficients that facilitate the identification of structural distortions, information-driven transitions, and market regimes. K-EVA provides a unified structural representation of implied volatility surfaces under stress and low-liquidity conditions, allowing discontinuities, local deformations, and information-driven transitions to be incorporated while preserving analytical tractability and geometric interpretability.

papers.title: The Physical Mean as a Practitioner Benchmark for Option Pricing through Feasible Hedging
papers.abstract: The Black–Scholes value has an exact economic meaning inside the ideal continuous, frictionless market: Namely, it is the initial cost of a continuously rebalanced replicating portfolio. This article addresses the question of how that meaning transfers to actual practitioners. When instantaneous rebalancing is not in the investor’s feasible trading class, the replication equality cannot automatically be assigned to the implemented cash-only or discretely traded position. We study the terminal physical mean MP(H) = 𝔼P[H] and its discounted version VP(H) = e−rT𝔼P[H] as the simplest operational benchmark. MP(H) is the writer’s expected cash payment at maturity, and VP(H) is the unique initial bank reserve that produces zero expected terminal profit under the cash-only strategy. The realized payment remains H, not its mean. This interpretation applies to every integrable payoff, including path-dependent claims. Monte Carlo simulation provides a general computational route; for a Markov diffusion, the conditional mean also satisfies the backward Kolmogorov equation and its discounted version satisfies the corresponding partial differential equation with the physical drift. Under geometric Brownian motion, the physical call benchmark exceeds the Black–Scholes value exactly when μ > r, whereas the physical put benchmark exceeds the Black–Scholes value exactly when μ < r. The difference is explained by the funding-gap identity Inside the ideal model, the continuously maintained stock exposure supplies the gap in expectation. A practitioner who charges the Black–Scholes value but does not implement its supporting hedge may therefore hold less than the cash-only mean-break-even reserve under P. Numerical applications to a European call, a weekly hedge with transaction costs, and a path-dependent Asian call show how the benchmark is used in real decision making. The physical mean is not proposed as a universal market price or a tail-risk measure. It is, instead, a transparent expected-liability benchmark against which feasible hedges and additional risk loadings can be assessed.

papers.title: Materiality and investor reaction to environmental corporate social responsibility : A replication and extension of Flammer (2013)
papers.abstract: Abstract Research Summary We replicate and extend Flammer's (2013) event study of investor reaction to environmental corporate social responsibility. Flammer found that investors react positively to eco‐friendly events and negatively to eco‐harmful events, with positive reactions diminishing and negative reactions intensifying from 1980 to 2009. We confirm her results in a narrow replication and find that these time trends persist in a quasi‐replication extending the sample through 2019, despite major shifts in the institutional environment for sustainability investing. We then extend Flammer by incorporating financial materiality and find that the investor reactions and time trends Flammer observed are primarily concentrated in material events. Notably, investors drew this distinction throughout the 40‐year window we study, predating the institutionalization of materiality‐based sustainability analysis. Managerial Summary We examine how investors respond to companies' environmental actions. Analyzing 40 years of data on US‐listed public firms, we find that investors reward companies for eco‐friendly actions and penalize them for harmful ones. Over time, these reactions have shifted: investors have grown less enthusiastic about eco‐friendly actions and more critical of harmful ones. Importantly, investors react primarily to environmental actions that are financially relevant, or “material,” to the business and were doing so well before formal standards existed. Within material actions, positive reactions to eco‐friendly initiatives have weakened while negative reactions to eco‐harmful ones have grown stronger. These findings suggest that managers should prioritize environmental initiatives closely tied to their company's financial performance.

papers.title: The intelligence loop and value creation in the age of AI agents
papers.abstract: Abstract Research Summary Artificial intelligence (AI) is moving from generating outputs to executing work. An agent that executes work autonomously produces something generative AI does not: operational experience that can raise its future intelligence. Prior research on AI emphasizes value creation through demand‐side feedback, notably data network effects, in which user data improve prediction and reinforce adoption. We develop the supply‐side counterpart, the intelligence loop: delegated usage generates operational experience, agentic capability converts it into future intelligence, and the resulting value maintains or expands usage. The loop cannot operate until autonomous execution is viable, a threshold we call minimum viable intelligence (MVI). Crossing MVI does not guarantee rising intelligence. Comparable deployments of AI agents can diverge as their loops decay, sustain, or accelerate. Three implications follow. Competitive advantage may depend more on the loop than on installed base. An above‐MVI agent supplies scarce expert skill as a non‐rival, replicable resource, so productive capacity can grow faster than expert headcount, with the one‐person company as a limiting case. And a venture with adequate demand, capital, and a capable team can still fail because its loop never functions or later deteriorates. Managerial Summary Artificial intelligence (AI) agents can execute work, and the experience generated through execution can raise their future intelligence, a feedback process we call the intelligence loop. An agent crosses a workflow's minimum viable intelligence (MVI) when it executes reliably without step‐by‐step direction, autonomous execution creates at least as much net value as the best alternative after oversight and correction costs, and governance arrangements keep residual risk acceptable and accountability clear. Investment belongs where one of these conditions keeps a valuable workflow below MVI. Deployment can begin with narrow, feedback‐rich workflows near MVI that ideally lead to harder workflows, since base model upgrades can match gains on simple work. Even above MVI, the loop is not automatic: it stalls when feedback is not timely and diagnostic, experience yields little intelligence gain, gains add little user value, or value does not maintain or expand usage. Human involvement shifts from executing work to specifying goals, evaluating outputs, governing execution, and supplying tacit knowledge. When the loop sustains or accelerates, productive capacity can grow faster than expert headcount. With capable base models widely available, advantage depends less on access to AI than on building and governing the loop, controlling proprietary operational experience, and converting it into intelligence more effectively than rivals. A venture with adequate demand, capital, and a capable team can fail because its loop never functions or later deteriorates. Cutting evaluation or oversight to scale faster may increase output in the short run but weaken the loop even while revenue remains healthy.

How Perceived Economic Inequality Shapes Consumers' Preferences for Self‐Improvement Consumption
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Despite the increasing prevalence of self‐improvement products and services, what encourages consumers to choose such products requires further exploration. Drawing from tournament theory, which suggests that individuals exert greater effort when reward differentials across levels are large (vs. small), we show that perceived economic inequality is one of the factors that encourages consumers to choose self‐improvement products. Through 6 studies (including 2 supplementary studies) across 3 countries (i.e., the United States, Japan, and China; N = 2626), this research shows that high (vs. low) perceived economic inequality significantly increases consumers' preferences for self‐improvement (vs. non‐self‐improvement) products, and finds a significant indirect effect through heightened status ambition. Alternative explanations of status anxiety, loss of control, negative mood, and envy were not supported as mediators. However, this research did not find evidence that perceived social mobility moderates the relationship between perceived economic inequality and preferences for self‐improvement consumption. Study 4 further demonstrates that the main effect extends to more direct consumption‐related outcomes, including purchase intention and recommendation likelihood. Together, these findings suggest that demand for self‐improvement products is shaped by consumers' perceptions of the economic inequality, providing insights for consumers themselves and for self‐improvement–related firms to develop more effective promotion strategies across different economic contexts.

papers.title: When technologies transform: a consideration of open innovation's contributions to operations management
papers.abstract: Purpose This paper examines what an open innovation (OI) perspective contributes to operations and supply chain management when a technology transition reshapes an industry. Earlier operations management research implicitly defined OI as a small set of isolated practices. This paper recovers its fuller depth as bidirectional knowledge flows and a mindset anchored in the business model. Design/methodology/approach The study traces innovation in the global automotive industry across three phases, then develops illustrative case studies of four Chinese electric vehicle (EV) entrants, Kandi, BYD, Xiaomi and Chery, analyzed through outside-in flows, inside-out flows and business model innovation. The cases build on a structured review of Chinese-language academic and industry literature, corroborated against company reports, trade press and industry data. Findings Chinese EVs have attained industry leadership, yet no dominant EV innovation strategy has emerged. All four firms drew heavily, but differently, on external knowledge, much of it from consumer electronics and smartphones, outside the automotive supply chain and each treated the vehicle as a platform. BYD and Chery also pursued inside-out flows, BYD through divisionalization and an open vehicle architecture, Chery through technology exports and internal suppliers. The contribution runs both ways: OI extends operations management research from project-and dyad-level openness to firm-level strategy, while operations management research helps explain organizational configuration and governance in innovation. Research limitations/implications The findings rest on a single industry. Future work should test them in other transforming sectors: pharmaceuticals, financial services and defense. Originality/value The paper reframes OI for operations management scholarship and uses the Chinese EV phenomenon to show how it complements operations management when industry architectures are disrupted.
papers.journal_name: International Journal of Operations & Production Management

papers.title: De-risking from China: how US firms reconfigure sourcing through decoupling, diversification and friendshoring across geopolitical disruptions
papers.abstract: Purpose We examine whether US firms use three location strategies—decoupling, diversification, and friendshoring—to de-risk their sourcing portfolios. We investigate how the use of these strategies varies across bilateral (2018 US–China trade war), systemic (COVID-19 pandemic) and alliance-based (Russia–Ukraine war) shocks. We also test whether firms operating in high-tech industries de-risk more aggressively. Design/methodology/approach Using Panjiva US seaborne import records, we build firm-year measures of the three strategies for 1,565 US firms over 2011–2024. We then estimate fixed-effects models that interact firm's pre-disruption China exposure with the three disruption periods and a high-tech indicator. Findings Highly China-exposed firms decouple during all three disruptions, with decoupling switching on sharply at the trade war. Diversification activates specifically at the COVID-19 pandemic. Friendshoring peaks during the COVID-19 pandemic and reverses once the war begins. Sourcing portfolios appear more diversified and politically aligned, but these gains vanish once the China sourcing share is excluded, revealing them as mechanical by-products of decoupling. High-tech firms generally do not de-risk more than their peers. Originality/value We move the study of de-risking from perception-based case evidence to large-scale observed sourcing behavior. We conceptualize decoupling, diversification, and friendshoring as three sourcing location strategies and match each to its most salient disruption type, laying the groundwork for a contingency theory of strategy–shock fit. We further show that portfolio-wide indices of diversification and political alignment may overstate genuine de-risking because they incorporate the effects of decoupling. Moreover, policymakers' ambitions to de-risk high-tech industries and promote friendshoring have generated only a limited corporate response.
papers.journal_name: International Journal of Operations & Production Management

papers.title: How peers influence headquarter attention to foreign subsidiaries
papers.abstract: Abstract Research Summary We examine how attention to foreign subsidiaries is structured by peer‐based cues originating both outside and inside the firm. Using the cognitive pillar of the attention‐based view, we show how executives rely on peer reference groups to allocate attention across subsidiaries, and we compare the relative influence of different peer types. Among peers outside the firm, industry peers exert a stronger influence on headquarter attention than home‐country peers, highlighting the dominance of competitive comparability. We also show that attention diffuses within the multinational enterprise, with attention to one subsidiary spilling over to other subsidiaries within the same cognitive category. Also, regional groupings drive stronger attentional spillovers than externally constructed categories. These findings reveal a category‐based process through which headquarter attention is allocated during ongoing foreign operations. Managerial Summary We examine how peer activity shapes where multinational headquarters focus their attention during foreign operations. Rather than monitoring every foreign subsidiary equally, headquarters rely on cues from peers to decide where to look more closely, but not all peer cues are equally influential. Among peers outside the firm, industry competitors have a stronger pull on headquarter attention than firms from the same home country, meaning competitive dynamics matter more than home‐country familiarity in directing headquarter attention. Within the firm, geographic regional groupings shape attention more powerfully than broad market categorizations. When attention is directed toward one subsidiary, it spills over to other subsidiaries in the same grouping, amplifying their visibility. Managers can anticipate where attention flows by understanding which peer categories headquarters finds most compelling.

papers.title: Discursive Institutional Work and the Social Control of Dangerous Objects
papers.abstract: Abstract Across societies and over time, the social control of objects deemed “dangerous”—i.e., as threats to public order, morality, or physical and psychological well-being—varies, from regulation to prohibition, with implications for responsibility, potential harm, and affected communities. Drawing on U.S. Congressional hearings on the issue of cannabis regulation and prohibition (1906–1951), we examine how shifts in social control track changing configurations of discursive institutional work. Our work demonstrates how configurations of rationalization, moralization, and syncretization shaped the meaning of cannabis as a dangerous object: rationalization calculates the risk, supporting calibrated regulation; moralization absolutizes the danger, promoting prohibition; and syncretization balances these two. We refer to this reciprocal dynamic as an epistemic ratchet, whereby rationalization and moralization each weaken the epistemic foundations of the alternative regime, making movement between regulation and prohibition difficult in either direction. Our study makes three contributions: (a) it extends the organizing-of-risk account of how danger is rendered governable to the form and reversibility of control; (b) it adds to research on discursive institutional work by identifying epistemology, complexity, and responsibility as the object-level qualities through which discourse becomes consequential for governance; and (c) it contributes to debates on responsibility, ethics, and harm by showing how the discursive redistribution of responsibility shapes the scope and coerciveness of control.

Dietary patterns and cardiovascular risk in adult survivors of childhood cancer: findings from the SCCSS-Nutrition Study
papers.abstract: PURPOSE: To identify dietary patterns among adult childhood cancer survivors (CCSs), examine their determinants, and assess whether they differ according to cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk profiles. METHODS: CCSs from the Swiss Childhood Cancer Survivor Study diagnosed before age 21 years (1976-2005), surviving ≥ 5 years and aged ≥ 18 years in 2017, completed a food frequency questionnaire (SCCSS-Nutrition). Factor and hierarchical cluster analyses of 52 food groups identified dietary patterns. We categorised CCSs as having CVD, CVD risk factors (obesity, hypertension, diabetes, high cholesterol), or being CVD risk-free. Multinomial logistic regression assessed associations between dietary patterns and CVD risk profiles. RESULTS: Among 802 CCSs (median age: 35 years; IQR: 29-41; 50% male), we identified five dietary patterns: Mediterranean-inspired diet (22%), Western indulgence diet (38%), Western sweet & fatty diet (26%), restrained indulgence diet (9%), plant-based & alcohol-rich diet (6%). Male sex, younger age, German-speaking region, smoking, and living with others were associated with Western indulgence, Western sweet & fatty, and restrained indulgence diets. Higher Swiss socioeconomic position (Swiss-SEP) and education, and not having children, were associated with the plant-based & alcohol-rich diet, higher Swiss-SEP was also associated with the Western indulgence diet. No associations were observed between dietary patterns and CVD risk profiles. CONCLUSIONS: Dietary patterns among adult CCSs were socially patterned and differed according to sociodemographic and lifestyle characteristics, but were not associated with CVD risk profiles. IMPLICATIONS FOR CANCER SURVIVORS: Dietary counselling and broader lifestyle support should be considered as part of long-term survivorship care for CCSs.

Intensifying Mainstream Wastewater Treatment via a Dual-Hydrogel Process Coupling Acidic Partial Nitritation and Anammox
papers.abstract: Abstract Partial nitritation and anammox (PN/A) process has been proposed as a sustainable biotechnology for mainstream nitrogen removal. However, it remains challenging to sustain high activities of ammonia-oxidizing bacteria (AOB) and anammox bacteria and suppress the growth of nitrite-oxidizing bacteria (NOB). In this study, a novel dual-hydrogel system comprising two reactors with distinct immobilized microbial communities was developed to integrate acidic PN and anammox for low-strength mainstream wastewater treatment. The system achieved a total inorganic nitrogen removal efficiency of 81.7% at a short overall hydraulic retention time of 5.5 h. In the acidic PN reactor, hydrogel beads effectively immobilized and enriched acid-tolerant AOB (“Candidatus Nitrosoglobus”), while creating a localized low-pH niche with sufficient free nitrous acid microenvironment to selectively inhibit NOB growth. This enabled high-rate PN without strict dissolved oxygen limitation. A pH-based feeding strategy allowed the bulk pH of the acidic PN reactor to be self-maintained at ∼6.1, achieving an appropriate effluent ratio of nitrite to ammonium and minimizing acid inhibition of the downstream anammox process. In the anammox reactor, the beads maintained a relatively higher internal pH, forming a favorable niche for retained anammox bacteria (“Candidatus Brocadia”) and facilitating high-rate nitrogen removal. The hydrogel beads also exhibited excellent structural stability during long-term operation (over 300 days). These results demonstrate an effective approach for simultaneously sustaining AOB and anammox activities while suppressing NOB, providing a promising approach for stable PN/A to treat mainstream wastewater.

papers.title: Stage-Resolved Dynamics of Antibiotic Resistance Genes and Mobile Genetic Elements in Full-Scale Anaerobic Digestion Systems
papers.abstract: Abstract Anaerobic digestion (AD) has the potential to reduce antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) and mobile genetic elements (MGEs) during waste treatment, yet evidence from full-scale systems remains limited. In particular, process-stage dynamics and host-associated resistance mechanisms are poorly understood, and the relative importance of operational and physicochemical drivers remains unresolved. Here, we profiled process-oriented, stage-resolved resistome and mobilome dynamics across substrates, digestates, and storages from ten farm-scale AD plants, resolving putative host-ARG-MGE coabundance associations across sequential process stages. An integrated framework combining high-throughput qPCR and 16S rRNA gene sequencing was used to quantify ARG and MGE dynamics and characterize microbial community structure. Across different AD systems, ARGs and MGEs exhibited heterogeneous abundance changes, with no consistent patterns. However, elevated pH and NH3 were associated with decreasing trends but were not solely determinative. Stage-resolved correlation networks revealed that ARG-MGE associations formed a conserved structural backbone, whereas putative host associations underwent continuous reshuffling across process stages. This indicates that resistance persistence is driven less by stable taxon associations and more by the redistribution of ARG-MGE units among microbial taxa. Collectively, these results demonstrate that stage-resolved, network-informed analyses provide an informative framework for evaluating resistance persistence and potential environmental risks associated with digestate application.

papers.title: Liquid Crystal Monomers in Paired Indoor Dust and Urine: Compound-Specific Enrichment Patterns and External–Internal Exposure Profiles
papers.abstract: Abstract Liquid crystal monomers (LCMs) are extensively used in liquid crystal display devices, yet the relationship between household contamination and human internal exposure remains unclear. We investigated fluorinated and nonfluorinated LCMs (FLCMs and NFLCMs) in paired indoor dust and urine samples. Widespread occurrence of LCMs was observed in 58 paired indoor dust and first-morning urine samples collected in Suizhou, with 48 of 49 LCMs detected in dust and 40 in urine. Median concentrations of ∑49LCMs were 255 ng/g in dust and 26.9 ng/mL in urine. FLCMs were predominant in dust, whereas NFLCMs contributed more to urinary burden. The dominant compounds differed markedly between dust and urine. Among these, only 2,3-difluoro-1-methoxy-4-[4-(4-propylcyclohexyl)cyclohexyl]benzene (DMPCB) showed a significant positive dust-urine correlation (r = 0.409, p < 0.01). Relative-enrichment analysis revealed compound-specific shifts, with several NFLCMs relatively enriched in urine and several FLCMs in dust. The median estimated daily intake of ∑49LCMs via dust ingestion was 0.110 ng/kg bw/day, far below levels reported for e-waste recycling areas. Although hazard quotients (HQs) for all 39 LCMs with available toxicity benchmarks were several orders of magnitude below 1, incomplete toxicity reference data remain a major source of uncertainty in risk characterization. Overall, the findings indicate widespread mixed exposure to LCMs and suggest that urinary LCM profiles may reflect contributions from multiple exposure pathways and compound-specific toxicokinetic processes in addition to household dust.

Assessment of carbon emissions and life cycle cost in railway infrastructure: comparison between steel slag ballast and natural aggregate
papers.abstract: This paper evaluates the use of steel slag aggregates (SSA) as ballast for railways, from environmental and financial perspectives. The environmental assessment employs the Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) methodology framework to compare steel slag ballast (SSB) with natural aggregate ballast. The study focuses on the Global Warming Potential (GWP) impact category (also known as carbon footprint), measured in kg of CO 2 equivalent. The study considers a functional unit of 1 km of railway track over an 8-year reference service period, from a case study in the Southeast region of Brazil. The CO 2 uptake through the natural carbonation of the SSA was obtained through thermogravimetric analysis, resulting in an estimated uptake of 17.7 kg CO 2 /t SSA under the conditions considered, a value that was incorporated into the assessment. In addition to the environmental assessment, a Life Cycle Cost (LCC) analysis was conducted to evaluate the economic performance of the railway ballast alternatives over their life cycle. Within the defined system boundaries, the results showed that the railway with steel slag ballast showed a lower GWP than conventional ballast, primarily due to the estimated CO 2 uptake during natural carbonation. For the same 8-year reference service period, we calculated −4.82E+04 kgCO 2 e for the SSB (thus absorbing CO 2 ) and 1.30E+04 kgCO 2 e for the conventional ballast. A sensitivity analysis indicated that the SSB maintains its environmental advantage even with transportation distances of up to 470 km. From a financial standpoint, the LCC of the railway with SSB was 32% lower than that of conventional ballast. The study confirms the potential of SSB as an environmental and financial alternative for railway ballast, given the premises adopted in this research.
authors: Kathleen Dall Bello de Souza Risson

papers.title: Centralized versus conventional anaerobic digestion of sewage sludge: An environmental and economic assessment
papers.abstract: High-solid anaerobic digestion (HSAD), in which dewatered sewage sludge from several small wastewater treatment plants is treated centrally, is an alternative to conventional low-solid anaerobic digestion (LSAD) for sludge stabilization and energy recovery from biogas. This work develops a modelling framework to compare centralized HSAD and decentralized LSAD through a coupled life cycle assessment (LCA) and economic analysis approach, supporting case-specific decision-making for sludge management under defined local boundary conditions. Four different sub-scenarios were modeled for both HSAD (S1.1-S1.4) and LSAD (S2.1-S2.4), forecasting different biogas uses, alternative sludge transportation routes, digestate valorization pathways, and ammonia extraction. The sub-scenarios were compared with the respective baselines (S1.0 for HSAD and S2.0 for LSAD), corresponding to full-scale Italian plant configurations. Under the investigated full-scale conditions, HSAD showed lower environmental impacts than conventional LSAD when transport distances were limited, due to higher credits generated by biogas and the avoided mineral fertilizer use in agriculture. However, input sludge/digestate transportation is a dominant driver of both environmental and economic impacts. Moreover, biogas upgrading to biomethane is environmentally preferable to electricity generation, but economically unfavourable at current market conditions. Overall, centralized HSAD can represent a favorable solution under regional-scale planning when logistics, digestate valorization, and gate-fee conditions are suitable, whereas optimized LSAD with dynamic sludge thickening can achieve comparable performance. Although the specific results are related to an Italian case study, this work provides a useful tool for decision-making among alternative sludge management solutions when local boundary conditions (sludge characteristics, transportation distances, HSAD/LSAD plant availability) are specified.

Regional end-of-life embodied carbon emissions of wood-frame housing: A hybrid-parametric assessment of single-family houses in Canada
papers.abstract: The aging wood-frame single-family housing stock in North America represents a major future source of demolition waste and a substantial supply of recoverable wood materials. However, the embodied carbon implications of alternative end-of-life (EoL) strategies remain poorly understood at the regional scale due to limitations in temporal resolution, empirical validation, and carbon pathway characterization. This study develops a hybrid-parametric modelling framework that integrates historical construction eras, material flow analysis, the 9R circular economy hierarchy, and life cycle module-based carbon accounting (C1 D) to assess 81,598 single-family houses in Vancouver, Canada. The framework incorporates uncertainty through Monte Carlo simulations and is validated against four real-world deconstruction projects, demonstrating its capability to represent both material flows and carbon outcomes. The modelled wood generation (155.9 kg/m 2 ) and diversion rate (90%) fall within the observed ranges (120.8–179.0 kg/m 2 and 84–99%). Results show that EoL scenario selection has a substantially greater influence on embodied carbon performance than building age. Conventional demolition generates average net emissions of 9.39 kgCO₂e/m 2 . Moderate deconstruction (75% diversion) reduces this to 3.12 kgCO₂e/m 2 (−67%), whereas high-diversion pathways achieve net savings of 1.23 and 6.92 kgCO₂e/m 2 at 90% and 95% diversion. Structural lumber represents the largest recoverable material fraction and the primary source of mitigation potential. Sensitivity analysis identifies labour intensity, recovery efficiency, and allocation among reuse, repurposing, and recycling pathways as the dominant determinants of carbon outcomes. Biogenic carbon assessment further demonstrates that circular strategies primarily alter the timing and distribution of carbon flows through material substitution and emission deferral rather than permanent carbon sequestration. A critical circular economy gap is identified between diversion quantity and recovery quality, as similar diversion rates can result in substantially different carbon outcomes depending on the value retained from recovered wood. These findings highlight the need for wood-specific recovery targets and carbon-based performance metrics that prioritize high-value material retention over diversion quantity alone to maximize embodied carbon mitigation and circular economy benefits.

papers.title: Interplay of synergistic emissions and synergistic efficiency for controlling pollutants and CO2 in Chinese urban agglomerations
Long‐Term Legacy of Exotic Pioneers: Over Two Decades of Biodiversity Monitoring Reveals Constrained Succession in a Restored Sanitary Landfill
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Long‐term ecological studies are critical for evaluating restoration strategies on challenging sites, such as closed landfills. This study presents a 23‐year biodiversity monitoring program (2000–2023) at the restored Southeast New Territories sanitary landfill in Hong Kong. We tracked the succession of woody trees and shrubs and of soil and litter invertebrates to assess the impact of initial revegetation with exotic pioneer species, particularly nitrogen‐fixing legumes. Our results reveal a constrained ecological trajectory dominated by a few exotic/pioneer species, with the leguminous trees Acacia confusa and Leucaena leucocephala becoming overwhelmingly dominant, correlating with a significant decline in overall plant diversity over time. This low‐diversity plant community supported a depauperate invertebrate assemblage, notably favouring detritivores and harbouring invasive ants such as Anoplolepis gracilipes (yellow crazy ant). While bird surveys indicated the presence of seed‐dispersing species, the ecosystem failed to develop high species richness. The findings demonstrate that while exotic pioneer trees effectively establish initial cover, their long‐term dominance, potentially exacerbated by allelopathy and site management practices like mowing, creates a biotic filter that hinders the development of biodiverse, self‐sustaining ecosystems. We conclude that landfill restoration requires frameworks that go beyond mere vegetation establishment to actively manage the legacy of pioneer species and promote heterogeneous habitats, such as constructed wetlands in restored landfills, to support diverse ecological communities and enhance functional biodiversity.

papers.title: Walter Benjamin on natural history and place
papers.abstract: Taking his radio broadcast on the Mississippi flood of 1927 as a point of departure, this article argues that Walter Benjamin has much to contribute to current debates concerning space, nature, and place. Benjamin’s episode on the devastating flood in the American South was his final transmission for Berlin Radio’s Youth Hour in 1932, and it concludes a series of episodes on disasters that are both natural and social at once. This article situates the radio broadcast in relation to two catastrophic ways of seeing: first, in Benjamin’s work on the German mourning play , where the spatializing function of allegory transposes the temporal events of history into a spatial image, and second, in the weakly messianic vision of history as “one single catastrophe.” Drawing on these reorienting modes of vision, I argue that Benjamin’s curation of ancient and recent catastrophes across the world prompts his young listeners to recognize interlinked moments of danger spanning both historical time and global space.

papers.title: Signaling with debt currency choice
papers.abstract: We document that firms in emerging markets borrow more in foreign currency when the local currency actually provides a better hedge in downturns. Motivated by this fact, we develop an international corporate finance model in which firms facing adverse selection choose the foreign currency share of their debt. In the unique separating equilibrium, good firms optimally expose themselves to currency risk to signal their type. Crucially, the nature of this equilibrium depends on the co-movement between cash flows and the exchange rate. We provide extensive empirical evidence for this signaling channel using a granular dataset including more than 4,800 firms in 19 emerging markets between 2005 and 2021. Our results have implications for evaluating and mitigating risks arising from currency mismatches in corporate balance sheets.

The Scope of Statistical Discrimination: An Experimental Study on Gender Barriers in Tech,
papers.abstract: Abstract Women are significantly underrepresented in the technology sector. We design an experimental study using field data to identify the role of statistical discrimination in job applicant assessments. First, we measure the programming skills of job applicants for a programming job. Then, we recruit a large sample of employers consisting of human resource and tech professionals and incentivize them to predict the performance of these applicants based on their standardized resumes. We find no significant gender differences in programming skills. However, consistent with statistical discrimination we find employers perceive female applicants to be significantly less skilled. We also provide experimental evidence that the perceived gender skill gap can be readily eliminated. Employers who were randomized to have access to additional information such as aptitude or personality do not believe that there are gender differences in programming skills. Together, these findings suggest that tech employers believe women are less skilled programmers. Nonetheless, in the context of hiring, the scope for statistical discrimination may be limited in practice as employers often have access to more information when assessing applicants.

papers.title: Offshoring and voting patterns in the US
papers.abstract: This paper studies the impact of offshoring by US firms on voting patterns in the US. Using county-level voting data combined with industry-level offshoring data, we ask whether an increase in employment at foreign affiliates of US multinationals in vertically oriented industries is associated with an increase in the vote share for the incumbent party candidate in Presidential, House, and Senate elections. We find that offshoring leads to an increase in the incumbent vote share for counties with more educated workers, and a decrease for counties with higher shares of workers in the manufacturing sector and in occupations that are more easily relocated abroad. These results are consistent with the labor market literature on offshoring, which shows that offshoring has heterogeneous effects on workers’ employment based on skill and occupational tasks. This suggests that voters respond to the economic effects of offshoring by rewarding or punishing incumbent party candidates.

papers.abstract: Abstract Welfare caseloads in North America halved following reforms in the 1990s and 2000s. We study how this shift affected families by linking Canadian welfare records to tax returns, medical care, educational attainment, and criminal charges. We find substantial and heterogeneous employment responses that increased average income despite reduced transfers. We find zero effects on aggregate healthcare costs, but mothers saw reduced preventative care and increased mental health treatment, consistent with the transition to employment elevating time pressure and stress. We find no effect on teenagers’ education or criminal charges as young adults but find some evidence of intergenerational welfare transmission.

papers.abstract: We consider testing zero pricing errors in high-dimensional linear factor pricing models. Existing methods are mainly based on either an $L_2$ statistic, which is effective under dense alternatives, or an $L_\infty$ statistic, which is powerful under very sparse alternatives. To bridge these two regimes, we develop a class of $L_q$-based tests for finite $q$, including the practically useful $L_4$ and $L_6$ cases. We show that larger $q$ leads to greater sensitivity to sparse alternatives. We further establish the asymptotic independence between the $L_\infty$ statistic and the $L_q$ statistic for any finite $q$, which motivates a Cauchy combination test that adapts to a broad range of sparsity levels. Simulation studies and a real-data analysis show that the proposed methods are more robust to the unknown sparsity of the alternative and can outperform existing procedures in finite samples.

papers.abstract: We consider nonparametric identification of independent private value first-price auction models, in which the analyst only observes winning bids. Our benchmark model assumes an exogenous number of bidders N. We show that, if the bidders observe N, the resulting discontinuities in the winning bid density can be used to identify the distribution of N. The private value distribution can be identified in a second step. A second class of models considers endogenously determined N, due to a reserve price or an entry cost. If bidders observe N, these models are also identifiable using winning bid discontinuities. If bidders cannot observe N, however, identification is not possible unless the analyst observes an instrument which affects the reserve price or entry cost. Lastly, we derive some testable restrictions for whether bidders observe the number of competitors and whether endogenous participation is due to a reserve price or entry cost. An application to USFS timber auction data illustrates the usefulness of our theoretical results for competition analysis, showing that nearly one bid out of three can be non competitive. It also suggests that the risk aversion bias caused by a mismeasured competition can be large.

papers.abstract: In many practical applications, only noisy proxies for the true regressors are available, which is commonly believed to induce an attenuation bias. In the linear-in-means model, however, estimated peer effects might be inflated, potentially leading to false positives. This paper shows that the asymptotic bias depends on the interplay between individual characteristics and network links and demonstrates how the network structure can facilitate identification without the need for additional external information. Based on these identification results, we present consistent GMM and 2SLS estimators that are easily implementable. Our results are illustrated by means of a Monte Carlo simulation.

papers.abstract: We study tournaments with managerial discretion in hiring. A manager selects a coworker from a pool of candidates and then competes against him in a Lazear--Rosen--style tournament with a prize equal to a share of total output. A profit-maximizing principal sets the prize share together with a head start (or handicap)---an advantage (or disadvantage) in the output comparison---granted to the manager. The head start affects output through three channels: (i) encouraging the manager, (ii) discouraging the new hire, and (iii) inducing the manager to hire a stronger candidate. The hiring effect dominates the discouragement effect until the strongest candidate is hired; beyond that point, any further head start discourages the new hire more than it encourages the manager. The optimal contract therefore grants a head start just large enough to induce the manager to hire the strongest candidate.

papers.abstract: -The 2021–2022 energy crisis generated pronounced episodes of explosive price behavior followed by sharp corrections in gas and electricity markets and raised concerns about whether observed price surges reflected fundamental scarcity or speculative dynamics. This paper examines the presence and synchronization of explosive price behavior across a comprehensive set of European and U.S. gas and electricity benchmarks, as well as carbon-neutral hydrogen and renewable Power Purchase Agreement (PPA) price series. We apply the multiple-bubble testing framework of Phillips, Shi and Yu (2015) and its panel extension to detect and date-stamp common episodes of explosivity across fossil-fuel and transition-related markets. Our results reveal synchronized explosive dynamics during the crisis period, with evidence that exuberance was not confined to traditional energy markets but also extended to hydrogen and renewable PPA benchmarks. For gas and electricity markets, where futures data are available, spot-forward diagnostics provide additional evidence on the interpretation of explosive episodes. Overall, the findings offer new insights into the propagation of instability across fossil and green energy price benchmarks and contribute to the debate on energy market dynamics during periods of systemic stress.

papers.abstract: We perform a behavioral experiment of karma, a class of mechanisms for repeated resource allocation with attractive fairness and efficiency properties, in theory. Individuals in these mechanisms bid non-tradable credits that flow from resource consumers to yielders. Human subjects recruited on Amazon MTurk are repeatedly and randomly paired to bid karma according to time-varying individual urgency to acquire resources. Treatments varied in the urgency process (frequent moderate versus sporadic high urgency) and the richness of the bidding scheme (binary versus full range). Benchmarked against random allocation, karma achieves an (almost) Pareto improvement, despite subjects deviating from the theoretically optimal Nash bidding policy: maximum improvement is attained by subjects deviating by up to one karma bid unit on average, and positive improvement with deviations of up to 3-4 units. These findings hold across all treatments, among which no significant differences are found, with the exception of the sporadic high urgency process with binary bidding being (weakly) favorable. They offer behaviorally robust lower bounds for karma's expected performance in human populations and guide its future implementation.

Notwithstanding its many merits, we show that EADA can improve only two students when an alternative mechanism that Pareto-dominates DA could benefit all but one student. This shortfall in the number of students improved is not exclusive of EADA but extends to all setwise minimally unstable mechanisms, i.e. those that generate a set of blocking pairs that is never a strict superset of that of another mechanism. The incompatibility between number of students improved and minimal instability disappears when blocking pairs are compared cardinally rather than by set inclusion. In some problems, EADA can be doubly dominated: improving fewer students while generating more blocking pairs.

Under certain distributional conditions the search for the optimal mechanism can be restricted to a class where there is no uncertainty about the number of units the buyer will receive, i.e. the buyer chooses whether to get 0, 1, or 2 units. papers.title: From global value chains to local jobs: Exploring FDI-induced job creation in EU-27
papers.abstract: This study explores the differential impacts of global value chain (GVC) participation on foreign direct investment (FDI)-related job creation in EU-27, emphasizing the role of sector-specific and regional factors. The study is based on a rich set of project-level data on FDI-generated jobs. It utilizes a labor demand function estimated through GMM estimator to account for endogeneity. Results indicate that forward GVC participation significantly boosts FDI-related job creation by enhancing domestic value-added and production capacity. However, this effect is moderated by sector-specific characteristics such as productivity or wages. Conversely, backward GVC participation, characterized by reliance on foreign inputs, generally reduces FDI-generated jobs due to lower domestic labor requirements and diminished competitiveness. Despite this, the negative impact of backward GVC participation on employment becomes less significant when regional diversification is considered, highlighting the importance of regional factors like infrastructure and skilled labor. The study also finds that the impact of GVC participation on employment varies with EU membership status and sectoral characteristics, with old EU member states and high-tech sectors benefiting more from forward GVC integration. In contrast, new EU member states and low-tech sectors face greater challenges, particularly with backward GVC participation.

papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The urban growth boundary (UGB) has been recognized as an effective policy instrument for controlling disorderly urban sprawl and improving the sustainability of urban development. However, summary studies in this domain are insufficient. Hence, this study conducted a holistic review of UGB based on 228 literature samples published between 2011 and 2025 to help resolve this academic gap. This work has four objectives: (1) to analyze principal journal sources, countries, authors, organizations, articles, and keywords in the literature on UGB using bibliometrics and science mapping methods; (2) to summarize current research topics relevant to UGB; (3) to discuss existing research gaps in UGB; and (4) to explore future research directions in UGB.

papers.title: The Rise and Reconfiguration of Asia–Pacific Finance Research: Evidence From 1990–2024
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT We examine the evolution of finance research in the Asia–Pacific region across 28 leading finance journals from 1990 to 2024. Our results reveal a substantial shift in regional research leadership, with China ranking first in research impact from 2017 onward and first in article quantity from 2018 onward, surpassing the region's previous leaders. Cross‐border collaboration patterns continue to reflect geographical proximity and historical ties. At the institutional level, the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology, the Chinese University of Hong Kong, and the University of Hong Kong rank highest in research influence. Scholar‐level rankings also identify the region's leading contributors in terms of both research influence and productivity.

papers.title: Bridging Micro and Macro Sustainability: How Sustainable Finance Connects Corporate esg to Sustainable Development Goals
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Sustainable finance (SF) has increasingly been conceptualized in the literature as a mechanism linking firm‐level ESG practices to broader sustainable development outcomes. However, the field remains theoretically fragmented, with limited integrated mapping of micro–SF–macro linkages. Using scientometric and bibliometric techniques, this study analyzes 1,024 Scopus‐indexed publications (2004–2025) through performance analysis, keyword co‐occurrence, text mining, and bibliographic coupling. Thirteen keyword clusters reveal the intellectual structure of the field, spanning green finance, ESG performance, governance, climate policy, and energy transition. Bibliographic coupling identifies six thematic clusters that suggest how sustainable finance is theorized to link firm‐level actions with macro‐level sustainability transformations. Despite rapid post–Paris Agreement growth, theoretical and methodological coherence remains limited. The study outlines future research directions, emphasizing disclosure harmonization, causal identification, innovation–policy alignment, and multi‐level approaches. Accordingly, the findings capture patterns in the literature rather than empirically verified causal relationships.

papers.abstract: This study analyzes the effect of the New Horizon educational reform on student achievements and on the academic environment in schools. New Horizon is a broad-based national reform initiated by the Ministry of Education and gradually implemented in elementary and lower-secondary schools in Israel beginning in 2008. The main elements of the reform are an increase in the time teachers spend in school, additional small-group instruction time (individual hours), an increase in teachers’ and principals’ salaries and posing higher requirements and incentives for professional development. We use a difference-in-differences (DID) approach to evaluate the effects of the reform on a multitude of outcomes related to student achievements and to measures of school academic environment. We find that in the short run, about two years after it was first implemented, the New Horizon reform has increased student test scores, mainly in math and English. In addition, the reform has improved a number of the school-learning environment’s attributes. We also find that the reform has had no effect on school violence and on the general level of students’ satisfaction with school. Furthermore, we explore how specific components of the reform are related to our findings. ∗We thank the Israel’s Ministry of Education and the National Authority for Measurement and Evaluation in Education (RAMA) for allowing access to restricted data at the Ministry online protected research lab. papers.title: Partitioning menus to nudge single-item choice
papers.abstract: Consumers must often choose items from a menu of options. Examples include patrons selecting entrees from a restaurant menu, employees deciding how to save for retirement from a list of 401(k) plans, or physicians choosing medical treatments from an order set. Options often need to be organized or grouped in some way, which raises the question of whether grouping menu items perturbs the options ultimately chosen by consumers. In a series of experiments, we find evidence for single-item partition dependence , where individuals are especially likely to choose an option from menu categories that are more finely partitioned (holding the total number of options constant). Unlike prior work on multi-item allocation decisions, the traditional explanation of partition dependence due to a bias towards even allocation cannot apply to single-item choice, because singular choices are not divisible. Instead, we find evidence that menu partitions influence choice because consumers view partitions as communicating information about what items are most frequently chosen (i.e., descriptive social norms). Our findings suggest that single-item partitioning can have a sizable influence on choice and behavior, and holds promise as a simple and effective tool for marketers and policymakers.

How do sexual activity and sexual satisfaction relate to levels of relationship desire?
papers.abstract: Sexual satisfaction and access to sexual activity outside committed relationships may be associated with individuals' motivation to pursue a long-term partner. We examined whether within-person changes in sexual satisfaction and intercourse frequency were associated with relationship desire among never-married men and women. Using all fourteen waves of the German Panel Analysis of Intimate Relationships and Family Dynamics (Pairfam), individual fixed-effects models linked change between successive waves to relationship desire at the later wave. Increases in sexual satisfaction were associated with lower relationship desire for men (b = (cid:0) 0.024, p < .001) and women (b = (cid:0) 0.026, p < .001), with no significant sex difference. Changes in intercourse frequency were not significantly associated with relationship desire in either sex. From an evolutionary perspective, these findings are consistent with relationship motivation being calibrated to cues about the benefits of long-term pair-bonding relative to other mating opportunities. Greater sexual satisfaction while single may indicate that some mating benefits are obtainable without commitment, whereas sexual frequency appears to provide a less consistent cue.

Enhancing feasibility of cost-optimal energy systems in surrogate-assisted design optimization
papers.abstract: Energy system design optimization often incurs high computational cost, which limits applications such as uncertainty analysis and interactive decision support. Surrogate models reduce this cost by emulating expensive original models. In surrogate-assisted design optimization (SADO), an upper-level optimization algorithm searches over designs while surrogate models emulate operational optimizations to evaluate each design. Existing SADO studies rarely enforce feasibility, defined here as the ability of an energy system to satisfy all demand constraints.This study quantifies how the choice of a feasibility predictor influences the cost and feasibility of designs obtained from SADO applied to a convex energy system model. We compare three feasibility predictors: two artificial neural networks and a convex hull predictor that classifies feasibility by membership in a feasible input space. We embed each predictor into SADO and evaluate predicted designs by their cost and feasibility when re-evaluated in the operational optimization.The results show that the feasibility predictor strongly affects both cost and feasibility of designs. SADO with neural-network-based feasibility predictors achieves feasible designs consistently only if oversizing is enforced. In contrast, SADO with the convex hull predictor yields guaranteed feasible designs by construction and produces designs whose objective values are typically within 2 % of the cost-optimal solution. This improved feasibility comes at the expense of increased computational cost compared to neural-network-based feasibility predictors. Overall, these results establish feasibility prediction as a critical design choice in SADO and identify geometric feasibility predictors as robust alternatives to data-driven surrogate models for convex energy system models.

UNCASExt – A systematic computational framework for uncertainty propagation and scope consistency in absolute environmental sustainability assessments (AESA)
papers.abstract: Absolute environmental sustainability assessment (AESA) has gained increasing attention in environmental research and policymaking. However, its reliability is challenged by several sources of uncertainty that remain insufficiently accounted for, as well as by scope inconsistencies within the absolute sustainability ratio (ASR), which compares estimated environmental burdens with allocated carrying capacities for a given human activity. This work introduces UNCASExt, an extension of the UNCASE framework for systematically propagating uncertainty and ensuring scope consistency in AESA, together with a supporting open-source Python package, pyaesa. At country and sector levels, the computational framework formalizes allocation procedures that match the scope of allocated carrying capacities with that of estimated environmental burdens across three dimensions: impact pathway modeling; production-based versus consumption-based accounting; business-to-consumer versus business-to-business activities. It also incorporates temporal dynamics, supporting both retrospective and prospective assessments with either static steady-state or dynamic carrying capacities, including greenhouse gas budgets from the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change Sixth Assessment Report under Shared Socioeconomic Pathway transition scenarios. The framework is applied to a case study of electricity consumption in France over the period 2019 to 2060. The results show that mismatches between the functional units of estimated environmental burdens and allocated carrying capacities can lead to substantial underallocation, with a median factor of 4.6x across all available sector-region pairs in EXIOBASE 3.10.2. Overall, UNCASExt and pyaesa provide a scalable solution to support AESA harmonization and a versatile way forward to bridge the gap between methodological guidelines and practical application.

Agroforestry development drives a progressive shift from physicochemical to microbially mediated organic matter cycling in tropical soils
papers.abstract: Land-use change in tropical soils alters dissolved organic matter (DOM) chemistry and carbon cycling, however, linkages to microbial functions remain unresolved. We tested whether microbial carbon-degradation potential is associated with DOM composition along an Amazonian agroforestry chronosequence (10, 20, and 30 years), using adjacent pasture and primary forest as references. We integrated shotgun metagenomics with high-resolution mass spectrometry to couple carbohydrate-active enzyme (CAZymes) profiles to DOM composition. Soil chemistry explained 41.6% of the variability in microbial composition, while land-use type accounted for 28.5% of DOM variability. Seasonality did not affect microbial composition but was a significant source of variation in DOM. Relative to pasture, agroforests showed higher potential for sucrose and α-glucan degradation and a greater abundance of aliphatic DOM, indicating enhanced microbial processing. Older agroforests were enriched in genes targeting lignin and microbial-derived substrates such as peptidoglycan, resembling primary forest, whereas younger agroforests had higher abundances of GH36, GH5, and CE3 genes linked to cellulose and hemicellulose degradation, resembling pasture. Soil pH and available P were marginally associated with microbial-derived compound degradation, while pH, P, and Ca showed a stronger association with plant-derived compound processing. These results suggest that as agroforestry develops, carbon cycling may shift from physicochemical to microbial regulation, while DOM remained related to vegetation inputs and seasonality. Soil management of pH and available P during early establishment could support this transition, but the recovery may take decades.
