papers.title: Standard setters’ use of qualitative characteristics in fair value standards: a Derridean analysis
papers.abstract: Qualitative characteristics (QCs) are accounting concepts stated in standard setters' conceptual frameworks, which are intended to guide their standard-setting decisions. This paper explores how the FASB and IASC/IASB used their primary QCs (relevance, reliability and faithful representation) in their fair value standards. Drawing on Derrida's notion of iterability, we analyse how and why these QCs were reiterated in different contexts to promote, defend and retreat from fair value. Our findings show that QCs are not fixed concepts, but rather evolve through reiteration across different standard-setting contexts. This malleability enables the Boards to justify standard-setting decisions as their preferences evolve. Our research contributes to the literature on conceptual frameworks by identifying the flexible use of QCs in standard setting as a subtle mode of standard setters' legitimacy work, while also showing that these reiterations shape, and sometimes subsequently reverse, revisions of conceptual frameworks. Ultimately, we reveal that neither conceptual frameworks nor standards act as fixed reference points for the meanings of QCs, which are mutually deferred in an endless process of reiteration.

papers.title: Algorithmic justice in AI-driven human resource management: Implications for workplace well-being and affective commitment
papers.abstract: Human resource functions are increasingly mediated, and sometimes directly governed, by algorithmic systems, yet little is known about how employees’ fairness perceptions of these systems relate to their workplace well-being and affective commitment. Drawing on organizational justice and social exchange theories and survey data from 307 employees in the Australian financial and insurance sector, we establish algorithmic human resource management (AHRM) justice as a multidimensional construct comprising distributive, procedural, interpersonal, and informational justice. We argue that AHRM does not simply place these dimensions in a new context but reconfigures the social exchange conditions under which justice perceptions form. AHRM justice was positively associated with workplace well-being and, both directly and indirectly through well-being, with affective commitment; informational justice emerged as particularly salient. Self-perceived AI understanding did not moderate these relationships. The findings extend the ensemble view of algorithmic HRM and support a human-centric approach to AI-driven people management.

papers.title: Restoring legitimacy under resource constraints: The impact of data breaches on corporate social responsibility
Enhancing or Transcending the Pipeline? How Incumbents Transition Toward Marketplace Platforms
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Business‐to‐business incumbents whose value creation rests on pipeline business models increasingly launch their own marketplace platforms. Yet how these business model transitions toward marketplace platforms unfold, and what they imply for the pipeline model, remains poorly understood. Adopting a cognitive perspective on managerial interpretations and decisions, we conduct a comparative case study of five marketplace platforms launched by incumbents in the European industrial products industry. We find that platform competition and the opportunities managers perceive in business‐to‐consumer platforms trigger platform creation, after which incumbents follow one of two pathways. In pipeline‐enhancing transitions, managers locate future value in the existing pipeline model and adopt platform features that strengthen it, resulting in cognitive alignment and interconnected platform–pipeline business models. In pipeline‐transcending transitions, managers locate future value in the marketplace platform and use business‐to‐consumer marketplaces as a reference point. This generates cognitive tensions with the pipeline model that ultimately resolve into independent pipeline and marketplace platform business models. Which pathway unfolds depends on the customer segments served, which shape managers' reference points for interpreting the evolving platform business model. Our process model explains these divergent outcomes and contributes to innovation management research on business model transitions toward platforms and their cognitive dynamics.

papers.title: Orchestrating inter-organizational technology networks to build data analytics capability: the case of a professional service firm
papers.abstract: Purpose This study examines how professional service firms (PSFs) orchestrate inter-organizational technology networks to develop data analytics capability. Adopting an organizational information processing perspective, we examine how PSFs vary orchestration modes across networks to mobilize distributed resources and increase their information-processing capacity. Design/methodology/approach We conducted a longitudinal single-case study of a global PSF in the UK construction sector, triangulating 37 interviews with observations and project documentation. Using an abductive theory-elaboration approach, we explain how the PSF accessed, bundled and leveraged network-embedded resources to build analytics capability. Findings We identify three interrelated components of analytics capability: data capture, data transformation and processing, and data visualization and interpretation. Closed-mode orchestration enabled standardized data capture across the supply network; hybrid orchestration combined broad open engagement with selective closure to integrate technological expertise from SMEs; and open-mode orchestration within the client network fostered use-case elicitation, sensemaking and interpretive alignment. We theorize how inter-organizational network orchestration enables PSFs to assemble information-processing capacity from distributed data, technical expertise and interpretive requirements, thereby improving fit between information-processing needs and capacity. Originality/value We conceptualize analytics capability as a composite inter-organizational capability assembled across organizational boundaries. We extend Organizational information processing theory by showing how information-processing capacity can be assembled across networks of external actors through inter-organizational network orchestration, and advance network orchestration research by identifying a contingency logic linking orchestration mode to the coordination conditions surrounding distributed resources.
papers.journal_name: International Journal of Operations & Production Management

papers.title: The Organizational Benefits of Neurodiversity: A Strategic Human Capital–Based Systematic Review and Research Agenda
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT There is growing interest in neurodiversity across multiple research domains, including human resource management (HRM). Within HRM research, discussions of neurodiversity have increasingly extended beyond inclusion as an ethical concern to raise questions about potential organizational benefits. However, there is limited clarity regarding how such benefits have been examined within the HRM literature. This paper addresses this issue through a strategic human capital–informed systematic review of 88 studies on HRM and neurodiversity. Our findings show that existing research provides a growing body of insights into potential organizational benefits. However, empirical evidence at the organizational level remains limited and uneven. Building on these findings, we propose a future research agenda focused on the organizational value of human capital associated with neurodivergence and the processes through which such value emerges, highlighting the need for more quantitative studies assessing organizational‐level outcomes and qualitative research unpacking emergence processes. We further develop an extended emergence perspective by showing how the recognition, creation, and realization of value shape the transformation of neurodivergent individual capacities into organizational‐level human capital resources. In doing so, the paper contributes to strategic human capital theory by offering a structured framework for understanding emergence processes, while highlighting neurodiversity as a particularly informative context for examining the conditions under which they occur.

papers.title: How economic policy uncertainty spreads across borders: The case of Latin America
papers.abstract: Latin America’s growth has been hindered by institutional instability and volatile economic policies, often driven by political cycles. These shifts generate uncertainty that deters investment and disrupts productivity. We analyze this phenomenon using Economic Policy Uncertainty (EPU) indices, assessing their impact on domestic macroeconomic variables via regional spillovers - spurred by regional proximity - and also considering the global transmission of EPU shocks to key trade and financial partners. To do so, we assemble a comprehensive and comparable database of EPU indices for the region: first, we construct new indices for Bolivia, Ecuador, Paraguay, Uruguay and Venezuela, and second, we update the ones available in other papers for Argentina, Brazil, Chile, Colombia, Mexico and Peru using a comparable methodology. Our results show that: (i) regional EPU shocks reduce regional GDP growth, deter capital inflows and spark exchange rate instability; (ii) Brazil and Mexico are key sources of uncertainty spillovers within the region; and (iii) EPU shocks in Latin America affect financial and real variables in major partner economies, with Spain being particularly exposed.

papers.title: A heterogeneous-agent model for the latin american financial market
The Effect of Clients’ Financial Resources, Mental Health, and Motivation on Frontline Workers’ Burden Reduction and Prioritizations
papers.abstract: Abstract The street-level bureaucracy literature shows that frontline workers’ decisions about clients are shaped by perceptions of deservingness based on clients’ demographic characteristics and behavioral conduct. Yet, we know little about whether frontline workers also act on clients’ financial resources and mental health, despite the administrative burden literature identifying these two factors as central to how citizens experience compliance demands. We contribute to both literatures by developing and testing preregistered hypotheses that examine how information about clients’ financial resources and mental health shapes frontline workers’ burden reduction and client prioritization. To do this, we run a large-scale vignette experiment with 775 caseworkers across 39 Danish unemployment agencies, manipulating client age, financial situation, mental health, and motivation but holding gender constant (all clients were male). We find strong evidence that caseworkers reduce burdens and prioritize clients with mental health issues and–consistent with prior work–clients displaying high motivation, alongside some evidence for clients struggling with financial hardship. Importantly, mental health appears more consequential than motivation and financial resources. Contrary to our preregistered expectation, clients with mental health issues received the most support when they also displayed low as opposed to high motivation. Rather than indicating that frontline workers reward low motivation, this pattern most likely reflects that caseworkers interpret low motivation as a symptom of the underlying condition, and thus as a signal of greater need. Our findings show how frontline discretion can operate as a redistributive mechanism that channels support toward clients signaling the greatest need.
papers.journal_name: Journal of Public Administration Research and Theory

papers.title: Crossing the Design–Use Divide: How Organizations Select Innovations to Adopt
papers.abstract: Prior scholarship on technology and organizations has focused either on how innovations are designed or how they are used, often assuming that successful selection stems from successful design. But this assumption has limited our understanding of patterns of resistance and advocacy that can influence how and whether innovations reach organizations in the first place. To explore these patterns, this study asks, how does selection unfold within organizations, and what are the consequences of this process for the design and use of innovations? Drawing on a two-year ethnographic study, I examine how entrepreneurs piloted their AI-based innovations with potential adopting organizations. Rather than testing for learning or generalizability, organizations set up committees that engaged in process manipulation by narrowing the scope of pilots, controlling conversations, assigning pilot responsibility, and using goal claiming to align pilot outcomes with committees’ majority preferences. Committees with more adversarial members designed pilots that tested advanced aspects of entrepreneurs’ innovations, hoping for failure. Committees with a majority that championed the innovations tested basic aspects, ensuring success. While pilots run by champions mostly succeeded, these innovations faced more resistance later, during implementation, than did innovations piloted successfully by adversaries. This study shows that innovation is endogenous to selection, and reveals that champions can temper innovation, while adversaries can enable it.

papers.title: Organizational sensemaking and AI adoption in U.S. local governments
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly entering public administration, yet adoption across U.S. local governments remains uneven. Existing explanations emphasize structural capacity, expecting internal barriers to constrain adoption. Drawing on Weick’s sensemaking perspective as an interpretive lens, this study examines AI adoption as shaped by how organizations interpret technological opportunity and enact deliberate responses. Using the 2024 ICMA Artificial Intelligence Survey, this study tests whether internal barriers, AI potential, and organizational initiative explain variation in adoption. Findings show that internal barriers are not significantly associated with adoption, whereas AI potential and organizational initiative are positively associated with it. These findings suggest that in equivocal technological contexts, structural conditions operate through interpretive processes, and that what organizations possess shapes adoption through how they make sense of emerging technologies and mobilize action. This study demonstrates the analytical value of sensemaking as a framework for understanding public sector responses to technological change.

papers.title: Resolving institutional fragmentation in a multilevel governance system: configurational logics of social health insurance integration in China
papers.abstract: Institutional fragmentation poses a significant challenge to effective social governance, particularly in the health sector. Prevailing literature often examines the drivers of integration – such as fiscal capacity and political will – in a linear, isolated manner, failing to capture their complex interplay. This study argues for a configurational approach to understanding institutional integration. Using the integration of China’s fragmented social health insurance system as a critical case, we employ fuzzy-set Qualitative Comparative Analysis (fsQCA) to analyse a large sample of 251 cities in their varying integration pathways. The analytical framework captures capacity and incentives as critical factors for institutional integration. The QCA analysis identifies four distinct configurations: the Capacitor, the Stabilizer, the Risk Manager, and the Negotiator. These findings suggest multiple equifinal pathways to successful institutional integration, highlighting the crucial conjunctural effects of economic strength, administrative status, coordinative capacity, and financial conditions.

papers.title: When negative control exposures fail to detect bias
papers.abstract: Abstract Researchers increasingly utilize negative control exposures (NCEs), variables known to have no effect on the outcome, to detect residual confounding. However, an NCE analysis may provide little evidence of confounding despite substantial bias in the estimated exposure effect. We study, analytically and via simulations, how the magnitude and source of exposure-NCE association affect the large-sample NCE coefficient and statistical power of regression-based bias-detection. We show that the power does not always increase with bias, and that stronger confounder-exposure associations can increase bias while reducing the NCE coefficient and power. Furthermore, the correlation between the exposure of interest and the NCE is insufficient to characterize how well the NCE will detect confounding. Additional exposure-NCE common causes that affect the outcome only through the exposure can attenuate the NCE coefficient toward zero or reverse its sign, even when confounding bias remains unchanged. These changes can occur even when the overall exposure-NCE correlation is fixed. Adjusting for such common causes alleviated sign reversal in our simulations but did not uniformly improve power. Negative controls can be a powerful tool to detect unmeasured confounding. Researchers should consider the sources of exposure-NCE association and interpret null or counterintuitive NCE findings with caution.

papers.title: Prevention of mpox by JYNNEOS vaccination: a case-control study comparing test-negative and alternative-disease control populations
papers.abstract: Abstract Risk-based vaccine recommendations complicate observational studies of vaccine effectiveness (VE), since recipients and non-recipients may differ in infection risk and likelihood of testing. For JYNNEOS—recommended for men who have sex with men at high mpox risk—prior studies have used differing control populations to estimate VE, with uncertain comparability. We conducted a multi-armed case-control study enrolling mpox cases (N=198), monkeypox virus (MPXV)-negative controls (N=208), and gonorrhea controls (N=155) reported to the California Department of Public Health between November 2022 and October 2024, conducting telephone interviews to capture behavioral risk data typically absent from surveillance and administrative records. Among recipients of 2 pre-exposure JYNNEOS doses, adjusted VE was 89.9% (95% CI, 69.6–96.7%) versus test-negative controls and 92.0% (70.6–97.8%) versus gonorrhea controls. Without behavioral adjustment, however, VE estimates using MPXV-negative controls were lower (50.4–65.4%) than those using gonorrhea controls (61.3–71.3%). Controls diagnosed with an alternative sexually transmitted infection may offer a better comparison group than test-negative controls for JYNNEOS VE studies based on disease surveillance or administrative records, although collection of risk factor data may be necessary to mitigate bias under either design.

papers.title: Why some emergency maneuvers succeed: Interpretable behavior graphs from expert drivers to automated control
The impact of an attorney guardian ad litem program on case disposition and custody agreements in domestic violence protective order cases
Effectiveness of school-based interventions in preventing violence against girls in low- and middle-income countries: Systematic review
papers.abstract: Background Violence against girls remains a major public health challenge in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), and schools represent a critical platform for primary prevention. Objective To review the effectiveness of school-based interventions for preventing violence against girls in LMICs systematically. Methods Seven databases were searched from inception to April 5, 2025, supplemented by grey literature searches. Eligible studies were intervention trials or longitudinal observational studies with a control arm in LMICs reporting sex-disaggregated outcomes for school-based interventions targeting physical, sexual, emotional violence, bullying and cyberbullying against girls. Heterogeneity precluded meta-analysis; narrative synthesis and vote counting based on direction of effect were conducted. The review is registered with the Open Science Framework. Results Twenty-seven articles reporting 29 interventions met the inclusion criteria: 11 curriculum-based, seven multilevel, six single-component, and five multicomponent interventions. Evidence from curriculum-based empowerment self-defence programmes indicated the most consistent favourable effects on sexual violence victimisation. By contrast, multicomponent and multilevel interventions had broader but more heterogeneous potential to prevent victimisation and perpetration. Across intervention types, effects on bullying were predominantly favourable direction. Measurement of victimisation and perpetration was unbalanced, with sexual violence perpetration substantially underrepresented. No eligible studies were identified from the Central Africa, Caribbean, or Pacific Island countries. Conclusions School-based interventions show potential to reduce violence against girls, with curriculum-based approaches offering the most consistent short-term benefits in preventing sexual violence victimisation. Effectiveness of multilevel and multicomponent interventions remains heterogeneous, and evidence on sustainability and scalability is limited across intervention types.

papers.title: The Art of Masturbation: An Analysis on the History and Theory of Self-Pleasure in the Renaissance
Measurement Invariance and Prevalence of Sexual Harassment Among University Students in Jordan
Assessing the Role of Board, Culture and Environmental Complexity on Performance Information Use in Nonprofit Organizations
papers.abstract: Despite growing expectations for Nonprofit Organizations to implement performance measurement, empirical research on its actual use remains limited. To address such a gap, this study investigates the decision-facilitating use of performance information focusing on environmental complexities, the role of the board of directors, and organizational culture. The empirical setting is provided by Nonprofit Organizations located in the province of Bergamo (Italy) to which a survey was administered. The analysis shows that environmental complexity does not directly increase the use of performance information. Rather, it operates indirectly through an externally oriented board and a flexible culture, both serving as bridges that connect external pressures to internal systems.

papers.title: Emulate the Leader? Explaining Crisis Policy Change in the Canadian Federal System
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT In times of crises, do governments coordinate or do they make their own choices independent of what others do? Convergence of COVID‐19 policy at the beginning of the pandemic has been widely studied in federal countries. Yet, there is limited literature looking at the mechanisms that made policy between jurisdictions so similar. Utilizing Canada's decentralized federal system, this paper posits that convergence can be explained by a process of policy diffusion through emulation and a series of leader‐follower relationships. Drawing on the policy diffusion literature, this paper proposes three hypotheses for why some jurisdictions take on leadership roles in crisis policy while others follow. Synthesized as proximity, capacity, and urgency, these hypotheses are tested using a series of pairwise vector autoregressions identifying significant leader‐follower relationships between Canadian provinces. The findings suggest that policy primarily flowed from only a small number of large provinces (Quebec and Ontario), lending partial evidence, but also exceptions to the hypotheses proposed.

papers.title: Application of the template methods in nano-structural design of proton exchange membranes for fuel cells and water electrolyzers
When does on-site renewable hydrogen pay off? Vehicle-gate co-design of an ALK/PEM multi-electrolyzer system under alkaline electrolyzer cycling limits
Cell-to-cell thermal and capacity fade progression in lithium-ion battery pack under fast and conventional charging
A tailored exact column generation method for China's large-scale inter-provincial path-based market clearing: Decomposition, optimality, and scalability
Compound effects of traffic and climate on electric vehicle HVAC energy consumption: a spatiotemporal framework with city-level attribution
papers.abstract: Electric vehicle (EV) energy consumption in real-world driving departs significantly from rated values due to the joint influence of ambient temperature, traffic congestion, and route characteristics. Existing studies typically evaluate these factors in isolation or under static conditions, leaving their compound effect on HVAC energy unquantified. This study develops a spatiotemporal simulation framework that couples traffic-aware driving speed, location- and time-specific ambient temperature, and physics-based energy submodels (cabin HVAC, traction, and battery thermal management) at the segment level, and decomposes HVAC energy variability into its temperature and trip-duration components per route. The framework is applied through a structured comparative design across seven UK cities and eight radial routes, varying departure time, regional climate, and road-network type. While total energy consumption varies by 14% across cities, the HVAC component varies by up to 89%, identifying cabin thermal management as the primary differentiator between routes in winter. The decomposition attributes 79–85% of London’s above-average HVAC energy to its extended trip duration rather than to temperature, the range reflecting how the temperature–time interaction is allocated; a same-route counterfactual shows that departure-time congestion accounts for about half of this excess duration and the network’s typical operating speed for the remainder. These attributions are robust to temperature, parameter, and correlated stochastic uncertainties, and the inter-city spread collapses in summer as heating demand vanishes. The decomposition yields a closed-form model estimating HVAC energy from three inputs (ambient temperature, average speed, and trip distance) with physical interpretability and negligible computational cost. Demonstrated for a heat-pump vehicle under UK winter conditions, the framework transfers to other vehicles and regions by re-fitting three coefficients, although the dominance of trip duration is specific to the narrow temperature range and high congestion studied. These findings indicate that the energy intensity of real-world EV operation, and hence achievable range, is substantially shaped by traffic and road-network characteristics.

papers.title: Co-generation of energy and data for hyperscale data center based on distributionally robust CVaR framework
Security-oriented optimization method for enhancing resilient operation of urban integrated energy cyber-physical system
Conservation governance challenges in the Karakoram: Analyzing the institutional transitions of Central Karakoram National Park, Pakistan
papers.abstract: Global commitments to conserve 30% of land by 2030 place renewed emphasis on protected areas (PAs), yet governance shortcomings and distributional conflicts often undermine both conservation and socio-economic development outcomes. This paper examines PA governance in Central Karakoram National Park (CKNP), Pakistan’s largest national park in Gilgit-Baltistan (GB), a region marked by constitutional ambiguity, contested land tenure, and infrastructure-driven market integration. Using a historical institutionalist lens, we examine CKNP’s historical trajectories and critical junctures, institutional continuity and change, input and output legitimacy, and implications for co-management. We combine archival and institutional analysis of legislation and management plans with field observations, semi-structured interviews and focus group discussions involving state agencies, park authorities, NGOs, and local communities in seven buffer-zone valleys. We find that administrative reforms and departmental restructuring shifted conservation authority to GB, while participatory, zoning, sustainable-use, and benefit-sharing provisions were layered onto a centralized, exclusionary 1975 legal framework. Input legitimacy remains constrained by uneven consultation, limited decision-making influence, and inadequate information for meaningful participation, whereas output legitimacy is weakened by limited implementation capacity associated with chronic understaffing, project dependence, and limited public financing. Dispersed implementation responsibilities and unresolved property and access rights concerns undermine both decision-making processes and governance performance, leaving co-management largely consultative and uneven. We conclude that co-management could be advanced through valley-level forums with clear decision-making mandates and representation, strengthened and trusted field staffing, sustained public resourcing, and transparent and equitable benefit-sharing. The study highlights how frontier conditions, historical institutional legacies, and valley-specific dynamics shape PA governance.

papers.title: Harnessing wind energy for rural development: the state-orchestrated approach to realizing community energy in rural China
Wind energy acceptance and forest owners’ land-leasing intentions: The role of beliefs and attitudes
papers.abstract: The expansion of wind power plays a crucial role in the European Union's decarbonization strategy. However, the social acceptance of wind power projects, particularly among landowners and non-landowners, remains a significant concern. Drawing on behavioural insights of the social acceptance literature, this study examines the beliefs, attitudes, and behavioural intentions of these groups towards wind power. We focus on the national context of Finland, where wind energy development has accelerated in recent years. Utilizing survey data from 2,103 respondents, including forest owners and non-forest owners, the study employs Structural Equation Modelling (SEM) and regression models to explore how beliefs shape attitudes, policy support and forest owners' behavioural intentions. The acceptance measures indicate that non-forest owners held more favourable attitudes towards wind power, associating it with environmental benefits and economic opportunities, while forest owners expressed greater concerns about landscape changes, land ownership, and economic impacts. The SEM model reveals that attitudes toward wind power were strongly influenced by beliefs about energy production and local impacts, which, in turn, shaped policy support. Additionally, forest owners’ willingness to lease land for wind turbines was associated with higher income level, owned land area size, and positive attitudes towards wind power. These findings highlight the need for tailored landscape-orientated policies that address explicitly address landowners’ concerns while fostering broader societal support for wind power. Enhancing procedural and distributive justice, improving compensation mechanisms, and integrating participatory planning processes could help accommodate resistance and facilitate a just energy transition.

papers.title: Is inclusive green growth resilient to energy-related geopolitical risk? The role of energy affordability as a binding constraint
Embodied transfers and driving factors of production-based natural gas consumption in China from the perspective of industrial linkages: An extended input-output analysis
Hydrometallurgical recycling of end-of-life photovoltaic modules and lithium-ion batteries
Spatio-temporal clusters of sugarcane bioelectricity in Brazil: Regional patterns and low-carbon transition pathways
Consumer engagement in the circular economy: An analysis of repair behaviours of irish consumers using survey data
Delphi-based scenarios for circular production and consumption systems in Brazil: Navigating between the highway to hell and the stairway to heaven
Highly Selective Lithium Extraction from Shale Gas Wastewater Using Al- and F-Doped LiMn2O4 Electrode in Rocking-Chair Capacitive Deionization
papers.abstract: Abstract Selective lithium extraction from shale gas wastewater (SGW) offers a promising strategy to expand lithium supply while reducing wastewater-management burdens. However, low Li+ concentrations and overwhelming competition from Na+ and Mg2+ make selective and energy-efficient extraction challenging. Lithium manganese oxide (LMO) is attractive for electrochemical Li extraction but remains limited by insufficient cycling stability and selectivity in complex ionic matrices. Here, we investigate the effects of Al and F modification of LMO on lithium extraction in a rocking-chair capacitive deionization system. Structural and spectroscopic characterizations show that the optimized modification contracts the spinel lattice and produces near-surface enrichment of F-containing species, improving electrochemical reversibility. Electrochemical analyses and density functional theory calculations further indicate favorable Li+ transport and stronger migration restrictions for Na+ and Mg2+ after lattice entry. In a simulated SGW matrix with a Li/Na/Mg molar ratio of 1:100:1, LMO-Al-F achieves a Li adsorption capacity of 9.54 mg g–1, Li/Na and Li/Mg separation factors of 2216 and 1509, and an energy consumption of 4.21 Wh mol–1 Li. Strong Li selectivity is also maintained in real SGW. After 100 competitive-ion cycles, 78% of adsorption capacity is retained, supporting repeated Li-selective extraction under high-salinity conditions.

papers.title: Water Footprint and Scarcity Risks of Low-Carbon Fuels
papers.abstract: Abstract Production of ammonia, methanol, and hydrogen is key to decarbonizing hard-to-electrify sectors but is also water-intensive. However, the water implications of scaling these energy carriers under low-carbon pathways remain poorly understood. Here, we integrate direct water consumption with facility-level geospatial analysis and hydrological modeling to quantify water-scarcity exposure across each production facility in North America. Low-carbon production routes require more direct and indirect water consumption than conventional pathways, with electrolytic hydrogen and e-methanol increasing water-intensity by up to 5-fold in regions with limited renewable availability─a trade-off further amplified by supply chain effects, particularly for solar PV-based electricity and direct air capture-based CO2 feedstocks. Water scarcity already affects about 58% of methanol production in Mexico, 2% of ammonia production in the U.S., and 5% and 27% of refinery production in the U.S. and Mexico, respectively. Under midcentury climate scenarios, exposure increases in both magnitude and spatial extent. Although irrigation accounts for over 80% of local water consumption in various fuel production facilities, municipalities and manufacturing often exert the greatest pressure on low-carbon fuel production, depending on the product and country.. These results demonstrate that technology choice, system design, and facility siting are as important as hydrology considerations in determining water risks. Incorporating water availability in low-carbon fuel projects is therefore essential to ensure that decarbonization pathways are scalable, operationally resilient, and truly sustainable.

papers.title: Calibration of Passive Sampling Eyewear to Assess Inhalation Exposure
papers.abstract: Abstract Calibrated wearable passive air samplers are critical tools for accessibly quantifying individualized and population exposures to airborne pollution, a leading cause of chronic disease. Our lab recently introduced passive sampling eyewear (PSE) to address gaps in tools tailored for measuring and mitigating risks from inhalation exposure. The PSE, like most existing designs of wearable samplers, is largely uncalibrated. An exception is the polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) brooch, and mini-polyurethane foam (PUF) samplers, which have been calibrated for only 27 compounds. Here, we calibrate PSE against active air samplers codeployed in both stationary and wearable forms in office and home environments to capture a wide range of exposure scenarios. We report sampling rates (RS) and inhalation exposure for over 200 features covering diverse physical-chemical properties measured using the Orbitrap gas chromatography coupled to mass spectrometry (GC–MS) system in both targeted and nontargeted modes. RS were 0.70 ± 0.62 m3 day–1 dm–2 for stationary and 0.85 ± 0.68 m3 day–1 dm–2 for wearable deployments, with no significant difference (p = 0.06) between the deployment types. Wearable calibration captured higher RS and variability, as expected for personal sampling, because participants’ movement and daily activity can alter airflow and disrupt the stagnant air-boundary layer around the sampler. In terms of analysis mode, RS derived from targeted and nontargeted analysis (NTA) were reasonably comparable for a given compound, differing by ∼1.5-fold, boosting confidence in using NTA approaches for expanding databases of RS. Applying the wearable RS, the profiles and levels of inhalation exposure varied widely between participants when at home versus in offices, reflecting differences in exposure sources and dynamics between the two environments. Overall, the findings from both the calibration and field studies represent a significant step toward quantitatively assessing inhalation exposure using PSE.

papers.title: Atmospheric Aging Modifies the Toxicological Profile of Biomass Burning Particles in Epithelial Lung Cells
papers.abstract: Abstract Wildfire activity and associated smoke emissions are increasing globally, leading to widespread exposure to biomass burning particulate matter (PM). Although people are mainly exposed to aged wildfire smoke rather than fresh emissions, the effects of atmospheric aging on wildfire particulate toxicity remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated how atmospheric processing (“aging”) modifies biological effects of biomass burning particles (BBPs) generated under controlled flaming and smoldering combustion conditions. BB emissions were produced in the Photochemical Large Aerosol Chamber (PHOTO-LAC) and aged under alternating photochemical and dark conditions. Fresh and aged BBP extracts were subsequently sampled and tested in human bronchial epithelial cells (BEAS-2B). We assessed cytotoxicity, oxidative stress, oxidative DNA damage, genome-wide transcriptional responses, and inflammatory and extracellular matrix-related protein expression. Atmospheric aging substantially altered BBP toxicity in a combustion-dependent manner. Aged BBP enhanced intracellular reactive oxygen species formation and oxidative DNA damage, particularly for smoldering emissions, while cytotoxicity remained largely unchanged. In contrast, inflammatory and matrix-remodeling responses were attenuated with aging in smoldering particles but remained stable for flaming BBP. These findings demonstrate that atmospheric aging can simultaneously amplify oxidative and genotoxic stress while dampening inflammatory signaling, underscoring the need to incorporate aging state into health risk assessments of wildfire smoke exposure.

papers.title: Coupled Geophysical and Technoeconomic Industrial Growth Constraints on Geological Carbon Storage Scale-Up: Application to UK Offshore Resources
papers.abstract: Abstract Geological carbon dioxide storage is central to meeting many national climate change commitments, but large-scale deployment may be limited by both techno-economic rates of growth and physics-based processes imposed by subsurface geology. We develop a modeling framework for the assessment of feasible CO2 storage scale-up trajectories that unifies constraints arising from industrial rates of growth, dynamic injection rate limits from reservoir pressurization, and static maximum cumulative storage resource. We employ logistic and Gompertz models to represent policy-compliant deployment trajectories, parametrized by the total cumulative storage resource. We then use a simplified physics model to estimate the resulting regional subsurface pressurization along these trajectories. Growth curves where reservoir pressurization exceeds safe limits are updated by reducing the static storage resource until residing in the safe deployment range. The result is both a growth trajectory and static storage resource achievable subject to injectivity limits. Applying the framework to the United Kingdom (UK), we find that offshore storage resources are sufficient to accommodate all government midcentury deployment rate scenarios up to 175 Mt yr–1. Cumulative storage of up to 78 Gt, representing a reference estimate of the UK storage resource base used in national planning, can be achieved under Gompertz growth trajectories. The more aggressive logistic trajectories are constrained by reservoir pressure, limiting the achievable resource base to 69 Gt. The framework is transferable to other regions to assess the feasibility of policy-driven CO2 storage pathways under coupled industrial growth and geophysical constraints, informing national decarbonization planning and global integrated assessment models.

papers.title: Fingerprints of Airborne Plastics in Urban PM2.5: Applications and Implications
papers.abstract: Abstract To better identify emission sources of airborne plastics, we employed nine plastic-associated chemicals (PlsACs) in 240 daily PM2.5 samples collected in Singapore during 2018–2020. A unique PlsAC, tris(2,4-ditert-butylphenyl) phosphate (I168O), is most abundant, accounting for 90% of the total quantified PlsACs and identifying at least 40% more PM2.5 linked to respirable airborne PlsACs. A newly resolved source of plastic production, use, and burning (PlasticPub) accounts for the highest fraction (37%) of the quantified PlsACs among the seven apportioned PM2.5 sources. Nearly all di-iso-butyl phthalate (DIBP) and more than half of di-n-butyl phthalate (DNBP) are attributed to two factors of Background and Marine aerosols, indicating their potential worldwide transport. More than 90% of diethyl phthalate (DEP) is associated with transported peat forest (PF) burning smoke, demonstrating involvement of anthropogenic activities. Following PlasticPub, Traffic & road dust is the second predominant source responsible for >20% of the near-range PlsACs and featured with a DNBP/di-2-ethylhexyl phthalate (DEHP) concentration ratio of 2.2. The DNBP/DEHP concentration ratio higher than 1 can indicate nonexhaust emissions from on-road traffic due to abrasion of tires, brakes, and road markings. The average enrichment ratio of quantified PlsACs within PM2.5 (ng PlsACs per μg PM2.5) for each resolved source provides a basis for assessing strategies to cocontrol airborne plastics and PM2.5.

papers.title: Free-Radical Cascade Mediates Humus Formation in Mineral-Rich Organic Matrices
papers.abstract: Abstract Humus formation in nature is traditionally viewed as a lengthy microbial enzymatic process, yet the abiotic pathways remain unclear. Here, by employing iron-mineral-rich composting as a model system that amplifies and accelerates natural humification, we reveal a free-radical cascade that drives abiotic humification. Magnetite addition amplified hydroxyl radical (•OH) production 1.5-fold (1289.4 μmol·kg–1) and enriched humus precursors (amino acids, polyphenols, reducing sugars), ultimately yielding 1.5 times more humic acid (135.6 mg/g) with higher molecular weight and stronger aromatic condensation. Mass spectrometry combined with density functional theory calculations identified multiple environmentally persistent free radicals (EPFRs), including semiquinone and phenoxy radicals as key intermediates that couple precursors into macromolecular humus. Simulated transformation experiments with selective microbial inactivation and •OH scavenging demonstrated that the abiotic radical pathway contributed approximately 33.4% to humus formation. We propose a free-radical cascade: •OH-driven oxidative fragmentation of organic matter followed by EPFR-mediated humus precursors coupling. These findings establish an unrecognized abiotic dimension of humification, reshaping our mechanistic understanding of organic carbon stabilization and offering nature-based strategies for soil carbon sequestration and remediation in organic-mineral interaction environments.

papers.title: Context-Aware Multitask Learning for Aquatic and Soil Ecotoxicity Prediction from Fragmented ECOTOX Records
papers.abstract: Abstract Large ecotoxicity databases contain extensive evidence, yet heterogeneous reporting and sparse coverage across chemicals, species, end points, and conditions limit predictive use. From relational U.S. EPA ECOTOX, we linked 1,234,077 traceable records and constructed model-ready aquatic and soil data sets of 219,818 and 11,532 records. We developed a context-aware multitask model that preserves end point-specific responses while sharing information across molecular, biological, and experimental contexts. On held-out condition keys and parent-species-task combinations, four-seed ensembles achieved pooled R2 of 0.758/0.751 for aquatic toxicity and 0.628/0.537 for soil toxicity. Compared with same-input single-task models, multitask fitting reduced soil task-macro mean absolute error (MAE) by 0.136/0.156 across 16 task heads; aquatic point estimates also favored sharing, although uncertainty across all aquatic task heads was not estimable. Under canonical-parent holdout, frozen shared representations reduced task-macro MAE by 0.170–0.180 in aquatic and 0.093–0.125 in soil tree models versus molecular-only inputs, indicating reusable predictive information. Multidimensional training support stratified parent-holdout errors, meeting prespecified criteria fully for soil and partially for aquatic predictions; benefits weakened under stronger structural separation. These results show model-ready ECOTOX data can support context-aware toxicity prediction across a sparse experimental matrix, helping prioritize informative measurements and providing a predictive evidence base for environmental hazard assessment.

papers.title: Modeling Decadal Organosulfates in Particulate Matter to Improve Estimations of Aerosol Hygroscopicity in the United States
papers.abstract: Abstract Organosulfates (OSs) can comprise a substantial fraction of secondary organic aerosol and exhibit significantly different hygroscopicity than inorganic sulfates, yet their spatiotemporal prevalence and climatic impacts remain poorly constrained because speciated measurements are sparse and common chemical transport models do not explicitly represent OS formation. This study develops a flexible and robust modeling framework to quantify isoprene-derived OS (iOS) concentrations and OS impacts on aerosol hygroscopicity (κ) across the contiguous United States (U.S.) for summers spanning 2013–2022. Using the Community Multiscale Air Quality (CMAQ) model with updated iOS chemistry, simulations reproduce Interagency Monitoring of Protected Visual Environments (IMPROVE) network-derived organosulfur and inorganic sulfate and agree with speciated iOS measurements from filter analyses. OS concentrations are elevated in the eastern U.S., with summertime mean values up to 0.51 μg m–3. OS formation produces a net 5.6% decrease in κ (direct OS contribution, +2.8%; indirect, −8.4% via sulfate reduction). We apply an interpretable machine-learning surrogate to identify predictive features associated with OS variability and enable efficient estimation without rerunning CMAQ. These results provide the first observation-validated, high-spatial-coverage OS reconstruction and nationwide quantification of OS-driven κ changes, underscoring the importance of representing OS formation and expanded observations to improve aerosol-cloud radiative effect assessments.

papers.title: Molecular Insights into a Precursor–Chlorine Trade-Off Governing Divergent Formation Pathways of PCDD/Fs and Emerging Cl-PAHs in Waste Cocombustion of Cellulose, PET, and PVC
papers.abstract: Abstract Co-combustion of industrial and municipal solid waste (ISW/MSW) is widely practiced, yet PCDD/Fs and emerging chlorinated polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (Cl-PAHs) formation under mixed-feedstock conditions remains poorly understood. Here, cellulose, polyethylene terephthalate (PET), and polyvinyl chloride (PVC) were combusted individually and cocombusted with MSW to elucidate how feedstock chemistry regulates chlorinated pollutant formation. Comprehensive mass-spectrometric profiling of target pollutants, aromatic precursors, and the top 50 combustion intermediates, combined with DFT calculations, revealed a precursor–chlorine trade-off governing pollutant formation. PET preferentially generated oxygenated aromatic intermediates, particularly dibenzofuran; PVC supplied the most PAHs and reactive chlorine, and cellulose primarily contributed carbon skeletons. Accordingly, two distinct pathways were proposed: dibenzofuran-centered, chlorination-limited formation of PCDD/Fs and stepwise aromatic growth followed by site-selective chlorination of Cl-PAHs. The higher HOMO energies of two representative PAHs, anthracene and phenanthrene, relative to dibenzofuran indicated their greater susceptibility to electrophilic chlorination. Consequently, Cl-PAHs exceeded PCDD/Fs by 1–3 orders of magnitude and accounted for 83.4% of estimated TEQ. Increasing chlorine availability alleviated the kinetic constraint on dibenzofuran chlorination, causing an approximately 42-fold increase in PCDD/F emissions at 20% PVC blending. These findings establish a molecular basis for feedstock-chemistry-guided management and broaden emission-control priorities from regulated PCDD/Fs to emerging Cl-PAHs.

papers.title: Hydrophilic Nanoisland Interface Engineering for Conquering Activity–Stability Trade-Off in High-Efficiency Salt Lake Lithium Extraction
papers.abstract: Abstract The adsorption-based lithium extraction technology from ultralow-grade salt lake brine is severely restricted by the inherent activity–stability trade-off of traditional granular Li/Al-LDHs adsorbents (GLDHs). Herein, a nanoisland encapsulation strategy integrated with hydrophilic interface engineering is developed to fabricate Li/Al-LDHs composite granules with tailored hydrophilic interfaces (HILDHs), breaking the long-standing bottleneck of conventional aluminum-based lithium adsorbents used in the salt lake industry. Systematic experiments and multiscale simulations reveal that the strong water affinity of polyacrylonitrile cyano groups (−C≡N) creates a highly hydrated microenvironment for rapid Li+ transport, while the nanoisland-confined structure anchors Li/Al-LDHs nanosheets to preserve the layered framework under harsh deep desorption conditions, thus enabling excellent cycling stability. The optimized HILDHs deliver a 3.02-fold higher working adsorption capacity (7.25 mg g–1 vs 2.40 mg g–1 for GLDHs) in actual Qarhan old brine within 60 min, along with a 13.36-fold increase in adsorption rate constant, 40% lower rinsing water consumption, and excellent cycle stability. It is calculated the nanoisland encapsulation strategy can achieve a nearly 5-fold increase for the annual Li2CO3 production capacity from salt lake lithium industrial lines.

papers.title: Polyethylene Terephthalate Oligomers in Disposable Diapers: Occurrence, Dermal Exposure and Health Assessment
papers.abstract: Abstract Disposable infant diapers commonly use multicomponent nonwoven fabrics containing polyethylene terephthalate (PET), from which PET oligomer byproducts may be released and transferred to infant skin. In this study, 6 cyclic PET oligomers (C[TPA+EG]2–7) were detected in the top sheets and absorbent cores of 37 disposable diapers. ∑C[TPA+EG]2–7 averaged 198 ± 98.7 μg/g (top sheets) and 66.6 ± 49.2 μg/g (absorbent cores), dominated by C[TPA+EG]3 (95.9% and 92.3%). Oligomer levels positively correlated with diaper PET content, confirming an in situ polymer source. During a 3-day in-use study, 1348–2318 ng of oligomers migrated to infant buttock skin and remained partially after water washing, corresponding to an estimated C[TPA+EG]3 exposure of 8.80–182 ng/kg BW/day. Network toxicology and molecular docking identified potential targets and pathways associated with local skin effects, including inflammation, barrier regulation, apoptosis, and extracellular matrix remodeling, suggesting potential local skin-health implications. Our results establish diaper dermal contact as a critical infant plastic oligomer exposure route and raise health concerns for vulnerable infant skin.

Spatiotemporal characteristics of water consumption induced by cooling and electricity use of data centers in China

Techno-economic and life cycle assessment of microalgae-derived sustainable aviation fuel with in-situ light hydrocarbon by-product reforming
Environmental and economic assessment of olefin synthesis from waste as an emerging alternative to conventional light olefin production routes
papers.abstract: Light olefins such as ethylene and propylene are essential petrochemical intermediates but remain highly energy- and carbon-intensive to produce using conventional fossil-based technologies. We conduct the life-cycle environmental and economic assessment (LCA/LCC) of seven olefin production pathways, such as coal-based, natural gas-based, shale gas-based, crude oil-based, bio-based, waste-to-olefins and waste-to-olefins with sorption-enhanced olefin synthesis, to understand trade-offs and identify decarbonisation opportunities. A cradle-to-gate LCA employs nine EF 3.1 midpoint indicators, using foreground data from industrial sources, Aspen Plus V14 modelling, and ecoinvent v3.10 inventories. Results show that coal-based olefin production exhibits the highest environmental burdens, particularly for climate change, freshwater ecotoxicity, eutrophication, and water use. Natural gas-based and crude oil-based routes perform better across non-climate categories but remain carbon-intensive. Bio-based olefin production route provides partial climate benefits but is penalised by large land and water requirements. In contrast, waste-to-olefins and waste-to-olefins with sorption-enhanced olefin synthesis achieve net-negative greenhouse gas emissions due to biogenic carbon uptake and integrated CO 2 capture. Sorption-enhanced olefin synthesis further reduces energy demand via in-situ water removal and process intensification, yielding lower GHG emissions (47%), reduced water use by 64%, and improved selectivity compared with conventional waste-to-olefin routes. However, higher impacts persist in ozone depletion and ionising radiation categories, driven by upstream electricity supply chains. Economic analysis indicates that gasification and CO 2 management dominate overall costs, while the sorption-enhanced synthesis adds only a modest incremental cost to waste-to-olefin pathways. Total life cycle costing for waste-to-olefins with sorption-enhanced olefin synthesis falls within EUR 2130 to 3550 t −1 olefin, including environmental cost, competitive with emerging green olefin pathways. Overall, the findings demonstrate that combining waste feedstocks, CO 2 capture, and sorption-enhanced process intensification offers a promising pathway for low-carbon, resource-efficient olefin production, especially within future decarbonised energy systems.

papers.title: From laboratory evidence to field-realized N2O mitigation by biochar: a global meta-analysis and mechanistic synthesis

Between symbols and substance: Voluntary impact reporting of funds
papers.abstract: Impact investing has emerged as a prominent investment approach to addressing social and environmental challenges while generating financial returns. Given its dual mandate to generate impact and financial returns, impact investing faces heightened pressures on its legitimacy, making transparent impact reporting essential to counter allegations of impact-washing and to safeguard the credibility of the approach. Despite the growing relevance of impact reporting, little is known about the underlying motivations and reporting strategies of fund managers who voluntarily publish impact reports. Drawing on legitimacy theory, the paper investigates the motivations and reporting strategies behind voluntary impact reporting by fund managers using a sequential exploratory design. First, 13 semi-structured interviews with impact-reporting professionals were analyzed following Grounded Theory principles. Second, a qualitative content analysis of 141 publicly available impact reports was conducted to analyze how reporting strategies are implemented in practice. The findings of the interviews reveal that fund managers’ motivations are driven by a need to show the alignment of profit with purpose, move beyond institutional compliance, and foster impact reflexivity. These motivations are operationalized through six reporting strategies: rationalization, contextualization, verification, institutionalization, participation, and transformation, which cluster around the dimensions of justification, integration, and adaptation. The content analysis assesses the potential for more substantive forms of legitimation in individual reporting elements. The paper contributes to legitimacy theory in the context of reporting by demonstrating that reporting strategies are interdependent and to practice by offering practitioners and standard setters a starting point for critically reflecting on the design of impact reporting.

papers.title: Study on variable-speed operating characteristics of the SCO2 Brayton cycle under different shaft configurations
Effect of active grout irrigation in ground heat exchangers with helical-shaped pipe
papers.abstract: Improving the efficiency of ground source heat pumps during their operation is a key aspect to foster their diffusion, and grout irrigation strategies could be valuable solutions to implement for this purpose. However, this strategy is still largely unexplored and needs thorough study. In this work, it is investigated whether the active irrigation of the grout surrounding helical borehole heat exchangers can improve the heat pump seasonal efficiency, and under which conditions this benefit is not offset by the consumption of the irrigation system itself. The effect of variable water content on the properties of a sandy grout was taken into account through empirical correlations reported in the literature and implemented in an open-source CApacity-Resistance Model, named pyCaRM, in order to be updated at each time step. Three main strategies, adopted only in the summer season, were compared against a baseline case over a twenty-year simulation, including the electricity consumption of the auxiliary water supply system. Results showed that, in the best-case scenario, the heat pump seasonal efficiency during cooling mode can improve by about 5.3%, dropping to 4.5% if considering the auxiliary system, at the end of the 20 th year, and that 96 m 3 /borehole/year were necessary to reach these values. As for the energy efficiency in heating mode, its relative reduction is about 2%. The total volume pumped and its source should therefore be taken into account when assessing the strategy, and the different strategies should be implemented according to the building load characteristics to achieve the highest rate of improvement.

papers.title: Soil nitrogen availability as a metabolic switch between microbial autotrophy–heterotrophy balance and soil carbon sequestration
Shotgun metagenomic surveillance of airport wastewater reveals microbial community restructuring and persistence of antimicrobial-resistance determinants after treatment
papers.abstract: Airport wastewater has emerged as a valuable matrix for wastewater-based epidemiology, providing insights into microbial circulation and antimicrobial resistance (AMR) among highly mobile populations. However, the effects of wastewater treatment on the microbial community structure and resistome of airport wastewater have not been comprehensively characterized. Here, we present the first comprehensive metagenomic assessment of paired influent and effluent airport wastewater, enabling characterization of treatment-induced changes in microbial community composition and antimicrobial resistance determinants. Paired influent and effluent wastewater samples were collected from the wastewater treatment plant serving Catania–Fontanarossa Airport (Sicily, Italy). Wastewater treatment significantly reduced microbial richness and induced a consistent shift in community composition, as demonstrated by paired beta-diversity analyses. Proteobacteria became the dominant phylum after treatment, whereas Bacteroidetes and Firmicutes markedly declined. Differential abundance analyses showed enrichment of treatment-associated taxa, including Thauera, Aliiarcobacter and Pseudomonas , accompanied by depletion of gut-associated genera such as Bacteroides, Prevotella and Alistipes . Qualitative resistome profiling indicated partial reduction of several ARG classes but persistence of clinically relevant resistance determinants, particularly those associated with beta-lactams, aminoglycosides, macrolides and sulphonamides. Functional profiling indicated treatment-associated metabolic restructuring; however, no functional features remained statistically significant after correction for multiple testing. Overall, these findings demonstrate that airport wastewater treatment acts as an ecological filter that substantially restructures microbial communities without completely eliminating antimicrobial resistance signatures. Shotgun metagenomic surveillance of airport wastewater may therefore provide valuable complementary information for monitoring AMR dissemination and microbial dynamics within a One Health framework.

papers.title: Conceptualising corruption in the extractive industries: Evidence from a systematic review
Process-based Monte Carlo cost simulation for offshore wind farm decommissioning: A scenario analysis for the German North Sea
papers.abstract: The decommissioning of offshore wind farms (OWFs) involves complex, multi-stage processes whose costs are subject to substantial uncertainty. With over 2,000 turbines approaching end-of-life in the German Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) alone, reliable cost estimation is essential for operators, regulators, and financial planning. Existing cost models are predominantly deterministic and lack industry-informed input parameters, correlation structures among risk drivers, or comprehensive scenario comparisons. Using a process-based Monte Carlo model with correlated operational and market risks, we estimate the cost distribution of offshore wind farm decommissioning across ten technological and logistical scenarios. Expected net costs in prices of 2022 range from approximately € 242,000 to € 543,000 per decommissioned MW across scenarios. Foundation removal dominates overall costs, accounting for roughly half of total expenditures, while partial decommissioning strategies significantly reduce expected costs. Vessel charter costs dominate. Partial decommissioning scenarios reduce expected costs by 18–27 % relative to the baseline. Feeder logistics concepts increase costs by 48–65 % due to additional vessels and amplified duration uncertainty. The widely used “installation backwards” approach is neither the most cost-effective nor the least risky option. Incorporating correlated risks substantially increases tail risk compared to deterministic estimates, suggesting that current provisioning approaches may underestimate financial exposure. ​

Reparative soil science: Soil, colonialism, and environmental justice between scientific knowledge and local cultures
papers.abstract: Soil is a repository for historical accounts of power, dispossession, and cultural continuity. This paper proposes the development of “reparative soil science,” a new paradigm that combines soil remediation with theories of environmental justice, decolonization, and multi-knowledge systems. We define it as an orientation within soil science that treats the discipline’s own concepts, classifications, and survey conventions as historical products, and that couples the biophysical repair of degraded soils with repair of the rights, relations, and forms of knowledge that colonial land regimes displaced. By analyzing examples from around the world, the paper shows how colonialism and postcolonial land governance have resulted in the devaluation of local epistemologies and the transformation of socioecological systems. Results indicate that successful integration of scientific and Indigenous knowledge requires mutual legitimacy, long-term trust-building, and equitable sharing of decision-making authority and benefits. It is argued that reparative soil science should extend beyond the purely technical rehabilitation of degraded soils to challenge existing structural inequalities and help restore cultural and ecological relationships between humans and the land. Soil is our entry point, but the same reasoning extends to land, territory, and natural resources more broadly. The perspective positions soil science within global agreements such as the UN Decade on Ecosystem Restoration, the Sustainable Development Goals, and Land Degradation Neutrality, and argues for a pluralistic, participatory, and politically aware practice serving both ecological resilience and social repair.

papers.title: An expert-informed framework for participatory soundscape design: From Interviews to co-design application
Urban form typologies in Seoul since 1960: A framework for block-level classification and their changing prevalence over time
papers.abstract: This study proposes a framework for classifying urban form typologies at the block level and examining changes in their prevalence in Seoul since 1960. The study identifies major typologies aligned with urban planning trends and analyzes their morphological characteristics. Key questions addressed include: how many distinct urban form types can be identified in Seoul; what unique features define each type; and how changes in the prevalence of these types over time reflect broader urban development trends. The analytical procedure consisted of three steps. First, block units were defined based on infrastructure boundaries such as arterial roads. Second, eight indicators were established to capture the morphological features of blocks, parcels, streets, and buildings—the fundamental components of urban structure. Third, Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM) clustering was applied to classify blocks with similar numerical indicators into five distinct types. The result effectively captures how many morphological features aligned with Seoul’s urban planning objectives by era. Compared with previous typologies, the study integrates multiple scales of urban form and examines changes in typology prevalence across different periods, providing a basis for interpreting the historical process of urbanization.

papers.title: Saving lives or freeing territory? Sacred values and tragic trade-offs in wartime Ukraine
papers.abstract: President Zelensky has asserted: “We do not trade our lands and our people.” Both territorial integrity and human lives are considered ‘sacred values’ in wartime Ukraine, values beyond cost-benefit and exchange calculations. Yet, the human costs of continuing war to retake territory are so great in Ukraine that these sacred values are forced into a tragic trade-off. Using a survey of frontline Ukrainians from 2022 made up of residents and displaced persons equally (n = 1800), this paper shows that how the ‘lives versus territory’ dilemma divided respondents. We examined the degree to which wartime hatred of the Russian leadership and material insecurity explain people’s choices, and the role that personal stress plays as a mediator for these attitudes. The results reveal that respondents with higher levels of stress were more likely to prioritize saving lives over freeing territory. Displaced persons were also more likely to prioritize lives. The respondent’s material insecurity had modest impacts. For those most stressed during wartime, lives come before land.

papers.title: Chinese PhD students in clinical medicine can graduate without a thesis — more degrees to follow
‘A perfect scientist, a perfect mum’: researchers mourn two biologists’ deaths in Spanish train crash
Fatty acid desaturation controls cellular fate decisions between senescence and ferroptosis
papers.abstract: Summary When subject to damage or stress, cells develop responses in order to maintain tissue homeostasis. Two such decisions are ferroptosis and cellular senescence, but how cells decide between these outcomes remains unclear. Here we show that senescent cells increase levels of multiple membrane-bound polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs), but a specific PUFA, dihomo-gamma-linolenic acid (DGLA, 20:3 ω -3) is reduced. Exogenous repletion of DGLA or inhibition of delta-5-desaturase, the enzyme that metabolizes DGLA, instead results in cell death by ferroptosis. Senescent cells had elevated levels of other fezzroptosis sensitizers, including labile iron and expression of lipoxygenases – but also increased Gpx4 levels to prevent ferroptosis. Oral DGLA lowered senescent cell burden in aged mice and improved age-related functional outcomes. Finally, obese humans with lowered DGLA desaturation rates showed lower markers of adipose tissue senescence. Together, our data implicate DGLA and its desaturation as a major driver of decisions between senescence and ferroptosis.

papers.title: Industrialization drives convergent microbiome and host physiological shifts in the human metaorganism
papers.abstract: Understanding how host lifestyle and industrialization shape the human gut microbiome and intestinal physiology requires multimodal analyses across diverse global host contexts. Here, we generate multivariate data from the Global Microbiome Conservancy cohort, including gut microbiome, IgA-sequencing, host genotyping, diet, lifestyle and fecal biomarker profiles, to investigate host-microbiome interactions across gradients of industrialization and geography. We show that industrialization is associated with homogenized microbial compositions, reduced microbial diversity, and lower community stability, independent of host confounders. We further show that industrialization is linked to elevated markers of gut stress, increased IgA secretion, and altered patterns of IgA-bacteria interactions. Finally, we show that microbiome-based disease predictors trained on industrialized populations lose accuracy in less industrialized cohorts, highlighting limited cross-population transferability. Together, our results suggest profound restructuring of host-microbiome interactions due to industrialized lifestyles, and emphasize the need for inclusive, globally representative data to improve translational microbiome applications across diverse human populations.

papers.title: Convergent genomic evolution of human gut bacteria along an industrialization gradient
papers.abstract: To what extent gut bacteria respond to the distinct ecological pressures imposed by human lifestyle remains unclear. Here, we investigate how genomic adaptation in gut bacteria differ between industrialized and non-industrialized human populations. We generated a broad collection of isolate genomes spanning diverse host geographies, lifestyles, species, and strains. We first found that compared to MAGs, paired isolate genomes recover more functional elements and signals of horizontal gene transfers (HGTs). Leveraging isolate genomes from multiple species, we find that strains from industrialized hosts experience an expansion of proteome size and harbor greater pangenome fluidity, driven by recent events of HGTs. Gene- and variant-level analyses reveal convergent patterns of lifestyle-specific adaptation in functions that are critical for ecological adaptation, such as stress response, cell envelope remodeling and central metabolism. Our results demonstrate that industrialization imprints evolutionary signatures on gut bacterial genomes, illuminating the effects of rapidly changing environments on human biology.

papers.title: Subsistence transition preceded population turnover in the eastern Colombian Andes
