Why Phytate Persists: Mechanisms of Exceptional Binding and Stability on Soil Mineral Surfaces
papers.abstract: Abstract Phytate, a six-phosphate compound that stores plant phosphorus, is a stable component of soil phosphorus, yet mechanisms underlying its persistence remain unclear. Here, we combined adsorption experiments, spectroscopy, X-ray scattering, and molecular modeling to investigate phytate interactions with five soil minerals: goethite, hematite, quartz, montmorillonite, and kaolinite. Iron oxides exhibited up to 5-fold greater adsorption capacities than quartz and clays. Natural organic matter caused negligible desorption of mineral-bound phytate, whereas phytate displaced adsorbed natural organic matter, demonstrating competitive and stable phytate-mineral associations. Adsorption capacities normalized to orthophosphate binding-site densities implied multiphosphate coordination for phytate on iron oxides, but binding beyond nominal orthophosphate sites on montmorillonite. Molecular dynamics simulations captured one to three phosphate groups in phytate associations with iron oxides; metal cation screening of electrostatic repulsion facilitated binding on negatively charged quartz and montmorillonite. Infrared spectroscopy revealed coupled vibrational responses of phosphate and inositol ring moieties on goethite, but primarily phosphate responses on montmorillonite. X-ray total scattering determined a feature at 2.7 Å, supporting inner-sphere coordination on iron oxides and consistent with quantum mechanics-based energy calculations, whereas quartz and clay features indicated interfacial reorganization. These findings establish mineral-specific mechanisms of phytate stabilization, with implications for persistence and bioavailability in soils.

papers.title: Climate-Driven Sink-to-Source Transitions for Microplastics in Terrestrial Systems
papers.abstract: Abstract Microplastics (MPs) are increasingly recognized as pervasive contaminants in terrestrial environments, where soils act as major dynamic reservoirs that retain particles but can also release them through hydrological, erosional, and atmospheric pathways. Climate change is altering the physical, hydrological, and biogeochemical controls that govern the MP retention-release balance. This review develops a climate-driven sink-to-source transition framework in which terrestrial systems shift episodically from retention-dominated to export-active states. We synthesize evidence that changes in freeze–thaw regimes and drought-rewetting reorganize pore networks and preferential flow; extreme rainfall and runoff can exceed hydrological retention and redistribute MPs vertically and laterally; and warming and salinization reconfigure interfacial interactions, polymer aging, aggregation behavior, and microbially mediated transport processes. Atmospheric entrainment and snowpack-snowmelt pathways further connect terrestrial MP reservoirs with other environmental compartments. Across these climate drivers, MP mobility depends on the coupled evolution of pore architecture, water flux, particle properties, and biogeochemical conditions rather than on any single forcing factor. By integrating laboratory studies, field observations, and emerging modeling perspectives, this review provides a mechanistic foundation for predicting terrestrial MP redistribution and associated environmental risks under ongoing climate change.

papers.title: Recovering Rare Earth Elements from Mining Effluent via Synergistic Angstrom-Scale Confinement and Phosphate-Mediated Coordination in MXene Membranes
papers.abstract: Abstract Recovering rare earth elements (REEs) from complex aqueous streams is essential for advancing sustainable resource recovery but remains hindered by low REE concentrations and strong competition with impurity ions. Herein, we introduce a biomimetic MXene membrane that integrates phosphate-based molecular recognition with angstrom-level control of interlayer spacing to achieve the selective and continuous recovery of REEs from wastewaters. By intercalating aminophosphonic molecules within Ti3C2Tx layers, the membrane precisely tunes the nanochannel size and establishes coordinatively active oxygen sites that preferentially bind trivalent lanthanides under nanoconfinement. Such a design enables a synergistic mechanism in which steric exclusion and ligand–metal coordination coregulate ion transport, leading to markedly improved selectivity toward REE recovery. The optimized 2-AEP-M membrane exhibited a Ca2+/Dy3+ selectivity of 243.47 in simulated solutions and 130.69 in actual REE mining wastewater. After membrane separation and subsequent precipitation and calcination, REEs constituted 90.2% of the quantified cationic species in the recovered solid products. Experimental and computational analyses reveal that phosphate groups promote Dy3+ coordination, underpinning the observed ion discrimination. The membrane also demonstrates antiswelling stability and antibacterial properties, supporting its potential for long-term deployment. This work integrates chemical affinity with angstrom-confined transport, offering a platform for precise ion separation and sustainable REE recovery.

papers.title: Targeted Coupling of Electrogenerated Reactive Oxygen Species for Deep Pollutant Mineralization
papers.abstract: Abstract Electrochemical oxidation technology holds great promise for wastewater treatment. However, the inherent limitations of single-component reactive oxygen species (ROS) and their low yield impede thorough mineralization of organic pollutants and elevate energy consumption. Herein, we develop a directed ROS coupling oxidation (DRCO) system, which employs a Ni–Sb–SnO2 anode that leverages Ni(III)/Ni(II) redox cycling for highly selective OH generation, coupled with a CrMn@C anode for 1O2 production, significantly enhancing the coexisting ROS yield. By leveraging the electron-withdrawing and donating synergistic effect of •OH and 1O2, the DRCO system removes 61.2–78.5% total organic carbon (TOC) for diverse organics within 20 min. The observed kinetic constants are 1.4–52.6 times higher than those of systems that use •OH or 1O2 alone. Furthermore, the DRCO system achieves 85.4% TOC removal for actual pharmaceutical wastewater and sustains operational stability over a 120 h continuous flow period. Compared to commercial anodes, the DRCO system reduces energy consumption by 72% (to 12.02 kW·h·kgTOC–1) while effectively suppressing the accumulation of toxic intermediate products. This work demonstrates that high-selectivity •OH generation and the elucidated dual-ROS synergistic mechanism jointly offer a viable strategy toward efficient and energy-conscious electrochemical water purification.

papers.title: Biogeochemical Control Points for Mitigating Metal(loid) Risk in Rice under Global Change
papers.abstract: Abstract The uptake of arsenic (As), cadmium (Cd), and mercury (Hg) in rice is a global health concern. The variable biogeochemical processes that govern contamination risk, along with increased anthropogenic pressures, present significant obstacles to implementing mitigation strategies. This perspective highlights the biogeochemical processes governing the mobility and rice uptake of metal(loid)s across the soil-rice continuum and provides recent insights into mitigation strategies. An overview of anthropogenic stressors that may further exacerbate rice contamination, particularly climate change, is also provided. Finally, in the context of historical knowledge, we identify and discuss a future roadmap for research priorities and mitigation strategies, including (1) addressing variability in soil-rice systems that alters metal(loid) uptake dynamics, (2) investigating practical applications and mitigation strategies for farmers, and (3) expanding research into the myriad effects climate change may have on metal(loid) cycling.

papers.title: Mechanistic Insights into Humic Acid-Mediated Photosensitized Activation of Mn(VII) under UVA Irradiation
papers.abstract: Abstract Ultraviolet A/permanganate [UVA/Mn(VII)] is a promising advanced oxidation process (AOP), while few studies have noticed that humic acid (HA) could enhance microcontaminant degradation in the process. For the first time, the promotive effect of HA and the underlying mechanisms were investigated in UVA/Mn(VII). HA significantly enhanced the generation of hydroxyl radical (HO•) and reactive manganese species (RMnS). Consequently, the pseudo-first-order reaction rate constants for microcontaminant degradation in UVA/Mn(VII)/HA were several to tens of times those in UVA/Mn(VII). The promotive effect of HA was attributed to the enhanced Mn(VII) activation by photogenerated reactive intermediates derived from irradiated HA. Among them, the excited triplet state of HA (3HA*) played a major role, which was also supported by benzophenone (BP), a model triplet state photosensitizer. The second-order reaction rate constants of Mn(VII) with 3HA* and 3BP* were determined to be 2.54(±0.31) × 108 and 2.88(±0.10) × 109 M–1 s–1, respectively. Spectroscopic analysis and theoretical calculations supported an electron transfer mechanism for the reactions of Mn(VII) with 3HA* and 3BP*. Mn(VII) accepted one electron from 3HA*/3BP* and was reduced to Mn(VI), which underwent disproportionation to form Mn(VII) and Mn(V), followed by HO• and other RMnS generation. These findings provide novel perspectives for the application of UVA/Mn(VII) in practical water treatment.

papers.title: Constructing Prospective Multiregional Input-Output Tables via Scenario-Constrained Optimization for Future Environmental Footprint Assessment
papers.abstract: Abstract Prospective multiregional input-output (MRIO) tables that integrate scenarios from integrated assessment models (IAMs) support forward-looking environmental footprint analysis, but the trade-off between historical structural fidelity and scenario compliance has not been quantified. We constructed 12 prospective MRIO tables from EXIOBASE 2019 and the IMAGE SSP2 scenario for 2035, including a Leontief-based projection and 11 optimization-based projections under different combinations of scenario constraints on GDP, value added, sector outputs, as well as energy and agriculture consumption. Among the constraints, those on energy and agriculture consumption were satisfied at the highest cost in coefficient deviations from the Leontief-based projection and shifted the corresponding transaction flows most significantly. Regional shares of the global carbon footprint remained stable, but sectoral attribution within each region was substantially reshuffled, and the identification of high-growth consumption hotspots was sensitive to scenario compliance level. Some hotspots persisted at all levels of compliance. The consumption-based carbon footprint driven by China’s final energy demand grew the fastest and emerged as a major new hotspot in 2035. The footprint of livestock consumption showed persistent high growth in multiple regions and India and the Rest of Asia rose in environmental significance through their industrial sectors.

Experimental investigation of a multi-buoy cooperative point-absorber wave energy
papers.abstract: This study presents a proof-of-concept experimental investigation of a multi-buoy cooperative point-absorber wave energy converter (WEC). The proposed concept consists of an array of surface-penetrating buoys connected through a shared closed-loop hydraulic power take-off (PTO) system. Energy is extracted through the collective motion of the buoy array, where pressurised flow generated by individual buoys drives a turbine within the hydraulic circuit. A 1:40 scale model was tested in the wave tank facilities at the University of Oslo. Experiments with regular and irregular long-crested waves at two different incident angles were conducted to assess power absorption, wave period response, and interaction effects. Two array configurations were investigated: an eight-buoy array with an axis-to-axis spacing of 1.5 buoy diameters, and a four-buoy array with a 3.0 diameter spacing. Although piston head leakage affected the power measurements, our results demonstrate that the WEC absorbs incoming wave energy and produces measurable power. The eight-buoy configuration achieved the highest power output per buoy compared to the four-buoy configuration, but exhibited increased sensitivity to wave period and wave heading, due to buoy-buoy interactions, such as collisions. This study highlights buoy count and internal buoy spacing as key design parameters for cooperative point-absorber wave energy systems. The results indicate that higher buoy counts enhance hydraulic cooperation, and increased buoy spacing improves robustness to wave heading and reduces destructive interaction effects. We also suggest that a lower system inertia can improve responsiveness to shorter waves. These insights provide a foundation for further optimisation and future full-scale development.

Reindeer habitat selection and movement change with cumulative impacts from mining and wind power development
papers.abstract: Industrial expansion often occurs in landscapes already affected by multiple disturbances, leading to cumulative impacts on biodiversity and local communities. With the societal pressure for an rapid ‘green transition’, land-use changes intensifies, yet most impact assessments remain local and project-based, disregarding cumulative impacts. We conceptualized and disentangled key dimensions of cumulative impacts and integrated them within habitat selection, calving site selection, and movement analyses in a case study of reindeer and Sámi reindeer husbandry in Scandinavia. Using GPS data collected before, during, and after the construction of four wind power plants, we quantified the effects of mining, wind power development, and other infrastructure across snow-free seasons and behavioural processes. We found strong avoidance of mines and wind power plants, with zones of influence extending up to 5-10 km at landscape scale and up to 5 km at patch scale. Impacts were strongest during calving but also present in summer and autumn. Wind power plants affected movement by acting as semi-permeable barriers, with reindeer avoiding crossing them and moving faster and more directionally near turbines during construction. At patch scale, cumulative impacts of several wind power plants were evident during calving. Our results highlight the need for regional and integrative land-use planning that accounts for cumulative impacts from multiple existing and planned developments. The framework we present here provides a general approach to quantify zones of influence and cumulative impacts of multiple features and infrastructure types across landscapes and ecological processes.

papers.title: Assessing commuting-related heat exposure deviations from Neighborhood effect averaging in a megacity
papers.abstract: Urban heat exposure in highly mobile cities cannot be fully characterized by residential conditions alone. Existing mobility-based assessments quantify absolute exposure or residential-to-mobile differences, but do not separate population-level exposure averaging from individual departures around that relationship. We develop a three-layer framework distinguishing absolute exposure, time-matched out-of-home thermal contrast, and conditional deviation from the Neighborhood Effect Averaging Problem (NEAP) relationship. NEAP-adjusted heat exposure deviation (NAE) measures the difference between observed mobile heat exposure (MHE) and the MHE expected given residential heat exposure (RHE). Using reconstructed hourly land surface temperature and mobile-phone trajectories for 179,588 commuters in Shanghai, we identify clear population-level averaging between RHE and MHE ( β = 0.730 ). NAE and the direct out-of-home contrast differed in direction for 32.3% of commuters. Elevated NAE formed a distinct peri-core and commuting-transition geography rather than reproducing absolute heat hotspots; 26.8% of upper-decile NAE grids were not simultaneously identified by high RHE, MHE, or direct out-of-home contrast. Higher NAE was associated with longer home–work paths, longer commuting duration, and more time spent away from home, whereas greater mobility entropy was associated with lower NAE. Higher-rent residential contexts and grids with mean commuter ages in the early-to-mid 30s also showed elevated NAE, while greater functional richness and development intensity were associated with lower NAE across parts of their observed ranges. These findings establish NEAP as an empirical reference for revealing structured mobility-related exposure deviations that remain hidden in conventional absolute or direct-contrast assessments.

papers.title: Investigating lead exposure in northern Indigenous communities of the Sahtú region, Northwest Territories, Canada
Towards a new generation of science-policy interfaces for biodiversity: Contributions from the State Biodiversity Strategies Initiative in Mexico
Impact of AI robotics, income, clean energy subtypes, and energy transition on environmental progress: An incremental analysis for China by KRLS model
papers.abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) has been widely applied in economies, understanding its environmental implications is highly critical. Consistent with this phenomenon, this research uncovers the impact of AI robotics (AIR), income, clean energy subtypes, and energy transition (ETI), along with traditional factors (namely, trade openness, urbanization, and financial development), on environmental progress. In this vein, the study focuses on China, the leading carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) emitter, uses CO 2 emissions (sustainable development index) in the main (robustness analysis) as the dependent variable, uses AI robotics as a novel proxy for AI, and performs novel Kernel-regularized least squares (KRLS) model on the most recent data from 2000 to 2024. The results suggest that (i) AIR, income, ETI, trade openness, and urbanization are not helpful to decrease CO 2 emissions, while financial development has an insignificant increasing impact; (ii) among clean energy subtypes, only nuclear energy has a reducing impact on CO 2 emissions at lower percentiles; (iii) in terms of interaction of AIR with clean energy subtypes, only hydro (other renewable) energy is statistically significant (insignificant) decreasing impact on CO 2 emissions at lower percentiles; (iv) KRLS model obtains successful estimation results, reaching ∼99.73%; and (v) the robustness checks using an alternative dependent variable confirm the empirical results. Therefore, the research empirically attests to the inefficient use of AIR, an unsuccessful ETI approach, and ineffective use of clean energy subtypes in China. At the same time, the marginal impacts of the factors considered on CO 2 emissions differ across percentiles. Based on these findings, we outline relevant policy implications for China.

papers.title: Evolutionary game theory for environmental governance: Theoretical foundations, multi-stakeholder dynamics, and policy design strategies for sustainable resource management
papers.abstract: Environmental governance fails less often for want of instruments than for want of an account of how stakeholders revise their choices once instruments are in place. This review asks what evolutionary game theory (EGT) can and cannot establish about that revision process, for problems in which populations differ in position, payoff exposure, and adaptation speed. The apparatus—evolutionarily stable strategies, replicator dynamics under heterogeneous learning rates, and multi-population stability criteria—is assembled first, its representational limits stated alongside its capabilities. Two governance settings are then examined in depth. In transboundary water allocation among upstream, midstream, and downstream jurisdictions, positional asymmetry produces stratified rather than uniform cooperation: upstream and midstream converge to high cooperation while downstream collapses under the baseline payoffs, and upstream and downstream paths correlate most strongly at a lag of about 25 years, set by infrastructure investment cycles and institutional adaptation. In tripartite industrial pollution control, single instruments leave the system in the low-cooperation basin (equilibrium near 0.01–0.02), whereas penalties and abatement-cost relief applied jointly move it to an equilibrium near 0.73; enterprise adjustment lags the regulatory shock by about 15 years and community mobilization by about 25 years. Such regularities are projections of a specified model rather than measurements of behavior, and the conditions under which they would fail are stated with them. For policy, instrument combination takes priority over instrument intensity, commitment horizons measured in decades over electoral cycles, and measures that lower participation costs for the actors whose monitoring extends enforcement reach.

papers.title: Microbial Respiration in Subtropical Urban Soils Depending on Vegetation Type
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Urban vegetation combines invasive and introduced species with native relics, whose litter is the primary source of organic matter inputs in urban soils. Plant litter quality regulates both organic carbon (C) storage and microbial activity in urban soils. Here we examined the microbial respiration and organic C stocks in the subtropical urban soils depending on plant litter decomposability. Five urban areas differing in vegetation (deciduous forest, shrubland, grassland, ruderal area, and turfgrass) were used for kinetic analysis of plant litter decomposition over a 12‐week incubation, and CO 2 efflux and microbial biomass C in soil were analyzed. The plant litter decomposability decreased as its C/N ratio increased. The decay constant of potentially mineralized litter components decreased progressively from turfgrass and grassland to shrubland and ruderal area, and finally to forest. Higher litter decomposition was associated with a faster rate of soil microbial respiration per unit of organic C content. Soil organic C stocks were 20%–38% larger in urban forest and areas with ruderal vegetation than in turfgrass. This was caused by the greater biostability of forest litter and lower microbial activity in the soils of semi‐natural areas compared with those of completely transformed and managed urban ecosystems such as turfgrass. Consequently, the decrease in decomposability of plant litter increased organic C stocks and reduced microbial respiration rates, highlighting the importance of vegetation type in managing C storage in urban soils.

papers.title: Microplastic‐Induced Shifts in Soil Leachate Chemistry, Redox Response, Biochemistry, and Biofilm Dynamics
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Microplastics (MPs) are increasingly recognized as soil contaminants, yet their time‐dependent associations with dissolved organic matter characteristics, redox behavior, biochemical constituents, and biofilm‐associated responses are often investigated separately. This study evaluated these responses within an integrated soil‐exposure framework using particles derived from three commonly used consumer products—surgical masks (predominantly polypropylene, PP), plastic water bottles (polyethylene terephthalate, PET), and cardboard cups (cellulose‐rich composites containing a polymeric barrier layer)—at three nominal loadings (0.1, 0.5, and 2.0 g per 200 g soil), three exposure periods (1, 3, and 7 weeks), and two extraction media (distilled water and phosphate‐buffered saline, PBS). UV–Vis‐derived aromaticity‐related (AR), humification‐related (HI), and spectral slope factor (SF) indices were assessed alongside DTT‐based redox responses, CUPRAC‐based extractable reducing capacity, extractable carbohydrate and protein contents, and crystal‐violet‐based biofilm‐associated responses. The investigated materials exhibited distinct material‐, loading‐, time‐, and extraction‐medium‐dependent patterns across these endpoints. At week 1, several treatments showed relatively elevated HI and SF ratios compared with matched soil controls. These responses generally declined by week 3, whereas selected PET‐bottle‐ and cardboard‐cup‐derived treatments exhibited renewed increases in aromaticity‐ or humification‐related optical indices at week 7, particularly in PBS extracts. DTT‐based redox responses also varied substantially across conditions, although these measurements did not directly quantify DTT consumption rates or ROS formation. Extractable carbohydrate contents and CV‐stainable biofilm‐associated material showed pronounced responses in selected cardboard‐cup and PET‐bottle treatments, whereas protein responses were generally modest. Overall, the findings demonstrate condition‐dependent changes in soil‐extract optical characteristics, redox‐related analytical responses, and extractable biochemical constituents, without establishing a consistent monotonic relationship with particle loading or a causal link between redox changes and biofilm formation.

papers.title: The material infrastructure of privatization, dispossession and resistance at the Zambian land frontier
papers.abstract: The privatization of communal lands continues to be a central tenet of capitalist and settler-colonial appropriations with devastating implications for the dispossessed and land denied. This article traces how dispossession and resistance become bound up in the material infrastructure of privatization – fences, concrete, rebar and survey lines – and the colonial histories sedimented within them. In dialogue with legal-geographical work on property and materiality, I show how such artefacts become the nodes through which law’s abstraction gives way to struggle; once law is materialized in objects, these become susceptible to alteration and enrolment in new lives of legal association that can subvert – and creatively invert – the power trafficked through property. The analysis draws from ethnographic fieldwork in Mulonga village, central Zambia, where a privatization scheme evolved into a localized struggle between creative cultivators who reworked the things of property to resist displacement, and a bureaucracy that struggled to make them perform the political work assigned to them. Abstract property, I conclude, must be read alongside the contingency and resistant reworkings of its material articulation, which creates new legal surfaces upon which people can act, redirect legal signs, and unsettle translations through which private property achieves exclusionary effect.

The influence of private equity investment on firm transaction costs in offshore emerging economies
papers.abstract: This study focuses on the transaction cost of share trading for listed firms with private equity ownership within emerging economies. We build on a recently advanced emerging market private equity business model (Taussig & Delios, 2016) and complement this model by applying the ownership competency theory of Foss, Klein, Lien, Zellweger & Zenger (2021). Our study draws on a unique sample of listed firms from eight national securities exchanges across the Caribbean region. We find that private equity ownership increases firms’ transaction costs, as reflected in higher estimated bid-ask quoted share price spreads. However, this association is negatively moderated by (1) the firm having a related party located in an offshore jurisdiction and (2) the firm adopting a shareholder value enhancing corporate governance model. In a broader context, our analysis highlights the importance of institutional fit of private equity in the local institutional fabric within which investee firms are embedded

papers.title: Rethinking Supplier Integration in Humanitarian Supply Chains: Feasibility and Constraints From an International Humanitarian Organization Perspective
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Despite the widely recognized importance of integrative practices in commercial supply chain operations, their application in humanitarian supply chains (HSCs) remains underexplored. HSCs differ from commercial supply chains in their relational dynamics and integration processes, operating under extreme uncertainty, demand volatility, infrastructural disruption, and resource scarcity across a complex web of actors. Using an embedded single‐case design, this study assesses supplier integration (SI) in humanitarian operations in a leading international humanitarian organization (IHO), as well as the IHO's relationships with eight key suppliers. Drawing on the relational lenses of power, trust, and commitment, distinct integration patterns were identified across different supplier types. The findings highlight humanitarian‐specific contextual constraints and are used to inform a typology of SI feasibility encompassing feasible, selectively feasible, and low‐feasibility integration. This typology provides a foundation for guiding supplier relationship management in complex humanitarian contexts. This study offers a framework for understanding how relational and structural conditions shape integration in humanitarian settings and underscores the need for IHOs to adopt context‐appropriate supplier management approaches that reflect the unique dynamics of humanitarian operations.

papers.title: Navigating Circular Economy Challenges in the Internationalization of Food Companies: MCDM‐Based Investigation
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT In today's rapidly changing and highly competitive environment, internationalization has become a strategic necessity. It is no longer merely a source of competitive advantage, but a fundamental requirement for organizational survival. This need is particularly pronounced in the food industry, which faces stringent quality requirements and growing pressure to comply with international regulations. However, the internationalization of these firms brings significant challenges related to circular economy (CE) practices. The main goal of this study is to identify and evaluate the most important challenges and obstacles to implementing CE in small and medium‐sized enterprises (SMEs) in the food industry. This study was conducted in three phases. In the first phase, through a literature review, the barriers to implementing CE in the internationalization process of food SMEs, along with the evaluation criteria related to these barriers, were identified. In the second phase, the identified criteria were weighted using the hesitant fuzzy best–worst method (HF‐BWM) in order to determine their relative importance. Finally, in the third phase, the barriers were ranked based on the obtained weights by applying the hesitant fuzzy CoCoSo (HF‐CoCoSo) technique, which is a rigorous multicriteria decision‐making (MCDM) method. The findings indicate that criteria “Loss of foreign customers' trust,” “Loss of sales and revenue,” and “loss of market share” received the highest weights. Moreover, the barriers “Financial constraints in implementing CE,” “Lack of successful business models and frameworks,” and “Uncertainty in reverse flows” were ranked as the most significant. The findings of this research contribute to enriching the existing body of knowledge on the internationalization of food industry enterprises by addressing the barriers associated with CE. Furthermore, the results provide decision‐makers with valuable insights to overcome the influential CE ‐ related obstacles affecting the internationalization process.

papers.title: Innovation Environment Matters More Than Policy? Evidence on Technology Adoption From Chinese Manufacturers
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines how policy regulation and external innovation environment jointly influence manufacturing firms' adoption of emerging technologies and subsequent operational performance. Drawing on institutional theory and the resource‐based view, we analyse survey data from 451 Chinese manufacturing firms using structural equation modelling. The results show that policy regulation does not directly drive technology adoption. Instead, it significantly shapes the external innovation environment, which fully mediates the relationship between policy regulation and technology adoption. Emerging technology adoption further improves operational performance. These findings reveal an institution‐resource conversion mechanism: Policy enables the environment, and the environment drives technology adoption. The study extends institutional theory by moving beyond the linear pressure‐response framework and theorising the external innovation environment as a conversion interface between institutional and resource logics. For practice, firms should embed technology adoption into long‐term capability building, while policymakers should shift from direct intervention to cultivating an innovation environment that supports resource coordination.

Ion Valence Difference Governs Membrane Charge Preference in Nanofiltration-Based Radionuclide Separation
papers.abstract: Abstract Selective separation of radionuclides with varying environmental hazards is critical for mitigating the disposal burden of high-level radioactive wastewater. Although positively charged (PC) membranes are generally considered effective for cation pair separation, the applicability of negatively charged (NC) membranes for separating cations with large valence differences remains unresolved. In this study, Ag+/Zr4+ and Ag+/Sr2+ were used as representative radionuclides with large and small valence differences, respectively, to evaluate the separation performance and underlying mechanisms of PC and NC membranes. Notably, NC membranes maintained near-complete rejection of Zr4+ while simultaneously exhibiting higher Ag+ permeability, thereby achieving superior Ag+/Zr4+ selectivity relative to PC membranes. DFT calculations and MD simulations revealed that strong ion–membrane interactions facilitated preferential partitioning of Zr4+ at the NC membrane interface, whereas differences in hydration energy governed the competitive transport of Ag+ and Zr4+. Furthermore, Zr4+ accumulated at the membrane surface induced incomplete dehydration of Ag+, reducing interfacial transport barriers and promoting Ag+ permeation. Comparative analysis of Ag+/Zr4+ and Ag+/Sr2+ systems further demonstrated that ion valence difference governs the preference of membrane charges: NC membranes are preferred for M+/M4+ separations, whereas PC membranes are preferred for M+/M2+ separations, which was further validated by Li+/Mg2+ and Li+/Ti4+ separations. These findings clarify the mechanistic distinction between co-ion and counterion competition, providing guidance for the selection of membrane charge types for energy-efficient radionuclide separation and selective resource recovery beyond the nuclear industry.

papers.title: Market-Average Data Can Misrepresent Supply Chain Environmental Impacts and Their Uncertainty
papers.abstract: Abstract Market-average data sets are often used in life cycle assessment and carbon accounting when the production route of a procured good is unknown. The uncertainty this introduces is commonly characterized using generic pedigree matrix factors, which do not reflect how variability across production geographies and technologies differs between goods. Here, we develop a hybrid method that combines pedigree matrix uncertainty characterization within individual production routes with market-share-weighted Monte Carlo sampling between known production routes to represent uncertainty about which route supplied the good. We compare it with conventional market-average uncertainty analysis for 30 economically important goods. For climate impacts, conventional 5th–95th interpercentile intervals are narrower than route-weighted sampling intervals for 25 goods, at least 50% narrower for 14 goods, and up to 82% narrower. Conventional intervals exclude the central climate impact estimates of 44% of possible production routes. Route-weighted sampling captures these outcomes and reveals multimodality and impact-category-specific uncertainty profiles that conventional analysis does not. Variance decomposition distinguishes geographical and technological differences between routes from uncertainty within routes, helping prioritize supplier data collection. These differences show that conventional uncertainty estimates can mislead and may not capture how substantially initial estimates could change when supplier-specific data become available.

Interactions among land use, climate, leaf litter traits, and consumers shape large-scale patterns of decomposition in streams of SW Europe
papers.abstract: Habitat degradation is one of the primary drivers of biodiversity loss and ecosystem alteration. In streams, leaf litter decomposition plays a key role in energy and nutrient cycling, which is influenced by leaf litter quality, microbial and invertebrate consumers, and environmental conditions. Land use changes alter stream habitats and can modify decomposition rates and dynamics, but large-scale assessments of these anthropogenic impacts remain limited. We explored the consequences of major land use changes (tree plantations, agricultural land, and urban settlements) on stream ecosystems by comparing sites in human-impacted catchments with reference unimpacted sites (i.e., surrounded by native vegetation) across several regions of southwestern Europe encompassing a wide climatic gradient. We quantified decomposition rates of multiple leaf litter types to evaluate the interaction between leaf litter traits and environmental variation, exploring changes in associated invertebrate assemblages. Overall, land use changes reduced total and microbial decomposition rates, with agriculture exerting the strongest effects, and caused marked shifts in invertebrate assemblages including replacement of sensitive by tolerant species and reduced detritivore richness, mainly in urban streams. Climatic variability seemed to modulate these responses, with seasonal climates showing higher vulnerability to impacts. Lastly, leaf litter types differed in their sensitivity to detect degradation, although no consistent trait-based patterns were observed. Our results show that land use changes alter stream ecosystems across climatic gradients, highlighting the urgent need to integrate environmental and biological drivers across spatial scales in watershed management and to provide actionable baselines to optimize riparian restoration and buffer the effects of ongoing climate change.

Metal enrichment and downstream concentration gradients in an agricultural ditch draining a long-term fertilisation experiment
papers.abstract: Agricultural sediment surveys seldom quantify the downstream extent of metal enrichment. We measured Cd, Co, Cr, Cu, Ni, Pb and Zn in 24 surface sediment samples below the Palace Leas long-term fertilisation experiment at Cockle Park, UK. Eighteen samples formed a 452.5 m ditch transect, with three samples each from the receiving stream and an adjacent diffuse runoff line. Concentrations declined downstream, with the strongest enrichment near the ditch head. Metal-specific segmented-fit breakpoints were 104 m for Cd (5–95% resampling interval, 78–129 m), 159 m for Co (129–185 m) and 159 m for Cu (104–236 m). These do not establish a shared boundary. Cr and Ni breakpoint positions were poorly constrained. The first 150 m contained 66.3–96.7% of the distance-integrated excess concentration for six metals, an index of profile shape rather than stored metal mass. Cd contributed 73.9% of a partial seven-metal risk index, while Ni exceeded its freshwater probable effect level in one third of samples. As and Hg were not measured, so the screening may underestimate multi-element hazard and cannot establish the overall priority contaminant. Missing grain-size and organic-carbon measurements leave sediment sorting and carrier mixing unresolved. Uniform concentration scaling preserves within-metal spatial contrasts, but absolute concentrations and screening classifications remain conditional on unmeasured digestion recovery. Detection-limit-aware uncertainty was therefore used for risk-score scenarios. The upper reach is a candidate for follow-up monitoring; a 150 m mitigation zone requires validation with sediment-flux and repeated sampling data.

A machine learning approach to understanding freshwater salinization dynamics and winter season controls in the Northeast United States
papers.abstract: Freshwater salinization is an increasing concern in colder regions where road-salt application, watershed development, hydroclimatic factors, and anthropogenic activities influence river salinity. This study evaluated winter freshwater salinization across six rivers in New York and New Jersey. We hypothesized that winter salinity reflects both shared watershed-scale relationships and site-specific dynamics, with predictor importance varying among watersheds with contrasting hydroclimatic, land-use, and anthropogenic characteristics. The study included 2570 daily observations across three winter seasons from November 2021 to March 2024. Spatial patterns were assessed through principal component analysis (PCA) and geospatial watershed characterization. Multiple linear regression (MLR), random forest (RF), and extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) were applied in pooled and site-specific models using snowfall-lag predictors, while SHAP explained the predictor importance. PCA identified climatic-salinity and hydrologic-flow gradients. The pooled XGBoost model achieved a strong test performance (R 2 = 0.79), with developed land identified as a dominant predictor. Site-specific ensemble models generally outperformed MLR, with XGBoost reaching R 2 = 0.81 at Cattaraugus Creek, a highly forested watershed. Larger drainage-area stations showed limited predictive skill, while highly urbanized watersheds performed moderately. Dominant predictors differed among stations and included discharge, pH, and turbidity. In the Bronx River case study, RF achieved R 2 of 0.56, with two-day lagged road-salt application as the most influential predictor, highlighting road-salt monitoring needs in highly urbanized watersheds. Overall, the findings advance understanding of winter stream salinity dynamics across diverse watersheds and emphasize the need for road-salt monitoring and management.

The driving role of proteins in enhancing lactate and propionate production during food waste fermentation: metabolic constraints and kinetic modeling
papers.abstract: This study aimed to quantify the fraction of lactate, derived from the fermentation of Food Waste (FW) attributable to proteins. Infact, recent studies based on cellular resource allocation suggest that proteins can promote the growth of lactic acid bacteria and enhance lactate production. The experiments were conducted in a chemostat, at a HRT of 20 h and a pH = 5 and 5.5, using a synthetic substrate composed of glucose and albumin in a 4:1 COD ratio, mimicking household FW composition. A pure glucose solution was used for comparison. Although lactate was detected at low concentrations, the glucose-albumin substrate produced a considerable amount of propionate, even when albumin was not consumed, in contrast to the pure glucose solution. It was hypothesized that most propionate was generated via the acrylate pathway, rather than glycolysis, thus confirming the significance of the lactate metabolic pathway. A mathematical model based on the variable stoichiometry approach was adopted as a tool to investigate this hypothesis. The model accounted for the metabolic constraint imposed by the conservation of electron carriers (NADH) throughout the fermentation process. The metabolic constraint made it possible to estimate that propionate production occurred with high probability via the acrylate pathway, thereby revealing that proteins were crucial in driving the metabolic shift of glucose fermentation toward lactate; model calibration estimated that lactate accounted for 35 – 65 % of the total electron flux. Furthermore, lactate was separately supplemented to the substrate in additional experiments, inducing a metabolic shift from acrylate pathway to chain elongation.

Decoding the regulatory programs governing glioblastoma plasticity
papers.abstract: Abstract Glioblastoma is incurable and resistant to therapy despite genomic stability under treatment 1–8 , suggesting that non-genetic cellular plasticity is a central driver of progression. Whether such plasticity reflects stochastic state switching or is governed by predictable gene regulation has remained unclear 9–13 . Here we introduce scDORI (single-cell deep multi-omic regulatory inference)—a deep-learning framework that infers enhancer-driven gene-regulatory networks at single-cell resolution—and apply it to single-nucleus multiome profiles of more than one million cells from primary glioblastomas. Integrating computational inference with systematic perturbation screens across patient-derived models, we show that a structured regulatory program with an asymmetric interplay of activators and repressors governs cellular plasticity in glioblastoma. The resulting transition landscape is hierarchical and predictable, but permits cross-lineage trajectories that are absent from normal neurodevelopment. Within this landscape, low-plasticity states such as the neuronal-like state are not stable differentiation end points but actively maintained configurations, stabilized by a network of safeguard repressors that silence alternative fates. We identify MYT1L as the dominant member of this network, and show that it binds to and represses master regulators of every alternative state to consolidate neuronal-like identity. MYT1L restricted plasticity even under standard-of-care therapy and suppressed tumour growth and invasion in vivo. Conversely, loss of MYT1L reactivated plasticity and accelerated malignant features, indicating that low-plasticity identity requires continuous repression. These findings reframe malignant cell state stability as a balance between activation and continuous repression, and nominate safeguard repressors as candidate therapeutic targets that are distinct from differentiation-inducing activators, with potential relevance across cancers in which phenotypic switching drives therapy resistance.

Accelerating commercialization and deployment of indoor photovoltaics

Multimodal X-ray imaging reveals hierarchical fibre mechanics
papers.abstract: Abstract Fibrous materials, ranging from connective tissues 1–4 to engineered composites 5–8 , are vital to many biological and man-made systems, optimized to withstand complex in operando or in vivo loading. The load-bearing capacity of intervertebral discs (IVDs) of the spine depends on a hierarchical extracellular matrix, where plywood-like lamellae of collagen fibres in the annulus fibrosus contain nanometre-scale fibrils built from staggered triple-helical monomers 4,9,10 . How intact IVDs couple fibril-scale mechanics to fibre-scale organization under load remains unresolved. Here we introduce TomoSAXS, a full-field 3D small-angle X-ray scattering tomography that maps fibril-to-fibre mechanics across an intact tissue. We show that intrafibrillar molecular pre-strain (D-period stagger) is lamellar textured and tightly correlated with microscale fibre strain. Pre-strain is inversely related to fibril strain and its variability, consistent with load-sharing through molecular unwinding. Radial strain bridges and high-curvature zones at the annulus fibrosus–nucleus pulposus interfaces emerge as critical regulators of local mechanics. These findings reveal concerted fibril–fibre interactions that sustain mechanical equilibrium in the IVD, preserving elasticity and shape. More broadly, TomoSAXS establishes a platform to visualize nanoscale-to-microscale matrix mechanics across biological and synthetic fibrous materials, with applications in ageing and disease, therapeutic evaluation and the design of bio-based and bio-inspired materials.

papers.title: Imaging exoplanets below the telescope stability limit
papers.abstract: Abstract Exoplanet imaging is the main method for detailed characterization of planets orbiting beyond 1 au (ref. 1 ) but it requires suppressing the bright glare of the star to see the faint planet light. As well as sophisticated instrumentation 2,3 , effective image processing is necessary for starlight suppression, which continues to be a substantial limitation 4 . Standard algorithms use reference images for starlight modelling and thus they are limited by inevitable telescope instabilities that change from reference to science observation 5,6 . Addressing this challenge will increase the number of planets amenable to direct imaging and will be a notable step towards imaging exo-Earths with future observatories 7 . Here we present a new physics-based method for starlight subtraction. Our method combines a multistep optimization with a flexible physical model to produce a starlight model, allowing modelling and compensation of instrument instabilities. We use automatic differentiation (autodiff) 8 to optimize millions of model parameters. We demonstrate our method on observations from the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) Near-InfraRed Camera (NIRCam) 9–11 coronagraph instrument. We achieve sensitivity 2–15 times superior to standard techniques, including the first detection of 51 Eridani b (ref. 12 ) at 4.3 μm. This is the first time, to our knowledge, that such an approach has demonstrated substantially improved sensitivity on real, on-sky coronagraphic imaging. Our framework can be extended to other current and future ground-based and space-based observatories, including the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope and the Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO), potentially relaxing the unprecedented stability requirements needed to make these a success.

papers.title: Conjugation-regulated self-assembled molecules for tandem solar cells
The deep Earth origin of the Great Unconformity
papers.abstract: Abstract The Great Unconformity marks a globally extensive erosive surface linked to climatic shifts 1 and environmental transitions 2 that preceded the Cambrian explosion of life. The processes proposed to explain the formation of the Great Unconformity include glacial erosion during the Snowball Earth 1,3,4 , rifting and plume activity 5–7 , sea-level fall 8 and mantle-driven dynamic topography 6,9–11 . However, the dynamics of these processes have not been tested. Here we show that continental-scale uplift and subsidence associated with long-wavelength dynamic topography 12 due to mantle convection drove the formation and preservation of the Great Unconformity. Our models predict prolonged continental-scale Neoproterozoic uplift and long-term Phanerozoic subsidence for Laurentia, Baltica and North China. This vertical motion scenario is ideal for the formation and preservation of the Great Unconformity, which is a first-order surface expression of deep Earth processes. The predicted prolonged continental uplift throughout Cryogenian times would have resulted in marked erosion due to the action of glaciers 13 . The large area of Laurentia and limited deformation at its margins explain why the Great Unconformity is best preserved and documented there. Our models predict cycles of dynamic topography that are broadly reflected in preserved sediment volume across continents 1,14 , and open new avenues for understanding the environments of Cambrian animal diversification.

papers.title: Tracing the spread of Celtic languages using ancient genomics
papers.abstract: Abstract Celtic languages are today restricted to Europe’s Atlantic fringes but were widely spoken across the continent during the Iron Age 1–3 . How Celtic achieved this early distribution remains contested 4 , with alternative archaeological and linguistic models proposing different homelands and dispersal routes. Here we analyse genome-wide data from 4,587 ancient individuals, focusing on Bronze and Iron Age Europe, to test the extent to which these models fit reconstructed demographic histories. We identify three main processes shaping European population structure that are relevant to the Celtic dispersal. First, the arrival of Steppe-related ancestry with Bell Beaker-associated groups after around 4400 bp (calibrated years before present or 1950 ce ) across the region in which Celtic and related languages were later spoken. Second, a movement from southwestern Europe into Britain during the Bronze Age (3800–3200 bp ), consistent with scenarios in which Celtic formed along the Atlantic façade. Third, a westward expansion of ancestry related to Late Bronze Age Knovíz–Urnfield-associated populations from eastern central Europe (3200–2800 bp ), affecting France, the British Isles, northeastern Iberia and Italy and later associated with Iron Age Hallstatt and La Tène contexts 5–8 . Although all three movements have parallels with proposed models, we argue that the final movement, from eastern central Europe, is most parsimonious for the spread of Celtic. Although human history does not necessarily follow a parsimonious trajectory 9 and language shifts need not track genetic change, these results delimit the demographic scenarios that are plausible for the emergence of Celtic in prehistoric Europe.

papers.title: Ecological and social cues orchestrate concerted courtship in Drosophila
papers.abstract: Abstract Mating decisions are often attributed to the sensory signalling between prospective sexual partners. Yet these interactions are also shaped by the broader environmental context in which they unfold, to appropriately align sexual arousal with reproductive opportunities 1–6 . Here we show that in Drosophila erecta mating is strictly contingent on the ecological and social environment generated as flies densely aggregate in groups on a food patch. We find that food volatiles directly promote male sexual arousal, triggering individuals to sample and pursue potential mates, giving rise to dynamic interactions across the group. The ensuing visual motion transforms each male’s visual field, which in turn further amplifies his arousal, generating a multisensory feedback loop that coordinately promotes courtship across individuals. D. erecta ’s strict dependence on environmental cues appears latent in related species, such as Drosophila melanogaster , where food odour can promote arousal 7 but is dispensable for vigorous courtship. Comparative circuit analyses show that species-specific thresholds for sexual arousal reflect variation in how olfactory input modulates conserved nodes controlling courtship drive, rendering food volatiles a strict sensory gate only in D. erecta . Together, our findings highlight how environmental cues not directly tied to sexual signalling can profoundly influence reproductive behaviour and reorganize the social landscape to ensure mating occurs in contexts where reproductive opportunities are abundant.

papers.title: Venousization enables angiogenesis in the absence of VEGFR signalling
papers.abstract: Abstract The VEGF ligand and its main receptor VEGFR2 are considered to be essential for endothelial differentiation, proliferation, sprouting and survival. Blood vessels cannot form in growing embryos or tissues when VEGF/VEGFR2 signalling is compromised in all cells. The Anti-VEGF blocking antibody is one of the most widely used antibodies in the clinics, blocking angiogenesis in cancer, wound healing or in ischemic diseases. However, vascular resistance to Anti-VEGF has been reported. Here we used iFlpMosaics and iSuRe-HadCre to induce and track genetic mosaics of endothelial cells (ECs) lacking VEGFR2 during the entire embryonic and postnatal development. Surprisingly, Vegfr2 KO ECs adapt, proliferate normally and compete with wild-type cells over time, ultimately forming a substantial portion of the capillary network in most organs. We found that Vegfr2 KO ECs are not able to sprout during the first wave of angiogenesis in most tissues, because it is highly VEGF-dependent and favours the growth and mobilization of wild-type ECs. However, due to their inability to respond to VEGF, over time Vegfr2 KO ECs become dominant in veins, which provide for a long term and continuous source of ECs for subsequent waves of VEGF-independent angiogenesis. Comparative scRNAseq analysis of ECs with acute and long-term loss of VEGFR2, revealed both common and organ-specific molecular mechanisms of adaptation and resistance to VEGF signalling loss. This included significant endothelial venousization and the upregulation of ligands for VEGFR1 and VEGFR3. VEGFR1 only partially compensated for VEGFR2 loss in capillary ECs, whereas VEGFR3 only compensated in arterial ECs. Loss of the three VEGF receptors did not compromise venous growth. This work changes our understanding of the role of VEGF signaling and its receptors in angiogenesis and reveals mechanisms of adaptation and resistance to their loss.

papers.title: Towards observing interstitial hydrogen in solution in metal lattices
papers.abstract: Abstract Hydrogen-bearing materials are central to low-carbon energy technologies 1 , but hydrogen itself is difficult to detect and localize at the nanoscale 2–6 . This hinders the development of advanced materials with better efficiency. Atom probe tomography (APT) can map hydrogen in three dimensions and at high resolution, yet characterization of dilute, mobile, interstitial hydrogen in metals has remained challenging because of low solubility, the ambiguity owing to hydrogen trapping by structural defects, as well as the artefacts introduced during hydrogen introduction 4–6 . Here we address whether interstitial hydrogen in solution in materials can be distinguished from defect-trapped hydrogen in APT. Using deuterium as a proxy for hydrogen, together with face-centred cubic (FCC) multi-principal-element alloys (MPEAs) containing coherent FCC precipitates, we show that deuterium atoms reproducibly concentrate in hydrogen-affinitive phases in a manner consistent with theoretical predictions. We further resolve differences in deuterium content between phases with distinct local chemistries and crystal structures, consistent with their different calculated hydrogen solution energies. These findings demonstrate that APT can move beyond identifying hydrides and solute-decorated defects to examine hydrogen in solid solution, providing new insights into hydrogen partitioning in structural alloys and informing materials design for hydrogen-related applications.

papers.title: A two-dimensional reticular triaxial molecularly woven fabric
Microbiome-wide PheWAS links gut microbial SNVs to health and exposures
papers.abstract: Abstract The importance of the gut microbiome in human health has been widely recognized, with alterations in species abundances now reported for many different diseases. In recent years, observations of within-species genetic diversity and strain-level functional differences have urged the field to transition to analyzing microbes at the genetic level, taking advantage of genetic variants in the metagenome to pinpoint relevant genes and pathways. Here, we conducted a phenome-wide association study (PheWAS) of 12.7 million gut microbial single nucleotide variants (SNVs) with 244 host health phenotypes and environmental exposures in 10,781 individuals from six independent cohorts from Europe and Africa. We found 3,018 associations supported by at least two cohorts for 105 host factors, including age, sex and cardiovascular and metabolic parameters. Moreover, we found 34,927 significant associations in single-cohort analyses where SNV–phenotype pairs were only available for one cohort. All identified associations are detailed in an online catalog (https://fulab.web.rug.nl/SNV-MWAS/). The associated microbial SNVs inform mechanistic hypotheses about microbial functionality in human health and provide insights into microbial adaptation and evolution in response to changes in the environment and host physiology. For example, we identified 718 age-associated gut microbial SNVs across multiple cohorts and used these microbial SNVs to accurately predict host age. We also identified SNVs in microbial genes associated with lipid concentrations and BMI, including SNVs in the isoleucine-tRNA synthetase gene of Clostridium phoceensis and an α-Melanocyte-stimulating hormone-mimicking clpB gene of Alistipes ihumii. Mediation analysis provided evidence that microbial genetic variations may be under selection enforced by environmental factors, but also that they mediate the effects on the host, e.g. the isoleucyl-tRNA synthetase gene of C. phoceensis mediated dietary effects on four phenotypes. Overall, this study identifies new biological connections between human host and microbial genetic variants, exposing the functional layer of gut microbiome data hidden at base pair resolution and revealing microbial adaptation and evolution in relation to host lifestyle and physiology.

papers.title: An open structure-guided RNA foundation model for generalizable prediction
papers.abstract: Abstract RNA language models have achieved strong performances across diverse downstream tasks by leveraging large-scale sequence data. However, RNA function is fundamentally shaped by its hierarchical structure, making the integration of structural information into pre-training essential. Existing methods often depend on noisy structural annotations or introduce task-specific biases, limiting model generalizability. Here, we introduce structRFM, a structure-guided RNA foundation model that is pre-trained on millions of RNA sequences and secondary structures data by integrating base pairing interactions into masked language modeling through a novel pair matching operation. The structure-guided mask and nucleotide-level mask are further balanced by a dynamic masking ratio. structRFM learns joint knowledge of sequential and structural data, producing versatile representations, including classification-level, sequence-level, and pairwise matrix features, that support a broad spectrum of downstream adaptations. structRFM ranks among the top models in zero-shot homology classification across fifteen biological language models, and sets new benchmarks for secondary structure prediction. structRFM further derives Zfold, which enables robust and reliable tertiary structure prediction, with consistent improvements in estimating 3D structures and their accordingly extracted 2D structures, achieving a pronounced 19% performance gain compared with AlphaFold3 on RNA Puzzles dataset. In functional tasks such as internal ribosome entry site identification, structRFM achieves a whopping 49% performance gain in F1 score. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of structure-guided pre-training and highlight a promising direction for developing multi-modal RNA language models in computational biology. To support the broader scientific community, we have made the 21-million sequence-structure dataset and the pre-trained structRFM model fully open-source, facilitating the development of multimodal foundation models in biology.

papers.title: A conserved flowering-time module underlies double-season cropping
Nectin-4 mediates rubella virus entry in airway and placental cells
papers.abstract: Abstract Rubella virus (RuV) causes rubella and, when acquired during pregnancy, congenital rubella syndrome (CRS). Despite its clinical significance, the cellular entry mechanism of RuV remains poorly characterized owing to limited knowledge of host receptors, hampering pathogenesis studies and therapeutic development. Here, we identify Nectin-4 as a functional RuV entry receptor through proximity biotin labeling-based proteomics coupled with CRISPR/Cas9 validation. Notably, Nectin-4 is shared with measles virus, revealing convergent evolution in viral entry despite the different viral families. Nectin-4 directly interacts with the RuV envelope glycoproteins through its ectodomain, facilitating receptor-mediated endocytosis following initial calcium-dependent viral attachment. In polarized respiratory epithelial cells, Nectin-4 mediates basolateral viral entry and subsequent apical release of progeny virions, enabling efficient respiratory transmission. Using human placental organoid models, we demonstrate that syncytiotrophoblasts serve as primary targets for transplacental RuV infection, with viral entry significantly inhibited by Nectin-4 blockade. These findings establish Nectin-4 as critical for both horizontal respiratory transmission and vertical maternal–fetal transmission of RuV. Our results provide fundamental insights into RuV pathogenesis and identify Nectin-4 as a promising therapeutic target for CRS. Importantly, the discovery of shared receptor utilization between RuV and measles virus opens new avenues for integrated elimination strategies targeting both pathogens.

papers.title: A spatiotemporal cancer cell trajectory underlies glioblastoma heterogeneity
papers.abstract: Abstract Cancer cells display highly heterogeneous and plastic states in glioblastoma, an incurable brain tumour. However, how these malignant states arise and whether they follow defined cellular trajectories across tumours is poorly understood. Here, we generated a deep single cell and spatial multi-omic atlas of human glioblastoma that pairs transcriptomic, epigenomic and genomic profiling of 12 tumours across multiple regions. We identify that glioblastoma heterogeneity is driven by spatially-patterned transitions of cancer cells from developmental-like states towards those defined by a glial injury response and hypoxia. This cellular trajectory regionalises tumours into distinct tissue niches and manifests in a molecularly conserved manner across tumours as well as genetically distinct tumour subclones. Moreover, using a new deep learning framework to map cancer cell states jointly with clones in situ , we show that tumour subclones are finely spatially intermixed through glioblastoma tissue niches. Finally, we show that this cancer cell trajectory is intimately linked to myeloid heterogeneity and unfolds across regionalised myeloid signalling environments. Our findings define a stereotyped trajectory of cancer cells in glioblastoma and unify glioblastoma tumour heterogeneity into a tractable cellular and tissue framework.

papers.title: Transcriptomic convergence and the female protective effect in autism
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is highly heritable, and mutations in hundreds of genes have been implicated as individually rare causes of ASD 1–3 . Understanding how disruptions to these functionally diverse genes lead to the core features of ASD remains a major challenge 4 . Moreover, ASD is three- to four-fold more common in males than females 5 , and autistic females tend to carry more autosomal risk alleles for ASD compared to autistic males 6,7 , but the biological basis of this “female protective effect” (FPE) is unknown 8,9 . Here we show that individual perturbations of 18 ASD genes in human neural progenitor cells converge on shared effects on gene expression, including widespread downregulation of other ASD genes. De novo reconstruction of a gene regulatory network (GRN) enabled the identification of central transcriptional regulators, including the prominent ASD gene CHD8 as well as novel candidates such as REST , that drive this transcriptomic convergence. Furthermore, the X-linked transcription factor ZFX , which is expressed from both the active and the inactive X chromosomes in females 10 , emerged as a key activator of many ASD genes: we propose that the higher ZFX expression level observed in female brain can buffer damaging mutations in diverse ASD genes, contributing to the FPE. Together, these results reveal how key GRNs can become broadly and similarly dysregulated upon disruption of individual ASD genes and provide molecular insight into the female protective effect in ASD.

papers.title: The neural basis of flavour–nutrient learning
Hard X-ray attosecond metrology

Comprehensive mapping of essential-gene interactions in M. tuberculosis
papers.abstract: Abstract Mycobacterium tuberculosis , the causative agent of tuberculosis, remains the world’s deadliest pathogen 1 . Despite intensive study, many of its genes remain uncharacterized, which limits the insight that can be gained into tuberculosis biology and constrains drug development. Genetic interaction (GI) mapping is a powerful strategy to define functional relationships between genes by quantifying how the phenotypic effects of combined perturbations deviate from expectations based on single-gene perturbations 2,3 . Here we develop a dual-sgRNA CRISPR-interference platform that enables high-throughput GI mapping in mycobacteria. We address key technical challenges in library construction and data interpretation by incorporating unique barcodes for each sgRNA pair and implementing a robust statistical pipeline for GI detection. Focusing on essential genes, we generate comprehensive GI maps in the model mycobacterium Mycobacterium smegmatis and the pathogen M. tuberculosis . These maps recapitulate known biology, uncover thousands of previously unrecognized interactions and identify functional connections between essential genes and drug targets. By generating AlphaFold3-based protein–protein interaction predictions 4 for all gene pairs in our GI maps, we show that a subset of GIs is likely to reflect underlying physical associations. Validation of selected GIs confirms both novel biological relationships and opportunities for synergistic targeting. Overall, this work establishes a generalizable framework for dual-gene perturbation and defines the architecture of essential-gene networks in mycobacteria, advancing both our understanding of tuberculosis biology and the rational design of combination therapies.

papers.title: Aggression experience and observation drive shared behavioural and neural changes
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The ability to observe the social behavior of others and use observed information to bias future action is a fundamental building block of social cognition 1,2 . A foundational question is whether social observation and experience engage common circuit mechanisms that enable behavioral change. While classic studies on social learning have shown that aggressive behaviors can be learned through observation 3 , it remains unclear whether aggression observation promotes persistent neural changes that generalize to new contexts. Here, to directly compare the effects of aggression experience and observation at brain-wide scale, we develop a strategy to perform large-scale cell-type specific recordings across subcortical networks for social behavior control and learning. We record longitudinally while animals “train” through direct experience or observation, then probe shared differences in behavior and neural activity in a novel “hard” aggression context. Using supervised and unsupervised methods for behavioral quantification, we detect unique signatures of a shared behavioral strategy not present in animals with no training. During observation, we find widespread activation that mimics experience in networks for behavior generation, with critical differences in signals associated with reward and threat learning. After observation, we observe that changes persist into the novel aggression context, with increased similarity in the neural dynamics between experience and observation groups. Network-level modeling reveals persistent shared changes to a core aggression network, with widespread decoupling of inhibition from a key hypothalamic output region. This demonstrates that “experience-like” activity during observation can recruit a shared plasticity mechanism that biases behavior toward adaptive defensive strategies in new contexts.

papers.title: Twist-angle-dependent quantum phase diagrams in moiré bilayer MoTe2
Synergy in viral–bacterial co-infection expedites algal bloom demise
papers.abstract: Algal blooms are hotspots for diverse microbial interactions affecting bloom dynamics. Viral infections often regulate the demise of these blooms, recycling >25% of oceanic fixed carbon. Although these blooms collapse synchronously, only 10-30% of algal cells show active viral infection, suggesting additional mortality agents. Using microbial communities from natural coccolithophore blooms, we discovered that bacteria significantly enhanced virus-mediated algal mortality. We quantified this interaction using two novel metrics: the Synergy Index (SI) measuring viral-bacterial interaction strength, and the Benefit Index (BI) assessing changes in bacterial fitness. We identified Alteromonas bacteria as drivers of viral-bacterial coinfection, with consistently high SI and BI. In natural communities, Alteromonas exhibited chemoattraction towards infected algal cells, leading to their enrichment in bloom demise particles. This viral-bacterial synergy represents a previously unrecognized mortality agent controlling bloom termination, modulating the balance between the carbon-recycling viral shunt and the carbon-exporting viral shuttle pathways, likely influencing global carbon cycling.

Faint exoplanets detected using computational approach to remove glare from stars
papers.abstract: An image-processing framework for detecting exoplanets directly has been developed. The technique overcomes the telescope-stability barrier that has limited previous methods, reveals fainter exoplanets than other approaches can detect and could make imaging exo-Earths easier for future observatories. A physics-based model enables the observation of exoplanets that were undetectable using standard techniques.

X-ray stopwatch can measure durations of just attoseconds
papers.abstract: The duration of short ångström-wavelength X-ray pulses, which lasted merely 170 attoseconds, has finally been measured accurately. The optical system designed for precision pulse duration metrology can be used as a ‘stopwatch’ to measure the rapid motion of electrons inside atoms and molecules, too. Short pulses generated by the system could be used to observe electrons moving around atomic nuclei.
