papers.abstract: Abstract Electrocatalytic nitrate reduction reaction (NO3RR) has attracted growing interest for converting nitrate (NO3–) into ammonium (NH4+), yet NH4+ production from dilute, low-conductivity waters is constrained by high energy consumption, limited NO3– availability, and costly product recovery. Steering NO3RR directly toward benign N2 therefore represents a more practical route, but this pathway is often suppressed by excessive surface *H coverage, which drives the overhydrogenation of nitrogen intermediates to NH4+. Here, we report a mild oxidant-assisted coelectrolysis strategy that regulates interfacial *H coverage and promotes NO3–-to-N2 conversion in a Cu nanoparticle-decorated Ni cathode membrane electrochemical reactor. This reactor separates a highly conductive electrochemical chamber from a NO3–-containing chemical chamber, enabling NO3– reduction in low-conductivity media while maintaining a less negative cathodic potential. Mild oxidants, including H2O2, O2, CH3COOOH, and KIO4, consumed excess *H and redirected the reaction pathway toward N–N coupling. With H2O2 as a representative oxidant, N2 selectivity increased from 13.47% without H2O2 to 87.25% at 100 mM H2O2. Mechanistic analyses revealed that H2O2 decreases interfacial *H abundance, which suppresses NH4+ formation and facilitates the dimerization of nitrogen-containing intermediates. Verification in real low-conductivity groundwater further supports this strategy as a mechanistic basis for designing selective, low-energy electrochemical denitrification systems for low-conductivity NO3–-contaminated media.

papers.title: Waste as Feedstock, Electrolyte, and Target: Closing the Loop in Electrochemical H2O2 Water Treatment
papers.abstract: Abstract Electrochemical H2O2 production is increasingly positioned as an on-site route for water oxidation, disinfection, and resource recovery. However, its environmental translation remains constrained by a basic design mismatch between catalyst development in clean electrolytes and deployment in chemically variable waste streams. This Perspective argues that progress should move beyond catalyst-centered performance metrics toward a closed-loop, waste-centered framework. The key issue is not how to isolate H2O2 electrosynthesis from wastewater complexity but when and how that complexity can be engineered. Solid and liquid waste streams can provide carbon, heteroatoms, and metals for impurity-resilient electrodes. Meanwhile, wastewater constituents can regulate interfacial ion distribution, water structure, oxygen transport, proton availability, intermediate stabilization, and side reactions. Electrogenerated H2O2 can be routed to contaminant transformation, disinfection, detoxification, and metal recovery. We discuss design principles for converting heterogeneous waste feedstocks into catalytic interfaces, defining wastewater operating windows, matching reactor architectures with real water matrices, and evaluating circularity through life-cycle and techno-economic accounting. We identify critical benchmarks─matrix descriptors, durability mechanisms, byproduct control, reactor-treatment matching, and transparent environmental safeguards─needed to turn circular H2O2 concepts into verifiable water-treatment technologies.

papers.title: Evaluating Individual Infection Risk: The Interplay between Air Mixing Intensities and Occupant Dynamics
papers.abstract: Abstract Aerosol transmission remains a critical route for the spread of respiratory infectious diseases, yet real-time exposure mapping in complex public spaces is computationally demanding. This study presents a robust and adaptable framework for estimating dynamic individual exposure (i.e., viral dose) by integrating high-fidelity computational fluid dynamics (CFD) with computer vision (CV) analysis. By overlaying validated steady-state viral aerosol plumes onto dynamic human interaction data, we evaluated the interplay between airflow patterns and human behaviors under two distinct air change rates (ACH: 25 h–1 and 3 h–1). Each scenario was simulated both with and without MERV-13 filtration. Applications in both a stochastic-movement hotel meeting room and a stationary-occupant office demonstrate that while high turbulence due to high ACH limits the spatial extent of plumes, sustained close proximity in structured settings can result in disproportionately high viral doses for specific individuals. MERV-13 filtration effectively reduced exposure within high-concentration zones. We propose a Reynolds number (Re)-based modeling guideline: steady-state CFD-CV for moderate mixing (900 ≤ Re ≤ 2300), a well-mixed assumption for high mixing (Re > 2300), and transient CFD-CV for low mixing (500 ≤ Re < 900) during breathing and speaking, and steady-state CFD-CV for coughing and sneezing regardless of Re value. This framework supports real-time monitoring and targeted interventions, providing a data-driven foundation for indoor occupant safety.

papers.title: Light-Induced Formation of Volatile Organic Compounds from Bleach Cleaning in Indoor Environments
papers.abstract: Abstract Surface bleach cleaning is a common indoor activity that releases abundant strong oxidants, including hypochlorous acid (HOCl) and chlorine gas (Cl2), which can significantly influence indoor chemistry. While bleach-driven chemical transformations are recognized, the specific role of illumination remains poorly understood. This study combines field measurements and laboratory flow tube experiments to investigate volatile organic compound (VOC) formation from reactions between bleach emissions and surface-sorbed species, e.g., kitchen-derived organic films, under illuminated conditions. In real-world indoor settings, we observed that bleach cleaning under light predominantly generates oxygenated VOCs (OVOCs), accounting for ∼92% of total emissions. Saturated carbonyls contributed the most (∼82%), such as C6H12O, C9H18O, and C2H4O. Flow tube experiments using surrogate compounds and kitchen-collected surface films confirmed that OVOCs are generated via heterogeneous reactions between surface-bound organics (e.g., fatty acids, amides, amino acids) and radicals produced from photolysis of bleach-derived oxidants. VOC production was found to depend on surface accumulation and aging, with more accumulated and aged surfaces producing greater quantities and more diverse products. These findings provide important insights into VOC production from indoor surface chemistry initiated by bleach cleaning under typical indoor lighting conditions, advancing our understanding of volatile byproduct formation from indoor bleach photochemistry.

papers.title: Ammonia Triggers Interfacial Breakpoint Chlorination to Enhance Micropollutant Degradation and Reshapes Chlorinated Byproduct Formation during Electrochlorination
papers.abstract: Abstract Electrochlorination is a promising technology for micropollutant degradation in decentralized water treatment. However, ammonia can alter chlorine chemistry. This study investigates the effect of ammonia on micropollutant degradation and chlorinated byproduct formation during electrochlorination using the RuO2/IrO2–Ti anode. Compared to electrochlorination at 10 mM chloride without ammonia, the presence of 1 mM ammonia increased the degradation rate constants of metronidazole and carbamazepine by 2.7- and 4.5-fold, respectively. This enhancement is consistent with interfacial breakpoint chlorination, defined as preferential chlorine–ammonia conversion within an anode-adjacent, chlorine-rich aqueous diffusion layer before complete bulk mixing. During electrochlorination with ammonia, dissolved HO• contributed to micropollutant degradation. Electron paramagnetic resonance provided qualitative evidence of HO• formation, whereas nitrobenzene was used as a probe to quantify its steady-state concentration. The ammonia-induced steady-state HO• concentration reached 2.4 × 10–13 M at 1 mM ammonia, whereas the HO• contribution was negligible without ammonia. Meanwhile, 1–5 mM ammonia reduced the total yields of chlorinated byproducts by only 25–31% during electrochlorination. The limited suppression is consistent with concurrent competition between ammonia and dissolved organic matter for locally generated chlorine within the anode-adjacent region. These findings identify near-anode chlorine–ammonia conversion as a route to reactive-species formation and micropollutant degradation, while showing that chlorinated byproducts remain a concern in ammonia-containing electrochlorination systems.

papers.title: Source or Sink: Bioanalytical and Chemical Profiling of New and Field-Weathered Plastics
papers.abstract: Abstract Plastics contain complex mixtures of chemicals that can leach into the aquatic environment. Conversely, the high sorption capacity of certain polymers renders plastics passive samplers for environmental pollutants from ambient waters. We evaluated whether effects from chemicals that are extractable or leachable from plastics from the North Pacific Ocean are dominated by plastic-associated or sorbed environmental compounds. First, bioanalytical profiling of chemical mixtures from solvent extracts of field-weathered marine plastics in cell-based bioassays was compared to that of chemicals from solvent extracts of newly purchased counterparts of the field plastics. Second, the new plastics were artificially UV-weathered and solvent-extracted, and the leachate waters were enriched with solid-phase extraction and dosed into a test battery of four in vitro bioassays where activation of the arylhydrocarbon receptor, oxidative stress response, and/or cytotoxicity were most responsive. Finally, chemical screening was performed using high-resolution mass spectrometry with subsequent mixture effect modeling to identify toxicity drivers. The results showed a multifaceted picture: Newly purchased high-durability outdoor products caused higher effects before weathering, whereas food packaging tended to show increased effects after field weathering. The analyzed chemicals could partially explain the observed effects (<0.1–98%). Our study underlines the relevance of field weathering for marine plastics and their potential to leach chemicals of concern into the environment.

papers.title: Spatially Coupled •H-involved Reductive Decomplexation of Cu(II)–EDTA for Sludge-Free Copper Recovery
papers.abstract: Abstract The electrochemical recovery of metals from stable complexes is often limited by the accessibility of coordinated metal centers at the electrode interface. Here, we develop a polyaniline-modified carbon felt (PANI@CF) cathode to regulate the interfacial microenvironment for selective Cu recovery from copper(II)–ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid (Cu(II)–EDTA). The PANI interface couples Cu(II)–EDTA enrichment with •H generation through complementary nitrogen functionalities, thereby promoting Cu(II)–EDTA decomplexation while preserving ligand integrity. Under optimized conditions, PANI@CF achieves high Cu recovery (up to 99.9%) over a broad Cu(II)–EDTA concentration range (0.5–5 mM) and pH range (3–11), with a 32.75-fold enhancement in the apparent reaction rate compared with pristine carbon felt. Mechanistic investigations reveal that imine (–N═) functionalities contribute to interfacial Cu(II)–EDTA enrichment, whereas amine (–NH–) functionalities facilitate N–H activation and •H generation. This spatial coupling promotes interactions between short-lived •H and coordinated Cu centers, weakening Cu(II)–EDTA coordination and facilitating Cu reduction while preserving EDTA integrity. After ten consecutive treatment cycles, the cumulative Cu recovery reached 215.07 mg cm–2, and the PANI@CF electrode was regenerated by mild acid washing. The selective recovery of Cu and EDTA was further demonstrated in actual electroplating wastewater. This work highlights interfacial regulation through spatial coupling as a strategy for overcoming accessibility limitations in the electrochemical transformation of metal–ligand complexes and supports selective resource recovery from complexed industrial effluents.

papers.title: Molecular Interactions between Styrene Oligomers and Human Serum Albumin: A Multiscale Computational Study of a Plastic-Derived Environmental Contaminant
papers.abstract: Abstract Micro- and nanoplastics are pervasive environmental pollutants known to accumulate in human organs. While the hazards of larger plastic particles are under intense investigation, the toxicological impact of molecular-level plastic oligomers with dimensions around 1 nm is a critical and underexplored area. This study provides a comprehensive molecular-level in silico characterization of the binding interactions between styrene oligomers (1–7 units) and HSA, characterizing their molecular basis and its potential relevance to HSA’s ligand transport function. A multilevel computational approach was employed, integrating molecular docking, MD simulations, DFT, MM/PBSA binding free energy calculations, and ProLIF interaction fingerprinting. FA1 accommodated 82–95% of the most favorable docking poses for oligomers containing three to seven styrene units and exhibited the lowest docking scores, reaching −11.9 kcal·mol–1, compared with −6.4 kcal·mol–1 for the monomer. MD simulations confirmed the structural stability of oligomer-HSA complexes, further supported by dynamic cross-correlation, principal component, and solvent-accessible surface area analyses. Quantum biochemistry analyses further confirmed FA1 as the most energetically favorable binding pocket, with an average interaction energy of −117.47 kcal·mol–1 compared with −73.96 kcal·mol–1 for FA6, a hierarchy independently reproduced by MM/PBSA calculations (R = 0.82). For the hexamer and heptamer, FA1 exhibited energetic advantages of 27.39 and 21.84 kcal·mol–1, respectively. These findings indicate that HSA binds styrene oligomers with high stability and affinity at FA1, providing a molecular basis for further investigation of their potential relevance to ligand transport and systemic exposure to plastic-derived contaminants.

papers.title: Soil Mineral Coatings on Biodegradable Microplastics: Formation and Control of Enzymatic Degradation
papers.abstract: Abstract In agriculture, biodegradable plastics weather and fragment into microplastics that inevitably acquire mineral coatings. However, the impact of mineral coatings on microplastic degradation remains poorly understood. We examined coating formation and enzymatic degradation of pristine and photoaged poly(butylene adipate-co-terephthalate) microplastics (PBAT-MPs) in loessial soil and red soil under drought, moist, alternate wetting-drying, and flooded regimes during 64 days. Soil type, moisture, and photoaging governed coating accumulation. Loessial soil produced greater Al and Fe loading on PBAT-MPs than red soil, while unsaturated regimes increased Al and Fe by 394%–1109% relative to flooding (p < 0.05). Synchrotron micro-X-ray fluorescence combined with absorption near-edge structure spectroscopy analyses showed heterogeneous elemental distributions and mineral speciation on PBAT-MPs that resembled those of the source soils. Unexpectedly, loessial-soil coatings increased PBAT-MPs’ terephthalic acid and adipic acid release by 9.1%–17.4% and reduced residual PBAT mass by 6.5%–23.5% (p < 0.05). Kinetic analyses showed that although mineral coatings slowed enzyme adsorption via diffusion limitations, localized leaching of Ca2+ from the coatings enhanced cutinase activity and outweighed this physical constraint. These findings demonstrate that mineral coatings can regulate the enzymatic degradation of PBAT, providing new insights into the environmental fate of biodegradable microplastics in agricultural soils.

papers.title: Interfacial Triplet-Energy Funneling Directs Energy-Transfer-Mediated Singlet Oxygen Generation for Deep Toluene Mineralization
papers.abstract: Abstract Photocatalytic oxidation is a promising strategy for volatile organic compounds (VOCs) abatement, but incomplete mineralization and carbonaceous intermediate accumulation remain major challenges, especially when conventional charge-transfer pathways generate nonselective radical reactive oxygen species. Selective activation of molecular oxygen toward singlet oxygen (1O2) offers a potential route to controlled oxidation, yet efficient energy-transfer-mediated 1O2 generation in solid-state photocatalysts remains difficult to achieve. Herein, a strongly coupled In(OH)3/ZnGa2O4 heterojunction with an electronic structure consistent with an S-scheme configuration is constructed to investigate interfacial excited-state regulation. Spectroscopic measurements indicate modified excited-state relaxation and a reduced effective singlet–triplet energy separation, which may favor singlet-to-triplet conversion. Combined spectroscopic analyses, quenching experiments, and density functional theory calculations support a proposed interfacial triplet-energy-funneling pathway involving ZnGa2O4-related/interfacial triplet-related states and subsequent energy transfer to adsorbed O2 for 1O2 generation. As a result, the optimized In(OH)3/ZnGa2O4 photocatalyst achieves 98.3% toluene removal and 92.4% mineralization in a continuous-flow gas-phase reactor, together with excellent cycling stability and humidity tolerance. Mechanistic results further suggest that a pathway involving 1O2 contributes to methyl oxidation and the subsequent conversion of oxygenated intermediates, potentially limiting carbonaceous residue accumulation. This work provides an excited-state-engineering strategy for selective molecular oxygen activation and offers a promising route toward efficient, durable, and deeply mineralizing photocatalytic VOCs abatement.

papers.title: Suppressing Proton Affinity of Surface Oxygen for Enhanced N2 Selectivity in Mn-Based NH3–SCR Catalysts
papers.abstract: Abstract Inferior N2 selectivity remains a critical challenge for Mn-based catalysts in NH3–SCR denitration. Here, using atomically dispersed Mn on anatase (Mn1/TiO2) and MnO2 as model catalysts, we elucidate the origin of surface oxygen activity and the role of surface oxygen in the formation of N2O. Both catalysts achieved >99% NO conversion in the temperature range of 175–300 °C (WHSV = 60,000 mL·g–1·h–1). Compared with the poor selectivity of α-MnO2 (1.2% at 300 °C), Mn1/TiO2 maintained >88.0% N2 selectivity in 50–300 °C. Density functional theory calculations revealed that the high affinity of surface oxygen for protons results in overoxidation of NH3-derived intermediates, thus promoting N2O formation. Orbital interaction analysis manifested that surface oxygen activity in octahedrally coordinated catalysts depends on the spin polarization in transition-metal 3d bands. Atomic dispersion of Mn sites on oxides with nonspin-polarized dxy orbitals was demonstrated as a universal strategy to boost N2 selectivity. This work deepens the fundamental understanding of surface oxygen activity in catalysts, paving a way for designing Mn-based catalysts with excellent N2 selectivity.

papers.title: UV328 Promotes Plastisphere Formation on Microplastics through Quorum-Sensing-Associated Signaling Interference
papers.abstract: Abstract Microplastics have created an expanding anthropogenic microbial niche known as the plastisphere, yet the mechanisms by which plastic additives influence these microbial assemblies remain poorly understood. Here, we show that UV328, a ubiquitous benzotriazole stabilizer recently listed in the Stockholm Convention, may be associated with quorum sensing signaling that accelerates plastisphere formation, biomass accumulation, and extracellular polymeric substance production on microplastics. In UV328-exposed polystyrene and polylactic acid plastisphere, the total expression levels of biofilm formation genes are upregulated by 1.38- to 2.94-fold compared to the control and quorum quenching manipulations. Molecular dynamics simulations predict that UV328 structurally mimics N-acyl-homoserine lactone (AHL) and may plausibly occupy ligand-binding domains of the quorum sensing receptor SdiA and CciR with favorable energetics. UV328 exposure was further associated with the upregulation of genes involved in bacterial chemotaxis, flagellar assembly, and central carbon metabolism. This physiological reprogramming alters community assembly trajectories and leads to a protein-rich plastisphere phenotype that was reversible by enzymatic quorum quenching, potentially supporting the involvement of AHL-sensitive processes. Our findings suggest that UV328 can alter plastisphere development through signaling-associated ecological processes, raising the possibility that microplastics may function as chemically active interfaces and highlighting microbial signaling interference as an overlooked dimension of the ecological risks associated with plastic additives in aquatic ecosystems.

papers.title: Coal Tar-Based Driveway Sealant Extract Induces Mutations in Liver, Bone Marrow, and Germ Cells of MutaMouse Male Mice
papers.abstract: Abstract Coal tar-based driveway sealants (CTS) are a widespread but underrecognized source of human exposure to mutagenic polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs). We used Duplex Sequencing, an error-corrected sequencing technology, to assess the mutagenicity of a complex PAH mixture extracted from a CTS in MutaMouse male mice. We observed significant dose-dependent increases in mutation frequency (MF) in liver and bone marrow, with mutation spectra dominated by C:G > A:T substitutions, closely resembling a mutational signature linked to human cancers associated with tobacco smoking. In germ cells, we did not observe a statistically significant increase in MF, although there was a positive dose–response trend and enrichment of C:G > A:T mutations at higher doses. The mutagenic effects of CTS in germ cells were supported by a statistically significant increase in mutant frequency measured using the plaque-based lacZ assay. Tissue-specific analyses revealed greater mutation susceptibility and potency in liver, likely reflecting its central role in PAH metabolism. Mutation spectrum analysis showed that the mutagenic profile of the CTS extract largely resembled that of benzo(a)pyrene; however, detailed spectral analysis indicated additional contributions from other PAHs or PAH metabolites that produced distinct mutational patterns. Collectively, our findings demonstrate that the CTS extract induces tissue-specific mutagenic responses driven by characteristic C:G > A:T mutations, offering mechanistic insight into how environmental PAH mixtures contribute to mutation burden and cancer risk.

Future environmental impacts of EU permanent magnet demand: a combined prospective MFA-LCA assessment
papers.abstract: Advancing climate change necessitates a transformation of the mobility and energy sector towards low-carbon technologies. Rare earth element-containing permanent magnets (PMs), a key component in efficient electric machines, are currently produced in only a few countries and not efficiently recycled, motivating efforts to diversify supply by establishing domestic recycling routes. This study inspects the projected environmental impacts of PM value chains, thereby providing context to transitioning from a geographically concentrated, linear value chain towards a circular value chain in the European Union. Combining material flow analysis (MFA) and prospective life cycle assessment (LCA), the emissions from 2025 to 2100 are estimated under alternative production and recycling scenarios. Results show that i) future impacts of PM production will increasingly depend on the footprint of the material, ii) guaranteeing high magnetic performance during the use phase is key to achieving environmental benefits of circular value chains, iii) end-of-life products can become a relevant source for PM materials if recycling technologies and value chains are developed, and iv) recycling material substitution rates strongly influence overall results. The article showcases how to meaningfully combine LCA and MFA in dynamic system studies and demonstrates the cumulative environmental benefits of diversifying PM supply. Findings support ongoing EU efforts to strengthen domestic critical raw material supply and circular economy strategies.

Well-to-wake climate performance of e-fuels in aviation based on life cycle assessment
papers.abstract: Aviation causes about 3.5% of effective anthropogenic radiative forcing. About two-thirds of this comes from non-CO 2 short-lived climate forcers (SLCFs), which current aviation policy does not yet regulate. This study compares the well-to-wake climate impact of e-kerosene, liquid hydrogen and ammonia, each made with wind or solar electricity, with that of conventional jet fuel (CJF). Contrail cirrus, NO x , water vapour, hydrogen and ammonia slip and N 2 O are included and assessed with four metrics: ATR 20 , ATR 100 , GWP 20 and GWP 100 . SLCFs cause 83% of the tank-to-wake impact of CJF under ATR 20 and 96–100% of that of the alternative fuels. Liquid hydrogen made with wind electricity has the lowest impact under all four metrics. It is 181.3 gCO 2 -eq·MJ −1 under ATR 20 (60% below CJF) and 58.0 gCO 2 -eq·MJ −1 under GWP 100 (66% below CJF). Per passenger-km, a long-range hydrogen aircraft that uses 42% more energy is still 46–59% below CJF if contrail cirrus is counted per kilometre. E-kerosene made with wind electricity is 26–53% below CJF. Ammonia made with wind electricity is only 7% (ATR 20 ) to 36% (GWP 100 ) below CJF at a NO x emission of 10 g·kg −1 , and above CJF under ATR 20 at more than 11.1 g·kg −1 . Under GWP 100 , the e-fuels are below CJF only with electricity below 126 (ammonia), 143 (e-kerosene) or 233 (liquid hydrogen) gCO 2 -eq·kWh −1 . At the 2025 EU grid average of 209 gCO 2 -eq·kWh −1 , e-kerosene and ammonia would therefore be worse than CJF. Fuel policy should include SLCFs and require additional renewable electricity.

papers.title: Experimental analysis of effects of load, intake pressure and equivalence ratio on a Semi-Closed Cycle Oxy-Fuel Combustion engine for carbon capture purposes
papers.abstract: In this paper, an experimental evaluation was conducted to determine the effect of engine load, intake pressure, and the O2-to-fuel ratio (λ) on a Semi-Closed Cycle Oxy-Fuel Combustion (SCC-OFC) reciprocating internal combustion engine (RICE). To this end, tests were carried out at low and mid-high loads in a commercial compression ignition (CI) RICE retrofitted to OFC, sweeping intake pressure and λ at a constant temperature while employing water injection for evaporative cooling. On the one hand, it has been demonstrated that the CI engine can operate across a very wide range of EGR rates—up to 95% at low loads—although with excessive O2 dilution, as inherently high cycle pressure means high EGR and high trapped mass. On the other hand, at mid-high loads, suitable O2 concentrations are achieved even at high cycle pressures, thereby enabling efficient combustion. The cycle operating intake pressure is identified as a key variable in the optimization and control of closed-cycle RICEs. Furthermore, it was shown that the exhaust dry CO2 concentration can be isolated from variations in load, water injection, or EGR, maintaining a constant level through the control of λinj. A critical correlation was observed between the quantity of liquid water ingested by the engine and the deterioration of combustion efficiency (an increase in CO and uHC emissions), presenting a fundamental challenge for closed cycles operating with high wet EGR rates. The extended ignition delay caused by OFC CI - RICE offers a promising avenue for the adoption of highly reactive fuels, such as high-cetane biodiesel, paving the way for the integration of biofuels with source CO2 capture directly from the highly concentrated flue gas of SCC-OFC RICEs.

papers.title: Integrating hydrogen into Ontario’s energy hub: A robust, carbon-aware framework for power–heat–transport
papers.abstract: Decarbonizing electricity generation, heating, and transportation simultaneously requires integrated planning tools that coordinate multiple energy carriers while remaining reliable under uncertainty. This paper develops a carbon-aware and uncertainty-resilient optimization framework for a grid-connected multi-energy hub that co-optimizes electricity, heating, cooling, and transportation services with an explicit hydrogen sub-hub. The model is formulated as a mixed-integer linear program over annual planning states from 2025 to 2050, representing 25 inter-year transition intervals. The hub integrates photovoltaic and wind generation, dispatchable natural gas-based conversion, storage, demand response, EV charging and V2G, and a storage-mediated hydrogen chain comprising an electrolyzer, hydrogen storage, FCEV demand, and stationary fuel-cell reconversion. Two policy archetypes are examined: a carbon tax, represented by an emissions-cost term in the objective, and a net-zero pathway, represented by a declining emissions constraint. Feasibility-critical operational uncertainty is treated through budgeted robust optimization with deviation bounds ± 30 % deviation bounds and a tunable uncertainty budget, applied to electricity and heat balances. Under the adopted representative-period design, the Ontario case yields an electrolyzer expansion from 300 MW in 2025 to 3800 MW in 2050, hydrogen-storage expansion from 2000 to 37,000 MWh, and a robustness premium of approximately 6.6%–9.0% in the policy cases. These numerical magnitudes are conditional on the compression of each planning year into a representative 48-hour window. Because this aggregation excludes sequences longer than that window, the 37-GWh result is not a validated seasonal-adequacy requirement and is likely downward-biased when multi-day low-renewable episodes are binding; the reported robustness premium should likewise be interpreted as conditional on the adopted temporal representation.

Decarbonization benefits of municipal solid waste recovery: A cross-country analysis of 32 countries
papers.abstract: Municipal solid waste (MSW) recovery is critical to global decarbonization agendas. Existing studies have provided important insights into the environmental performance of alternative waste-treatment pathways through life-cycle and scenario-based assessments. However, less is known about whether recovery expansion translates into measurable reductions in observed carbon emissions. This study employs an instrumental-variable framework to estimate the economy-wide carbon-emission effects of MSW recovery using a 32-country panel from 1998 to 2023, addressing reverse-causality concerns in the recovery-emission relationship. The results show that, across the 32-country sample, a 10% increase in aggregate MSW recovery is associated with an average 0.95–1.15% reduction in per capita carbon emissions. This estimate reflects the net system-level effect of recovery expansion under the observed mix of recovery pathways and national conditions, rather than a common effect of individual recovery technologies. The effect varies substantially across recovery systems: energy-recovery-dominated systems show stronger mitigation effects than recycling-dominated systems, with further differences across recovery scale, energy structure, and socioeconomic conditions. Finally, selected non-sample countries are compared with the 32-country sample across key structural moderators to identify where recovery expansion is most likely to deliver large mitigation gains. Overall, the study provides cross-country causal evidence on how MSW recovery translates into economy-wide emission outcomes under different national conditions, offering a system-level basis for aligning recovery strategies with broader decarbonization goals.

papers.title: The synergy of building information modeling and artificial intelligence for building carbon management: A systematic review
Modified Biochar for Wastewater Nutrient Recovery and Slow‐Release Fertilization in Sandy Agroecosystems
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Modified biochars are increasingly recognized as multifunctional materials for wastewater nutrient recovery and slow‐release fertilization in sandy agroecosystems. This review evaluates modified biochars, with particular emphasis on tyre‐derived biochar (TBC), for (i) recovery of nitrogen (N) and phosphorus (P) from wastewater and digestate and (ii) reuse of nutrient‐enriched biochar as a slow‐release fertilizer in sandy agroecosystems. Importantly, pristine biochar often shows limited affinity for anionic phosphorus species such as orthophosphate because its surface is commonly negatively charged, whereas chemical or mineral modification can markedly enhance P adsorption by introducing reactive sites and improving surface functionality. Across the literature, modified biochars generally outperform pristine materials in nutrient recovery due to increased surface area, porosity, and functional group density, with adsorption governed by ion exchange, electrostatic attraction, surface complexation, pore filling, and mineral precipitation. Following soil application, nutrient‐loaded biochars can improve nutrient retention, reduce leaching losses, and supply nutrients gradually, making them particularly relevant for sandy soils in arid and semi‐arid regions where low organic matter and rapid drainage constrain nutrient‐use efficiency and crop productivity. In this context, biomass‐derived biochars more directly support biogenic nutrient recycling, whereas TBC is more appropriately framed as a waste‐derived resource recovery material within a broader waste‐valorization pathway rather than a closed circular nutrient cycle. However, performance varies with feedstock, modification strategy, wastewater composition, nutrient form, and soil conditions, while contaminant risks including heavy metals, polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), and phytotoxicity remain important limitations, especially for waste‐derived chars. Overall, modified biochars show strong potential to link wastewater treatment, nutrient recovery, and improved fertilization efficiency in sandy agroecosystems, but future work should prioritize long‐term field validation, contaminant safety, and site‐specific biochar design for arid and semi‐arid farming systems.

Robust equilibria in cheap-talk games with fairly transparent motives
papers.abstract: For cheap-talk games with a binary state space in which the sender has state-independent preferences, we characterize equilibria that are robust to introducing slight state-dependence on the side of the sender. Not all equilibria are robust, but the sender-optimum is always achieved at some robust equilibrium.

Does voluntary health insurance lead to better health outcomes? Evidence from the Italian NHS
Non‐Traditional Roles and Unmet Care Need During Primary Care Appointments
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Primary healthcare systems worldwide face a shortage of General Practitioners and Nurses. One response by the English Health System to combat this shortage is to expand the role of non‐traditional roles in primary care, often shifting away tasks from Nurses. Non‐traditional practitioners, though less taxing on budgets, tend to have less formal training than Doctors and Nurses, which may affect quality of care. Using data from 614,115 respondents to a survey of primary care patients in England between 2018 and 2022, we assess the extent to which non‐traditional practitioners meet patients' needs in primary care appointments. Patients who see a non‐traditional provider have a 12.6 percentage points lower probability that their care needs were met, relative to those seeing a Nurse. Findings are consistent across linear, probit and instrumented recursive bivariate probit models, and concentrated amongst patients aged 35–54.

papers.title: The Ubiquity of Business Groups around the World: A Property‐Rights Theory
papers.abstract: Abstract Business groups (BGs) are collections of legally independent firms connected by ownership ties and are widely present in both developing and developed economies. We develop property‐rights theory (PRT) to explain this prevalence, extending its scope from the allocation of rights over a bundle of assets to the legal partitioning of assets as another allocative mechanism of property rights. Our conceptual framework complements traditional theories understanding BGs primarily as responses to institutional voids. Drawing on a large global dataset of firms, we examine how firm asset specificity and ownership sharing influence the controlling owners' decision to organize their economic activities as a BG or as a standalone firm. We find that the likelihood of adopting a BG organizational form over a standalone entity increases when (1) controlling owners rely on more firm‐specific assets, and (2) ownership is shared or potentially shared. Moreover, our findings are robust across three commonly observed firm strategic configurations: focused, vertically integrated, and diversified. Our study expands the PRT by developing a theory of property‐rights architecture, moving forward from the institutional voids perspective to explain BGs as efficient governance responses to asset and ownership complexities, hence contributing also to the strategic management and international business literatures.

papers.title: An Integrated Three‐Phase Green Quality Function Deployment Framework for Evaluating Lean–Green Criteria Under Uncertainty
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Manufacturers need decision models that translate environmental and customer requirements into operational priorities while integrating lean and green practices within a unified programme. This study develops and applies an integrated decision framework to identify, structure and prioritise lean–green manufacturing criteria and to examine how their relative importance changes as strategic requirements are translated into technical, environmental and operational priorities. An initial literature‐derived set of 15 criteria and 55 subcriteria was refined through expert screening to eight criteria and 42 subcriteria. Fuzzy analytic network process (FANP) was first used to capture interdependencies among the retained criteria and derive their network‐based priorities. These priorities were subsequently carried through three linked green quality function deployment (GQFD) matrices, sequentially relating lean–green criteria to gearbox technical characteristics, environmental requirements and lean enablers. The resulting lean‐enabler weights were then incorporated into interval VIKOR to obtain the final compromise priorities under uncertainty. FANP ranked workforce, environmental performance and process highest, whereas the final analysis placed supply chain, performance outcomes and environmental performance in the leading positions. This cross‐stage reordering shows that structural importance within an interdependent decision network does not necessarily translate directly into implementation priority and demonstrates the value of tracing how lean–green priorities are reconfigured across successive deployment stages.

papers.title: From Good to Green: Entrepreneurial Pathways to Eco‐Innovation
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The connection between personal well‐being and planetary health is often overlooked. This study is aimed at researching into the effects of entrepreneurs' well‐being on eco‐innovation. More specifically, and grounded on the entrepreneurship literature, we argue that entrepreneurial orientation, as an internal factor, and ecosystem exploitation, as an external factor, mediate the relationship between well‐being and eco‐innovation. Based on a sample of 401 entrepreneurs and using an SEM analysis, results suggest that entrepreneurial well‐being does not directly promote eco‐innovation. Thus, feeling well is not an enough precondition to promote improvements for the environment. Instead, working internally toward more entrepreneurial attitudes, as well as working externally by leveraging the available mechanisms in the ecosystem, may help entrepreneurs to engage in eco‐innovation. Our research supports a holistic view of entrepreneurship as a human and ecological endeavor, contributing not only to economic value but also to the resilience of individuals, organizations, and their ecosystems.

papers.title: Engagement is not enough: Unlocking the path from green leadership to environmental sustainability

Accounting and the fragmented self: institutional opacity, spiritual inequality and moral burden in Islamic finance
papers.abstract: Purpose This study examines how Islamic financial institutions, despite claiming ethical legitimacy, may reproduce spiritual and moral inequalities. Drawing on Muhammad Iqbal's concept of khudi (Self), the study examines how institutional opacity, limited theological engagement and compliance-oriented practices displace moral responsibility onto individuals, forcing consumers to navigate financial choices amid guilt, uncertainty and fragmented ethical agency. Design/methodology/approach The study adopts a qualitative interpretive approach, drawing on 30 semi-structured interviews with UK-based Muslim consumers who currently hold or have previously held Islamic financial products. The data were analysed thematically to explore how individuals experience ethical ambiguity, self-surveillance and clerical authority, and how they resist the commodification of their faith within modern financial systems. Findings Rather than a transparent ethical alternative, Islamic finance asserts moral authority without substantive justification. Facing institutional opacity and limited theological reasoning, participants internalise moral risk through guilt and self-surveillance. This uneven clarity erodes trust in religious authority, intensifies spiritual disorientation, and exposes how institutions can privatise accountability while retaining institutional legitimacy. Research limitations/implications By introducing khudi as a counter-accountability framework to demonstrate that inequalities take spiritual and moral forms, the study offers a new ontological lens for reimagining accountability as a dialogical and emancipatory practice. It urges institutions, Shariah boards and standard-setters to move beyond formal, audit-driven compliance. It repositions accountability as a substantive ethical practice, demanding that claims of Islamic legitimacy be structurally transparent and publicly justified. Originality/value Extending critical accounting scholarship, the study reveals that inequality in Islamic finance is spiritual and moral. By introducing Iqbal's khudi (Self), it provides a novel framework demonstrating how calculative regimes can either fragment or sustain the transcendent Self, repositioning accountability as a site for reclaiming spiritual agency.

Size- and Time-Resolved Emission Rates of Particulate Matter Mass, Chemical Constituents, and Oxidative Potential from Indoor Sources
papers.abstract: Abstract We quantified the time- and size-resolved emission rates of particulate matter (PM) mass, its chemical constituents, and OP (via dithiothreitol assay) from six indoor sources in a test chamber (two types of incense, candle, toaster, humidifier, and cigarette). Both the chemical composition and mass-normalized OP (OPm) varied little temporally. However, both the chemical composition and OPm varied with particle size from <0.25 to 10 μm, with quasi-ultrafine particles (Q-UFPs < 0.25 μm) showing the highest OPm. The particle size distribution of the PM emitted from these sources was mostly unimodal, with both PM10 mass and OP emission rate concentrated in the Q-UFP size range. Given the abundance of Q-UFPs in the emitted PM with their high intrinsic OP, we find that 37 ± 3% of the emitted PM10 mass and OP from these sources has the potential to deposit in the respiratory tract, 45 ± 2% of which deposits in the alveolar region. An exploratory exposure assessment suggests that for an equal dose of PM10 mass and OP originating from these indoor sources vs ambient PM, the emissions from the tested indoor sources will likely result in a 76 ± 10% higher dose of alveolar-deposited mass and OP. Collectively, these results emphasize the need to better quantify the size-resolved toxicological properties of PM from myriad indoor emission sources to reliably estimate the resulting health risks.

papers.title: Thermal analysis of a ground-mounted photovoltaic system coupled with the crop of a metal-hyperaccumulating plant using multiple modelling approaches
papers.abstract: Understanding the operating temperature of photovoltaic (PV) modules is crucial for assessing their electrical performance, yet most agrivoltaic models focus on crop yield rather than PV thermal behaviour. This study addresses this gap by proposing a one-dimensional dynamic thermal model based on a nodal approach to simulate the PV modules’ temperatures. The model was validated using PV back-surface temperatures measured during a two-year experiment and integrate soil and vegetation surface temperatures and meteorological parameters. This model (Model 3) was evaluated against two simplified thermal models: the Ross thermal model (Model 1) and the Normal Operating Cell Temperature model (Model 2). Model 3 showed the greatest precision with a Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) down to 1.6°C and a Nash-Sutcliffe Efficiency coefficient (NSE) > 92 %, outperforming Models 1 and 2 by 20 % in NSE and 50-80 % in RMSE reduction. Model 1 performed better under cloudy conditions (RMSE 3.6-4.5°C; NSE 72-80 %), while Model 2 slightly improved sunny-day predictions (NSE up to 82 %). Model 3 consistently provided the best results (NSE > 92 %). Comparing simulated and measured electrical energy production of an opaque module, Models 1 and 2 overestimated output (+2 % to +3 %, more under sunny conditions), while Model 3 exhibited the closest agreement (deviation < 1 %). Parametric simulations with Model 3 also highlighted the potential of brownfield sites in southern France for ecovoltaic deployment. This work provides a robust thermal modelling framework for ecovoltaic systems, improving performance predictions and supporting sustainable energy integration.

Impact of global supply chain pressures on energy demand and stability: The role of global sustainability initiatives
papers.abstract: Global supply chain pressures (GSCP) have become a major challenge for multinational enterprises (MNEs), influencing firm-level operational decisions, including evolving energy demand patterns. This paper investigates the impact of global supply chain pressures on energy consumption in Chinese MNEs from 2013 to 2022. Results from Double-Selection Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO) linear regression indicate that GSCP increases the energy demand of Chinese MNEs. One possible explanation is that GSCP undermines production stability and operational efficiency, prompting firms to intensify production, extend operating hours, and adopt additional shifts to meet volatile demand conditions. Furthermore, global shocks (i.e., US-China Trade War and COVID-19) and global green initiatives (i.e., Montreal Protocol–Kigali Amendment, the EU Innovation Fund, and the Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative) significantly moderate the relationship between GSCP and energy demand. The heterogeneity analysis exhibits that the GSCP impact is most pronounced among state-owned MNEs, firms with substantial overseas investment experience, and enterprises exhibiting lower degrees of internationalisation. This study contributes new empirical and theoretical insights into how global supply chain disruptions affect corporate energy demand and shape the strategic responses of Chinese MNEs.

Quantum gases below 10 picokelvin in space
papers.abstract: Ultracold atom platforms enable low temperatures and long free evolution times, which are crucial for fundamental physics tests and atom interferometry. The lowest equivalent temperature reported in such a system is 38 pK with a free expansion time of 2 s, achieved in atom-chip-based magnetic traps in microgravity. Optical dipole trap (ODT) systems offer better optical access and the flexibility to condense both magnetic and non-magnetic atoms, but have not been used to prepare quantum degenerate gases under microgravity conditions. Here we report an ODT-based Bose-Einstein condensate created aboard the China Space Station, containing 2.0 × 10 4 atoms, reaching an equivalent temperature of 9.7 − 2.7 + 3.2 pK with a free expansion time of 7.0 s. This record-low temperature could stimulate a new generation of ODT-based experiments in quantum simulation and precision measurements in space.

papers.title: Stacked porous NiTi structure with low cost and ultrahigh fatigue life for elastocaloric cooling
papers.abstract: Elastocaloric cooling (eC) uses shape memory alloys (SMAs) as energy-efficient, eco-friendly refrigerants. However, cost-effectively fabricating SMAs into fatigue-resistant, heat transfer–enhanced structures remains a key obstacle to commercialization of the eC technology. We introduce a “stamping and stacking” (S-S) method for producing porous, fatigue-resistant SMA structures. Honeycomb-like chips are stamped from nitinol (NiTi) thin sheets and then stacked into a layered tubular structure to increase heat exchange surface and at the same time avoid buckling and splitting failures encountered in existing SMA structures. The stacked structure endures >10 8 compression cycles and can deliver high specific cooling power of 3850 watts per kilogram. Our S-S method reduces fabrication costs by one order of magnitude compared with existing approaches, enabling mass production of eC refrigerant structures for commercial deployment.

papers.title: Echoes of the Anthropocene: Noise pollution as a global threat
papers.abstract: Anthropogenic noise is a rapidly expanding global pollutant, but its effects across biological levels from individuals to ecosystems remain unquantified. We conducted phylogenetically controlled meta-analyses of 214 experimental studies on 177 aquatic and terrestrial species with ranges that span six continents. Noise altered at least one physiological, developmental, or behavioral trait in 80% of species studied, with declines in fitness and abundance and disruptions of predator-prey interactions. Effects occurred in every habitat, although response mechanisms varied for some traits and species, creating winners and losers. Only multispecies analyses can reveal such species- and ecosystem-level impacts of anthropogenic stressors. Our results establish noise as a novel selection pressure reshaping ecosystem dynamics and as a pervasive stressor requiring soundscape protection alongside habitat conservation.

papers.title: Obesity pharmacotherapies and cognition
papers.abstract: Pharmacotherapies for obesity and type 2 diabetes are increasingly being evaluated for their effects on cognition and brain health. Evidence from preclinical models, observational cohorts, and clinical trials has intensified interest, but findings remain mixed. A central challenge is to determine whether potential cognitive effects arise from direct actions on neural circuits, indirect consequences of improved cardiometabolic health, or both. This Review examines the evidence across cardiometabolic disease, aging, and Alzheimer’s disease, focusing on glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1)–based therapies and combination approaches that engage glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide, glucagon, and amylin pathways. We assess how receptor pharmacology, brain exposure, metabolic context, and disease stage shape cognitive outcomes and discuss how mechanistic clarity could guide therapies aimed at preserving or improving cognition.

Seafloor geodesy delineates fast megathrust relocking after the giant 2011 Tohoku earthquake
papers.abstract: How and when the subduction megathrust recovers its locking state after a great earthquake is important to understanding earthquake-cycle physics and future hazards. Here we report the delineation of the relocking process after the 2011 magnitude 9 Tohoku earthquake with 14 years of postseismic seafloor geodetic observations. These data, combined with onshore geodetic observations, analyses of repeating earthquakes, and numerical modeling, reveal how the recovery of locking is interrupted by afterslip on the megathrust and accompanied by stress relaxation in the viscoelastic upper mantle. The results indicate that the megathrust has already arrived at a locking state today similar to that before the earthquake despite the ongoing stress relaxation. The acquired knowledge aids understanding of megathrust earthquake cycles at other subduction zones.

papers.title: Tumor metastasis co-opts liver hematopoiesis to promote immunosuppression
papers.abstract: Cancer-associated hematopoietic abnormalities contribute to systemic immunosuppression. However, whether tumors can initiate localized extramedullary hematopoiesis to suppress antitumor immunity remains unclear. In this study, we identify a distinct form of hepatic hematopoiesis driven by liver metastasis–associated hematopoietic stem cells (LM-HSCs). Liver metastases establish ectopic periportal hematopoietic niches that recruit bone marrow HSCs through Kupffer cell–dependent C-C motif chemokine receptor 1 (CCR1) signaling. Although LM-HSCs retain self-renewal and multipotency, cAMP response element–binding protein (CREB) activation skews their differentiation toward the myeloid lineage, particularly annexin A1–positive (ANXA1 + ) immature neutrophils. These neutrophils produce glucocorticoids, which activate glucocorticoid receptor signaling in a paracrine manner and induce immune checkpoint receptor expression and functional anergy in CD8 + T and natural killer cells. Collectively, these findings suggest that liver metastases reprograms hepatic hematopoiesis to promote immunosuppression.

papers.title: Can artificial intelligence align with Indigenous science?
papers.abstract: As the use of generative and agentic artificial intelligence (AI) increases, alarms are being raised about how the technology could replace human contribution, override human supervision, ignore ethical and technical guardrails, and cause increasingly irreparable harm to the environment. This creates potentially destructive outcomes for life on Earth. From a traditional Indigenous science perspective, such possibilities in themselves would be enough to immediately stop presently configured AI releases. In a Lakota context, science must ensure as little harm as possible is done to life. Therefore, AI as presently configured simply would not qualify to advance further from an ethical and scientific standpoint. Indigenous science asks something fundamentally different than what AI presently seeks to, or can, answer. But that does not mean that future forms of AI can never align with Indigenous science.

papers.title: Equivalence of pseudogap and pairing energy in a cuprate high-temperature superconductor
papers.abstract: The pseudogap stands out in the phase diagram of the cuprate high-temperature superconductors because its origin and relationship to superconductivity remain elusive. The origin of the pseudogap has been debated, with competing hypotheses attributing it to preformed electron pairs or local order, such as charge density waves. We present unambiguous evidence supporting the pairing scenario, using local shot-noise spectroscopy measurements in Bi 2 Sr 2 CaCu 2 O 8+δ . Our data demonstrate that the pseudogap energy coincides with the onset of electron pairing and is spatially heterogeneous with values reaching up to 70 milli–electron volts. Our results exclude a pure local order origin of the pseudogap, link the pseudogap to Cooper pair formation, and suggest that the limiting factor for higher critical temperature in cuprates is phase coherence.

papers.title: The first 1000 days: Modeling language learning from individual children’s everyday speech
papers.abstract: Abstract A longstanding challenge in developmental science is to understand how children learn language from naturalistic everyday input. To study this process, we leveraged the First 1,000 Days (1kD) dataset, which provides longitudinal, ultra-dense daily audiovisual recordings for individual children in their home environments. This unusually detailed, child-specific record of early experience enabled us to pair each child’s rich language input with a cognitively grounded learning agent, linking naturalistic experience (“nurture”) to internal learning mechanisms (“nature”). Trained incrementally on each child’s input without prior linguistic knowledge, the learning agent discovered speech units corresponding to the English phoneme inventory and acquired thousands of words, closely mirroring individual developmental trajectories. Learning generalized across children while preserving individual differences in rate and timing. Interestingly, learning relied not only on linguistic input but also on the rehearsal of past experiences at the end of each training day. These findings demonstrate that everyday environments provide sufficient structure for language acquisition and establish a unified mechanistic framework for studying development in real-world contexts.

papers.title: When fat adapts: From physiological remodeling to disease
papers.abstract: Adipose tissue undergoes extensive remodeling to adapt to changing physiological demands. This plasticity encompasses changes in adipocyte metabolism and number, extracellular matrix organization, vascularization, immune composition, and innervation. When coordinated, these processes preserve energy buffering, thermogenesis, endocrine function, and local tissue support. Pathological adipose tissue remodeling drives obesity-related complications and contributes to many diseases involving organ-associated adipose depots throughout the body. In cancer, tumor-associated fat can develop a metabolic and fibroinflammatory niche that promotes tumor growth and invasion, and remodeling of other depots can directly disrupt neighboring tissues. Recent studies have identified mesenchymal, immune, vascular, and adipocyte states that govern adaptive or pathological outcomes. These findings broaden therapeutic goals beyond reducing fat mass toward restoring adipogenesis, substrate turnover, thermogenic capacity, and tissue-niche function.

Targeting hormone conversion through dietary fiber improves polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome
papers.abstract: Excessive androgens serve as a primary driver for many phenotypic features of polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS). Although dietary fiber has been shown to alleviate PMOS, its effects on androgen concentrations and the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. In a clinical trial, we demonstrated that a dietary fiber combination consisting of inulin, resistant starch, and β-glucan reduces androgen concentrations in patients’ plasma. Mechanistically, dietary fiber increased the abundance of Bacteroides xylanisolven s, which converts androstenedione into a nonandrogenic secondary hormone metabolite we named coproandrosterone, which is further metabolized by gut microbiota into dihydro-coproandrosterone. This metabolic pathway was validated in a mouse model. These findings highlight the potential of dietary fiber to alleviate PMOS by modulating androgen homeostasis through gut microbiota, offering insights for prebiotic and probiotic therapies.

papers.title: Discovering molecular modulators with nanoswitch screening
papers.abstract: Molecules that modulate protein-protein interactions, including through ternary complex formation, have been established as key therapeutics. Yet they can be challenging to discover, as standard screening approaches often lack throughput or fail to directly assay multibody interactions. We addressed this by combining DNA nanoswitch–based selection of nucleotide-encoded libraries with next-generation sequencing to create FIND (Functional Interaction–based Nanoswitch Discovery), which enables ultrahigh-throughput discovery of compounds that induce or increase protein-protein interactions. We demonstrate FIND by discovering nanobodies that stabilize the interaction between angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 and the receptor-binding domain of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 and by discovering agonists of peroxisome proliferator–activated receptor gamma from a DNA-barcoded small-molecule library. By enabling rapid discovery of molecular modulators, FIND could lead to new therapeutics across many conditions.

papers.title: Glacial abrupt transitions in ocean circulation were much slower than ice-core records imply
papers.abstract: Dansgaard-Oeschger (DO) events during the last ice age are thought to reflect rapid shifts in the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC). Greenland ice cores suggest warming transitions within only a few decades—or even just over 10 years. Using precisely dated speleothem oxygen-isotope records from the Asian monsoon region, we have shown that the same DO warmings unfolded over more than a century. Isotope modeling revealed that Greenland records primarily capture a rapid atmospheric reorganization triggered by the initial sea-ice retreat in the northeastern North Atlantic, whereas the parallel AMOC recovery and hemispheric thermal adjustment proceeded much more slowly. These findings reveal that natural AMOC transitions evolved more slowly than the rapid North Greenland oxygen-isotope shifts would imply, thereby refining our understanding of “abruptness” during DO events.

papers.title: Obesity management medications: The way forward
papers.abstract: Obesity is now widely recognized as a chronic progressive condition. The altered biological mechanisms that cause obesity frequently require long-term treatment, including pharmacotherapies or bariatric surgery. In recent decades, the pathophysiology of obesity has been understood to an extent that obesity management medication (OMM) discovery could be rationally pursued. Advances in defining the regulation of food intake and energy expenditure by molecular communication from peripheral organs to the brain led to the development of OMMs that appear capable of safely achieving scalable and sustained body weight loss. However, side effects, heterogeneous treatment responses, long-term metabolic adaptations, adherence, and other factors may limit the use of existing OMMs and justify the development of additional medications to improve the health of people living with obesity.

papers.title: In the image of their tools
Denoising the US Census: Succinct block hierarchical regression
papers.abstract: The 2020 United States Census adopted differential privacy to protect individual confidentiality, adding calibrated noise to summary demographic measurements that are then reconciled into population tables. We developed BlueDown, a postprocessing algorithm that combines techniques from linear regression and constrained optimization while exploiting measurement structure for efficiency. On 2020 Census data, BlueDown reduced the error of groupings by race at the county level by 21 to 36% and of all county-level groupings by 9 to 58%; at the tract level, it reduced error of groupings by housing type by 38 to 61%. These gains came at no cost to confidentiality or computational efficiency and would improve the validity of research relying on this definitive dataset and analyses used to guide the distribution of more than $1.5 trillion in annual federal spending.

Direct evidence for psychoactive cannabis use 2800 years ago
papers.abstract: Cannabis is the world’s most-used illicit psychoactive plant, yet direct prehistoric evidence for its consumption is rare. In this study, we present the earliest direct evidence of cannabis use: offerings of plant parts and chemical compounds in ancient human hair recovered from a monumental tomb in Siberia. The findings suggest that the plant was used for its psychoactive qualities across Eurasia, where specific wild populations might have had naturally higher active compound levels. We show that the practice of cannabis consumption dates back at least 2800 years, anchoring debates around contemporary usage and informing discussions on cannabis in medicine, public health, law, and industry.

Why Do Union Jobs Pay More? New Evidence from Matched Employer-Employee Data
papers.abstract: Abstract We use Canadian matched employer-employee data to assess the sources of the union pay premium. After controlling for worker heterogeneity using the two-way fixed effects approach of Abowd, Kramarz, and Margolis (AKM), we find that unionized firms pay about 15 log points more than non-unionized firms. Forty percent of this gap is linked to productivity differences between unionized and non-unionized firms as measured by value added per worker. The remaining gap reflects unions’ ability to extract more rents for workers. Our estimates imply that unions raise pay among unionized workers by around 9 log points, with considerable heterogeneity by industry and firm birth cohorts. The union effect grows to about 11 log points in an extension of the AKM approach where unions also affect the returns to unobservable worker characteristics.

papers.title: Financial constraints and the transmission of monetary policy: Evidence from relaxation of collateral constraints
Shadow banks on the rise: Evidence across market segments
papers.abstract: This paper examines the comparative advantages of shadow banks across market segments. Combining credit bureau data on retail loans in India with weather shocks as a proxy for credit demand, we show that Fintechs respond more in uncollateralized markets. In contrast, non-Fintech shadow banks exhibit stronger responsiveness in collateralized markets. Exploiting geographic heterogeneity in the adoption of digital payments, we identify technology as the key advantage for Fintechs. Leveraging four natural experiments, we document the significance of lower regulation for non-Fintech shadow banks. Our results suggest that the comparative advantage of shadow banks differs across market segments.

papers.title: Perceived Political Bias of the Federal Reserve,
papers.abstract: Abstract We conduct a survey experiment with a politically representative sample of more than 5,000 U.S. consumers to study how perceptions of the Federal Reserve’s (Fed) political stance shape macroeconomic expectations, trust, and information processing. Overall, 63.5% of respondents view the Fed as politically neutral, 9.4% as aligned with their own party (in-group), and 27.2% as opposed (out-group). The non-neutral minority differs sharply: out-group respondents report substantially higher inflation expectations and lower trust than neutral or in-group respondents, even after controlling for partisanship and demographics. They also pay more to avoid opposing media and are less likely to receive Fed communication—yet update their expectations by more once exposed to it, placing less weight on their priors when the same article carries a Fed label. In a hypothetical Trump presidency, the neutral share falls to 37.2%, with respondents in both parties shifting toward viewing the Fed as Republican-leaning, consistent with expected political capture. Perceived neutrality is thus central to the Fed’s credibility and the reach of its communication, and it can shift with changes in political leadership.

Are the Hedges of Funds Green?
papers.abstract: Abstract Over the past decade, hedge funds have increasingly embraced green investing. We develop a novel return-based measure of fund greenness and find that greener funds earn higher average returns, consistent with capturing a positive green premium, and are associated with lower risks, especially during adverse periods. We further show that performance gains are greatest among directional funds, whereas risk reduction is most pronounced among nondirectional funds. We also provide evidence that managers of these funds exhibit superior green investment skills through green stock selection and green factor timing. Finally, investors reward greener hedge funds only when they demonstrate strong performance.

Developing technological expertise through ecosystem orchestration for industrial circularity
papers.abstract: Research on circularity often assumes that the more technological expertise industrial firms build, the more circular they become. This study challenges this assumption by showing that technological expertise alone is insufficient; how firms orchestrate collaboration to build such expertise also matters. We examine collaborations between large industrial firms and specialist SMEs, using the ecosystem-as-structure perspective to understand how technological expertise and orchestration come together. Based on a qualitative multiple-case study of seven Indian industrial firms with global operations and their 12 SME partners, drawing on 46 interviews and a validation seminar, we identify three types of technological expertise: material traceability, resource foresight, and decision integration. Each is associated with a distinct orchestration mechanism: ecosystem protocol alignment, cross-boundary validation, and milestone-anchored co-specialization, respectively. We further identify three structural conditions that shape which pairing is viable: activity interdependence, position complementarity, and link transfer specificity. The study contributes to circular economy research by showing that circular value depends on the fit between technological expertise and orchestration, and that different configurations produce distinct forms of circular value rather than simply higher or lower levels of circularity. It extends the ecosystem-as-structure perspective by explaining how structural conditions shape this fit. For practitioners, the findings show how large firms can better align technological expertise development with partner orchestration, while SMEs can use these collaborations to progress from technical service providers towards more strategic co-creation roles.

papers.title: China’s fiscal stimulus, global financial intermediaries, and international spillovers
Ancestor's Legacy? The Effect of Folklore on Corporate Innovation
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT This paper investigates how ancestral narratives shape contemporary corporate innovation. Drawing on pre‐industrial folklore from 20 countries, we exploit within‐country variation in local cultural motifs to examine their impact on firm innovation. We focus on two types of motifs: narratives depicting heroes’ successful challenges relative to challenge‐losing ones and narratives containing supernatural entities. We show that firms located in societies whose local folklore prevalently features heroes overcoming challenges exhibit greater R&D investment and higher patent‐based innovation efficiency, with directionally similar but statistically insignificant evidence for citation‐based efficiency. In contrast, firms in societies where folklore emphasizes supernatural entities display lower R&D investment and lower innovation efficiency. Cross‐sectional analyses indicate that these effects are moderated by regional economic openness and national patent protection and are more pronounced in highly innovative industries and among firms with higher levels of corporate transparency. Our findings are robust after controlling for regional factors or alleviating large country sample bias. The relationship between folklore and R&D investment remains directionally consistent, albeit with lower statistical significance, after instrumenting the folklore measure with historical immigration patterns to the United States. We further show that the net prevalence of challenge‐encouraging motifs is associated with more radical innovation strategies and greater corporate risk‐taking, while supernatural motifs exhibit the opposite pattern. Overall, our findings support the view that folklore persists across generations and meaningfully influences firms’ contemporary economic decisions and outcomes.

The DNA of Neuroticism and Financial Decisions
papers.abstract: A polygenic score (PGS) capturing genetic predisposition toward neuroticism predicts heterogeneity in risk aversion, return beliefs, and stock market participation. This approach addresses key methodological and interpretive concerns associated with phenotypic measures of neuroticism. Risk aversion and return beliefs are important, but incomplete, channels linking the neuroticism PGS to stock market participation. The neuroticism PGS also predicts heterogeneity in demographic and behavioral characteristics previously shown to influence financial choices. These characteristics serve as key channels through which the genetic propensity for neuroticism shapes financial choices.

papers.title: Political uncertainty, social legitimacy, and nonmarket strategy
papers.abstract: Abstract The Decade Award–winning article by Darendeli and Hill (2016) presents a novel yet nuanced approach to the question of whether and how foreign firms can strategically navigate a volatile and unpredictable political environment. Their 2026 retrospective builds on their earlier contribution by showing how their insights have contributed to a number of contemporary IB research streams, including those addressing political risk, political action, and political ties. Going beyond their earlier contribution, in the retrospective, they describe the relational and physical pillars of social legitimacy (Darendeli & Hill, 2026). They then assess the efficacy of their original perspective in an environment characterized by heightened geopolitical conflict and political polarization. Finally, they develop a model that delineates four strategic approaches to legitimacy building in host countries. In this commentary, I offer perspectives that complement and extend their contributions by discussing (1) the nature of political uncertainty and the use of real options in responding to that uncertainty, (2) the literature on substantive versus symbolic CSR and how that might further extend some of their insights, and (3) research regarding when and how multinational enterprises provide public goods and services typically provided by government. I conclude by outlining how Darendeli and Hill’s (2016, 2026) insights have relevance for contemporary practice and policy.

papers.title: Co‐Constructing the Illusion of Progression: How Boundary Blurring and Affirming Reproduce Social Exclusion in Elite Professions
papers.abstract: Abstract Social exclusion is a persistent problem in elite professions. While scholarship has emphasized structural and cultural barriers, less is known about the relational practices and mechanisms through which social exclusion is sustained. Drawing on interviews with 84 lawyers, paralegals, and managers in elite UK law firms, we develop a conceptual model of how the blurring and affirming of social and symbolic boundaries between higher‐status and lower‐status groups reproduces social exclusion. We show how both groups blur and affirm boundaries across three domains: professional work, professional space, and systems of professional advancement. Boundary blurring makes symbolic boundaries more permeable, positioning lower‐status actors as prospective professionals, while boundary affirming maintains social boundaries around professional membership. We identify and theorize the illusion of progression as a relational mechanism emerging from intertwined blurring and affirming, constructing lower‐status roles as pathways into the profession even though progression is rare. The illusion perpetuates liminality by sustaining hope, individualizing failure and undermining lower‐status groups' collective challenge to social exclusion. Our findings advance understanding of the relational mechanism through which social exclusion persists in elite professions, show how boundary blurring can sustain rather than threaten status distinctions, and help explain why organizational diversity and inclusion efforts have produced little substantive change.

papers.title: The Anti‐SLAPP Statutes and Corporate Environmental Policies
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT We examine whether legal protection for civic participation affects corporate pollution. Polluters may deter public discipline through strategic lawsuits. Anti‐SLAPP (Strategic Lawsuit Against Public Participation) statutes mitigate this threat by enabling prompt dismissal and recovery of legal costs. Using a difference‐in‐differences design, we find that enacting an anti‐SLAPP statute in a state significantly reduces toxic emissions from that state by increasing local public pressure. The reduction is greater when the statutes provide stronger protection, when local stakeholders have stronger incentives and abilities to discipline polluters, and when local public pressure increases more after the enactment. Plants lower emissions by improving abatement rather than by reducing output or relocating emissions. Our paper underscores the role of legal protection in environmental governance and informs policy debates over anti‐SLAPP legislation.
